# Transport of insertions on a reference torus

The all-history fixed-jet interface remains open. The fixed bare exponential-source disc required by the original I-1 for every gauge-invariant polynomial is false. In particular the physically normalized dimension-six frustration has a Wilson source zero within O(a²) for a constant smooth test (§7.48). The unamplified frustration and the dimension-four action source have distinct, still open, all-history questions.

The current positive results include the original first-step source integration, the physical coupling and source rows, and the two-step clean and charged large-field subcases. On the homogeneous near-identity clean graph, (7.149) gives a complex connected attachment with the three incoming grades and a positive age gain. Sections 7.49–7.51 construct its new physical curvature kernels, quartic remainder and pointed projection. Equations (7.163)–(7.166) carry these bounds through arbitrarily many fixed clean blocks for the paths that stay in the stable sector, under the stated native margins. The bare action variance bound (7.168) also requires a contact subtraction for cutoff-uniform Tr F² second jets. The amended interface statements and their T5/T6 dependencies are in §6.4. Equations (7.182)–(7.202) treat a pinned first H birth and the actual signed sum over healed bodies, including all fixed live neighbors and a conditional extensive bound for wholly stored stencils at bounded depth. A promoted boundary coefficient crosses the next mixed T in (7.197), with both second log rows retained; (7.200) controls separated real live neighbors and §7.82 verifies a two-seed geometry. Equations (7.203)–(7.219) give the joint-history normalization, the age and incident-volume estimates for witnessed and subsequently healed bodies, and two-home connected bounds for simultaneous releases and the retained native terminal R/B rows. Section 7.96 identifies the same-torus terminal lower bound at the specified fixed stop; arbitrary-physical-volume local control of all terminal survivors and cross-torus vacuum matching are separate. Sections 7.97–7.102 bound intermediate layers and arbitrary multiscale sums of incident live volumes, and control the fresh covariance of complete direct ordinary rows on the admitted mixed T charts, including the real exterior selector change. Sections 7.103–7.111 give the actual two-jet marginal/contact recurrence, regular uniform-action cancellation, profile-difference summation, and matched signed returns. Sections 7.112–7.116 reduce the constant anisotropic trace to a native determinant-window comparison and compute its negative slope in the matched Dirichlet prototype. Sections 7.117–7.123 instead use a true quantized periodic flux, bound the charged fine determinant and hard-constraint correction, and prove the negative upper window for the completed compact Gaussian transfer. Sections 7.124–7.132 prove summable ordinary outputs from admitted mixed returns, keep the signed exterior covariances, and bound all subsequent physical variances for late boundary births or continuous survival to half the tower. The preintegrated analytic B filings have a separate two-jet transfer margin (7.265). Sections 7.133–7.139 give a positive replica expansion on a real mixed bracket, bounded-test comparison on ordinary punctured fibers, a fixed-disc induction for the early homogeneous independent-P reference and the protected real conditional mean comparison. Sections 7.140–7.141 verify the single-step real support margin and handle two genuinely different positive internal kernels through a common outer replica. The arbitrary off-shell internal score, same-source full-law zero-free disc and unrestricted mixed transport remain open. The homogeneous results use the stated CMP109-type selector margins. CMP119 (1.18) uses a shrinking fluctuation selector even on its globally clean sector; §7.74 records the distinction.

The complete clean pressure estimate in §§1–5 requires the additional hypotheses in §1.5. Section 6 gives the current interface, §7 contains the proofs, and §8 gives the consequences.

## 1. Target and interfaces assumed

### 1.1 Target (I-1, restricted form)

On the fixed reference torus T* (side t*, a multiple of ℓ₀), for the Wilson SU(N) theory on Λ_{a,T*} = (aZ/t*Z)⁴ with bare coupling g₀(a) on the admitted trajectory (g_k ≤ ḡ for all k ≤ K = log_L(ℓ₀/a)), insert one smeared gauge-invariant local observable

  O^bare(J) = Σ_{x ∈ Λ_a} a⁴ J(x) 𝒪_a(x),  𝒪_a(x) = a^{-4} Σ_{μ<ν} (1/N) Re Tr(1 − U_{p_{μν}(x)})   (1.1)

(the lattice Tr F² density; normalization conventions in 2.2) with a complex source J: Λ_a → C obtained by restriction of a function J ∈ C⁵(T*) (chessboard-replicated sources W J_c of I-5 are of this form), ‖J‖_{C⁵} ≤ r₀. Prove that the small-field renormalization map of I-0c carries the sourced density ρ_k[J] through K steps in the form

  ρ_k[J] = ρ_k · exp( ⟨J_k, O_k⟩ + W_k[J] ),   k = 0, …, K,   (1.2)

with (i) a transported local observable O_k = Φ_{k-1,k}O_{k-1} + (local corrections), (ii) a source polymer expansion W_k[J] with activities bounded by the graded norm of the inserted births times contraction factors, (iii) first and second J-derivatives at J = 0 represented with bounds uniform in a, (iv) the MT36-form contraction for clean transitions,

  ‖P₄ L^{(2)}_{V_k}(R_j ∘ Φ_{j,k}, V_k)‖_{k} ≤ C g_k L^{−s(k−j)} (g_k/g_j)^{q} ‖R_j‖_{graded, j},   s = 2, q = d,   (1.3)

for a birth R_j of canonical degree d ≥ 3 (and the explicit marginal rows for d = 0, 2), and (v) analyticity of p_{a,T*}[J] − L_a(J) in J on a fixed polydisc, with L_a(J) a strictly local counterterm functional of finite range ≤ C ℓ₀, additive over cells with margins.

The dimension-six projection P₆ (appropriate to the dimension-six H-type source) becomes P₄ here because the inserted observable has engineering dimension four; section 2.5 makes the correspondence explicit, and section 3.4 states the dimension-six (H-type) variant as a corollary with s = 2 unchanged and the marginal row absent.

### 1.2 Interfaces assumed (verbatim imports)

- **I-0c** (fixed-volume representation of the effective density with large fields; coupling flow g_{k+1}^{-2} = g_k^{-2} − b₀ log L + r_k, |r_k| ≤ C g_k²). Used in the form: on T*, for every k ≤ K, Z_{a,T*} = ∫ ρ_k dHaar on Λ_{ℓ_k,T*}, ρ_k = exp(−Vol(T*) e_k(a)) ρ̃_k, ρ̃_k a convergent sum over large-field regions with the small-field part exp(−g_k^{-2} S_{eff,k} − V_k), V_k a sum of exponentially decaying polymer activities, with constants uniform in k and a.
- **I-2** (admission on T*): assumed exactly as stated; it is invoked only in section 7 to formulate the large-field residual transitions, never in the proofs of sections 3–4.

Nothing from I-1, I-3, I-4, I-5 is assumed. Exact finite-cutoff identities from the Wilson-source volumes [W] (see [source_estimates](source_estimates/README.md); cited by source page) are re-proved here where used (Prop. 2.1, [W, p. 10], re-proved as Lemma 4.3.1).

### 1.3 Labels

(P) proved here; (P | SF) proved here from the standing hypothesis SF(k) of section 2.6 (itself (L)/(C) item by item, see 2.6 and section 5); (L) literature, with theorem number and hypotheses checked in section 5; (C) conditional on a displayed hypothesis; (O) open.

### 1.4 Conventions

G = SU(N), Λ_{a,T} = (aZ/TZ)⁴ periodic, dμ_{a,T} = Z_{a,T}^{-1} exp(−β_a S) dHaar with S = Σ_p (N − Re Tr U_p), β_a = 2N/g₀(a)². Block scale L odd ≥ 3, ℓ_k = L^k a, K = log_L(ℓ₀/a), running couplings g_k, admitted bound ḡ, p_{a,T} = Vol(T)^{-1} log Z_{a,T}. One further convention is used: the dimensionless plaquette curvature at scale k (2.3).

### 1.5 Restrictions on §§2–5 (P: the algebraic diagnoses; O: the missing estimates on the actual gauge construction)

1. **Action convention.** With the fixed `S = Σ_p(N − Re Tr U_p)` and `β = 2N/g₀²`, the normalized plaquette observable of (2.2) obeys `S = N O₀(1)` and `βS = 2N²g₀⁻² O₀(1)`. The factor N is included in (2.2′) below. Its SF1 action, written with coefficient `g_k⁻²` times the normalized plaquette action, must likewise be converted before identifying it with the running coupling of §1.4; it is not a verbatim I-0c import.
2. **Source amplitude.** Equations (3.7)–(3.9) allow `z_K` to grow with the cutoff. Their right-hand sides therefore do not prove cutoff-uniform bare-source norms or a fixed source radius. A multiplicative source renormalization is a new hypothesis, not an automatic consequence of local contact subtraction. Proposition 7.12 below proves an alternative bounded-z result under a stronger, explicitly stated complex coupling-flow bound.
3. **Logarithm.** Analyticity and an upper bound for an integral do not imply a zero-free disc or an analytic logarithm there. Proposition 7.10 supplies the missing sufficient criterion. The expression (3.12) also appears to count its linear expectation twice; the exact formula is `Vol⁻¹ log E_K exp(H_K(J))` after the full stated identity functional has been removed.
4. **Locality and age.** A background map with exponentially decaying tails does not put the pullback on a carrier of strictly shrinking support. Consequently the support argument in Lemma 4.2.4 does not prove the claimed absolute anchor moments. Weighted coefficient kernels, with all tails retained, are required; §7.1 supplies an algebra for them, not a construction of their gauge-theory bounds. The signed moments in §2.5 do not control the required sums of absolute coefficients. The identification there of P₆ with removal of all ordinary jets of orders ≤3 is not the engineering-dimension-six projection of [W, MT33/MT36, pp. 691–692]: MT33/MT36 retain covariant completions and lower/contact rows. Corollary 3.4 is therefore not established by that identification.
5. **Clean theorem labels.** Theorems 3.1–3.3, Corollary 3.4 and the corresponding target items of §1.1 are **proposals with unresolved proof obligations**, not certified (P | SF) theorems. In particular SF2(c)'s enlarged holomorphic disc does not follow from a bound on the smaller domain; this enlargement is an independent hypothesis. The `(P | SF)` markings in §§3–4 mean only the intended conditional scope of that derivation and are qualified by this item. The elementary age inequality (4.3), finite-source algebra when its hypotheses hold, and the new lemmas explicitly labeled P remain available.
6. **Compact entry bound.** For (2.2), the own-scale compact bound is `|O_k(J;X)| ≤ 12 n_k(X) ‖J‖∞`, where `n_k(X)` counts based sites (six plaquettes per site, each normalized excess ≤2). There is no extra `ℓ_k⁴` after canceling the density's `ℓ_k⁻⁴`. An analytically defined effective birth need not have any compact extension. R-1 is consequently conditional on a proved compact extension of the *actual* marked activity; the finite-scale compactness of the original Wilson insertion is insufficient for arbitrary descendants.
7. **Pressure and contacts.** The full pressure is the logarithm of the sum of sector partition functions, not `p^sf + Σ_Z` of raw sector integrals. A counterterm supported at a fixed positive range `CMℓ₀` is not automatically a diagonal contact; cancellation for supports separated by that range does not prove reflection-positivity preservation. The statements of §§3–5 on these points are restricted accordingly. The susceptibility application further requires lattice-scale frustration marks for susceptibility, a stronger source class than a bounded physical C⁵ ball.

These are direct checks of the argument of §§2–5, not counterexamples to four-dimensional Yang–Mills existence.

## 2. Definitions and conventions

### 2.1 Lattices, blocks, polymers, distances

Λ_k := Λ_{ℓ_k,T*} = (ℓ_k Z / t* Z)⁴, k = 0, …, K; Λ₀ = Λ_a, Λ_K = Λ_{ℓ₀,T*}. Bonds 𝔅_k, plaquettes 𝔓_k. A *block* of Λ_k is a cube of side ℓ_{k+1} = Lℓ_k centered at a site of Λ_{k+1} (L odd), so Λ_{k+1} indexes the blocks of Λ_k. Fix once and for all an integer M ≥ M₁ (M₁ from Theorem 3.1 of CMP 99 and from Dimock's Lemma 6; both depend only on d = 4 and L). An *M-cube* at scale k is a cube of side Mℓ_k, union of M⁴ sites of Λ_k, centered at a point of the lattice (Mℓ_k Z/t*Z)⁴; an *M-polymer* X at scale k is a connected union of M-cubes (connected: the union is connected as a subset of the continuum torus). 𝒟_k denotes the set of M-polymers at scale k. For X ∈ 𝒟_k: |X|_M = number of M-cubes in X; d_M(X) = (length of the shortest tree in the continuum torus joining the M-cubes of X)/(Mℓ_k). Standard facts (Dimock 1108.1335 (122)–(123), proved there in Appendix A for any dimension; (P) by the same tree argument in d = 4):

  d_M(X) ≤ |X|_M ≤ 3⁴(1 + d_M(X)),   Σ_{X ∋ □} e^{−κ₀ d_M(X)} ≤ K₀   (2.1)

with constants κ₀ ≥ 1, K₀ depending only on d = 4. *Reblocking*: for X ∈ 𝒟_k, X̄ ∈ 𝒟⁰_{k+1} is the union of the LM-cubes (side LMℓ_k, i.e. M-cubes of scale k+1) meeting X; L⁻¹ maps 𝒟⁰_{k+1} onto 𝒟_{k+1}. All block and M-cube grids are chosen so that T* is a union of LM-cubes at every scale (t* a multiple of ℓ₀ and of M L^{K} a; this fixes the admissible values of t*/ℓ₀ as multiples of M and is recorded as a condition on T*).

Vol(X) = ℓ_k⁴ · #(sites of X). A *cell* (for I-5) is a cube of side ℓ_c ≥ 2Mℓ₀ in T*.

### 2.2 The observable, the source, the physical normalization

Plaquette variable U_p = U(∂p) ∈ SU(N) for p ∈ 𝔓_k, with U_k: 𝔅_k → SU(N). Define the lattice Tr F² density at scale k and the smeared observable

  𝒪_k(x) := ℓ_k^{−4} Σ_{μ<ν} (1/N) Re Tr(1 − U_{p_{μν}(x)}),   O_k(J_k) := Σ_{x∈Λ_k} ℓ_k⁴ J_k(x) 𝒪_k(x).   (2.2)

With U_p = exp(ℓ_k² F_p), F_p ∈ 𝔰𝔲(N) (small-field branch), (1/N) Re Tr(1 − U_p) = (1/2N)ℓ_k⁴ |F_p|² + O(ℓ_k⁸|F_p|⁴), |F|² = −Tr F² = Tr F*F; so 𝒪_k(x) = (1/2N) Σ_{μ<ν} |F_{μν}(x)|² + O(ℓ_k⁴|F|⁴): it is the physically normalized Tr F² density (no factor g^{-2}), engineering dimension four, canonical field degree two (2.5). The Wilson action is β_a S = (2N/g₀²) Σ_p (1 − (1/N) Re Tr U_p), and Σ_p over all plaquettes equals Σ_x Σ_{μ<ν} over the plaquettes p_{μν}(x) based at x; we record the exact identity

  β_a S = 2N² g₀^{-2} · Σ_{x∈Λ_a} a⁴ 𝒪₀(x).   (2.2')

Hence the sourced Wilson weight is exp(−β_a S + O^bare(J)) = exp(−Σ_x a⁴ (2N² g₀^{-2} − J(x)) 𝒪₀(x)): **the Tr F² source is a position-dependent shift of the bare inverse coupling** (exact, (P)). This identity is the origin of the marginal (non-contracting) row and of the mixing with the identity operator (Theorem 3.1(iii)).

Source class. 𝒥(r₀) := {J ∈ C⁵(T*, C): ‖J‖_{C⁵} ≤ r₀}; J_k := block average of J over the ℓ_k-cube of x ∈ Λ_k (J₀ = J|_{Λ_a}). Then ‖J_k‖_∞ ≤ ‖J‖_∞, and |J_k(x) − J_k(y)| ≤ ‖∇J‖_∞ |x − y| — the source is smooth on the physical scale ℓ₀, so ℓ_k‖∇J_k‖_∞ ≤ (ℓ_k/ℓ₀)(ℓ₀‖J‖_{C¹}) = L^{−(K−k)} ℓ₀ ‖J‖_{C¹}: *source derivatives are suppressed by the age* L^{−(K−k)} of the current scale relative to ℓ₀. The polydisc radius r₀ is fixed in Theorem 3.3.

### 2.3 Small-field domains, canonical coordinates, tree charts

**Curvature radius.** For X ⊂ Λ_k a union of M-cubes and ε > 0, the real small-field domain is

  𝒮_k(X, ε) := {U_k on 𝔅_k(X): |U_p − 1| ≤ ε for all p ∈ 𝔓_k(X)}  (Hilbert–Schmidt norm),

i.e. the dimensionless plaquette curvature f_p := ℓ_k² F_p satisfies |f_p| ≤ ε(1 + O(ε)). The running small-field radii are ε_k := g_k p_k, p_k := A₀ (log g_k^{-2})^{p₀} (Balaban's p₀(g) = A₀(log g^{-2})^{p₀}, LFR I (0.1) and the surrounding text; A₀, p₀ fixed), so that in *canonical* units (f = g_k f^{can}) the radius is α_k := p_k → ∞ slowly as g_k → 0.

**Tree chart.** For every M-cube □ at scale k fix the spanning tree T_□ of the bonds of □ rooted at the center (axial gauge: first along direction 1 from the root, then 2, 3, 4). For U_k on □ let u_T(U) be the unique gauge transformation on □ with u_T = 1 at the root and U^{u_T}(b) = 1 for b ∈ T_□; define the chart potential A_T(U) ∈ 𝔰𝔲(N)^{𝔅(□)} by U^{u_T}(b) = exp(ℓ_k A_T(U)(b)) (principal logarithm; well defined on 𝒮_k(□, ε) for ε ≤ ε* since every non-tree bond's holonomy is a product of at most 4M plaquette variables... precisely, |U^{u_T}(b) − 1| ≤ 4M·ε < 1 for ε ≤ 1/(8M)). Properties (P): (a) A_T(U^v) = Ad_{v(root)} A_T(U) for every gauge transformation v (gauge covariance up to the root); (b) U is gauge equivalent on □ to exp(ℓ_k A_T(U)); (c) on 𝒮_k(□, ε): ℓ_k|A_T(U)(b)| ≤ 4M ε (each non-tree bond's holonomy is a loop of at most 4M plaquettes) and the chart is analytic in U. For a polymer X, A_T is defined cube by cube (the charts of adjacent cubes are related by the transition holonomies, which are part of the data).

**Complex domain.** 𝒮^c_k(X, ε) := {U_k = U'·Ũ: Ũ ∈ 𝒮_k(X, ε), U'(b) = exp(ℓ_k A'(b)), A' ∈ 𝔰𝔩(N,C)^{𝔅(X)}, ℓ_k |A'(b)| ≤ ε, ℓ_k²|(∇A')(p)| ≤ ε} (the form of Balaban's complex configuration spaces, CMP 99 (3.37) and LFR I (1.64)–(1.65)); it contains 𝒮_k(X, ε) and is contained in {|U_p − 1| ≤ Cε}. Gauge transformations act by SU(N)-valued v only.

**Canonical scaling.** For U ∈ 𝒮_k(□, ε) and t ∈ C define U^{(t)} := exp(t ℓ_k A_T(U)) (bondwise, in the tree gauge). Then (P) for |t| ≤ τ: U^{(t)} ∈ 𝒮^c_k(□, 4Mτε + (4Mτε)²) (the curvature of tA is t dA + t²[A,A]/2 + …). So the family t ↦ U^{(t)} stays in the complex domain of radius C_M τ ε as long as C_M τ ε ≤ ε*.

### 2.4 Local functionals and the weighted norm

Fix κ > 0 (chosen in SF(k) and Theorem 3.1; κ ≥ 10(κ₀+1)). An *activity* at scale k on the domain radius ε is a map K: 𝒟_k × (fields) → C, K(X, U) depending on U only through U|_{𝔅_k(X)}, gauge invariant, analytic and bounded on 𝒮^c_k(X, ε). Norms:

  ‖K(X)‖_{k,ε} := sup_{U ∈ 𝒮^c_k(X,ε)} |K(X,U)|,   ‖K‖_{k,ε,κ} := sup_{X∈𝒟_k} ‖K(X)‖_{k,ε} e^{κ d_M(X)}.   (2.4)

𝒦_k(ε, κ) is the Banach space of such activities with finite norm; by (2.1), Σ_{X∋□} ‖K(X)‖_{k,ε} ≤ K₀ ‖K‖_{k,ε,κ} for κ ≥ κ₀. An activity depends in addition on the source J ∈ 𝒥(r₀) (and possibly on the scale-k fluctuation variable W, 2.6); dependence on J is always required to be analytic on the polydisc and the norm is then the sup over J as well.

### 2.5 The graded state space (explicit norms)

Let K(X, ·) ∈ 𝒦_k(ε_k, κ) and let □_X be a distinguished M-cube of X (the one containing the lexicographically first site; "anchor"). Using the tree chart of □_X extended along a fixed spanning tree of the M-cubes of X (so A_T(U) is defined on all of 𝔅_k(X)), the *jets* of K at the flat field are

  K^{(n)}(X; A) := (1/n!) (d/dt)^n K(X, exp(tℓ_k A))|_{t=0},   n = 0, 1, 2, …,   (2.5)

homogeneous polynomials of degree n in A ∈ 𝔰𝔲(N)^{𝔅(X)} (complexified). Facts (P): K^{(0)} = K(X, 1) (constant); K^{(1)} = 0 (gauge invariance under constant gauge transformations Ad_v and simplicity of 𝔰𝔲(N): an Ad-invariant linear form on 𝔰𝔲(N)^{𝔅} vanishes); K^{(2)}(X; A) is a quadratic form invariant under A ↦ A + ∇λ + O(A λ) hence (P) a quadratic form in the linearized curvature dA plus an exact harmonic-mode term, K^{(2)}(X; A) = Σ_{p,p' ∈ 𝔓(X)} ⟨dA(p), 𝐊₂(X; p, p') dA(p')⟩ + h_X(A), with 𝐊₂ the *quadratic covariant kernel* (ℓ_k⁴-normalized so that dA(p) is the dimensionless curvature; conventions: dA(p) := ℓ_k² (curl A)(p)) and h_X supported on the torus harmonic forms (zero unless X wraps T*, which cannot happen for d_M(X) < t*/(Mℓ_k)); for the activities produced by the step these kernels are evaluated on the physical graph (anchor and path conventions of □_X fixed as above).

**Anchor moments.** For the quadratic kernel define, with x_p the center of plaquette p and x₀ the anchor,

  m₀(X) := Σ_{p,p'} 𝐊₂(X;p,p') ⊗ (δ_{μν,μ'ν'} structure),   m₁^μ(X) := Σ_{p,p'} 𝐊₂(X;p,p') (x_{p'} − x₀)^μ/ℓ_k,   m₂^{μν}(X) := Σ_{p,p'} 𝐊₂(X;p,p')(x_{p'}−x₀)^μ(x_{p'}−x₀)^ν/ℓ_k².

Only the scalar lattice-symmetric part of m₀ (the coefficient of Σ_{μ<ν}|f_{μν}|²) is marginal; the remaining components of m₀ (anisotropic tensors) are allowed by the hypercubic symmetry but are *also* of dimension four and are retained in the marginal row (Theorem 3.1(iii) records them; they are the lattice artefacts of Tr F² that T7 must show vanish as a → 0; they are not needed for I-1).

**Grading by canonical degree.** For a birth R (an activity carrying one factor of J) define the *canonical degree* d(R) := min{n: R^{(n)} ≠ 0}. The *graded norm* at scale k with radius α (canonical units, so the physical curvature radius is ε = g_k α):

  ‖R‖_{graded,k} := ‖R‖_{k, g_k α_k, κ} + Σ_{n=0}^{3} g_k^{−n} α_k^{n} ‖R^{(n)}‖_{k} + g_k^{-2} α_k^{2} (|m₀| + |m₁| + |m₂|)(R) + ‖R_{≥4}‖_{k, g_kα_k/2, κ},   (2.6)

where ‖R^{(n)}‖_k := sup_X e^{κd_M(X)} sup_{|A|_∞ ≤ 1} |R^{(n)}(X; A)| (ℓ_k|A(b)| ≤ 1 normalization) and R_{≥4} := R − Σ_{n≤3} R^{(n)}(X; A_T(·)) is the *quartic analytic tail*. Each term in (2.6) is finite for R ∈ 𝒦_k(g_kα_k, κ) by Cauchy estimates (Lemma 4.2.1), and (2.6) is equivalent to the plain norm up to constants depending on α_k; the point of (2.6) is that the *transport* bounds of Theorem 3.1 are stated term by term with different contraction factors, which the plain norm cannot see.

**Projections.** P₄ R := R − R^{(0)} − R^{(2)}_{m₀} where R^{(2)}_{m₀}(X;A) := ⟨m₀(X), Σ_{p ∈ □_X} f_p ⊗ f_p⟩ is the local quadratic jet with the kernel collapsed to the anchor cube (the "removed projection"); P₆ R := R − R^{(0)} − R^{(2)} − R^{(3)} (all jets through canonical degree three; for the dimension-six insertions of [W, pp. 691–692]). *Lower-dimensional families*: {R^{(0)}, R^{(2)}_{m₀}}; *proper differences*: R^{(2)} − R^{(2)}_{m₀} (controlled by m₁, m₂ and the kernel's exponential decay); *contacts*: the J²-terms generated when two births meet (3.1(iv)). This is the explicit form of the state named in [W, p. 692].

### 2.6 Standing hypothesis SF(k) (the small-field step; a strengthened interface on I-0c)

Fix k < K. SF(k) consists of the following items, with constants C_*, κ, M, L, ε*, δ, c depending only on N, L, M and not on a, k, T*.

**SF1 (small-field density; = I-0c restricted to the clean sector).** On 𝒮_k(Λ_k, ε_k): ρ̃_k(U_k) = χ_k(U_k) exp(−g_k^{-2} S_k(U_k) − V_k(U_k)), where χ_k is the indicator of 𝒮_k(Λ_k, ε_k), S_k = Σ_p (1 − (1/N)Re Tr U_p) + (the exactly known quadratic/gauge-fixing corrections of Balaban's effective action, local), and V_k = Σ_{X∈𝒟_k} V_k(X, ·) with V_k ∈ 𝒦_k(ε_k, κ), ‖V_k‖_{k,ε_k,κ} ≤ C_V g_k, and V_k(X, 1) = 0, V_k^{(2)} with vanishing marginal moment (the vacuum energy and the Tr F² coefficient have been extracted into e_k and g_k: this is the "normalized for small polymers" condition, Dimock (135)).

**SF2 (background map).** There is a gauge-covariant map Ψ_k: 𝒮_{k+1}(Λ_{k+1}, ε_{k+1}) → 𝒮_k(Λ_k, ε_k) (Balaban's U_k = U(B_k, M'(V)) built from the constrained minimizer, LFR I (1.74), (1.77)–(1.79), Proposition 1) which extends analytically to 𝒮^c_{k+1}(Λ_{k+1}, ε_{k+1}) and satisfies: (a) locality: Ψ_k(U_{k+1})(b) depends on U_{k+1} on bonds within distance Rℓ_{k+1} of b up to an error exponentially small in the distance (LFR I (1.80): influence decays like e^{−δ dist/ℓ_{k+1}}); precisely, for every M-cube □ at scale k+1 there is a localized expansion Ψ_k = Σ_{Y ∋ □} Ψ_{k,Y} with ‖Ψ_{k,Y} − (contribution of Y)‖ ≤ C e^{−δ d_M(Y)}; (b) **scaling**: for U_{k+1} ∈ 𝒮^c_{k+1}(Λ_{k+1}, ε), |Ψ_k(U_{k+1})_p − 1| ≤ C_Ψ L^{-2} ε for p ∈ 𝔓_k (LFR I (1.80): "|U₀(∂p) − 1| < 2ε_kη²", η = ℓ_k, i.e. the background's fine-plaquette curvature is the coarse curvature in fine units); (c) consequently the pulled-back family t ↦ Ψ_k(U^{(t)}_{k+1}) is analytic for |t| ≤ τ_L := L²/(2C_ΨC_M) with values in 𝒮^c_k(Λ_k, ε_k) whenever U_{k+1} ∈ 𝒮_{k+1}(Λ_{k+1}, ε_{k+1}) and ε_{k+1} ≤ 2ε_k.

**SF3 (fluctuation parametrization and the Gaussian).** On 𝒮_k, U_k = Ψ_k(U_{k+1}) · exp(ℓ_k g_k 𝒞_k^{1/2} W) in the gauge fixed by Balaban's tree T₀ (LFR I (1.81)–(1.82)), where W: 𝔅'_k → 𝔰𝔲(N) runs over the independent fluctuation bonds, 𝒞_k = 𝒞_k(U_{k+1}) is the unit-lattice fluctuation covariance C^{(k)}(Λ) of CMP 99 §E, (3.155)–(3.158), and the step has the form

  ρ̃_{k+1}(U_{k+1}) = 𝒩_k(U_{k+1}) ∫ dμ*_k(W) ρ̃_k(Ψ_k(U_{k+1}) e^{ℓ_k g_k 𝒞_k^{1/2} W}) · exp(+quadratic form cancelled by 𝒞_k) ,   dμ*_k(W) = N_{χ,k}^{-1} χ'_k(W) dμ_I(W),

with dμ_I the unit Gaussian on W, χ'_k(W) = Π_b 1{|W(b)| ≤ p_{0,k}}, p_{0,k} := A₀'(log g_k^{-2})^{p₁}, p₁ < p₀ (the cutoff (1.82), δ'_k = g_k p_{0,k}), N_{χ,k} = ∫ χ'_k dμ_I ∈ [1 − |𝔅'_k| e^{−p_{0,k}²/2}, 1], and 𝒩_k the determinant/Jacobian factor of Balaban's step, a product of local factors independent of the source. The fluctuation field 𝒞_k^{1/2}W, and ℓ_k g_k 𝒞_k^{1/2}W as a potential, satisfy |ℓ_k g_k (𝒞_k^{1/2}W)(b)| ≤ C g_k p_{0,k} =: g_k p_{0,k} C ≤ ε_k/4 (since p₁ < p₀).

**SF4 (covariance decay and localized expansion).** 𝒞_k(U_{k+1}; y, y') satisfies |𝒞_k(y,y')| ≤ B₀ e^{−δ₀|y−y'|/ℓ_k} (CMP 99 Theorem 3.15, (3.187)) and has a convergent random-walk expansion 𝒞_k = Σ_ω 𝒞_{k,ω} (CMP 99 Theorem 3.10, (3.107)–(3.108), transported to C^{(k)} by Theorem 3.15), each term depending on U_{k+1} only in the localization domain X_ω of the walk and bounded by (C/M)^{|ω|} e^{−δ₀ d(ω,y,y')}; the same holds for 𝒞_k^{1/2} via the resolvent representation (Dimock (193)–(195), (223)). Hence the *weakened* kernels 𝒞_k^{1/2}(s) := Σ_ω s^ω 𝒞_{k,ω}^{1/2}, s = (s_□)_{□ LM-cube}, are analytic in s on |s_□| ≤ M^{1/2} with bounds of the same form (Dimock §2.5, (103)–(104), and Lemma 19's argument), and at s_{□} = 0 for □ ∉ Z the kernel preserves functions supported in connected components of Z.

**SF5 (regularity of the background for the propagator theorems).** Ψ_k(U_{k+1}) satisfies the regularity conditions (3.35), (3.36) of CMP 99 with Mα₀ sufficiently small whenever U_{k+1} ∈ 𝒮^c_{k+1}(Λ_{k+1}, ε_{k+1}) (this is LFR I (1.84)–(1.87): |A₀|, |∇A₀|, |∂η*∂ηA₀| < O(1)B₃B₅M⁶ε_k in the AL gauge).

**SF6 (unmarked step output and the coupling flow).** With no source, the output of the step is of the form SF1 at scale k+1 with e_{k+1}, g_{k+1} and V_{k+1} given by the extraction (3.6)–(3.8) below, ‖V_{k+1}‖_{k+1,ε_{k+1},κ} ≤ C_V g_{k+1}, and g_{k+1}^{-2} = g_k^{-2} − b₀ log L + r_k, |r_k| ≤ C g_k² (I-0c).

Labels: SF1, SF6 are I-0c verbatim (restricted to the clean sector) — (C) on T0. SF2(a),(b) and SF5 are (L) LFR I Proposition 1, (1.80), (1.84)–(1.87), whose displayed formulas are not independently checked here: recorded as (L*) = literature, hypotheses checked on the prose statement only. SF2(c) is (P) from SF2(b) and 2.3. SF4 is (L) CMP 99 Theorems 3.10, 3.12, 3.14, 3.15 (hypotheses: (3.35)–(3.36) with Mα₀ small, supplied by SF5) together with the square-root localization, which is (L) Dimock 1108.1335 Appendix E for the scalar resolvent and (C) for the gauge covariance 𝒞_k (the resolvent (𝒞_k + r)^{-1} must be given the same random-walk treatment; this is the one genuinely new propagator statement SF4 asks of T0, and section 6.3 says so). SF3 is Balaban's parametrization (LFR I (1.81)–(1.82), (1.99)) in Dimock's ultralocal form: (L*) for the gauge fixing and cutoff, (C) for the use of 𝒞_k^{1/2}W with ultralocal μ*_k in place of Balaban's own expansion.

## 3. Main theorems

Throughout, k < K, SF(k) holds, g_k ≤ ḡ with ḡ small enough that all displayed smallness conditions hold (they are finitely many and listed in 4.6), and r₀ ≤ r₀(N, L, M). Constants C depend only on N, L, M, κ unless indicated.

### 3.1 Theorem 3.1 (one-step transport of a single Tr F²-type insertion; clean sector). (P | SF)

Let the scale-k sourced small-field density be

  ρ̃_k[J](U_k) = ρ̃_k(U_k) · exp( O_k(J_k; U_k) + W_k[J](U_k) ),   (3.1)

where O_k(J_k; U) = Σ_{x∈Λ_k} ℓ_k⁴ J_k(x) 𝒪_k(x; U) + Σ_{x} ℓ_k⁴ J_k(x) c_k(x) with 𝒪_k the local density (2.2) multiplied by a running factor z_k (z₀ = 1) plus the lattice-symmetric dimension-four completions (anisotropic Tr F² components, coefficients bounded by C g_k²), c_k(x) a constant (identity mixing), and W_k[J] = Σ_{X∈𝒟_k} W_k(X; J, ·) a source polymer expansion with

  W_k(X; 0, ·) = 0,   W_k(X; J, ·) analytic in J ∈ 𝒥(r₀),   ‖∂_J W_k‖_{k,ε_k,κ} =: w_k^{(1)},   ‖∂_J² W_k‖_{k,ε_k,κ} =: w_k^{(2)},   (3.2)

(derivatives in the direction of J, i.e. in the complex parameter z for J ↦ zJ), and at k = 0: O₀ = O^bare(J), W₀ = 0. Then the step SF3 produces ρ̃_{k+1}[J] of the same form (3.1) at scale k+1 with:

(i) **Linear image.** O_{k+1}(J_{k+1}; U_{k+1}) = Σ_{x∈Λ_{k+1}} ℓ_{k+1}⁴ J_{k+1}(x) [z_{k+1} 𝒪_{k+1}(x; U_{k+1}) + (anisotropic completions)] + Σ_x ℓ_{k+1}⁴ J_{k+1}(x) c_{k+1}(x), where

  z_{k+1} = z_k (1 + γ_k),   |γ_k| ≤ C g_k²,   c_{k+1}(x) = L^{-4}·Σ_{y∈block(x)} c_k(y) + ℓ_{k+1}^{-4} e^{(1)}_k,   |e^{(1)}_k| ≤ C,   (3.3)

i.e. the Tr F² coefficient is marginal (multiplicative renormalization by 1 + O(g_k²) per step: the anomalous-dimension row) and the identity coefficient receives a bounded ℓ_{k+1}^{-4}-normalized increment per step (the vacuum-energy mixing row, divergent like a^{-4} when summed, exactly as the vacuum energy e_k).

(ii) **Source polymer expansion.** W_{k+1}[J] ∈ 𝒦_{k+1}(ε_{k+1}, κ) with W_{k+1}(X; 0) = 0 and

  w_{k+1}^{(1)} ≤ θ w_k^{(1)} + C_1 g_k ‖J‖_∞ (z_k + ℓ_k‖J‖_{C¹}/‖J‖_∞) ,   θ := L^{-1}(1 + C g_k) < 1,   (3.4)

(θ = L^{-1} is the worst row, the first anchor moment m₁; the rows of canonical degree ≥ 3 and the m₂ row contract with L^{-2}(1 + Cg_k), see 4.7),
  w_{k+1}^{(2)} ≤ θ² w_k^{(2)} + C_2 (w_k^{(1)})² + C_2 g_k ‖J‖_∞² ,   (3.5)

where the term C_1 g_k‖J‖_∞ z_k is the *birth* of first-order source activities at step k (the connected part of the insertion with one fluctuation vertex of V_k or of the fresh cubic action vertices, each carrying a factor g_k), and the contraction θ = L^{-2}(1+O(g_k)) is the one-step factor for source activities of canonical degree ≥ 3 and for the proper differences of degree-2 activities (anchor moments m₁, m₂), after the marginal part has been moved into O_{k+1} by (i).

(iii) **Extraction (what moves from W to O).** The map W_k ↦ W_{k+1} is the composition: (pullback by Ψ_k and fluctuation integration, Lemma 4.4.1) → (localization and ultralocal cluster expansion with the source as a spectator, Lemma 4.4.2) → (reblocking, Lemma 4.2.2) → (extraction of R^{(0)} and R^{(2)}_{m₀} of every small marked polymer into c_{k+1}, z_{k+1}, Lemma 4.2.3) → (scaling, Lemma 4.2.4). The extracted quantities are the anchor-cube values R^{(0)}(X) (into e^{(1)}_k) and the marginal moment m₀(R^{(2)}(X)) (into γ_k); "small" means d_M(X) < L.

(iv) **Second-order (contact) row.** ∂_J² W_{k+1}|_{J=0} contains, besides θ²-contracted transported terms, the *contact births*: for two births R, R' of degree 2 whose carriers meet, the connected Gaussian pairing E*_k[R^{(2)} R'^{(2)}]_{conn} is a J²-activity of canonical degree 0 (identity) and 2 (Tr F²); its degree-0 part is extracted into a J²-local counterterm ℓ_{k+1}^{-4} e^{(2)}_k(x, x') supported on |x − x'| ≤ C M ℓ_{k+1} with |e^{(2)}_k| ≤ C (z_k² + (w_k^{(1)})²); this is the contact term of the Tr F² two-point function, and it is the only source of the a^{-4}, a^{-2}, log a divergences of the J² part of the pressure (Theorem 3.3).

(v) **The MT36-form bound for births of degree d ≥ 3 (and for P₄ of degree-2 births).** Let R_j be a *completed* birth at step j (a first-order source activity generated at step j, R_j ∈ 𝒦_j(ε_j, κ), with its degree-d jets as in 2.5), and Φ_{j,k} := Ψ_j ∘ … ∘ Ψ_{k-1} the composed background map. Then its transported image R_j ∘ Φ_{j,k} (a function of U_k on the reblocked carrier) satisfies, for the attachment to one interaction vertex of V_k (the connected second-order coefficient L^{(2)}_{V_k}(·, V_k) of Lemma 4.4.2),

  ‖P₄ L^{(2)}_{V_k}(R_j ∘ Φ_{j,k}, V_k)‖_{k,ε_k,κ'} ≤ C g_k · L^{−2(k−j)} (g_k/g_j)^{d} · ‖R_j‖_{graded,j}   for d(R_j) ≥ 3,   (3.6)

with κ' = κ − κ₀ − 2 (one fixed locality loss, paid once), and for d(R_j) = 2 the same bound with (g_k/g_j)² for the proper-difference part P₄R_j^{(2)} and with L^{−4(k−j)}(g_k/g_j)⁴ for the quartic tail; the marginal part (1 − P₄)R_j^{(2)} contributes to γ_k, c_{k+1} by (i). Here s = 2 and q = d exactly; the age factor L^{−2(k−j)} is the product over the intermediate steps of the one-step factor L^{-2} of SF2(b), and the coupling ratio is the canonical-unit conversion (section 4.5).

### 3.2 Theorem 3.2 (iteration; summability in k). (P | SF)

Under SF(j) for all j < K and the trajectory of I-0c (g_j ≤ ḡ), the recursion (3.3)–(3.5) with the initial data z₀ = 1, c₀ = 0, w₀^{(i)} = 0 gives, for all k ≤ K, uniformly in a:

  |log z_k| ≤ C Σ_{j<k} g_j² ≤ C Σ_{j<k} (x_k + b(k−j)/2)^{-1} ≤ (2C/b) log(1 + b k/(2x_k)),   x_j := g_j^{-2}, b := b₀ log L,   (3.7)

using x_j ≥ x_k + b(k−j)/2 from I-0c; so **z_k and z_k^{-1} are bounded by a power of log(ℓ₀/a)**, not uniformly in a: this is the logarithmic wave-function renormalization of Tr F² (the Z_{Tr F²}(a) of I-3), as asymptotic freedom predicts; z^{max} denotes this bound;

  w_k^{(1)} ≤ C g_k ‖J‖_∞ z_k^{max} · (1 − θ)^{-1}·(1 + C_drift)   (the birth sum Σ_{j<k} θ^{k−j} g_j z_j converges because θ^{k−j}(g_j/g_k) ≤ L^{−2(k−j)} e^{(k−j) b₊/(2h)} is summable, (MT34)–(MT35) of [W, p. 692], re-proved as Lemma 4.5.2 with explicit constants),   (3.8)

  w_k^{(2)} ≤ C (‖J‖_∞ z_k^{max})² ,   (3.9)

and Σ_{j≤k} L^{−2(k−j)} (g_k/g_j)^{q} ≤ (1 + C_drift/h)^{q/2} (1 − L^{-1})^{-1} for every fixed q ≥ 0 once ḡ is small enough that q b₊/(2h) ≤ log L/2 (h := min_k x_k = ḡ^{-2}). Consequently the state (O_k, W_k) stays in the space defined by (3.2) with norms bounded uniformly in a for all k ≤ K, and the complete small-field sourced density at scale ℓ₀ on T* is

  ρ̃_K[J] = ρ̃_K exp( Σ_x ℓ₀⁴ J_K(x)[z_K 𝒪_K(x) + c_K(x)] + W_K[J] ),   ‖∂_J^m W_K‖_{K,ε_K,κ} ≤ C_m ‖J‖_∞^m (m = 1, 2),   (3.10)

with W_K analytic in J on 𝒥(r₀).

### 3.3 Theorem 3.3 (fixed-polydisc analyticity of the sourced pressure on T*; clean sector). (P | SF)

Define the strictly local counterterm functional

  L_a(J) := Σ_{k<K} [ Σ_{x∈Λ_{k+1}} ℓ_{k+1}⁴ J_{k+1}(x) ℓ_{k+1}^{-4} e^{(1)}_k + Σ_{x,x'} ℓ_{k+1}⁸ J_{k+1}(x)J_{k+1}(x') ℓ_{k+1}^{-4} e^{(2)}_k(x,x') ] + (the J³, J⁴ analogues extracted in Lemma 4.2.3 with range ≤ CMℓ_{k+1})   (3.11)

(finite range ≤ C M ℓ₀, polynomial of degree ≤ 4 in the block-averaged sources with coefficients that are a-dependent but bounded by C ℓ_{k+1}^{-4} per scale — their sum over k diverges like a^{-4}, a^{-2}, log a as it must). Then on the clean small-field sector of T* (the term of I-0c with no large-field region),

  p^{sf}_{a,T*}[J] − p^{sf}_{a,T*}[0] − Vol(T*)^{-1} L_a(J) = Vol(T*)^{-1} [ Σ_x ℓ₀⁴ J_K(x) ⟨z_K 𝒪_K(x)⟩_K + log ⟨exp(O_K(J_K) + W_K[J])⟩_K − (terms already in L_a) ]   (3.12)

is holomorphic in J on the polydisc 𝒥(r₀) (as a function of the finitely many complex parameters z_i in J = Σ z_i f_i, f_i ∈ C⁵ fixed, Σ r_i‖f_i‖_{C⁵} ≤ r₀, |z_i| < r_i) and bounded there by C₁ uniformly in a, where ⟨·⟩_K is the normalized scale-ℓ₀ small-field expectation on T* (a finite integral over Λ_{ℓ₀,T*} with (t*/ℓ₀)⁴ sites). In particular the connected functions κ_n(O(f₁),…,O(f_n)) with pairwise separated supports (distance > CMℓ₀) are given by Cauchy's formula on the polydisc, uniformly in a (Prop. 2.1 and Cor. 2.2 of [W, p. 10], re-proved as Lemma 4.3.1 and Lemma 4.3.2), and the first and second J-derivatives at J = 0 are the explicit convergent series (4.3.3).

With I-2 assumed as stated and the large-field sum of I-0c, the same conclusion for the full p_{a,T*}[J] requires the residual propositions R-1…R-6 of section 7 (the large-field transitions); Theorem 3.3 as proved is the clean-sector statement, which is exactly the input T5(a) uses when the sum over large-field regions is controlled by I-2 together with R-1…R-6.

### 3.4 Corollary 3.4 (dimension-six, H-type insertion). (P | SF)

For the ordinary source r_f = βD[f] − ℓ[f]/3 (canonical degree 2, engineering dimension six, times β = c_β g^{-2}) and for the C♯-type cubic (degree 3), the same transport applies with P₄ replaced by P₆ and *no* marginal row: all jets through degree three of the reblocked activity carry L^{4−6} = L^{-2}·(moment factors), so the entire birth contracts with s = 2 after the lower-dimensional (dimension-four: identity and Tr F²) projections — which are *relevant* for a dimension-six insertion and must be extracted as the mixing of H into {1, Tr F²} with coefficients growing like L^{2(k−j)} and L^{0}: this is the lower-dimensional mixing of I-3 — have been removed. The bound (3.6) with q = d ∈ {2, 3} holds for P₆ of the transported H- and C♯-births; the removed projections are the contact and lower-dimensional rows that T3 must renormalize. The coefficient table (MT44) of [W, p. 695] is reproduced with its three rows (quadratic, cubic, quartic) by Lemma 4.5.1 applied to d = 2, 3.

**Remark 3.5 (exact coupling-shift check; P).** Put `x = g⁻²` and `c_N = 2N²`. For a constant source t multiplying O₀(1), the fine Wilson weight is exactly the weight at `x₀ − t/c_N`. If the entire unsourced effective density is differentiable in x with all domains/normalizers treated consistently, its inserted first coefficient is `−c_N⁻¹ ∂_{x₀} log ρ_K`. Thus the action row has coefficient `∂x_K/∂x₀`, and the identity/polymer rows retain derivatives of their own scalars with this sign and factor. A bound `|r_k(x_k)| ≤ C/x_k` at real trajectory points does not bound `r'_k(x_k)`; Proposition 7.12 states sufficient complex hypotheses. Position-dependent sources additionally require spatially localized response estimates, not just this constant-source identity.

## 4. Proofs

### 4.1 Combinatorial lemmas (no gauge theory; (P), or (L) with proof reference)

**Lemma 4.1.1 (ultralocal cluster expansion with analytic parameters).** (L) Dimock 1108.1335 Theorem 27, d = 4, with the following parametric addendum (P). Let dμ = Π_x dμ(Φ(x)) be an ultralocal probability measure on fields Φ on a 4-dimensional unit toroidal lattice and let H(X, Φ; λ), X ∈ 𝒟 (M-polymers), be localized functionals (depending on Φ only in X) that are, for each X, analytic in a parameter λ in a polydisc 𝒫 and satisfy |H(X,Φ;λ)| ≤ H₀ e^{−κ d_M(X)} on supp μ × 𝒫 with κ > 3κ₀ + 3 and H₀ ≤ c₀ (c₀ depending only on d = 4 and κ). Then Ξ(λ) = ∫ exp(Σ_X H(X,Φ;λ)) dμ(Φ) = exp(Σ_Y H^#(Y;λ)), where H^#(Y;λ) depends only on H(X;λ) for X ⊂ Y, is analytic in λ ∈ 𝒫, and |H^#(Y;λ)| ≤ O(1) H₀ e^{−(κ−3κ₀−3) d_M(Y)}. Moreover, if H = H₀(X,Φ) + λ H₁(X,Φ) + λ² H₂(X,Φ) with |H_i| ≤ h_i e^{−κd_M(X)} and h₀ + r h₁ + r² h₂ ≤ c₀ for |λ| ≤ r, then

  |∂_λ H^#(Y;0)| ≤ O(1) h₁ e^{−(κ−3κ₀−3)d_M(Y)},   |∂²_λ H^#(Y;0)| ≤ O(1)(h₂ + h₁²/c₀) e^{−(κ−3κ₀−3)d_M(Y)}.   (4.1)

*Proof.* Theorem 27's construction (Mayer expansion (300)–(302), integration (308)–(309), exponentiation (311)–(312) with the Kotecký–Preiss-type bound in (313)–(330)) is a convergent series each term of which is a finite product of the H(X_i;λ); uniform convergence on 𝒫 (the bound (299) holds at every λ) gives analyticity in λ by Weierstrass, and H^#(Y;λ) depends only on X ⊂ Y by (301). For (4.1), apply Cauchy's estimate in λ on |λ| = r' := min(r, c₀/(2h₁ + 2r h₂)) where the hypothesis H₀(λ) := h₀ + r'h₁ + r'²h₂ ≤ c₀ holds; one obtains |∂_λH^#(0)| ≤ O(1)H₀(r')/r' e^{−…} ≤ O(1)(h₀/r' + h₁ + r'h₂)e^{−…}. To remove the h₀/r' term, note that H^#(Y;λ) − H^#(Y;0) is the connected output of the *difference* Σ_X [H(X;λ) − H(X;0)], which has activity ≤ (|λ|h₁ + |λ|²h₂)e^{−κd}: apply Theorem 27 to the measure dμ' := exp(ΣH(X;0))dμ/Ξ(0) — this is not ultralocal, but the Mayer expansion of step 1 (which is where (303)–(307) are used) applies to the product Π_X e^{H(X;λ)} = Π_X e^{H(X;0)} Π_X e^{H(X;λ)−H(X;0)}, and the standard "two-species" polymer argument (Brydges, Park City lectures, Thm 5.4; or Kotecký–Preiss, CMP 103 (1986) Thm 1 applied to the joint gas with weights a(X) = (κ−κ₀)d_M(X)) shows that the λ-dependent part of log Ξ is a sum over clusters containing at least one λ-dependent polymer, bounded by the λ-dependent activity norm times O(1); differentiating at λ = 0 kills all terms with two or more λ-factors for the first derivative and leaves at most two for the second. The factor h₁²/c₀ in the second derivative is the cluster with two first-order marks (the "contact" cluster). ∎

**Lemma 4.1.2 (reblocking in d = 4).** (P; Dimock Lemma 10 with 3 → 4.) For E ∈ 𝒦_k(ε, κ) define (BE)(Y, U) := Σ_{X∈𝒟_k: X̄ = Y} E(X, U), Y ∈ 𝒟⁰_{k+1}. Then with κ' := L(κ − κ₀ − 1),

  ‖(BE)(Y)‖_{k,ε} ≤ 3⁴ K₀ L⁴ ‖E‖_{k,ε,κ} e^{−κ' d_{LM}(Y)},   (4.2)

and the number of X with X̄ = Y containing a given M-cube is controlled by (2.1): Σ_{X: X̄=Y} e^{−κ₀d_M(X)} ≤ K₀ L⁴ |Y|_{LM}. *Proof.* d_M(X) ≥ L d_{LM}(Y) when X̄ = Y (a minimal tree on the M-cubes of X joins the LM-cubes of Y); then Σ_{X̄=Y}‖E(X)‖ ≤ ‖E‖ e^{−(κ−κ₀)Ld_{LM}(Y)} Σ_{X̄=Y} e^{−κ₀d_M(X)}, and each such X contains one of the L⁴|Y|_{LM} M-cubes of Y, so the last sum is ≤ K₀L⁴|Y|_{LM} ≤ K₀L⁴·3⁴(1 + d_{LM}(Y)) ≤ 3⁴K₀L⁴ e^{d_{LM}(Y)}. ∎

**Lemma 4.1.3 (age sum).** (P; = (MT34)–(MT35) of [W, p. 692] with explicit constants.) Let x_j = g_j^{-2} satisfy x_j ≤ x_k + b₊(k − j) + C_drift for j ≤ k (true with b₊ = b₀ log L + C ḡ², C_drift = 0 under I-0c) and x_k ≥ h := ḡ^{-2}. Then for every q ≥ 0 and every s > 0 with q b₊/(2h) ≤ (s/2) log L,

  (g_k/g_j)^q = (x_j/x_k)^{q/2} ≤ (1 + C_drift/h)^{q/2} e^{q b₊(k−j)/(2h)} ≤ (1 + C_drift/h)^{q/2} L^{s(k−j)/2},   Σ_{j≤k} L^{−s(k−j)}(g_k/g_j)^q ≤ (1 + C_drift/h)^{q/2}/(1 − L^{−s/2}).   (4.3)

*Proof.* x_j/x_k ≤ 1 + (b₊(k−j) + C_drift)/h ≤ (1 + C_drift/h) e^{b₊(k−j)/h}; raise to q/2 and sum the geometric series. ∎ (Any absolute factor g_j^{-q} at fixed age is *not* summable this way: with k − j = 1 it diverges as j → 0; this is why only *relative* ratios appear in (3.6).)

### 4.2 Complex-analytic lemmas on the graded state (P)

**Lemma 4.2.1 (jets by Cauchy).** Let R(X,·) be analytic and bounded on 𝒮^c_k(X, ε). Then with the chart of 2.3, for A with ℓ_k|A(b)| ≤ 1 and τ := ε/(8M C_M) (so that U^{(t)} = exp(tℓ_kA) ∈ 𝒮^c_k(X, ε/2) for |t| ≤ τ by 2.3),

  |R^{(n)}(X;A)| ≤ τ^{−n} ‖R(X)‖_{k,ε},   |R_{≥n₀}(X; U)| ≤ (|t_U|/τ)^{n₀} (1 − |t_U|/τ)^{-1} ‖R(X)‖_{k,ε}   (4.4)

for U = U^{(t_U)} with |t_U| < τ, where R_{≥n₀} := R − Σ_{n<n₀} R^{(n)}(X; A_T(·)). *Proof.* Cauchy's estimate for the holomorphic function t ↦ R(X, exp(tℓ_kA)) on |t| ≤ τ and the Schwarz-lemma form of the Taylor remainder. ∎ In canonical units (ε = g_kα_k, A = A^{can} g_k... i.e. the actual field has t_U = g_k|A^{can}|_∞ℓ_k) this is the statement that a degree-n jet of an activity analytic on the canonical radius α_k has canonical size ≤ (C_M/α_k)^n‖R‖·|A^{can}|^n — the "canonical Cauchy" estimate MT38/MT41 of [W, pp. 693–694].

**Lemma 4.2.2 (pullback and the L^{4−2n} count).** Assume SF2. Let R ∈ 𝒦_k(ε_k, κ) and define R'(Y, U_{k+1}) := Σ_{X: X̄=Y} R(X, Ψ_k(U_{k+1})) for Y ∈ 𝒟⁰_{k+1}, then scale: R'_{L^{-1}}(Z, U_{k+1}) := R'(LZ, U_{k+1}) for Z ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}. Then: (a) R'_{L^{-1}} ∈ 𝒦_{k+1}(ε_{k+1}, κ) with ‖R'_{L^{-1}}‖_{k+1,ε_{k+1},κ} ≤ 3⁴K₀L⁴ ‖R‖_{k,ε_k,κ} provided κ' = L(κ−κ₀−1) ≥ κ (true for κ ≥ 2(κ₀+1), L ≥ 3); (b) for each X, the function t ↦ R(X, Ψ_k(U^{(t)}_{k+1})) is analytic on |t| ≤ τ_L = L²/(2C_ΨC_M) with sup ≤ ‖R(X)‖_{k,ε_k}, so its coarse jets satisfy |R'^{(n)}_X(A)| ≤ τ_L^{−n}‖R(X)‖ and its coarse remainder of order n₀ at the actual field (t = 1) satisfies |R'_{X,≥n₀}| ≤ 2 τ_L^{−n₀}‖R(X)‖; (c) consequently, for the *reblocked* activity on Y,

  ‖(R'_{≥n₀})(Y)‖_{k+1,ε_{k+1}} ≤ 2·3⁴K₀ (2C_ΨC_M)^{n₀} L^{4−2n₀} ‖R‖_{k,ε_k,κ} e^{−κ'd_{LM}(Y)}.   (4.5)

*Proof.* (a) is Lemma 4.1.2 plus the inclusion Ψ_k(𝒮^c_{k+1}(ε_{k+1})) ⊂ 𝒮^c_k(ε_k) of SF2. (b) is SF2(c) and Lemma 4.2.1 with τ replaced by τ_L. (c): sum (b) over X̄ = Y using Lemma 4.1.2. ∎

The exponent 4 − 2n₀ is the engineering dimension count: a jet of canonical degree n has dimension 2n; the L⁴ is the number of fine M-cubes per coarse M-cube (the volume factor of the smeared density). For n₀ = 3 the factor is L^{-2}: **s = 2.** For n₀ = 4 it is L^{-4}. For n = 0 the factor L⁴ is the vacuum-energy growth (relevant), for n = 2 it is L⁰ (marginal). This is the whole content of the contraction; the rest is bookkeeping of what is extracted.

**Lemma 4.2.3 (extraction of the dimension-≤4 jets of a small polymer).** Let R' be a reblocked activity on Y ∈ 𝒟⁰_{k+1} with d_{LM}(Y) < L (small) and let R'^{(0)}, R'^{(2)} be its coarse jets (2.5). Define

  e(Y) := R'^{(0)}(Y) = R'(Y, 1),   m₀(Y) := (hypercubic average of) Σ_{p,p'∈𝔓(Y)} 𝐊'₂(Y;p,p'),   R'_{m₀}(Y;U) := m₀(Y)·2N·ℓ_{k+1}⁴ 𝒪_{k+1}(x_Y; U)  (the quadratic jet with its kernel collapsed to the anchor site x_Y of □_Y),

  𝒫R'(Y) := R' − e(Y) − R'_{m₀}(Y),   so that 𝒫R'(Y, 1) = 0 and the marginal moment of (𝒫R')^{(2)} vanishes.   (4.6)

Then (P): |e(Y)| ≤ ‖R'(Y)‖, |m₀(Y)| ≤ C_M τ_L^{−2} Σ_{X̄=Y}‖R(X)‖ (Lemma 4.2.1 applied to the quadratic jet, with the moment sum over p' paid by the finite size of Y), and ‖𝒫R'(Y)‖_{k+1,ε_{k+1}} ≤ 3‖R'(Y)‖; moreover 𝒫R' decomposes as (𝒫R')^{(2)} + R'_{≥3} with (𝒫R')^{(2)} = ⟨m₁, ·⟩ + ⟨m₂, ·⟩ + (degree-2 remainder with vanishing moments through order 2) and R'_{≥3} bounded by (4.5) with n₀ = 3. The *total* extracted quantities over Y ∋ x are the local densities entering (3.3): e^{(1)}_k(x) := Σ_{Y∋x, small} e(Y)/|Y|_{LM} (J-linear part) and γ_k(x) := Σ_{Y ∋ x, small} m₀(Y)/|Y|_{LM}, both bounded by O(1)·(sup over small Y of the J-linear activity norm) by (2.1). *Proof.* Cauchy estimates (4.4) for the jets; the hypercubic average of m₀ is the only invariant part (Σ_{μ<ν}|f_{μν}|² is the unique hypercubic-invariant gauge-invariant quadratic in f that is reflection-even); the bound on 𝒫R' is the triangle inequality. ∎

**Lemma 4.2.4 (proper differences and the age factor).** Let R_j be a birth at scale j with carrier X_j (d_M(X_j) < L, so diam X_j ≤ 3⁴M(L+1)ℓ_j), transported to scale k by the composed background map Φ_{j,k}. In the chart of scale k its carrier has diameter D_{j,k} ≤ 3⁴M(L+1) L^{j−k} ℓ_k =: M' r ℓ_k, r = L^{j−k}. For the quadratic jet with kernel 𝐊₂^{(k)} the first and second anchor moments satisfy |m₁| ≤ M' r |m₀-size|, |m₂| ≤ (M'r)² |m₀-size| where m₀-size := Σ_{p,p'}|𝐊₂^{(k)}(p,p')|; hence the proper difference (𝒫R)^{(2)}, evaluated on a coarse field with ℓ_k|∇f| ≤ ε_k, satisfies

  ‖(𝒫R_j∘Φ_{j,k})^{(2)}‖ ≤ C (M' r)·ε_k · τ^{-2} ‖R_j‖ + C (M' r)² ε_k τ^{-2}‖R_j‖,   (4.7)

i.e. the m₁ row carries r = L^{−(k−j)} (s = 1) and the m₂ row r² (s = 2). When the birth is smeared against J, the m₁ row is a total derivative: Σ_x J_k(x)⟨m₁, f·∇f⟩(x) = −½Σ_x ∇J_k(x)·⟨m₁, f⊗f⟩(x) + (lattice boundary terms of the same size), so it is additionally bounded by ℓ_k‖∇J_k‖_∞ ≤ L^{−(K−k)}ℓ₀‖J‖_{C¹}. *Proof.* Taylor expansion of the coarse curvature across the carrier in the chart (as in Dimock (146)–(148), with the derivative bound of the domain replacing his |∂φ| bound) and the moment definitions of 2.5. ∎

### 4.3 Source algebra (P; no gauge theory)

**Lemma 4.3.1 (separated sources remove local counterterms; = Prop. 2.1 of [W, p. 10], re-proved).** Let Z[J] be any finite-cutoff generating functional with Z[0] = 1, f₁,…,f_n smooth with pairwise supports at distance > ρ, J_A = Σ_{i∈A} z_i f_i, C_n(z) = Σ_{A⊆[n]} (−1)^{n−|A|} log Z[J_A] (branches chosen continuously near z = 0). If L[J] is any functional of the form Σ_{cells c} ℓ_c(J|_{c+margin}) with range ≤ ρ (i.e. L[J] depends on J only through its restrictions to sets of diameter ≤ ρ, additively) and L[0] = 0, then replacing log Z by log Z − L leaves C_n unchanged for n ≥ 2, and ∂_{z₁}…∂_{z_n} C_n(0) = κ_n(O(f₁),…,O(f_n)). *Proof.* Each local piece of L[J_A] sees at most one f_i, so L[J_A] = Σ_{i∈A} L[z_if_i]; the coefficient of L[z_if_i] in the alternating sum is Σ_{B⊆[n]∖{i}} (−1)^{n−1−|B|} = (1−1)^{n−1} = 0 for n ≥ 2. The derivative statement is the definition of cumulants. ∎ The counterterm L_a(J) of (3.11) is of this form with ρ = CMℓ₀ (it is a sum over scales of block-local polynomials of range ≤ CMℓ_{k+1} ≤ CMℓ₀), so it drops out of all connected functions of sources separated by more than CMℓ₀.

**Lemma 4.3.2 (Cauchy on the polydisc; = Cor. 2.2 of [W, p. 10], re-proved).** If C_{n,a}(z) is holomorphic on Π_i{|z_i| < r_i} uniformly in a with sup |C_{n,a}| ≤ M_n, then |κ_{n,a}(f₁,…,f_n)| ≤ M_n Π_i r_i^{-1}; if also sup|C_{n,a'} − C_{n,a}| ≤ ε_{a,a'} → 0, the cumulants converge. *Proof.* Multidimensional Cauchy formula on concentric polydiscs. ∎

**(4.3.3) The first two derivatives at J = 0.** With (3.10) and ⟨·⟩_K the normalized small-field scale-ℓ₀ expectation on T*,

  ∂_z log Z^{sf}[zJ]|_{z=0} = Σ_x ℓ₀⁴ J_K(x)[z_K⟨𝒪_K(x)⟩_K + c_K(x)] + Σ_Y ⟨∂_zW_K(Y;0)⟩_K,   (4.8)
  ∂_z² log Z^{sf}[zJ]|_{z=0} = Var_K(O_K(J_K) + Σ_Y ∂_zW_K(Y;0)) + Σ_Y⟨∂_z²W_K(Y;0)⟩_K,   (4.9)

where the variance is over the finite scale-ℓ₀ measure on T* and every term is bounded by C‖J‖_∞ resp. C‖J‖_∞² Vol(T*)/ℓ₀⁴ times the scale-K norms (3.10), uniformly in a. (The terms with c_K and the J²-part of L_a carry the a^{-4}-divergent identity and contact rows; they are exactly the strictly local functionals that Lemma 4.3.1 removes from separated connected functions.) The scale-ℓ₀ expectation involves (t*/ℓ₀)⁴ group integrals with a density bounded above and below on the small-field set by the final-step version of SF1; no further estimate is needed at fixed T*.

### 4.4 The fluctuation step with a spectator source (P | SF)

Fix k < K and write B := 𝒞_k^{1/2}W (a 𝔰𝔲(N)-valued field on the fluctuation bonds), U_k = Ψ_k(U_{k+1}) e^{ℓ_kg_kB} =: Ψ e^{ℓ_kg_kB}.

**Lemma 4.4.1 (the sourced integrand is a small local perturbation on the cutoff domain).** Under SF1–SF3, for U_{k+1} ∈ 𝒮^c_{k+1}(Λ_{k+1}, ε_{k+1}) and |W(b)| ≤ p_{0,k} for all b, with ‖J‖_∞ ≤ r₀ and |z_k| ≤ z^{max}:

(a) U_k = Ψe^{ℓ_kg_kB} ∈ 𝒮^c_k(Λ_k, ε_k) (SF2(b) gives |Ψ_p − 1| ≤ C_ΨL^{-2}ε_{k+1} ≤ ε_k/2 for L² ≥ 4C_Ψ; SF3 gives ℓ_kg_k|B| ≤ Cg_kp_{0,k} ≤ ε_k/4; the plaquette of a product is within the sum of the curvatures plus a quadratic error ≤ ε_k/4). Hence every scale-k activity, including 𝒪_k(x;·), O_k(J_k;·), and W_k(X;J,·), is evaluated inside its analyticity domain: *no large-field integration occurs in the clean sector* — this is the point of the cutoff χ'_k and of the shrinking of ε_{k+1} relative to ε_k (SF2(b)).

(b) The source factor is a product of local factors: exp(O_k(J_k;U_k)) = Π_{□} exp(Σ_{x∈□} ℓ_k⁴J_k(x)[z_k𝒪_k(x;U_k) + c_k(x)]) and on the domain of (a), |Σ_{x∈□}ℓ_k⁴ J_k(x) z_k 𝒪_k(x;U_k)| ≤ M⁴ r₀ z^{max} ε_k² (since ℓ_k⁴𝒪_k(x) = (1/N)Σ_{μ<ν}Re Tr(1 − U_p) ≤ Σ|U_p − 1| ≤ 6ε_k on 𝒮_k, and ≤ 6ε_k² after the first-order cancellation Re Tr(1−U_p) = ½|U_p−1|²_{HS} for unitary U_p; on the complex domain the same bound holds with a constant). The constant part Σ_x ℓ_k⁴J_k(x)c_k(x) is field-independent and factors out of the integral exactly. Thus, in the notation of Lemma 4.1.1, the J-linear source activity has size h₁ ≤ C M⁴ z^{max} ε_k² = C M⁴ z^{max} g_k² p_k² per M-cube — *small* for g_k ≤ ḡ.

(c) The transported polymer part W_k(X; J, U_k) is analytic in J and in U_k on its domain with ‖W_k‖ ≤ w_k^{(1)}r₀ + w_k^{(2)}r₀² (Taylor in J). The unsourced activities V_k(X;U_k), the fresh cubic-and-higher action vertices g_k^{-2}S_k(Ψe^{ℓgB}) − (quadratic form) =: Σ_X F_k(X;U_{k+1},B) (local, |F_k(X)| ≤ C g_k p_{0,k}³ e^{−κd} on the domain, as in (MT27) of [W, p. 689], which is Balaban II (1.37)–(1.40); here taken as part of SF1/SF3: the step's unmarked activities have total norm ≤ C_V g_k·(polylog)) are source-independent.

*Proof.* (a) and (b) are the displayed inequalities; (c) is the definition of the state and SF1/SF3. ∎

**Lemma 4.4.2 (localization in W and the marked cluster expansion).** Under SF3–SF4, write the integrand of the step as exp(Σ_X H(X; U_{k+1}, W, J)) with H = (unsourced local factors of SF1/SF3, including V_k∘(Ψe^{ℓgB}) and F_k) + (source factors of Lemma 4.4.1(b),(c)). Each H(X;·) is local in U_{k+1} on X (by SF2(a), up to exponentially small tails which are expanded into larger polymers as in Dimock (226)–(228)) and *nonlocal in W* through B = 𝒞_k^{1/2}W. Introduce the weakened kernel 𝒞_k^{1/2}(s) of SF4 and interpolate in each s_□, □ ∉ X, by the fundamental theorem of calculus (Dimock (225)–(226)); the resulting localized activities

  H^{loc}(Z; U_{k+1}, W, J) := Σ_{Y⊂Z} ∫ds_{Z∖Y} ∂_{s_{Z∖Y}} H(Y; U_{k+1}, 𝒞_k^{1/2}(s)W, J)|_{s_{Z^c}=0, s_Y=1}   (4.10)

depend on W only in Z (SF4: at s_{Z^c} = 0 the kernel preserves functions supported in components of Z), are analytic in J, and satisfy, by Cauchy in each s_□ on |s_□| ≤ M^{1/2} (SF4) exactly as in Dimock Lemma 19 ((230)–(233), with his λ_k^{1/4−10ε} replaced by our activity sizes),

  |H^{loc}(Z)| ≤ O(1)L⁴ (h₀ + ‖J‖_∞h₁ + ‖J‖_∞²h₂) e^{−L(κ−2κ₀−2)d_{LM}(Z)},   h₀ := C_Vg_k(polylog),   h₁ := CM⁴z^{max}g_k²p_k² + w_k^{(1)},   h₂ := w_k^{(2)},   (4.11)

the first-order-in-J part of H^{loc} being bounded by the h₁-term alone and the second-order part by the h₂-term plus the h₁ term's square (Taylor in J). Then Lemma 4.1.1 with the ultralocal measure dμ*_k (SF3) gives

  ∫dμ*_k(W) exp(Σ_Z H^{loc}(Z;U_{k+1},W,J)) = exp(Σ_{Y∈𝒟⁰_{k+1}} H^#(Y; U_{k+1}, J)),   |H^#(Y)| ≤ O(1)L⁴(h₀ + r₀h₁ + r₀²h₂) e^{−L(κ−5κ₀−5)d_{LM}(Y)},   (4.12)

with H^# analytic in J ∈ 𝒥(r₀) and in U_{k+1} ∈ 𝒮^c_{k+1} (parametric Weierstrass convergence as in Lemma 4.1.1; the U_{k+1}-dependence enters through Ψ_k and 𝒞_k(U_{k+1}), both analytic by SF2, SF4), and with the derivative bounds (4.1):

  |∂_JH^#(Y;0)| ≤ O(1)L⁴h₁ e^{−κ''d_{LM}(Y)},   |∂_J²H^#(Y;0)| ≤ O(1)L⁴(h₂ + h₁²/c₀)e^{−κ''d_{LM}(Y)},   κ'' := L(κ − 5κ₀ − 5) ≥ κ for κ ≥ 10(κ₀+1), L ≥ 2.   (4.13)

The smallness condition of Lemma 4.1.1 reads O(1)L⁴(h₀ + r₀h₁ + r₀²h₂) ≤ c₀: this is the first smallness condition on ḡ and r₀ (4.6).

**Definition (the attachment coefficient).** For a first-order source activity R (a "birth", here R = ∂_J of the J-linear part of some H(Y) or of W_k∘(Ψe^{ℓgB})) and the unmarked interaction V := Σ_X[V_k + F_k](X), define L^{(2)}_{V_k}(R, V)(Y) := the part of ∂_JH^#(Y;0) in which exactly one unmarked polymer activity (one V-vertex) enters together with the marked one — the "two-polymer cluster" term of the Mayer expansion (Dimock (302) with n = 2, one factor (e^{H}−1) replaced by its J-derivative). By (4.13) and the structure of Theorem 27's clusters, ‖L^{(2)}_{V_k}(R,V)‖_{κ''} ≤ O(1)L⁴ h₀·‖R‖ ≤ C g_k ‖R‖ — **the attachment of one interaction vertex costs one factor g_k**, which is the prefactor C g_k in (3.6). The terms with no V-vertex are the pure Gaussian (Wick) transport E*_k[R], and those with ≥ 2 vertices are O(g_k²)‖R‖.

**Lemma 4.4.3 (the Gaussian transport of the inserted density: Wick rows).** Under SF3–SF4, for the inserted density: E*_k[ℓ_k⁴𝒪_k(x; Ψe^{ℓ_kg_kB})] = ℓ_k⁴𝒪_k(x;Ψ) + g_k² ℓ_k⁴ 𝒲_k(x; U_{k+1}) + g_k⁴ (remainder), where 𝒲_k(x;U_{k+1}) := ½ E*_k[(d/dt)²𝒪_k(x;Ψe^{tℓ_kB})|_{t=0}] is a local analytic function of U_{k+1} (through Ψ and the covariance 𝒞_k(U_{k+1}) and the cutoff normalization N_{χ,k}), bounded by C B₀ M⁴ on the domain, and even in B so that the first-order term vanishes (μ*_k is even). Its coarse jets: 𝒲_k(x;1) = ½Tr(d 𝒞_k(1) d^T)(x) — a constant (the identity row, the one-loop ⟨Tr F²⟩), and 𝒲_k^{(2)} — a coarse quadratic form (contributing C g_k² to γ_k: the one-loop anomalous-dimension row). *Proof.* Expand 𝒪_k(x;Ψe^{tℓ_kB}) in t to second order; the t-linear term is odd in W; the second-order coefficient is a quadratic form in B = 𝒞_k^{1/2}W whose μ*_k-expectation is the restricted-Gaussian second moment, equal to the Gaussian one up to the factor N_{χ,k}^{-1}(1 − O(e^{−p_{0,k}²/4})) (the cutoff removes only a tail of relative size ≤ |𝔅'_k ∩ supp| e^{−p_{0,k}²/2}); the remainder is bounded by Lemma 4.2.1 in t on |t| ≤ 2 (the domain allows ℓ_kg_k|B|·2 ≤ ε_k/2). Analyticity in U_{k+1} is SF2 + SF4. ∎

The **marginal coefficient** produced in one step is therefore

  γ_k = [classical part: the coarse Tr F² coefficient of Σ_{x∈block}ℓ_k⁴𝒪_k(x;Ψ(U_{k+1})) minus 1] + g_k²·[m₀ of 𝒲_k] + [m₀ of the J-linear part of the V-attached clusters, O(g_k·g_k²p_k²)],

and by Remark 3.5 the classical part is exactly ∂x_{k+1}/∂x_k − 1 restricted to its classical (g-independent) piece, which is 0: the coarse effective action's plaquette term is *defined* as the minimal fine action given the coarse constraint, so Σ_{x∈block}ℓ_k⁴𝒪_k(x;Ψ(U_{k+1})) = ℓ_{k+1}⁴ 𝒪^{eff}_{k+1}(x_{block}; U_{k+1}) with 𝒪^{eff}_{k+1} the density of S_{eff,k+1} of SF1, which differs from 𝒪_{k+1} by the exactly known local corrections of SF1 (coefficients bounded by C, dimension ≥ 6 after the plaquette term is isolated). Hence |γ_k| ≤ C g_k², and the a-independence of the classical row is an identity, not an estimate. (In the language of [W, p. 686]: the primitive column T₀ = L^{-2}I₂ for the dimension-six pair, (MT20), is replaced here by the exact marginal column T₀ = 1 for Tr F², with the O(g²) correction (MT26) given by the Wick row and the V-attached row.)

### 4.5 Coupling grades (P)

**Lemma 4.5.1 (canonical conversion along the flow).** Let R_j be a birth at scale j of canonical degree d, bounded in the graded norm (2.6) at scale j: in particular its degree-d jet satisfies |R_j^{(d)}(A)| ≤ g_j^{d}α_j^{−d}‖R_j‖_{graded,j}|A^{can}|^d where A = g_jA^{can} (the canonical potential at scale j). Transported to scale k by Φ_{j,k} and evaluated on a scale-k field written in scale-k canonical units A_k = g_kA_k^{can}, the same jet reads |·| ≤ (g_k/g_j)^{d} (L^{−2(k−j)})^{d} … — precisely, by SF2(b) iterated, the scale-j dimensionless curvature of Φ_{j,k}(U_k) is ≤ (C_ΨL^{-2})^{k−j} times the scale-k one, and the scale-k canonical curvature is g_k f^{can}; so the degree-d jet of R_j∘Φ_{j,k} at the scale-k field has size ≤ ‖R_j‖_{graded,j}·(g_k/g_j)^d·(C_ΨL^{-2})^{d(k−j)}·α_j^{-d}|f^{can}|^d. Combined with the reblocking count L^{4(k−j)} (Lemma 4.1.2 iterated, with the exponential weight absorbing the (3⁴K₀)^{k−j}·C_Ψ^{d(k−j)} factors once κ is large enough that e^{−(κ'−κ)d} pays them — see 4.6), the net factor is (g_k/g_j)^d L^{(4−2d)(k−j)}: this is (3.6) for d ≥ 3 with s = 2d − 4 ≥ 2 (we state the weaker uniform s = 2), q = d. *Proof.* Unit conversion and Lemma 4.2.2 applied k − j times. ∎

The combination *age factor × relative coupling ratio* is what Lemma 4.1.3 sums; the absolute canonical size g_j^{-d} of the birth at its own scale never appears alone (this is the content of the warning after (MT35) in [W, p. 692], which the grading (2.6) is designed to respect: the graded norm is defined with the *own-scale* canonical radius α_j, so that ‖R_j‖_{graded,j} is O(1)·‖J‖ for the Tr F² insertion by Lemma 4.4.1(b), not O(g_j^{-2})).

### 4.6 Smallness conditions (explicit list)

All constants C, C_Ψ, C_M, B₀, δ₀, K₀, κ₀ depend only on N, L, M (and κ). The proofs require:

(S1) L² ≥ 4C_Ψ (Lemma 4.4.1(a)); (S2) κ ≥ 10(κ₀+1) and L(κ−5κ₀−5) ≥ κ (Lemma 4.4.2); (S3) e^{−(L(κ−κ₀−1)−κ)} · 3⁴K₀ C_Ψ³ ≤ L^{-1} (the locality margin κ' − κ = L(κ−κ₀−1) − κ > 0 pays the reblocking and composition constants of Lemma 4.5.1; the exponential weight is restored after scaling because d_{LM}(LZ) = d_M(Z), Dimock (133)–(134), so there is no net loss of κ per step and no accumulation over k); (S4) O(1)L⁴(C_Vḡ(polylog) + r₀CM⁴z^{max}ḡ²p² + r₀²w^{max}) ≤ c₀ (cluster-expansion smallness, Lemma 4.1.1); (S5) C_Mτ_Lε_k ≤ ε*, i.e. ε_k ≤ ε*·(2C_ΨC_M)/(L²C_M) (the scaled family stays in the chart domain: SF2(c)); (S6) p₁ < p₀ and Cḡp_{0} ≤ ε_k/4 (SF3); (S7) q b₊/(2h) ≤ log L/2 for q ≤ 4 (Lemma 4.1.3 with s = 2): h = ḡ^{-2} ≥ 4b₊/log L; (S8) r₀ < h/2 (so that the coupling shift x − J stays in the admitted interval for the exact check of Remark 3.5). Conditions (S1)–(S3) fix L and κ; (S4)–(S8) fix ḡ and r₀ given L, M, κ, N. None depends on a, k, or T*.

## 6. Current interface statement

### 6.1 Assumed and verified imports

I-0c and I-2 are imported only as stated in the stated hypotheses. They do not include a marked reserve, a cutoff-uniform complex coupling flow, or a zero-free source disc. The literature used for the original first small-field step is identified separately in §7.11; that application uses Balaban's native restrictions on L,M and the locality/smallness parameters. No susceptibility estimate, I-3, or mass gap enters the new proofs.

### 6.2 Results toward I-1

The target list of §1.1 is not claimed as proved. Its proposed full graded contraction, all-order pressure, and marginal/contact bounds are not established under the SF hypotheses. The current results are these:

- **P:** absolute anchor algebra, source-jet multiplication, undivided positive-kernel transport, conditional covariance tower, joint fixed-moment reserve payment and merger bookkeeping (§§7.1–7.4). These statements specify their norms and retain the global normalization when it has not canceled.
- **P/L on the displayed native mixed transitions.** Sections 7.67–7.73 keep the proper signed denominator, including arbitrary fixed still-live neighbors. A bounded readout at a returning body or an admitted crossing Mayer edge retains one rare factor; the placement sum is controlled through a prescribed home. The polynomial degree of the pre-Mayer marked expression gives an extensive conditional pressure estimate for sources summed over every healed body. The physical application treats completely stored microscopic H stencils through bounded depth. The coefficientwise promoted exterior source is given by (7.193). Equations (7.197)–(7.202) transfer its bounded-incident-volume part through the next mixed T and identify the waiting budget; §7.80 treats arbitrarily many separated real live components. Sections 7.85–7.96 use the true joint outer normalization: (7.210) pays every subsequently healed ancestral shape and (7.211)–(7.213) retain the terminal factor for the others. Equations (7.214)–(7.219) give the continuous-age simultaneous-release row and the genuine stopped covariance for specified R/B source families. The same-torus terminal scalar is bounded at fixed g_*; other source births, unrestricted physical volume and cross-torus scalar comparison remain separate. Sections 7.97–7.102 give intermediate layer bounds, arbitrary inspection-time volume moments, the fresh two-home covariance of direct ordinary rows on the specified mixed charts, and its exact identity under the external selector change. Sections 7.103–7.111 keep both sourced homes and the proper R completions at every new marginal/contact filing. The regular scalar Ward defect is summable; the remaining trace criterion (7.242) and the unrestricted joined replacement are open. Sections 7.112–7.116 prove the prototype comparison. Equations (7.248)–(7.252) use the true periodic constrained determinant and close the completed compact one-loop subsystem uniformly. The independent charged diagonal (7.253) and the unrestricted nonlinear signed R replacements remain open.
- **P:** an exponential-moment zero-free criterion and a rare-spike obstruction to deriving a fixed source disc from fixed-order moments (§7.5). **C:** bounded marginal source iteration under the explicitly stronger complex-flow hypothesis CF (§7.7).
- **P:** actual compact Wilson integrals on contractible cubes, including polylogarithmically growing cubes and the quantitative retained-boundary neighborhood, have a fixed complex source/coupling disc after their exact analytic critical scalar is extracted (§§7.8–7.10). The hypotheses and constants are explicit; periodic sectors and native constrained effective actions are outside these theorems.
- **P/L on the displayed clean families.** The original first-step source integral has absolute anchored kernels and a proportional coupling remainder (§§7.11–7.15). Theorem 7.32 varies only the physical Wilson coefficient and gives its exact mean and variance, including the physical Gaussian dimension. Theorems 7.44 and 7.57 cover regular nonflat frustration backgrounds with a sourced saddle and the original sharp cutoff. Equations (7.123)–(7.124) give the conditional mean and covariance through one loop with rooted O(g² log²(1/g)) errors on that chart. Sections 7.16–7.17 account for the distinct flux in a family with a varying physical chart.
- **P/L at two fixed clean steps.** Theorems 7.34–7.35 carry the normalized plaquette source and independent physical coupling source through the inherited interaction. Theorem 7.37 gives the frustration disc at flat terminal field using both fluctuation species. Proposition 7.46 identifies the smooth weighted identity row and its spatial-gradient error. The finite-scale constants and native margins are stated in the proofs.
- **P/L on actual retained compact records.** Propositions 7.38–7.40 use the LFR II (1.79)–(1.89) wait and merger bank for entire source series on literal stencils assigned to charged native sites, including energy-dominated βH tags where their Wilson coefficients match. Corollary 7.39 gives the marked logarithm of the bracket in (1.72). Theorem 7.47 pays fixed marked live ages; Corollary 7.48 pays post-release Cauchy factors on admitted paths. Equations (7.125), (7.127) give fractional curvature regularity through repeated original averages. The oriented path expansion (7.130) retains the area term that cancels against the cubic center.

The native inherited vertex obeys Corollary 7.66. The physical restrictions and rough walk localization of §§7.44–7.45 restore the age to a connected-carrier norm. ### 6.3 Remaining interface changes

**ICR-1, native small-field transport.** Equations (7.149), (7.152)–(7.154) now give a homogeneous complex connected attachment, its low curvature kernels and the next physical quartic readout under their explicit native margins. Equations (7.155)–(7.166) now supply the homogeneous principal comparisons, actual block normalizations, and a stable-only age convolution with a common domain. The remaining coupling must propagate every filed marginal, lower, contact and winding row when it re-enters later, and must match the nonhomogeneous exterior records on their actual domains. CMP119 (2.28) uses shrinking parameters; every mixed-chart displacement requires its actual margin.

**ICR-2, saved history packet:** admission must apply to the complete frozen marked readouts, including their old coupling grade and all mean/contact rows. Supply a single joint reserve of the form used in Theorem 7.6, with its actual initial bank, age/size expense and external retained data. A small rare numerator and a different small-field denominator require relative domination or a complete undivided identity; positivity alone is insufficient. Native path counting is supplied in T2, but its transfer to every joined current record remains part of admission.

**ICR-3, susceptibility-specific endpoint:** it is enough for the bounded frustration sources needed by T3 to obtain an exact all-history representation `Z(η)/Z(0)=exp L(η) Eν exp Fη`, with L holomorphic and a uniform relative bound `Eν|exp Fη−1|<1` on a fixed source disc. Here ν is the normalized, positive source-free stopped measure including all histories. This narrower endpoint avoids assuming the full all-operator I-1, but neither the flat first step nor the fixed-order moment bounds prove it. Strictly diagonal contact extraction and the ordinary bare susceptibility are kept distinct, as in T3.

### 6.4 Proposed replacement for the source interface (O except where explicitly restricted)

The original universal I-1 is false. The following three separate statements specify the remaining targets. Their conjunction has not been proved.

1. **I-1A, finite-radius directions.** Specify the cutoff-normalized analytic source family before applying the transport. The concrete dimension-four test direction here is `Y₄(J)=N⁻¹ Σ_p J_p s_p`, with the same scalar profile on all plaquette orientations for the scalar action; cell-supported C⁵ profiles and their chessboard replicas are included. The susceptibility-specific direction is the *unamplified* matching sum `Y_c(η)=Σ_b η_b h_b`, `h_b=β₀ d_b`. Allow the bounded comb or plane-wave arrays actually needed for SUS, as separate finite source parameters, rather than only smooth physical tests. Require a fixed zero-free disc for the chosen full Wilson family, or a direct second-moment theorem for the unamplified source. For T5's exponential route one additionally needs a uniform **physical-volume** upper bound on the renormalized replicated log, not mere nonvanishing. The SUS test instead uses a bound of order the **lattice site count** for the unamplified log and its second row. A fixed disc has been proved here only on the explicit subfamilies and homogeneous charts in §§7.8–7.25 and 7.61; the all-history replicated statement is O. A bounded compact readout or an engineering label alone is not a zero-freeness certificate.
2. **I-1J, physical H and general finite-order observables.** For physical `O_H(f)=(2N)⁻¹a⁻²Σ_b f_bh_b` use distinct nilpotent labels `ε_i²=0`. For the first and second derivatives at fixed cutoff keep respectively `(2N)⁻¹a⁻² E h_f` and `(2N)⁻²a⁻⁴ Cov(h_f,h_{f′})`, with independent tests including their reflected replicas. Transport the actual vacuum, Tr F² and allowed tensor/lower mixing coefficients, pointed derivatives, ordinary Ward/EOM partners, and all diagonal operator-valued and scalar contacts. If a nonlinear local source map Ψ_a and scalar L_a are used, define the renormalized generating **jet** as the coefficient in `exp[−L_a] Z_a(Ψ_a)/Z_a(0)`; include the Ψ_a″ insertion as well as L_a″ and the two Ψ_a′ insertions. Their test scaling and subtraction are part of I-3. The quadratic H contact has degree-eight diagonal Taylor order and requires a ninth displacement moment for the summable remainder (T3 §4). Separate the bare susceptibility `Var(r_f)≤CΣ|f_b|²` from this contact-renormalized physical second derivative. For an m-source Schwinger theorem require the corresponding degree-m nilpotent algebra, compatible orders, and an explicit bound in m, dimension D and test norm. Fixed orders one and two do not give that bound. Proposition 7.86 rules out a fixed bare physical-H disc even for a constant test; Proposition 7.103 excludes a uniform unrenormalized second action row. An extra a⁴ rescaling or a different nonlinear renormalized source is a new observable and needs its own identification.
3. **I-1M, history scope.** Seek the all-history graded estimate for the exact *combined* physical contribution, with original phase assignments, all pinned data, and genuine undivided normalization. Require separately normed subfamilies only after proving their boundary/contour domination; (7.136) and T2 Proposition 4.44 show why a generic sharp branch cannot be granted the complete age. Record the original N_{I}-norm and identify which signed brackets are formed before applying absolute values. The first and second source jets require the same-mass kernel, the variation of its reference normalization and the between-history mean. A hypothesis that bounds each return by a new clean age on its current coarse chart is not a permissible substitute. The challenged raw branch and the complete signed sum are logically different.

**Consequences for T5 and T6.** I-5(a)'s existing complex replicated pressure route now has to be proved separately for the I-1A class, including the uniform bound, the cell-additive diagonal normalizers and the actual full T* torus. For the physical H and higher irrelevant types replace that route by a replicated finite-coefficient/moment estimate such as §7.66. In a complex replica test, reflection and conjugation on alternate cells describe an antilinear diagonal slice; holomorphic Cauchy uses independent parameters before that slice. I-5(b) still requires fixed-volume convergence (or a stated subsequence), separated-cube growth uniform in m and D, and the OS-II coincidence-flat extension. Neither a zero-free disc nor two fixed derivatives alone proves these. I-6(a)'s complete source-free S94 and common scalar comparison remain separate obligations. For I-6(b)–(c) the original exponential split-and-Cauchy argument in T6 §4.5(iv) cannot be used for the disproved physical disc; §7.66 gives a conditional polynomial replacement that needs the new replicated reference bounds and strict cell/half-space locality. Limit positivity, temperedness and compactness then need their original hypotheses. The modified T5/T6 interfaces are not established here.

## 7. Transition status and new proofs

Stronger reserve and denominator bounds than those proved below are not used. The actual LFR II remainder estimate contains `exp[−p₀(g_k)]exp[−κd_k(X)]`; an `exp[−c/g_k²]` reserve may be used only where a separate estimate proves it. The results below use `p₀(g)≍(log g⁻²)^p`, p>1, when that is the stated available bank.

**R-1, mixed entry.** A complete original compact plaquette mark has the literal bound `2Σ_p|J_p|` in normalized-trace convention. Its lattice-volume factor is not canceled by an extra power of ℓ. Lemma 7.19 treats a different, flat small-field analytic source class. Admission of an inherited analytic activity to a compact current readout, preserving its old grade, remains O; compactness of the original group does not supply that extension.

**R-2, live transport.** Theorems 7.3 and 7.5 prove exact undivided transport and all first/second source rows through positive replacements, with constant one in the integrated norm and with every conditional history mean retained. A stored mark unchanged during a live wait is not copied at each step. Theorem 7.47 now pays every fixed live-age cost on a continuously occupied recorded interval. The full external-moment and pre-entry-grade estimates remain C on the admitted saved packet and its stated initial size. Sections 7.69–7.73 do integrate the live neighbors of a returning body in the original signed operation, for the stated bounded marks and connecting norms.

**R-3, renormalization.** For the same native operator T′, §7.6 and T2's relative-phase estimate control `T′F/T′1` relative to its own positive reference mass. The schematic positive replacement preserves mass exactly, so its localized denominator cancels in the complete undivided integral. Neither argument asserts that a rare numerator divided by a different small-field denominator is small. That application remains O until its relative domination or exact undivided identity is supplied. A denominator being positive and nonempty does not imply a volume-uniform lower bound.

**R-4, merger.** The source algebra gives the exact second row `A₂B₀+2A₁B₁+A₀B₂`, including the cross term. Theorem 7.6 pays the product of all inherited packet powers from one joint exponential reserve after summing their age exponents; Lemma 7.7 telescopes the bank. Proposition 7.38 also replays the original native merger for bounded tags assigned to charged compact stencils. For general inherited packets the corresponding statement remains C until their simultaneous certificate and complete child data are verified. Two rare masses are not multiplied when there is only one joint event.

**R-5, healing and promotion.** Healed coordinates become inherited coefficients and are never reopened as compact integration variables. Theorems 7.17–7.18 prove analytic integration on specified actual compact blocks, not admission for every healed effective activity. Promotion of the saved dimension-six packet on the original simultaneous complex domain, with exact source/mean/contact rows and old coupling grade, remains O. The marginal-CF lemma is conditional and does not silently convert this issue into a real coupling-flow estimate.

**Clean-selector scope.** In particular the homogeneous pressure/variance results in §§7.61–7.65 use the stated CMP109-type conditional selector and common graph margins. Their identification with the specific globally clean branch cut out by CMP119 (1.18) is conditional; see §7.74. The R-operation statements §§7.67–7.73 instead use LFR II (1.71)–(1.104) directly.

**R-6, exit.** A finite stopped lattice controls the number of variables but not, by itself, the source dependence accumulated before stopping. The near-one criterion in §7.5 proves the endpoint once the exact normalized all-history residual satisfies its relative bound. Terminal retained means appear explicitly in Theorem 7.5; they are not dropped because the lattice is finite.

**R-7, full pressure.** The pressure is the logarithm of the complete sector sum. It is not a sum of sector logarithms. All-history zero-freeness is therefore a separate endpoint, as in §6.3. No full-pressure analyticity follows just from controlling each rare sector separately. The succeeding proofs establish concrete pieces of these transitions and distinguish every remaining native application.

### 7.1 Absolute anchor norms and a finite source-jet algebra (P)

This section is independent of the old norm (2.6). It gives exact norms for the *carrying algebra*, not a proof that the actual gauge-theory kernels belong to it with the required constants.

Fix a finite metric lattice `(Λ,d)`, a finite-dimensional coefficient algebra with submultiplicative norm (tensor products may instead be given the projective norm), a locality exponent κ≥0 and an integer p≥0. An anchored kernel of order n is an array `K_n(x;y₁,…,y_n)`; tensor/color indices are included in its coefficient norm. Let τ(x;y) be the minimum spanning-tree length of the displayed points, and `R(x;y)=max_i d(x,y_i)`, with τ=R=0 for n=0. Define

`‖K_n‖_{κ,p} = sup_x Σ_{y₁,…,y_n} exp(κτ(x;y)) (1+R(x;y))^p ‖K_n(x;y)‖`.   (7.1)

Every sum is a sum of absolute coefficients *before* spatial moment cancellation. Norms for physical-current jets, source jets, quadratic/cubic covariant completions, proper differences and removed rows are finite direct sums of (7.1), with their actual dimensionful/coupling/radius prefactors recorded separately. A norm for an analytic tail is added as a separate sup norm on its **specified** common domain; it is not obtained by extrapolating (7.1). This construction allows the retained rows of [W, MT36–MT48, pp. 692–696] without identifying their projections with ordinary Taylor truncation.

**Lemma 7.1 (anchor product and averaging).** For the anchored concatenation

`(K_n ⊙ H_m)(x;y₁,…,y_n,z₁,…,z_m)=K_n(x;y) H_m(x;z)`

one has `‖K_n ⊙ H_m‖_{κ,p} ≤ ‖K_n‖_{κ,p}‖H_m‖_{κ,p}`. The same inequality holds for the averaged symmetrization of this product. If `K_n(ω)` is measurable and a finite positive measure μ integrates its norm, then

`‖∫ K_n(ω)dμ(ω)‖_{κ,p} ≤ ∫ ‖K_n(ω)‖_{κ,p} dμ(ω)`.   (7.2)

*Proof.* Two trees sharing x join to a connected graph, so `τ(x;y,z)≤τ(x;y)+τ(x;z)`. Also `1+max(R_y,R_z)≤(1+R_y)(1+R_z)`. Apply these inequalities termwise and factor the two sums. Averaged symmetrization is an average of permutations preserving the weight; the triangle inequality gives its contraction. For (7.2), apply the triangle inequality coefficientwise, interchange nonnegative sums and integration, and use `sup_x ∫ ≤ ∫ sup_x`. ∎

One must not multiply two kernels at different anchors as though they shared one. Moving an anchor x′ to x costs the genuine factor coming from the path x–x′, for example `exp(κd(x,x′))(1+d(x,x′))^p`, as well as the corresponding geometric response. A local tensor contraction sums its contracted indices with its actual operator norm. None of these costs is silently one.

For two source derivatives use **derivative coefficients**, not coefficients divided by factorials:

`A(t)=A₀+tA₁+(t²/2)A₂ (mod t³)`,

`‖A‖_{r,2}=‖A₀‖+r‖A₁‖+(r²/2)‖A₂‖`.   (7.3)

The underlying norm can be (7.1) with the product just defined, or a sup norm on one common analytic domain. For finitely many sources use multi-indices α with `|α|≤2` and norm `Σ r^α ‖A_α‖/α!`.

**Lemma 7.2 (exact merger algebra).** The truncated product has

`(AB)₀=A₀B₀`, ` (AB)₁=A₁B₀+A₀B₁`,

`(AB)₂=A₂B₀+2A₁B₁+A₀B₂`,   (7.4)

and `‖AB‖_{r,2}≤‖A‖_{r,2}‖B‖_{r,2}`. Positive integration commutes with all these derivative coefficients and is contractive in the integrated norm (7.2). For general multi-indices the middle term is the exact Leibniz sum `Σ_{β≤α} binom(α,β) A_β B_{α−β}`.
