Take `K=Δ²` with `(ΔF)_n=F_{n+1}−2F_n+F_{n−1}` in the ν direction. Its coefficients 1,−4,6,−4,1 have precisely the stated moment cancellations. Write D={0,…,m−1}. Per unit transverse cross-sectional volume the sharp form is
`t Σ_{n∈D} t⁻² F_n (Δ²F)_n = F_0−2(F_{m−2}−2F_{m−1})=5/4+3t.`   (7.136)

Indeed ΔF_n equals t times the jump of λ from n to n+1. At n=−1 that jump is 1, with only its right neighbor in D after the second Δ. At n=m−1 it is −2 with only its left neighbor and center in D. At all other jumps the second difference has no support in D (take m≥3). On the full torus the same form is `t⁻¹Σ_n (ΔF_n)²=6t` by self-adjointness and the jump squares 1,4,1. In particular the complement has the opposite limiting flux. ∎

This example excludes a universal positive age gain for two separately normed *sharp* subfamilies on the basis of their old moment conditions and physical regularity alone. If both branches at an artificial seam use precisely the same actual field, coefficient, test phase, and grade, their two complementary indicators add to one before taking norms. For a smooth test supported across that seam the combined expression is again governed by (7.129) or (7.132). T2 identifies such a common determining problem on its displayed inner seam inside one selected live component. Matching a true entry or exit boundary requires its actual partner and record; (7.136) gives a quantitative reason to retain that requirement.

### 7.41 Fixed projected field derivatives on the normalized kernel

One can obtain finite external-field derivatives without assuming a Poincaré inequality for a complex measure. Differentiate the physical finite-dimensional integral at its real reference point. The resulting terms are connected cumulants on the same real law. This also retains the derivatives of the source-free density and of its denominator.

**Lemma 7.70 (anchored cumulants from the real covariance estimate).** On a real law satisfying (7.114), take m≥2 fixed. Suppose F_i has anchor x_i and, for p=2m or any larger fixed p, `‖F_i‖_p≤b_i`, `‖∂_y F_i‖_p≤b_i exp(−c dist(x_i,y))`. Then
`|cum(F₁,…,F_m)|≤C_m(Π b_i) exp[−c_m tree(x₁,…,x_m)]`.   (7.137)
One can use connected finite anchor sets instead, charging their diameters to their carrier weights.

*Proof.* For any split into two nonempty groups, the difference between a mixed moment and the product of the two group moments is a covariance. Apply (7.114) to the two products, use the product derivative rule and Hölder for at most m factors. Summing the exponential kernel yields `C_m Πb_i exp[−c′ dist(group₁,group₂)]`. This applies as well after deleting some variables. In the ordinary partition formula for a cumulant, replace every mixed block moment by the product of its two submoments. The result is the cumulant on two independent copies of the law for the two groups and hence is zero. Telescoping the replacements and using the covariance bound at each mixed block gives the same estimate for the cumulant. Split the anchors at a longest edge of a minimum spanning tree. All distances across this cut are at least the length of that edge, and its length is at least tree/(m−1). This proves (7.137). The proof uses the joint moments of the one law, and permits complex-valued observables evaluated on that real law. ∎

Let θ denote canonical external field coordinates at finitely many current-scale anchors. The original cutoff is fixed in the common integration coordinates B. Write ρ_θ(B) for the unnormalized density, and `S_I=∂_{θ_I} logρ_θ|₀` for a nonempty labelled derivative block I. Constants in S_I need not be estimated in a cumulant with at least two further entries. With R and V also depending on θ, the exact formula is
`∂_{θ_[m]}Cov_θ(R,V)|₀ = Σ cum₀(∂_{I_0}R, ∂_{I_1}V, (S_D)_{D∈π})`.   (7.138)
The sum is over ordered disjoint subsets I₀,I₁ of [m], and all partitions π of their complement. Empty I₀,I₁ give the undifferentiated observable. To verify it, use labelled nilpotent variables u_i and two additional tags a,b. Extract the coefficient of ab u₁⋯u_m in `log E₀ exp[logρ_u−logρ₀ +a R_u+b V_u]`. A normalization depending only on u drops out. This proof at a finite cutoff may equivalently be performed by ordinary differentiation under the compact integral. The score of a moving selector requires the separate face terms of §7.16; (7.138) is stated for the fixed canonical selector.

**Proposition 7.71 (localized scores for the fundamental first clean step, P/L).** At the first native clean small-field integration take an external physical target `W(θ)_c=exp(g θ_c)` in its original tree-based target chart about identity. For any fixed m the derivatives S_I in (7.138), up to constants, are sums over current anchors x of functions S_{I,x} with, for every fixed p,
`‖S_{I,x}‖_p + sup_y e^{c_m dist(x,y)} ‖∂_{B_y} S_{I,x}‖_p ≤ C_{m,p} g^{|I|} exp[−c_m Σ_{i∈I} dist(x,y_i)]`.   (7.139)
Here y_i is the anchor of the external derivation. Use the real clean reference and spare physical parameter/cutoff charts of §§7.11, 7.25, 7.29. The constants are independent of the number of blocks for fixed L,M.

*Proof.* Use the actual first-step physical fiber coordinates at W(θ). Its conditional exponent is the bare Wilson and gauge action in the original finite-corridor readout, plus the original Jacobian, as in (7.102a) at η=0. The original regular first constrained minimum varies analytically with its external target, with first response exponentially localized by CMP102 (172),(190); at this one step the native physical lengths differ only by the fixed L. The input field and output coordinates can be taken in the same small physical chart. Equivalently the local tree chart and exponentially bounded restricted inverse of the first Hessian give these derivatives about identity, with the actual gauge term retained. Each stenciled action or Jacobian coefficient therefore has a fixed physical complex neighborhood and a first external derivative with that exponential to y. Higher fixed derivatives are obtained by holding any one of their slots fixed and using the remaining Cauchy radii. This yields the weaker but sufficient exponential to the sum of their distances divided by |I|.

Subtract the B-independent critical action. The integrated first variation of the augmented action on the physical constraint fiber vanishes identically for every W. If local action terms have nonzero linear jets, subtract their individual jets first: their total is precisely zero at the actual constrained minimum, also after each external derivative. The remaining phase has the integral second-derivative form `g⁻² g² Σ_{ij} B_i B_j ∫₀¹(1−s)D²Φ(sgB;W)_{ij}ds`. On the fundamental scale its representatives have fixed local stencils in B with analytic physical coefficients depending on the nearby minimizer and external data. Subtracting the B-independent Jacobian value leaves localized analytic terms on the same chart. Derivatives with respect to any θ_y contribute g times the corresponding physical derivative. Derivatives with respect to B cost only a fixed local polynomial in B, since the chart extends past the selector; overlapping fixed stencils are combined at x. This gives a pointwise bound `C_m g^{|I|}(1+Σ_{z near x}|B_z|)^q exp(−c_mΣ dist(x,y_i))` for a fixed q and the same for its B derivative with fixed local support. All its required p-th moments follow from the local probe in Lemma 7.51. Any B-independent Gaussian normalization cancels in (7.138). This proves (7.139). ∎

For the higher clean precisions C*Δ_k C, which are quasi-local, finite stencils in the preceding proof must be replaced by an absolute carrier estimate for their field derivatives on the original physical chart. A convenient sufficient requirement is a decomposition of `D_{θ_I}(C*Δ_k C)_{bb′}` into carriers containing b,b′ whose exponentially weighted kernel sums are bounded by `C_m g^{|I|}`, with external decay to y_i or with their anchors included in the same sums. For the interaction scores, the local coefficient bounds of CMP116 (1.34),(1.42) suffice if the actual (U,J) graph response is bounded in their native chart with exponential weights. A sup bound for an independently varied current, or locality only in the field, would not verify this requirement.

**Corollary 7.72 (fixed formation jets).** Suppose R is one of the p=2,3,4 remainder rows in Theorems 7.65, 7.68, its joint (B,θ) physical readout has the same complex chart, valuation and first localized response, and V is an actual inherited or fresh vertex with the corresponding external derivatives on its original chart. Use scores (7.139), or the quasi-local higher-step variant just stated. Then each fixed m-jet at θ=0 of the normalized real connected coefficient satisfies
`|∂_{θ_[m]}Cov_θ(R,V)|₀|≤C_{m,f} M_p t^s g^p g exp[−c_m tree(x₀,Y,y₁,…,y_m)−κ′n(Y)]`.   (7.140)
Here M₄ includes the physical factor `A_j α_j^{d−4}g_j^{-d}`. The support weight allows summation with all fixed spatial polynomial moments.

*Proof.* Center V by its deterministic value at B=0 for each θ; this leaves the covariance and all its derivatives unchanged. For the inherited V′ this difference gains g on the fixed physical B chart by one derivative and the segment from zero. The same argument after external differentiation costs one g per canonical external derivative and local polynomial moments, as in Corollary 7.66. The actual fresh cubic remainder has the same bound by its fixed physical degree. The joint form of (7.134) is obtained by the identical two-constants argument when the actual combined readout has the stated chart and first localized response. For each physical derivative at θ=0 the remaining valuation can be filled using the segment in gB. If the number of canonical derivatives (including one B gradient when applicable) exceeds p, their number of factors g already exceeds p; otherwise the remaining factors come from the Taylor integral. This proves the L^q bounds of size `C M_p t^s g^p` with the external anchors from each derived R, and their B-gradient bounds. Apply (7.138) and (7.137). Sum the score anchors x using (7.139). The exponentials connecting all clusters of external slots and score anchors form a connected graph; spending a fixed fraction on the sums preserves a positive decay to their spanning tree, since m is fixed. Size losses from the finite vertex Y are absorbed into its spare carrier weight. This proves (7.140). ∎

At the fundamental first step the combined external chart for physical plaquette readouts uses the same finite-corridor fiber map as in (7.102a), so the corollary includes their actual projected finite jets and the original conditional density scores. At higher ages the result specifies the additional *physical* graph and precision-kernel response needed for fixed jets. It neither differentiates a hidden independently varying current nor identifies an arbitrary collection of external Taylor coefficients with the full covariant projection P₆.

### 7.42 From the hard gauge covariance to the actual precision response

CMP109 (2.11) explicitly replaces the axial delta gauge in CMP99 (3.156) by an exponential gauge. Although both gauges use the same physical constrained quadratic action, their covariance matrices act on different spaces. We give the change of variables before differentiating the precision; the two covariances are not identified directly.

**Lemma 7.73 (the two Gaussian gauges, P/L on the homogeneous clean graph).** Let v be a physical current-link tangent vector on the linearized coarse constraint `Qv=0` at the critical current field V=V^{(k)} in CMP109 (2.2)–(2.3). Write D_V for the based infinitesimal gauge map, with generators at the interior sites of each current block and zero at its center. Let L_V be the linear averaged-contour map from (2.5), normalized so its positive quadratic gauge action is `½⟨L_V v,G_g⁻¹ L_V v⟩`. The fixed block-diagonal G_g has uniform positive lower and upper bounds. Let C_ax be the physical-link covariance on the hard axial slice of CMP99 §E, embedded by zero on its eliminated tree bonds. Then the covariance on the full constrained link space with the actual exponential gauge is
`C_exp=P C_ax Pᵀ + D_V R⁻¹ G_g R⁻ᵀ D_Vᵀ,`
`R=L_V D_V,   P=I−D_V R⁻¹ L_V.`   (7.141)
The covariance in the independent coordinates B of CMP109 (2.12) is the submatrix `C_B=Γ C_exp Γᵀ` on the free bonds, where Γ deletes the selected corridor bonds. It is this C_B which has inverse H_B in (7.138).

*Proof.* A based gauge change leaves the actual coarse constraint fixed, hence `Q D_V=0`. At each block center fix the generator zero. Solving the tangent equations on its spanning axial tree edges from parent to child gives a unique based generator u such that `s=v−D_Vu` is zero on the hard tree. All paths have bounded length at this current blocking step because L is fixed. This is an invertible linear decomposition of the physical tangent fiber. The hard quadratic form on s is exactly the constrained Wilson Hessian, including the constraint-curvature/current term in (3.156). At a constrained critical point the Hessian of the physical Wilson action annihilates gauge tangents, including mixed pairs with an arbitrary tangent vector: differentiate the exact gauge invariance of the restricted action once in the orbit direction and once in the other direction; the term involving the differentiated tangent vector is multiplied by the first derivative of the restricted action, which is zero. Thus its quadratic value on v equals its value on s.

The averaged contour in the actual soft gauge transforms by its two endpoint matrices, since each path between the endpoints has this covariance and the contour average preserves it. At the gauge-fixed critical field its value is identity by G(V)=0. A based orbit variation therefore changes each associated contour coordinate by the negative of its generator at that site (up to the fixed orthogonal endpoint convention). This shows R is an invertible block map with uniform inverse. Even if one writes the coordinates relative to their original reference transporter, the conjugations involved are unitary on the real chart and analytic on its smaller complex extension. Use the variables s and `σ=L_V v`. Then `v=P s + D_V R⁻¹ σ`. The Wilson quadratic form depends only on s, and the added quadratic gauge term depends only on σ. Their linear Jacobian is constant in s,σ and cancels from normalized Gaussian expectations. The two centered Gaussians are independent and their pushed-forward covariance is (7.141). The free coordinates in (2.12) are precisely the non-selected components of v, giving the submatrix assertion. All maps in (7.141) other than C_ax use a fixed number of current blocks and have uniformly bounded derivatives on the small chart. For physical data the identity extends from real to complex parameters by analyticity. CMP99, pp. 427–432, (3.155)–(3.158), Theorem 3.15, [CMP109, pp. 265–268, (2.2)–(2.12)](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01215223). ∎

**Theorem 7.74 (homogeneous near-identity precision jets, P/L with native walk slack).** Use the pure full periodic clean hierarchy with external physical upper target `W_c=exp(g θ_c)` about identity, common CMP102 (172),(190) graph radius, and the strict native walk margin in (7.102b). In the localized current representative of the original gauge-invariant scalar specified in Lemma 7.79, the Gaussian precision in independent coordinates has, at θ=0, the fixed-order derivative bound
`|∂_{θ_I}H_B(b,b′)|≤C_m g^m exp[−c_m tree(b,b′,y₁,…,y_m)]`, `m=|I|≥1`.   (7.142)
The rates are in the current unit lattice, with the fixed final L change of units absorbed. The scalar determinant variation is independent of B and drops from the normalized covariance derivative. Constants depend on the fixed native M,L and the available analytic margins, uniformly in clean depth. The chart here is the original homogeneous near-identity physical graph; a different joined determining problem requires its own response estimates.

*Response of the native covariance walks.* Use the physical C_ax expansion in CMP99 Theorem 3.15, which the source gives as the convergent generalized walks of (3.107)–(3.108). Its terms depend only on the field restricted to the corresponding localization sets. The tree-walk variants for the nonlinear Hessian have the same bounds as (3.108), as explained immediately before §E. On the smaller physical chart about identity each term admits the analytic variations (3.37)–(3.38). Its weight may be taken to include a positive exponential in the connecting length and a summable walk factor, after reserving a small fraction of the weak-decay margin in (7.102b). Here all localization cubes are homogeneous current-scale cubes.

To check its physical directions, at identity use CMP102 (172),(190) on the extended smaller external polydisc. In current units its value, discrete first difference and d*d-rows for one anchor y are bounded by `C exp(−c dist(x,y))`. These are exactly the size and the second-divergence variation required by CMP99 (3.37)–(3.38). For the physical current, the fine plaquette expansion followed by its covariant divergence gives the same one-anchor bound by the fourth row of (190), as checked in T3 §4.49. Specifically the linear term is d*dA, the derivative of the local bracket uses first differences, and the remaining η times bounded local expressions lose at most their one η on applying the lattice divergence. Further fixed target derivatives of all these rows follow by Cauchy at any one of the fixed slots on the larger original polydisc. At θ=0 each such derivative carries g per canonical slot and decays exponentially to the most distant slot, hence at a reduced rate to the sum of their distances. These uses of (190) pertain to its actual original coarse-target perturbation, about the trivial target.

One may estimate derivatives of the walk in its field arguments using only this directional norm on its own support X. To see this, multiply a direction by a smooth current-unit cutoff equal to one on X and supported in a fixed enlargement. Such a cutoff with uniformly bounded first and second finite differences may be obtained by smoothing the indicator of a fixed enlargement of X, containing a unit neighborhood of X, by a fixed smooth compact kernel. The product rule for d*d costs only the first difference and value besides d*d of that direction. Thus this extension is admissible in the tangent complex ball of (3.37)–(3.38) with its *local* norm, independently of the number of fine bonds in X. In the independent-current extension, cut off that component in the same collar. The walk only sees the original direction in its support. Cauchy and the finite chain rule at θ=0 therefore bound each derivative by its original enlarged-chart walk weight times `C_m g^m exp[−c_mΣ_i dist(y_i,X)]`. Attaching paths from each external y_i to X costs those distances. Connecting the endpoints, attachment points and the entire X costs at most a fixed multiple of the walk length plus its bounded local-cube endpoints. Spend part of the walk's length decay on this connection and sum the walks with the remaining strict margin. This gives the tree estimate of (7.142) for the derivatives of C_ax.

The local maps D_V, R⁻¹, L_V and P inherit the same physical response to external slots. The needed current background is the actual `V^{(k)}=M^k U_{k+1}` in (2.3), on its critical gauge orbit. For clarity the gauge-adjusted map (7.117) also gives the raw terminal response: the endpoint frame of each averaging has logarithm and target derivative bounded by a fixed constant times its physical mesh τ_l and the local field/response norm. The product of all the frames at a surviving site has uniformly bounded norm and variation since Σ_l τ_l is bounded; the variation retains its spatial exponential after the fixed cumulative collar shift. At the final current mesh this controls the original raw averaged links. If the fine minimizer is evaluated in its near-identity relative Landau representative, restore the current axial representative of (2.3) by the actual based averaged-contour gauge at this last step. Its site matrices are just the current block contours of the input, with a fixed L stencil. It retains those same bounds. The relative field and gauge-covariant kernels can equivalently be evaluated in this representative because the original integral and selector transform as CMP109 (2.16). On actual real parameter families these are changes by real orthogonal matrices; their analytic at-zero identities suffice for the fixed derivatives. The fine physical covariance transforms at its current bond endpoints, also with these local rotation factors. Substitution in (7.141) and restriction by Γ prove the tree estimate for all derivatives of C_B.

*Invert the covariance in the actual coordinates.* C_B(0) and its inverse have uniform operator bounds. For the lower bound on C_B use the hard-slice precision upper bound from the uniform exponential row sum at (3.158) and the positive gauge covariance in (7.141). The linear coordinate map `(s,σ)↦Γv` and its inverse have uniform norms: reconstruction of v from Γv uses only the invertible local selected corridor equation in CMP109 after (2.11), and reconstruction of s,σ uses only the fixed block tree and gauge coordinates above. Here s is measured in its independent hard-slice coordinates with the same local equivalence. Thus (7.141) gives a uniform lower eigenvalue for C_B and a uniform exponential kernel upper bound. Its inverse H_B(0) then has exponentially decaying entries: conjugate by a sufficiently weak exponential distance weight; the change to C_B in operator norm is arbitrarily small relative to its lower eigenvalue by its exponential Schur bound. Invert the conjugate and use a weight based at the second endpoint. This proof makes no finite-range assertion for H_B.

Now use the exact inverse derivative `∂H_B=−H_B(∂C_B)H_B`. Higher derivatives are finite sums of open products alternating H_B(0) with nonempty derivatives of C_B whose labels partition I. In each product the kernel exponentials give a connected graph between b,b′ and the indicated y_i. Spend half their decay on the internal anchor sums and keep a fixed positive rate for the external spanning tree. Multiplying the factors g proves (7.142). ∎

The Gaussian part of any score S_I in (7.138) is therefore a sum of `−½ B_b ·[∂_I H_B(b,b′)]B_{b′}` plus a deterministic constant. Assign it to b and sum b′ using (7.142) and the local moment probe. Differentiating with respect to B leaves one factor of B and the corresponding exponential connection to its slot. This proves (7.139) for that Gaussian part at every admitted homogeneous clean depth. It also proves directly why a field-independent or exactly finite-range replacement for the precision is unnecessary.

### 7.43 Fixed physical formation jets at arbitrary homogeneous clean depth

**Theorem 7.75 (homogeneous fixed-jet formation on the original map, P/L).** Use the homogeneous original clean current graph near identity, all cutoff, exponential-moment, walk and chart margins of Theorems 7.65, 7.68, 7.74, and the actual completed row and moment identities in (7.131). For a fixed smooth test anchor, the graded physical external jets of its one-step connected attachment at the identity obey (7.140) at every old-to-current age. This includes the original complete inherited vertex (1.33) and fresh vertices with the physical Taylor bound in Corollary 7.53. For the quartic sector take the original physical graph and both analytic tail conditions in Theorem 7.68. On this regular class the resulting finite external jets have every fixed spatial moment, the factor g_k, the positive age gain and their respective old grades.

*Actual combined target.* In physical variables z=g_k B, q=g_k θ, the argument of the k-step old minimizing map in CMP116 (1.33) is precisely `exp(iB′) V^{(k)}`, with the local physical B′ obtained from the selected-corridor equation CMP109 (3.2). The retained field is `V^{(k)}=M^k(U_{k+1}(exp q))` in its current axial representative (2.3). As in the proof of Theorem 7.74, the k accumulated endpoint frames in (7.117) have logarithms O(τ_l) in current units and a bounded sum. The homogeneous original minimum and its first target response at the fine links are bounded by (172),(190) in their relative near-identity coordinates. The raw terminal field and the bounded current based-contour correction thus give `|log V^{(k)}|≤C‖q‖` and a bound `Ce^{−c dist(x,y)}` for its physical first variation at q_y, uniform in k. A choice of fine representative affects the gauge-invariant scalar readout only by its based and endpoint frame changes; the actual current axial representative is fixed before forming B′. On this representative the restricted independent B coordinates transform by the adjoint rule (2.16). This is why a frame change of a physical background cannot be made only in the numerator.

The map `B′=C z−hD(Cz)` has fixed current corridors by the selected-bond equation, with its coefficients evaluated on V^{(k)}. Analyticity, bounded derivative and uniform invertibility of the selected coefficients hold in a fixed physical near-identity neighborhood, as in Lemma 7.19 and CMP109 between (2.10) and (2.11). Consequently `b=log[exp(iB′)V^{(k)}]` is a holomorphic function of (z,q), with b(0,0)=0; taking a fixed sufficiently small polydisc makes its norm fit strictly in the native (172) domain. Its derivative in one z_y has only a fixed corridor footprint; the q_y derivative has the previous exponential kernel. Composing the actual old minimizing graph U_k(exp b) and the original iterated old averages retains an exponential to that slot by a convolution of the (190) and (7.117) response bounds. This verifies the joint chart and its external anchor hypothesis in Corollary 7.72 on the homogeneous graph. The real portion is still the same regular original minimum used in (7.132). Applying (7.134) separately to its two remainders on this combined (z,q) chart therefore gives the valuation and fixed external derivatives used in (7.138). For an actual old reconstructed-current tail, it is the original CMP109 (1.15) pair that must satisfy the physical tail certificate. On the homogeneous near-flat reconstruction its current is the appropriately rescaled current of the same critical orbit, as verified in T3 §4.49.

*Density derivatives.* The exponential-gauge part has the scores from (7.142). For the remaining factor use CMP116 Lemma 2, (1.41)–(1.43): a complete local V_Y is the sum of a quadratic-growth expression in the B slots of Y and an analytic scalar bounded on its original domain. Their bounds there have native exponential decay in d_k(Y). In particular their common bound on the real selector has the form `a_Y(1+Σ_{b∈Y}|B_b|²)` with a rooted exponentially summable a_Y on the stipulated parameters. To differentiate with respect to the physical external q, use the original `(U_{k+1},J_{k+1})` on Y. On the near-identity homogeneous graph, its potential, first difference and native current variations have a physical norm ≤`C exp(−c dist(y,Y))` in the required local chart, by (190) and the current calculation in T3 §4.49. Its higher fixed field derivatives at zero obey this estimate for each slot separately, by Cauchy on the smaller original near-identity disc. For a derivative of the analytic localized coefficient in such a direction, cut off its field/current variations in a fixed collar as in Theorem 7.74. The sufficient small native domain conditions (1.12)–(1.14) on these variables give a mesh-independent directional Cauchy radius at identity. This argument estimates a direction before summing fine sites. It incurs no fine-site count.

Thus the I-labelled derivative of V_Y has size `C_m g_k^{|I|} a_Y(1+Σ_{b∈Y}|B_b|²) exp[−c_m Σ_{i∈I} dist(y_i,Y)]`. The same estimate up to another fixed polynomial holds for a B derivative, supported in Y, by Cauchy on the spare B chart. Taking any fixed L^p norm costs at most a polynomial in the number of current bonds of Y, by the single-site exponential probe. Designate one coarse root of Y and sum supports there. Replacing distances to Y by distances to that root and summing its B-gradient anchors requires only a small multiple of diam Y and a polynomial support factor. These are paid by the fixed spare exponential in a_Y. This verifies (7.139) for the whole non-Gaussian score, hence for the full original normalized clean fiber. For the distinguished inherited vertex, first take the difference from its value at B=0. Analyticity on the same spare B chart gives the g_k factor of Corollary 7.66, also after finitely many external derivatives. The actual fresh local cubic term has that factor by its degree. Apply Corollary 7.72 and sum the physical source/field anchors at any fixed spatial moment. ∎

This proves the ordinary physical Taylor and moment tests through degree three (and any other fixed finite order) of the connected output for the stated class. Applying a fixed local extraction that is a bounded combination of those moments preserves its bound. The full P₆ output norm additionally requires construction of the next generation's covariant carrier kernels on a common complex physical core, its absolute off-shell readouts, and all lower/contact and exterior records. Those data cannot be replaced by the numerical fixed jets at identity.

### 7.44 Recovering the age in an absolute connected-carrier norm

The physical moment cancellations in (7.130) were proved on the actual minimizing graph. A rough auxiliary localization may use weakened operators where that cancellation does not hold. The next interpolation keeps the graph for every use of its improved estimate.

**Lemma 7.76 (physical coordinate restrictions and carrier interpolation).** Group all physical inputs in each current native cube as one vector w_D. On a finite torus let F(w) have distinguished root o and a rough decomposition
`F=Σ_{X connected, X∋o} f_X(w|X)`, `Σ_X e^{κ |X|} sup_{‖w‖∞<δ}|f_X|≤A t^{-h}` for h≥0, 0<t≤1. Suppose also that on a smaller fixed physical disc `sup_{‖w‖∞<δ₁}|F(w)|≤A t^s`, s>0. Let B_d be a bound on the exponential number of connected cube sets of a given size containing o (e.g. encode them by a depth-first walk of at most 2n steps in the neighbor graph). Fix `0<λ<s/(s+h)`, and `0<ω<1`. If
`κ_out + log B_d + log(1+2ω) < λκ,`
then F has a decomposition on the actual physical disc of radius ωδ₁ obeying
`Σ_{X connected, X∋o} e^{κ_out |X|} sup |F_X|≤ C A t^{s−λ(s+h)}.`   (7.143)
A physical field valuation through degree p is preserved. This estimate can group arbitrarily many coordinates inside one cube.

*Proof.* For a subset S of input cubes put
`F[S](w)=Σ_{D⊂S}(−1)^{|S\D|} F(w 1_D)`.
The sum over S equals F by finite inclusion-exclusion. Each F[S] depends only on S and vanishes if any of its vector inputs vanishes. Every partial evaluation is on the same true graph family as F. Hence `sup_{δ₁}|F[S]|≤2^{|S|}A t^s`. Applying the rough representation shows that f_X cancels unless S⊂X; each included contribution has this same factor 2^{|S|}. If l(S) is the minimum number of cubes in a connected set containing o and S, this gives `sup_{δ₁}|F[S]|≤2^{|S|} A t^{-h}e^{−κl(S)}`. On radius ωδ₁ both bounds gain ω^{|S|}: multiply each vector input by its own scalar parameter, use the zero on each coordinate hyperplane and apply the one-variable Schwarz bound successively. Interpolate the first estimate with weight 1−λ and the second with λ.

Choose one deterministic minimum connecting set X(S) and group F[S] there. For a fixed X of size n the sum over S⊂X of (2ω)^{|S|} is (1+2ω)^n. There are at most B_d^n such X, so summing the resulting geometric series gives (7.143). Every partial evaluation preserves a common Taylor valuation at w=0, hence so does every output term. The empty-set term has carrier {o}. ∎

The localization is in the original physical coordinates w, even when the rough decomposition was obtained from unphysical weak parameters. It requires the quantitative slack in (7.143); an arbitrary weak exponential rate need not suffice.

**Lemma 7.77 (rough expansion for the base-identity clean minimizing map).** On the homogeneous original first-stage target family of CMP116 (1.1)–(1.21) with identity external field, fix any desired finite carrier rate κ. Use the native weakening radius ρ=e^{κ₁} and choose it, M and the physical input radius so that (i) the weakened walk and contraction requirements (1.11)–(1.21) hold and (ii) `(ρ−1)>B_d e^{c_L κ+c_L}` for the fixed cube/corridor enlargements. Then the physical relative potential of H_k(b) on a fixed current patch has a rooted carrier expansion `Σ_X h_X(b|X)` with
`Σ_X e^{κ|X|} ‖h_X‖_{C^1(patch)}≤C_κ δ_b` on a physical current-target polydisc `‖b‖∞≤δ_b`. Constants are uniform in the homogeneous clean age. CMP116 (1.17) starts with arbitrary small B′=b; the special independent substitution (1.19) can be made afterward.

*Proof.* Choose the fixed root patch and its collar inside the unweakened root region in the localization construction. Introduce the scalar walk weights s(D) as in CMP116 after (1.7). Apply its fundamental theorem of calculus (1.9), setting the inactive exterior weights to zero. The active support must join the root patch, or the differentiated component disconnected from it vanishes by the localized equations (1.1)–(1.5); this is the component Y₀ argument after (1.9). The solution on the root depends only on b in that connected component and its fixed stencil collar. On `|s(D)|≤ρ`, CMP116 (1.17)–(1.21) bound the full weakened physical relative field by `C e^{16κ₁} δ_b` in its native value and first-difference norms. Cauchy costs `(ρ−1)^{-1}` per active differentiated cube, uniformly for interpolation values in [0,1]. Count connected supports after fixed enlargements, retaining the specified e^{κ|X|}, and sum. A fixed-size root patch changes its initial constant only. In applying this estimate choose the input radius with the original exponential smallness condition (1.21), in particular `e^{32κ₁}δ_b` sufficiently small. For a prescribed finite κ₁ the original walk radius also requires sufficient initial walk decay; it is part of (i), not a free conclusion for fixed previously chosen parameters. [CMP116, pp. 2–7, (1.1)–(1.23)](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01239022). ∎

**Corollary 7.78 (actual flat-terminal physical carrier formation).** For the homogeneous clean graph at terminal identity and the explicit oriented quadratic/cubic path families of Theorem 7.64, strengthen the path moment and weakening margins as specified below. Then their remainders R_p, p=2,3, have a physical current-coordinate carrier representation on a smaller fixed disc, with `Σ e^{κ_out|X|}sup|R_{p,X}|≤C_f M_p t^{s′}` for a positive s′ and prescribed finite κ_out. Each R_{p,X} has valuation p at the physical identity. This applies to the true constrained minimum at every homogeneous age, and to the actual integration coordinates z=g_k B at flat terminal field.

*Proof of the rough representation.* Work first on one terminal patch containing a fixed old curvature root and the stencil needed for all its successive original averages. In current units the cumulative collar from (7.117) is bounded by C_L. The map sending an input physical fine potential on this patch to its old curvature F_j at that root is analytic with sup norm C on a fixed small C¹ ball, uniformly in j,k. Indeed (7.117) and its product bound preserve the C¹ norm by `Π_l(1+C_L ε τ_l)`; the old four-link curl cancels its first mesh factor before dividing by t². The map to the *gauged* old link minus identity has norm C t on that ball and vanishes at zero. The terms for local curvature and parallel transports may be computed in this same recursively gauged representative because their complete contraction is gauge invariant. The patch may be enlarged by a bounded number of current localization cubes.

Use the h_X of Lemma 7.77 on the patch. Substitution in these local analytic maps is bounded in the rooted carrier norm without summing individual fine slots: for a holomorphic Banach-space function bounded by C on a ball of radius δ₀, its degree-n symmetric multilinear coefficients have norm at most `C n^n/(n! δ₀^n)≤C(e/δ₀)^n` by polarization and Cauchy. Join all input carriers at the fixed patch and use the geometric series when `C_κ δ_b<δ₀/(2e)`. Thus each old curvature has rough carrier norm O(C_κ δ_b), and each old link deviation has norm O(C_κ t δ_b). This proof treats the local field as a function in a mesh-independent norm and incurs no count of the finest sites. Replacing b by the actual local input `Cz−hD(Cz)` at identity costs only fixed stencil enlargement and a smaller fixed δ_b.

For a word of l old links, connect its entire deterministic path and its local collars once. A path of physical length tl can be covered by at most `C_L(1+tl/M_b)` adjacent localization cubes of side M_b≥1: divide it into pieces of length M_b, each lying in a fixed neighborhood of a single initial cube. Then expanding the product of link adjoints costs at most `exp(C_κ δ_b t l)` in the attached carrier norms. The root/corridor weight costs at most `exp[κ C_L(1+tl/M_b)]`. Require
`κ C_L/M_b + C_κ δ_b < a/2`
on the common arrangement, where a is the original exponential path-moment rate in Theorem 7.65; for multiple words use their total length. These explicit sufficient restrictions pay all path weights and finite powers of l. The subtraction of the true local area and cubic polynomials has the same or smaller rough norm. Integration over old roots in the fixed terminal patch uses its bounded physical volume in the curvature inner product. The rough normalized quadratic carrier sum has bound `C_f M₂ t^{-2}`, and the rough cubic sum has bound `C_f M₃`. In this rough construction no cancellation is requested at weakened wall parameters.

The improved true-graph value bound on a smaller fixed physical disc was proved in (7.134), including at m=0. It applies also when any collection of grouped current input cubes z is set to zero, since that is still an actual small target on the homogeneous chart. Apply Lemma 7.76 with the respective rough exponent h=2 or 0. Choose the rough κ with the strict interpolation margin there for the requested κ_out. All constants, cube arrangements and source-independent cutoffs must meet these finite choices simultaneously. One sufficient ordered choice is first to fix s,λ,κ_out and the resulting κ; then choose M_b and the native walk parameters to meet the displayed decay requirements, and finally choose δ_b and the physical selector sufficiently small to meet the analytic margins. This is an application on the displayed stronger native clean subfamily, not a claim that preassigned mixed parameters obey them. The constant multiplying M_p may depend on these choices. The field valuation p follows from (7.131) and the exact subtraction of the corresponding local centers before localization. This proves the result. ∎

### 7.45 The physical representative and joint external localization

**Lemma 7.79 (computing a conditional scalar in a localized representative).** The physical precision jets in (7.142) can be evaluated in a specified current representative while retaining the original gauge-invariant scalar at each prescribed W(q). They need not be asserted for the matrix entries in every raw axial frame. The distinction matters because the Landau-to-axial transformation in CMP102 (124) obeys an averaged gauge condition `R₀u_j=1`. It need not fix each coarse site.

*Proof.* About the identity target, use the relative Landau field `Uᴸ(q)=exp[iη H_{k+1}(q)]`. CMP102 Proposition 9, printed p.309, explicitly identifies its B with `(1/i)log V′` in the statement of that proposition. For real q this fine field is in the same fine gauge orbit as the prescribed critical field U_{k+1}(W(q)). Gauge covariance of the actual averages gives
`Ŵ(q)=M^{k+1}Uᴸ(q)=W(q)^{u_T(q)}`
for some coarse gauge. No estimate on u_T or its derivatives is used. Form `Vᴸ=M^kUᴸ`. On each last current block, apply a based current site gauge with root value one to restore the contour gauge in G(V)=0. The required site matrix at x is the actual averaged contour from the center y to x (with inverse if the orientation is reversed): its transformation under a based gauge multiplies by the inverse at x. Thus it sends each such contour to identity with a finite current-block operation. Call the result `V^c(q)`. Its coarse constraint equals Ŵ(q). The two previous steps show it represents the critical current orbit at Ŵ(q), and the gauge condition and CMP109 (2.2)–(2.3) select its actual soft-gauge saddle there.

Compute the conditional scalar using V^c and a corresponding fine representative, transforming the entire numerator, denominator and the free fluctuation vectors by the simultaneous adjoint rule (2.16). The original real canonical balls are invariant under these rotations. The scalar for W(q) equals the scalar for Ŵ(q) pointwise on real q by gauge covariance. Hence their Taylor jets agree there, and their holomorphic extensions agree on any common connected domain about zero. To calculate a hard covariance walk or extended scalar on the fine chart one may first use Uᴸ and then transform the current endpoints. Its fine gauge need not be cut into discontinuous representatives or differentiated across a sharp cutoff. The final current rotation just constructed is analytic with localized derivatives by (7.117) and the fixed current contour bounds. This proves the claimed representative assertion, including the case of invariant scalar covariances formed using the actual gauge-invariant vertex V′_k(Y).

Accordingly (7.142) is asserted in this localized computational representative of the actual scalar kernel. The statement for the invariant scalar jets in Theorem 7.75 is independent of that choice. A gauge-sensitive raw axial component or frozen off-shell history variable needs its own original frame response; the preceding argument does not differentiate the inverse gauge in (124). ∎

**Lemma 7.80 (composition of rooted analytic expansions).** Suppose f_X is holomorphic with norm a_X on the independent vector ball of radius r in each native cube of X. At a cube D∈X replace its vector by b_D(w), with a decomposition into connected carriers rooted at D whose total weighted vector norm is at most b. If `eb/r<1`, the weighted norm of the substituted contribution, including the original support X, costs at most
`e^{κ|X|} a_X (1−eb/r)^{−|X|}.`   (7.144)
The constant is independent of the number of coordinates inside each cube.

*Proof.* Expand in the separate cube variables. Applying Cauchy to one scalar radius per cube bounds the multihomogeneous polynomial of degree (n_D) by `a_X r^{-Σ n_D}` on products of unit balls. Polarize its coefficients within each cube, at cost `Π n_D^{n_D}/n_D!≤exp(Σ n_D)`. Substitute the decomposed b_D in every multilinear slot. Each resulting carrier touches the connected original X at D, so the weight on its union is bounded by the product of the weights and e^{κ|X|}. Summing the independent geometric series gives (7.144). ∎

**Theorem 7.81 (joint physical carrier norm on the homogeneous scalar graph, P/L).** Under the stronger native walk, support, interpolation and cutoff margins of Corollary 7.78, the same physical carrier conclusion holds jointly in the current physical z and external physical q. Take a common localization grid for the current step and its single next step, paying the fixed L-dependent grid enlargement in the required decay. Use the invariant scalar representative of Lemma 7.79. For R₂,R₃ one then has
`R_p(z,q)=Σ_{X∋o} r_{p,X}(z|X,q|X),`
`Σ_X e^{κ_out |X|} sup_{‖(z,q)‖∞<δ_in}|r_{p,X}|≤C_f M_p t^{s′},   ord₀ r_{p,X}≥p.`   (7.145)
This is a current-unit connected-carrier bound on a fixed complex physical disc at an arbitrary homogeneous clean age. The localized summands produced by input restrictions may transform separately under changes of representative. Their sum represents the original invariant physical scalar.

*Proof.* For the rough bound, apply Lemma 7.77 at the upper step to the potential H_{k+1}(q) on a fixed patch large enough for each current unit bond. Its constants on the common grid change only by the fixed L rescaling. Apply the analytic repeated-average map from (7.117) on this patch, including the raw endpoint frames and the explicit last current gauge of Lemma 7.79. The accumulated physical stencil has bounded radius. On a fixed small C¹ ball the gauged potential map and its raw endpoint products have a mesh-independent sup bound: the logarithm of each undoing frame is O(τ_l‖A_l‖), with Σ τ_l bounded. The finite current gauge after it uses bounded analytic operations. Banach polarization on the patch, as in Corollary 7.78, gives a rooted expansion of `V^c(q)−I` with norm O(C_κ δ_q). Choose the upper native walk rate with enough slack for the fixed common-grid enlargement.

Now put `b(z,q)=log[exp(iB′(z;V^c(q))) V^c(q)]`. The selected-corridor maps are analytic finite current stencils with uniformly invertible local coefficients; expanding them on the same representation gives a rooted norm `C_κ(δ_z+δ_q)` for b on each current input cube. Choose these radii so this norm is below r/(2e), where r is a permitted input radius for the rough minimizing map H_k(b). Apply (7.144) to each rooted term of that map. Its original decay must have the spare factor `(1−eb/r)^{-1}` per cube, which is at most two per cube with the indicated choice. The resulting rough current representation of the old curvature and path families therefore has the same respective bounds M₂t⁻² and M₃ as in Corollary 7.78, now in both types of input. Covariance of the complete old-path contraction makes the physical value at full data exactly the readout on U_k(exp ib), even though the rough weak fields used to localize it are only auxiliaries.

The stronger actual-graph bound on the joint disc is exactly the combined (z,q) version checked in Theorem 7.75 from (7.134). Setting any group of z,q variables to zero keeps a genuine near-identity target and a genuine minimizing problem. Apply Lemma 7.76 on groups containing both types of physical coordinate. Its entropy depends on the number of cubes, not on the number of variables in a group. This proves (7.145) on a smaller fixed disc. ∎

### 7.46 A normalized complex clean attachment with localized physical carriers

There is a direct way to integrate the localized families in (7.145). Only two labels are needed for the connected coefficient. The original quadratic reserve therefore pays for their two polynomial factors even on a complex external field chart.

**Lemma 7.82 (two polynomial tags in the native clean expansion, P/L).** Take a CMP116 clean integral on its smaller (1.34) external domain, with strict spare positive quadratic and Mayer margins in Lemma 3, (2.26)–(2.41). On its fixed real selector insert one label for `F=Σ_X F_X` rooted at o and one for a single G_Y. Suppose on this selector
`|F_X|≤a_X(1+max_{b∈X}|B_b|)^p,   |G_Y|≤b_Y(1+max_{b∈Y}|B_b|)^q,`
with fixed p,q, `Σ_{X∋o} e^{κ₁′ |X|} a_X≤A` and `b_Y≤B₀ e^{−κ₁′ |Y|}`. The tagged functions must depend on B and any extra external coordinates only in their carriers, be holomorphic in the external coordinates on the same smaller domain, and be evaluable on the fixed interior variables prior to the exterior whitening. Take κ₁′ large enough for the fixed native support counts and the desired smaller output weight. Then the coefficient of the two labels in the connected logarithm has a connected-carrier norm bounded by
`C_{p,q} A B₀ exp[−c dist(o,Y)−κ′ |Y|]`,   (7.146)
uniformly in volume. This coefficient is exactly the complex covariance normalized by the original source-free denominator.

*Proof.* Use independent commuting labels e,h with e²=h²=0. The source factor is exactly `(1+e Σ_X F_X)(1+hG_Y)`; hence only one tag of each type can ever occur. Place each selected support with the originally selected Mayer supports before the conditioning in CMP116 (2.3)–(2.5), enlarging the interior domain by the fixed boundary collar for the recorded coordinates. The exterior variable in (2.6) is the only one whitened; no derivative in (2.8) acts on a tagged interior field or selector. Disconnected sets of marked supports and unmarked supports factor in the same decoupled integrals, because their functions are localized in those supports. The two labels multiply in the finite algebra `1,e,h,eh`.

For an actual term, with at most the two selected tags, use the single bound `(1+max_{X}|B|)^p≤C_{p,σ} exp[σΣ_{b∈X}|B_b|²]`, and the counterpart for Y. Their total enhancement is at most `exp[2σΣ_{b∈Z₀}|B_b|²]`, also on overlapping supports. Take 2σ strictly inside the spare quadratic comparison margin of (2.26)–(2.38). The conditioned positive joint Gaussian and determinant cancellation then apply as in the unmarked proof. The bound for (2.40)–(2.41) acquires only the coefficients a_X,b_Y, the factors C_{p,σ},C_{q,σ} and fixed enlargements of the two supports. Their factors `e^{−κ₁′ |X|},e^{−κ₁′ |Y|}` pay the fixed enlargement and native smallness weights for a distinguished support. Concretely, normalize e by a sufficiently small constant times 1/A and h by a sufficiently small constant times 1/B₀ (zero factors require no insertion). The absolute sum of the integrated activities with either normalized tag attached at a specified cell then fits the original strict polymer margin, by the two coefficient sums and fixed connected-set counting. With both labels present the same proof uses the two coefficient factors together and the one enhanced quadratic bound above. Up to polynomial support factors for the two possible distinguished positions, this gives the same rooted convergence majorant as for the unmarked activities. Those polynomials are paid by a further fixed fraction of κ₁′. After this integration the usual connected log expansion applies in the finite label algebra by the same absolute cluster majorant. It never sums an unrestricted number of polynomial insertions on the Gaussian reference.

A term in its eh coefficient has both marked supports in one connected output; otherwise the partition subtraction in the logarithm cancels it. The spare native size exponent thus pays the distance to Y and leaves its stated size decay. Undo the two label normalizations to obtain (7.146). Finally, directly expanding the scalar finite-algebra logarithm gives `I(FG)/I(1)−I(F)I(G)/I(1)^2`. The unmarked native log guarantees I(1)≠0 on this domain. This proves the normalization assertion. The same rare faces or failed selectors that appear in the unmarked conditioning are included with the actual bounds; no estimate for a different positive denominator is used. ∎

**Theorem 7.83 (complex two-norm attachment on the homogeneous chart).** Take an actual R_p, p=2 or 3, in Theorem 7.81, and the original inherited V′_k(Y) of Corollary 7.66 or a fresh vertex with the same fixed-degree physical difference bound. Use the fixed selector and positive-reserve restrictions of Lemma 7.82 and choose κ_out in (7.145) with enough spare size decay for that lemma. There is a positive s′ and a fixed complex physical disc such that for every external size `0≤d_q≤δ_in/4`,
`sup_{‖q‖∞≤d_q} ‖Cov_{W(q)}(R_p,V_Y)‖_{root} ≤ C_f M_p t^{s′} g_k (d_q+g_k)^p e^{−c dist(o,Y)−κ′|Y|}.`   (7.147)
The norm here sums the resulting connected carriers, with their original fine external fields and the explicit physical q coordinates on each carrier. Evaluate on the invariant graph of Lemma 7.79. The bound includes the compact canonical external disc d_q=O(g_k) and a fixed physical external disc d_q=cδ_in. It is independent of the number of homogeneous clean scales in the age t=L^{j−k} and of the current torus size, with the stated fixed parameters. It does not assert an all-source pressure for unbounded polynomial marks.

*Proof.* In (7.145) use the individual carrier sup bounds a_X and their vanishing up to degree p−1 in the *joint* physical variables z,q. On the inner selector `g_k max |B_b|<δ_in/4`, radial Schwarz gives
`|r_{p,X}(g_kB,q)|≤C a_X δ_in^{−p} (d_q+g_k)^p(1+max_{b∈X}|B_b|)^p`.
For the distinguished inherited interaction subtract V′_k(Y,W,0) at the same external field; this is an exact subtraction inside the covariance. On the physical B chart of (1.34) the segment from zero and scalar radial Schwarz give
`|V′_k(Y,W,B)−V′_k(Y,W,0)|≤C E₀ e^{−κ n(Y)} g_k max_{b∈Y}|B_b|`
with the fixed native constants and available slack. This last estimate takes one radial direction of sup norm one on Y, so it incurs no number of coordinates of Y. For the fresh physical cubic remainder divide its third-order physical Taylor term by g_k²; the canonical bound is (C g_k(1+max_Y|B|)^3) times its fixed carrier weight. Apply Lemma 7.82 with the two extracted numerical factors.

More explicitly, in the tagged construction q is an additional external physical variable on the localized source carrier X. The Gaussian and unmarked interactions retain their original external U,J coordinates on the native extended chart; the new source factors have already been localized by (7.145) in z,q, before weakening those original coefficients. Hence the output is a sum of connected coefficients depending on the native fields restricted to their carrier and on the extra q coordinates there. On the physical scalar graph insert the actual appropriate U,J and q together, with the simultaneous real-frame argument of Lemma 7.79. Their holomorphic continuation on the smaller stated domain gives (7.147). If the original decay of V′_k in (1.36) is measured by d_k(Y), retain the same source calculation with this size and the fixed homogeneous support conversion/slack, as in Corollary 7.66. ∎

The fixed physical output norm in (7.147) retains a current g_k even away from the canonical external ball. Its absolute coupling grade still comes from M_p. On a fixed clean physical-core radius α, inserting `M_p≤A_j min(g_j^{-p},α^{d−p}g_j^{-d})` gives the separate canonical and physical caps of MT41. The new source coefficients in this construction carry an explicit current physical q coordinate in addition to the native external fine pair U,J. Showing that the *next* full P₆ extraction and wall recursions preserve the same gauge-covariant carrier representation, including proper differences and current/contact partners, remains part of the all-history problem.

### 7.47 The complex quartic carrier and the three graded rows

**Theorem 7.84 (complex physical quartic row on the homogeneous clean graph).** Take the fixed clean radius and the completed old tail E_X of Theorem 7.68. For its rough source localization require that the old physical analytic ball includes the fields described below. This holds both for the local compact readout of item 1 there and for an old reconstructed pair holomorphic on the homogeneous native ball of T3 §4.49 with its stated slack. Use the stronger input carrier/weakening margins from Theorem 7.81, retaining the explicit long-carrier condition below. Then the joint expansion (7.145) and the normalized complex attachment (7.147) hold at p=4 with `M₄=A_j α_j^{d−4}g_j^{-d}` and a possibly smaller s′>0.

*Proof of rough domain and localization.* Fix an old carrier of n native old cubes. Its complete support, collar and initial root can be covered and joined by a connected base set X₀ of current localization cubes with `|X₀|≤C_L(1+nt)`, allowing fixed old/current native block size ratios in C_L. Traverse its old connected carrier by a walk of at most Cn old cube steps and group the walk into pieces of bounded current-grid length; each piece meets only a bounded number of current cubes. The original finite readout collars and the bounded cumulative collar in (7.117) change the constants only. This estimate includes wrapping carriers.

First use the true old minimizer at unweakened b and then localize the *source extension* as follows. In the auxiliary construction take the identity-background relative potential H_k(s,b) from Lemma 7.77, with the root set X₀ unweakened. For old compact readouts compute its actual original averaged old links, using a common gauge of these averages as in Lemma 7.54; an own compact Wilson current is computed directly there. At unit-normalized old variables their link size is O(t δ_s) and their curvature/current are bounded by Cδ_s, where `δ_s=C e^{16κ₁}δ_b`, by (1.18) and analytic local products. For an old *reconstructed* fine pair, use U=exp(iη H_k(s,b)) expressed at its old mesh η/t and its own Wilson current in those same units. Its old logarithmic potential, first difference and current have respective sup bounds `C t δ_s,C t² δ_s,C t³ δ_s`. For the last bound expand the fine current in d*dH plus bounded local nonlinear terms, keeping the factor η on the remainder before the divergence as in T3 §4.49. CMP116 (1.18) supplies the admissible derivative norms of the weakened solution, including those of the original CMP102 implicit map. All these estimates are independent of n. On the stated fixed old analytic core choose δ_b small enough to keep these inputs in its smaller native domain, including its original independent-current slack. At s=1 the reconstructed pair is the actual old minimizing pair, by the homogeneous nesting, critical-orbit uniqueness and mesh rescaling in T3 §4.49. At other s the explicit evaluation is solely a localization tool; it is not identified with a different minimum.

Thus the weak source coefficient has ungraded norm ≤`A_X(α_j/g_j)^d` on every required wall polydisc. Apply (1.9) to its exterior walls, exactly as in Lemma 7.77, allowing all walls inside X₀ to stay one. A disconnected differentiated exterior component vanishes by the same separated local implicit equations. A term with m activated exterior cubes gains `(ρ−1)^{-m}` and uses the connected carrier containing X₀ and those m cubes with fixed enlargements. The total weighted norm is bounded by `C A_X(α_j/g_j)^d e^{C(κ+log B_d)|X₀|}` under the original strict ρ margin; this follows by counting all connected sets of size comparable to `|X₀|+m`. Once the upper q-dependent readout is substituted, (7.144) adds a fixed base factor per cube, which may be included in this exponent. For all ages in this theorem require the incoming old carrier rate a to satisfy `C_L C(κ+log B_d)t<a/2`, or supply the equivalent weighted bound with X₀ retained. For a fixed positive a the condition automatically holds at sufficiently old ages. An assertion covering the remaining finitely many ages requires the corresponding original recent-scale reserve; taking a with the displayed slack at t=1 suffices. Summing n and counting the t⁻⁴ old roots with their extra t⁻² normalization gives the rough bound `C A_j (α_j/g_j)^d t^{-6}`. No physical cancellation was used at the walls.

The sharp actual bound on the true smaller joint graph follows from the real radial and long-carrier estimates in Theorem 7.68, and its small complex-disc interpolation. For the reconstructed fine pair, on short carriers use the local old potential/current coordinates of T3 §4.49, with value O((1+n)δ t²); they replace the tree-gauge small variables in that same radial estimate. On large carriers the fixed old-core graph bound and its exponential tail again suffice. The physical composition has valuation at least four after the entire covariant lower completions have been subtracted. All these true-graph facts survive setting any set of the physical (z,q) cube inputs to zero. With α_min≤α_j≤α_* fixed, apply Lemma 7.76 to the rough exponent h=6 and the positive true-graph exponent, paying its explicit interpolation margin. This gives (7.145) for p=4. Lemma 7.82 and the radial estimate in Theorem 7.83 then give
`‖Cov_{W(q)}(R₄,V_Y)‖_{root}≤C_f A_j α_j^{d−4}g_j^{-d} t^{s′}g_k (d_q+g_k)^4 exp[−c dist(o,Y)−κ′|Y|].`   (7.148)
All polynomial factors on the marked support are paid by the same joint comparison as in (7.146). ∎

**Corollary 7.85 (the graded complex clean attachment).** With the exact ordinary/pointed moment removals and one combined area-cubic cancellation, and the homogeneous admissibility and support conditions above, the current complex connected coefficient satisfies
`C_f g_k t^{s′} [M₂(d_q+g_k)²+M₃(d_q+g_k)³+M₄(d_q+g_k)⁴] e^{−c dist(o,Y)−κ′|Y|}`   (7.149)
as a bound on its localized output norm. Take the smaller of the three proven age exponents. At d_q=O(g_k) and `M₂≤A_j g_j⁻², M₃≤A_j g_j⁻³`, this gives the two relative grades and the quartic grade in MT39; with the intersection caps in MT41 it gives the table MT44. Multiplying the physical-disc estimate by the declared `(g_k/α)^d` gives its physical cap when d_q=O(α) lies inside the actual current disc. For d=2 the intersection cap on M₃ supplies the extra g_k/α in the canonical cubic row. No fixed positive α is used for a recorded shrinking live core.

Equation (7.149) is an attachment of a specified *actual* regular physical birth with an original interaction through one original homogeneous clean integral. The output representation still contains localized native external U,J arguments and explicit physical current-coordinate q. The equality to the physical graph is sufficient for this passage. Constructing every next birth as a gauge-covariant completed kernel of the same admissible class, with its projection and all history partners, is an additional recurrence problem.

### 7.48 The bare physical H pressure has zeros on scale a²

T3 §4.56 sharpens the obstruction in Theorem 7.41 to the dimension-six insertion itself. We record the normalization here because the source used in the clean zero-free theorems of §§7.11–7.25 is unamplified.

**Proposition 7.86 (P, via T3's compact source estimate).** Let `h_b=β d_b`, where d_b is the nonnegative local cross-matching force-square contraction of T3 §2. In the normalization of [W, (PD12.1), p. 1182, and (PD12.6)–(PD12.7), p. 1183], with β=c_βg⁻² and c_β=2N, `O_H(f)=(2N)⁻¹a⁻²Σ_b f_b h_b`, take a nonnegative bounded test occupying a fixed positive fraction of sites, including a constant smooth test. On the original Wilson trajectory satisfying the first-moment bound in T3 §4.11, the distance of a zero of `E_β exp[z O_H(f)]` from zero is at most `C_f a²`. In particular a fixed bare exponential-source log-pressure polydisc for this physical H cannot hold all the way to the ultraviolet endpoint.

*Proof.* With V=n⁴ let `D=Σ_b f_b d_b`, normalized so 0≤f≤1. The complete compact stencils have |D|≤MV. The Haar mean per site is bounded below: varying the opposite parallel link of one plaquette in a fixed nonzero Lie-algebra direction while the other nearby links stay near identity gives a nonzero matching force difference on an open set. All other colors in the squared difference enter nonnegatively. Its local Haar cylinder has measure independent of n once the stencil does not wrap onto itself. Summing over the occupied sites gives `P_Haar(D≥bV)≥p>0` by boundedness. Under the Wilson law the local force-square bound by nearby plaquette energies and the first-moment estimate in T3 give `E_β D/V≤C/β`, eventually at most b/4.

Write `λ=βa⁻²/(2N)` and `Z(z)=E_β exp(zλD)`. On a zero-free disc of radius R the normalized log `f(z)=log Z(z)/(λV)` has real part ≤MR, f(0)=0 and slope ≤b/4. Schwarz applied to f/(2MR−f), followed by Cauchy at radius R/2, gives `f(t)≤bt/4+16M t²/R` for 0<t≤R/4. The Haar event and the compact upper bound C_S V for the Wilson action give `f(t)≥bt−C_Sβ/λ−log(1/p)/(λV)`. Taking `t=K(β+1)/λ` for fixed sufficiently large K forces R≤C t. Thus the nearest zero of the finite-volume entire function is within C_f a². Multiplication by a holomorphic scalar exponential does not remove it. For the same quantitative argument applied to the dimension-eight squared plaquette with λ=a⁻⁴, the bound is `C(β+1)a⁴`. T3, §4.56. ∎

The bare physical source disc is therefore false even in this specified dimension-six direction. The unamplified `Σ f_b h_b` has λ=β in this comparison and yields only an order-one upper bound on the radius. Its possible smaller uniform source disc, its ordinary susceptibility, and the finite-jet, contact-renormalized interface remain different questions. Equation (7.149) concerns the actual graded finite insertion and uses two nilpotent labels. It does not require any exponential-source disc for a physically amplified irrelevant operator.

### 7.49 Physical output coordinates and the covariant quadratic/cubic kernels

The explicit q argument in (7.149) can be combined with the other external field arguments on the homogeneous physical graph. The following construction also recovers the first two curvature kernels of that output, with both input grades.

**Lemma 7.87 (localizing the physical output graph).** On the homogeneous near-identity scalar graph of Theorem 7.83 or 7.84, assume the native output has a spare field/current analytic ball as provided by (1.12)–(1.14). With a smaller fixed external q-disc and spare carrier decay in (7.145)–(7.149), its complete scalar output admits a representation `F_o(q)=Σ_{X∋o} f_X(q|X)` on connected current cubes. For `0<r≤r_*` in that disc its weighted norm obeys
`Σ_X e^{κ₂ |X|} sup_{‖q‖≤r}|f_X(q)| ≤ C M_p t^{s′} g_k(r+g_k)^p e^{−c dist(o,Y)−κ′n(Y)}`   (7.150)
for each of the three rows, with M_p from (7.149). Its constant may depend on the fixed physical margins.

*Proof.* Use the relative Landau potential H_{k+1}(q) on each fixed patch in Lemma 7.77. In its native value/difference norms that expansion has size C_κ r on an input disc of radius r, by (1.18) applied to the smaller inputs. Its reconstructed current also has a carrier expansion of size C_κ r: expand the plaquette current at identity on the same patch. The linear term uses d*dH, the local quadratic term uses first differences, and the nonlinear remainder with its factor η pays its single divergence difference. The directional products are bounded multilinear maps on the stated native norms, uniformly in the fine mesh, as in §7.34 and T3 §4.49. Banach polarization as in Corollary 7.78 proves the carrier bound. On the scalar representation of Lemma 7.79 perform any required final current adjoint rotation on the B arguments of the tags instead of on the fine Landau potential. On the real graph this is the exact simultaneous change of all integration variables, including the unchanged orthogonal selector. The local current rotation and its inverse have rooted expansions by Lemma 7.79 and the proof of Theorem 7.81. After a smaller complex radius their norms fit the original inner selector margin. The equalities of physical scalar functions extend by holomorphy.

To substitute the physical fine (U,J) in a connected output supported on Z, work in logarithmic coordinates near identity. Split these external potentials and currents with smooth current-unit functions χ_D of a partition of unity of bounded overlap, each supported on a fixed enlargement of D. First and second fine lattice differences of χ_D are uniformly bounded. Consequently independent small patch inputs added with these χ_D remain in the common native ball, with mesh-independent radius: use the product rules for ∇ and d*d and the fixed overlap. For currents the value norm suffices. This supplies the independent cube radii needed for Lemma 7.80. Using raw sharp cutoffs on a fine background variation here would introduce inverse lattice spacings. The same construction works for a localized analytic coefficient already restricted to Z, by taking only the patches meeting its fixed collar. Include the explicit local q slots in the same substitution. Each group has a convergent rooted representation of norm O(C_κ r), so (7.144) costs a fixed small exponential per cube of Z inside the retained output decay. The native bound of (7.149) was uniform on its original (U,J) ball for the stated explicit q range. Its fixed polynomial in r+g_k is therefore retained. The resulting carrier expansion gives (7.150). ∎

**Theorem 7.88 (covariant physical low kernels and a winding remainder).** Let F_o be the gauge-invariant actual scalar of Lemma 7.87, with fixed source anchor o (an additional distinguished Y is allowed). Let `K_m(e₁,…,e_m)=D_{q_{e₁}}⋯D_{q_{e_m}}F_o(0)` for m=2,3. Their absolute weighted tree/path moments in current units are bounded, respectively, by
`C M_p t^{s′} g_k min_{r∈{g_k,r_*}}(r+g_k)^p r^{-m}`   (7.151)
when g_k≤r_*; a fixed fraction of these radii makes no change to the statement. The factors in o,Y of (7.150) are retained. The two jets have exact covariant quadratic and cubic completions in local plaquette logarithms with connecting paths, plus a separately retained exponentially small winding family. The same bound holds for all their fixed polynomial path moments, with reduced exponential rate.

*Proof of the moment bound.* In each rooted f_X take the fixed-coordinate Cauchy derivatives on its r-disc. Each support has at most C|X| link/color slots on the current grid. The sum over m slots costs at most (C|X|)^m and every such slot is joined to o inside X. For fixed m and desired polynomial moment, pay these factors with spare exponential decay in (7.150). Apply this once at canonical and once at physical radius to obtain (7.151). The first derivative of F_o at the identity vanishes, since its color vector at each link would have to be fixed by all constant SU(N) conjugations.

*The two completions.* Choose a shortest-coordinate-order spanning tree based at o on the coarse torus, with one cut in each direction at a distance comparable to the terminal period n_T/2 from o. At finitely many very short periods enlarge the constants. For an old edge e=(x,x′) of this output grid let C_e(W) be the holonomy along the tree from o to x, then e, then the reverse tree path from x′ to o. Setting each tree link to identity by a site gauge makes C_e the actual new representative at e. For every fixed finite torus and every infinitesimal q, the fields on a sufficiently short radial segment and their tree-gauge transforms lie in the analytic physical neighborhood. Gauge invariance there gives the ordinary link jets of F_o by evaluating its Taylor polynomial in `log C_e` and summing K₂,K₃. The permitted radial segment in this finite-jet identity need not have volume-independent length. The final analytic curvature completions below have their own fixed radius and bounds.

For a nonwinding e of tree distance R from o, the elementary coordinate swaps used in §7.9 express C_e exactly as an ordered product `Π_i exp φ_{e,i}`. Here each `φ_{e,i}` is an oriented old plaquette logarithm transported to o along an explicit word of length at most C(1+R). The number of plaquettes and swaps is bounded by C(1+R)²; the comb tree gives a linear count on a rectangular box. Each swap exchanges two adjacent steps by one oriented plaquette conjugated by the prefix reaching the swap. Canceling backtracking steps accounts for the remaining word. Define
`L_e=Σ_i φ_{e,i}`, `N_e=½Σ_{i<j}[φ_{e,i},φ_{e,j}]`.
The Taylor jets of `log C_e` through curvature degree two equal L_e+N_e by the ordinary BCH formula. Through ordinary link degree two the same statement holds, since all φ vanish linearly. Retain the full compact path/plaquette expressions in L_e,N_e, including their transports. The quadratic completion is
`½Σ_{e,f}K₂(e,f)[L_e,L_f]`,
and the cubic completion is
`⅙Σ_{e,f,h}K₃(e,f,h)[L_e,L_f,L_h] + ½Σ_{e,f}K₂(e,f)[N_e,L_f] + ½Σ_{e,f}K₂(e,f)[L_e,N_f]`.   (7.152)
In these formulas K₂ and K₃ are multilinear forms; the square brackets after K_m denote their evaluations. The brackets inside N_e are Lie commutators. Terms involving the constant vacuum are kept separately. This construction includes the cubic response of the quadratic completion itself, before the total cubic center is extracted.

All color arguments in (7.152) transform at o under a simultaneous site gauge, and each K_m is an invariant tensor under constant SU(N) transformations. The expressions are therefore gauge invariant. Every term of (7.152) selects at most three of the plaquettes or paths arising from its indicated links. Their number costs at most a fixed polynomial in 1+R, and their actual selected paths fit in a connected carrier of size at most C(1+Σ R_i), not the volume of every filling surface together. Joining any two transported slots at o gives a single oriented path between the plaquettes; three slots give the analogous two-path trilinear. Thus these are precisely absolutely summable covariant curvature families of the form used in §7.36, with source offset retained. On the fixed complex q-disc the adjoint transports cost at most exp(C r_* Σ R_i); reduce r_* to absorb this in the available tree decay. Finite polynomial path moments likewise fit by (7.151).

A seam edge whose tree loop winds is at distance at least c n_T from o. For these edges use the covariant holonomy proxy `P_e=Π_{Lie}[(C_e−C_e⁻¹)/2]` with the analytic traceless projection onto the complexified Lie algebra. Near identity it equals `log C_e+O((log C_e)^3)`. In (7.152) replace L_e by P_e and N_e by zero for each such slot. This matches the same ordinary jets through degree three, since there is no linear term of F_o. These terms retain their winding type. On the complex disc their paths still have length O(1+R), and the root exponential gives an extra e^{−c′n_T} for every family with at least one winding edge. Keeping that family explicitly avoids representing harmonic holonomies as local curvature. ∎

Subtracting the constant and (7.152) leaves a physical analytic remainder whose ordinary link-field jets vanish through degree three. Its analytic norm follows from (7.150) and the full complex estimates on the two completions. For example at the fixed radius r_* the physical sizes of the completions are bounded by their kernel norms times O(r_*²+r_*³). The canonical strengths for m=2,3 in (7.151) keep the smaller of the physical and canonical caps. This constructs low curvature kernels for a *new* homogeneous physical birth on the near-identity chart. Incorporating its entire remainder in the next old-domain representation still requires care about localized gauge covariance, rooted phase pairing, and winding/history partners.

### 7.50 The newly born physical quartic tail at its next clean readout

Individual terms produced by the physical-coordinate restrictions in (7.143) need not be gauge invariant. There is nevertheless a single gauge choice for the *complete physical remainder at one source root*. It keeps the entire input in its original analytic disc and recovers the required fourth power carrier by carrier.

**Theorem 7.89 (closure of the homogeneous physical quartic tail).** On the homogeneous near-identity clean chart, let E_o(q) be the actual output in (7.150) after its constant and the two covariant completions (7.152), including the winding partners, have been subtracted. Use a fixed smaller physical radius α>0. It has a decomposition
`E_o(q)=Σ_{X∋o} e_X(q|X),  ord₀ e_X≥4,  Σ_X e^{a|X|} sup_α|e_X|≤A`
with a>0 and A bounded by the physical cap from (7.150)–(7.152). At a subsequent homogeneous regular graph with old spacing t in new current units, multiply by t⁻² and sum the old roots in a bounded current test patch. On the new real target disc of physical size ε one has
`|t⁻² Σ_{o old roots} f_o E_o(log MʲU_k)|≤C_f A α^{-4} ε⁴ t².`   (7.153)
The same tail is an admissible input to (7.148) under the previously specified fixed physical and carrier margins. There is no separate invariance assumption on the e_X.

*Construction of the tail carriers.* The complete scalar and its covariant completions are gauge invariant on the physical orbit. Each of the latter is holomorphic on the fixed reduced link-log ball with exponential carrier norm, by the proof of Theorem 7.88, including the trigonometric holonomy proxy on a winding path. Consequently their difference has the same kind of convergent carrier expansion. At each carrier subtract its raw Taylor polynomial of orders zero through three. The sum of these polynomials vanishes identically as a polynomial in all q, since the first three jets of the complete difference vanish by (7.152). Thus the new carriers still sum to the same *invariant total*. Finite-order multivariate Cauchy bounds on a smaller ball preserve their weighted norm (a fixed polynomial in |X| may be paid with a small decay loss). Each individual new carrier now has valuation at least four on that ball.

*One real gauge for the whole root.* In current-unit coordinates let `MʲU_k=e^{t A_j}` in its recursively gauged homogeneous representative, where `‖A_j‖_{C^{1,α₀}}≤Cε` by Lemma 7.54. The choice of α₀ here is a Hölder exponent, distinct from the core radius α. For fixed old root o choose a smooth cutoff χ on the current torus supported in a small fixed coordinate ball at o and equal to one on a smaller ball. Its support lies inside the injectivity radius, uniformly when the terminal torus contains at least one unit in every direction. In that ball put
`u(x)=exp[χ(x)Σ_μ (x−o)_μ A_{j,μ}(o)]`
and set u=I outside its support. The transformed old links have logarithms q^u on the common small branch. Globally `‖q^u‖∞≤Cε t`, because u has first difference bounded by Cε. In the inner ball,
`|q^u(x,μ)|≤C ε t (|x−o|+t)`.
Indeed in `u(x)e^{tA_{j,μ}(x)}u(x+t e_μ)^{-1}` the leading constant tA_{j,μ}(o) cancels. The field difference uses the Lipschitz bound of A_j. The error in differentiating the exponential of the affine gauge logarithm costs at most `Cε²(|x−o|+t)t`, from its commutator with A_{j,μ}(o) and the single-step Taylor remainder. These inequalities hold also at all intermediate strengths of this gauge. For large t where a link crosses the cutoff patch, the global bound suffices below.

The old support of n current-native-at-birth cubes containing o lies at physical distance at most C n t. If n t is small enough its complete stencils stay in the inner ball and the local bound gives `sup_X |q^u|≤C ε(1+n)t²`. If n t exceeds that fixed threshold, the global bound Cεt implies the identical inequality. At the same time every q^u lies in the global physical α-ball for ε sufficiently small; no large gauge holonomy branch is used. Further, for real inputs gauge invariance of the *sum* gives
`E_o(log MʲU_k)=E_o(q^u)=Σ_X e_X(q^u|X)`.
Neither evaluating different carriers in unrelated gauges nor extending them separately along entire gauge orbits would give this identity. Apply radial Schwarz to the original e_X at q^u. This gives `C a_X α^{-4} ε⁴ (1+n)^4 t^8`, where a_X is its sup norm. The spare old exponential pays the polynomial; the t⁻⁴ root count and t⁻² normalization give (7.153).

For the rough complex localization use the e_X in the unadjusted common near-identity weak field chart. Each input is in its α-ball by the smallness in Lemma 7.77 and the repeated-average estimate. No age gain or single-carrier gauge invariance is needed there. The actual integrated physical scalar is invariant and (7.153) applies on every true real partially activated target. Interpolating the crude t⁻⁶ bound and then applying (7.143), with its quantitative old support margins, gives exactly the p=4 input norm required for (7.148). For this newly born family the actual argument is the old *retained coarse field q*, so there is no ambiguous substitution of an independently extended fine current. An old term intrinsically defined on a different joined fine (U,J)-record still needs its own matching. ∎
