This produces a second-generation quartic physical family with its complete ordinary/compact subtraction, its old tested root, a fixed admissible complex carrier norm and the required positive age. The operation works on the homogeneous near-identity scalar chart. It has not assigned an analytic center or a common gauge to a frozen large-field return.

### 7.51 A pointed moment projection with fixed compact representatives

The quadratic sources produced by (7.152) can have the test at a point different from either curvature slot. The corresponding moment conditions include derivatives of that test. A bounded projection is available without discarding them or quotienting an equation of motion.

**Lemma 7.90 (pointed form of (7.130)).** For a homogeneous translation orbit of old roots, write a quadratic term after translation as
`Σ_{a,b,P,z}K_{abPz} ⟨f(·+tz) F_a,T_P F_b⟩`.
Here z is the recorded source offset in old lattice units. It may include a replicated subcell phase; |z| is included in the path moment. Put h equal to the endpoint displacement of P. On the graph of Theorem 7.61 with smooth f of class C^{2,v}, its complete local rows through dimension six are determined by all moments of the quadratic array in monomials of total degree ≤2 in (z,h), and the one combined cubic polynomial (7.131). If those moments and the combined polynomial vanish, the bound (7.132) holds with `(1+|z|+|P|)^{2+v}` in the quadratic sum, and the analogous test offset in the cubic moment.

*Proof.* Apply (7.130) with X=f(·+tz)F_a and expand the shifted test at its unshifted point. In its constant pair use `f+t z·∇f+(t²/2)(z·∇)^2 f`. In the term with coefficient t h_μ use `f+t z·∇f`, and in the order-two derivative pair and area term use f itself. The errors cost `C_f ε²[t(1+|z|+|P|)]^{2+v}` for short shifts. In particular D_μ of the difference of two shifted test functions costs at most C_f t|z|, not an inverse t. In the area row the third field contributes an additional ε. For shifts or paths reaching beyond the local collar the same bound holds by the longer-path estimate in (7.130) and bounded-volume translated test supports. In the cubic local comparison translating its test by tz costs at most C_f min(1,t|z|). Thus the coefficients of f, ∇f, ∇²f, D^0F, D(fF) and the mixed `(∂f)F DF` pair occur with the announced polynomials. The local area and cubic terms must still be combined before taking the absolute remainder norm. This retains, in particular, the pointed derivative terms in the CD17a pairing of [W, pp. 661–662]. ∎

**Theorem 7.91 (explicit bounded local projection and second-generation low kernels).** In the real and complex near-identity clean scalar class above, after a complete translation/phase-family sum, the vacuum, the quadratic moments through degree two and the complete local cubic center may be filed by a bounded projection with fixed covariant representatives. Its complement has the exact moment cancellations in Lemma 7.90. Its kernel norm obeys
`‖K^{st}‖_{a′}≤C‖K‖_a,  ‖D^{st}‖_{a′}≤C(‖D‖_a+‖K‖_a)`   (7.154)
for fixed a′<a with the stated source/path weights. Winding components remain separately filed. On a later true homogeneous clean readout this stable output again obeys (7.132),(7.149), with the canonical and physical caps (7.151). The construction retains the uncontracted component tensor and all indicated test descendants.

*Proof of the projection.* Treat each component/color tensor separately. Let u=(z,h)∈ℝ⁸. For every input path coefficient at u distribute it to the following fixed finite representative nodes: 0, ±e_i, and e_i+e_j, i<j, in ℤ⁸. Use the weights specified, for any test polynomial P of total degree at most two, by
`P(u)=P(0)+Σ_i u_i [P(e_i)−P(−e_i)]/2`
`+½Σ_i u_i²[P(e_i)+P(−e_i)−2P(0)]`
`+Σ_{i<j}u_i u_j [P(e_i+e_j)−P(e_i)−P(e_j)+P(0)]`.
The identity follows on the monomial basis. Its weights have absolute sum ≤C(1+|u|)². At each output node choose the indicated integer test offset and a fixed coordinate-order nearest-neighbor path with its indicated endpoint, including the empty path. This gives a local compact quadratic kernel K_loc carrying all specified moments, depending linearly only on their values. Fixed finite hypercubic rotations can be averaged if the full input has that symmetry; the same polynomial identities remain exact after averaging. The construction applies equally to fractional subcell test offsets because the reproduced functions are polynomials in real u.

The quadratic representative produces its own area polynomial. Use a local cubic representative with three curvature slots at one site whose invariant trilinear coefficient is the *total* cubic polynomial of (7.131) for the input minus that area polynomial of K_loc. Allow the full finite-dimensional space of invariant trilinear tensors actually present, including the Lie commutator term supplied by a quadratic path. A fixed basis in its image realizes this prescription with bounded coefficients. The resulting K_loc,D_loc have the same pointed moments and total local cubic polynomial as the input; their assignment depends only on those moments. Hence applying it a second time gives the same representatives. Subtract them to define K^{st},D^{st}. Fixed cardinal nodes and a cost of at most C(1+|z|+|P|)² for the quadratic moments and areas prove (7.154). The whole physical analytic quartic tail is as in Theorem 7.89. Subtract the scalar vacuum separately.

The transfer K→D in (7.154) is a real grade distinction. On the canonical graph it is multiplied by three powers of g_k. In particular a quadratic kernel of size `A_j g_j^{-2}` contributes to that canonical cubic row at most `C A_j g_k(g_k/g_j)^2`, the extra factor required by MT45. For the two-norm cap take the minimum of the canonical and fixed physical bounds in (7.151) before this finite transfer. A fixed physical core of radius α≤1 and g_j≤1 allow the quadratic cap to be included in the corresponding cubic cap, with the additional canonical g_j just displayed. Lemma 7.90 and Theorems 7.81–7.84 therefore apply to a later homogeneous clean use of this output.

The phase condition is part of the assertion. For a translation-covariant original sum on a homogeneous torus, translating a complete marked root and its distinguished interaction translates the original integration variables and the chosen source offsets. The normalized measure and the block map are equivariant under current-lattice translations. One can therefore organize the full sum by these actual orbits. Each retained subcell phase contributes its *actual* z and f, with its coefficient weight, before taking its moments above. A single fixed absolute root polymer without its translated partners is not assigned such a cancellation. Nor does this calculation compare fields on opposite sides of a sharp mixed boundary, where (7.136) applies. ∎

This is one concrete finite moment-filing scheme on the homogeneous physical chart. It retains the complete derivative tensor and all source offsets, rather than identifying the invariant derivative sector with a single O(4)-scalar. Exact Wilson equation-of-motion and contact identities still belong to the larger joint source state. No effective-background field identity is substituted for them.

### 7.52 Separating the Gaussian principal row from the actual clean mean

**Lemma 7.92 (the full clean interaction in a marked first difference).** On the homogeneous source-free graph with the spare physical and support margins above, the full difference of the fresh bare fluctuation phase from its extracted Hessian, the scalar measure terms, and the inherited term of (1.33) have a representation by current carriers V_Y. After subtracting each B-independent value (irrelevant inside a covariance), their bounds on the actual selector are
`|V_Y(B)−V_Y(0)|≤C a_Y g_k (1+max_{b∈Y}|B_b|)^3`,
with a rooted exponentially summable a_Y. Use the original unmarked interaction summed over Y in the density.

*Proof.* CMP109 (2.10)–(2.13) extracts the entire constrained quadratic physical phase (including its current term and the exponential gauge). For fixed physical retained field the remaining part with g_k⁻² in front has zero jets through order two in the physical fluctuation z=g_kB, after its constant has been taken out. The scalar measure/Jacobian terms instead are unscaled analytic functions of z with fixed local stencils and a spare disc. The inherited difference is the separate bounded analytic family in CMP116 (1.33)–(1.36). For the bare residual use CMP116 (1.37)–(1.43), where the Wilson residual (1.38) obeys the cubic bound (1.39) and the source treats the remaining fresh terms by the same localization. Multiplying its quadratic-growth expression by g_k² gives a bounded analytic physical function on the larger fixed z-disc. If the chosen localization splits cancelling lower Taylor terms between carriers, subtract from each such physical bare residual its raw Taylor polynomial through degree two on that disc. The sum of the subtracted polynomials is exactly zero on the physical graph by the quadratic extraction just noted. Carrierwise finite-order Cauchy and a small loss of size decay pay this rearrangement. Radial Schwarz then bounds each divided term by `C a_Y g_k^{-2}(g_k max_Y|B|)^3`. For the unscaled nonconstant scalar terms the same argument at order one gives `C a_Y g_k max_Y |B|`, including (1.36). This proves the estimate. Evaluating on the actual graph matters if independently varied current terms have a different lower Taylor identity. The unmarked integral itself is unchanged there.

For (0≤s≤1) multiply its entire original fluctuation interaction by s. The native quadratic/Mayer upper bounds still use the same strict positive reserve; the physical polynomial rearrangement above is needed only to obtain the distinguished tag's small factor. Thus (7.149) applies to the connected derivative along this interpolation, summing all Y with their actual weights. ∎

**Proposition 7.93 (principal clean Gaussian comparison at canonical external size).** For one of the physical rows in (7.149), define P_p(z,q) to be its degree-p homogeneous joint polynomial at the identity on the actual relative physical graph. Let B⁰ be the full centered Gaussian with the true flat exponential-gauge covariance C_B(0). On the external disc `‖q‖≤c g_k`,
`E_{W(q)} R_p(g_kB,q) = E P_p(g_kB⁰,q) + E_{p,rem}(q)`,
`‖E_{p,rem}‖_{root}≤C M_p t^{s′} g_k^{p+1}`.   (7.155)
The fixed physical-disc decomposition keeps the deterministic tag explicitly:
`‖E_{W(q)}R_p(g_kB,q)−R_p(0,q)‖_{root}≤C M_p t^{s′} g_k(d_q+g_k)^{p−1}`   (7.156)
for `‖q‖≤d_q≤cδ_in`. The constants include the appropriate source/test anchors.

*Proof.* First interpolate s in Lemma 7.92. Differentiating the normalized mean gives exactly the covariance with the full interaction. The two-tag bound summed over Y costs `C M_p t^{s′} g_k(d_q+g_k)^p`. At s=0 the original selector is still present. In each scalar carrier of R_p subtract its homogeneous degree-p polynomial using radial Cauchy on its larger fixed physical disc. On the actual real selector at canonical external size the tail is bounded by `C a_X g_k^{p+1}(1+max_X|B|)^{p+1}`. Its normalized integral satisfies the same root bound by the one-tag proof of Lemma 7.82, now with no unmarked interaction. For the remaining polynomial P_p compare the truncated and full Gaussian by the original failed-selector expansion: after subtracting the untruncated log/tag, every surviving connected term contains at least one failed bond. Keep half the joint Gaussian tail there and use the other half for the polynomial in B. This costs `C e^{-cP²} M_p t^{s′}g_k^p` in the rooted norm, where P is the actual canonical threshold and the margins of §7.14 apply. For P=ε₁/g_k this is bounded by the stated error at weak coupling. This comparison extends only the polynomial P_p, not a nonlinear minimizing map outside its physical chart.

The full Gaussian expectation of the polynomial is a finite Wick sum with its actual C_B(q). On the smaller homogeneous graph disc the relative covariance walk and (7.141) are analytic with weighted operator norm uniformly bounded; applying one radial Cauchy bound to their difference from q=0 gives `‖C_B(q)−C_B(0)‖_{exp}≤C d_q`. For its physical-coordinate carrier norm, localize the field arguments of each walk as in Lemmas 7.77, 7.80 and 7.87. The walk's native locality depends on U,J in its actual support; the individual growth factor per support cube from (7.144) is paid by its strict walk margin. The same radial bound holds after summing these carriers. Every replaced covariance in the fixed-degree Wick sum therefore costs O(g_k) on the canonical disc, giving (7.155). Any Gaussian normalization determinant is already included in the centered expectation. The vacuum contractions of P_p are kept on the right hand side.

For (7.156) take the actual proper difference `R_p(g_kB,q)−R_p(0,q)` carrierwise. The segment and the degree-p valuation on a spare physical disc bound it by `C a_X g_k(d_q+g_k)^{p−1}(1+max_X|B|)^p`. The original one-tag conditioning proves (7.156) with the full unmarked interaction. In particular the deterministic term has not been declared a new small activity. On a homogeneous critical hierarchy where nested minimizers agree by uniqueness, it evaluates the old retained field on that same minimizing graph. ∎

A quadratic principal polynomial in (7.155) has the deterministic part and its scalar Gaussian trace. For a cubic invariant principal polynomial the two-fluctuation contraction with one external color slot is zero at flat covariance: it would be a color-invariant linear functional on the simple adjoint representation. This leaves its deterministic principal cubic after Wick averaging. Higher-order or off-flat conditional scalar rows do not follow from that color identity.

### 7.53 The free stable-to-local block on a complete cell sum

**Theorem 7.94 (free alias cancellation with the original averages).** On the periodic homogeneous flat hierarchy of Theorem 7.58, take a translation-covariant complete root orbit and its exact source subcell phase. Let the oriented quadratic carrier have all pointed moments of total degree ≤2 in (z,h) removed as in Lemma 7.90. Its deterministic induced *quadratic* free kernel has zero local quadratic field symbol through total momentum degree four, including the weak source momentum. The remaining Gaussian contraction at this principal degree is its scalar trace. For a pure cubic principal occupation the degree-three local symbol is the transported zero-momentum cubic tensor. If its local tensor in the combined subtraction is the negative of the area tensor of the quadratic kernel, that residual standalone tensor carries the quadratic kernel grade, as in MT45. The assertion uses the homogeneous Bloch symbols or their periodic lifts with separately retained winding partners.

*Proof.* In terminal unit coordinates write p for a small terminal momentum, η for the finest mesh, and `p_l=p+2πl` for its fine aliases in the fine Brillouin zone. The exact gauge-adjusted constraint T from Theorem 7.58 gives a fine multiplier equation
`d*d A=T*λ`, together with `dF=0, F=dA`.
Use the band-limited right inverse from that theorem at the frequency p. Its curvature norm is now ≤`C|p|‖B(p)‖` because it uses only the principal mode and the box/segment denominators are uniformly bounded below. Minimization gives the same bound for F, and testing the multiplier against this right inverse applied to an arbitrary terminal mode yields
`|λ(p)|≤C |p|² |B(p)|.`   (7.157)
The pure gradient freedom is harmless in the curvature equation and λ annihilates coarse gradients.

For the adjoint-average filter denote its alias coefficient by w_l(p). Then `Σ_{l≠0}‖w_l(p)‖²≤C |p|²`. Indeed applying T* to a terminal Fourier mode gives on a unit cell the transverse constant/longitudinal hat interpolation of its coarse values from (7.126). Up to the demodulating phase exp(−ip·x) its difference from the constant principal value is uniformly O(|p|) there. By Parseval the sum of the squares of all nonprincipal alias coefficients has the asserted bound. This argument is componentwise in the link direction. For every nonzero alias its fine derivative symbol ω_l has norm bounded below by a positive constant; this includes aliases near the fine Brillouin edge. Fourier Hodge applied to the multiplier equation gives
`Σ_{l≠0}(1+|ω_l|²)|F_l|²≤C |p|⁶ |B(p)|².`   (7.158)
The principal curvature itself is O(|p| |B|). Averaging forward to any old mesh τ gives its exact area average as in Theorem 7.58. The fine principal component stays principal, and the ℓ² contraction (also with one derivative by its alias classes) shows that the nonprincipal old curvatures still satisfy (7.158).

In the principal/principal term of the pointed quadratic form the kernel factor is `Σ_{P,z}K_{Pz} exp[iτ(k·z+p′·h)]`, up to consistent endpoint phases, where k is the source momentum and p,p′ are the two external field momenta. Complete lower moment removal gives a bound `C (τ(|k|+|p′|))^{2+v}‖K‖_{2+v}`. Plaquette placement or a fixed fine test phase can be included in z,h before taking these moments. The two principal curvature factors cost O(|p| |p′|). Hence there is no term of degree ≤4 in this joint symbol. Counting the entire old-root cell for a plane-wave sampled at its recorded subcell locations imposes total alias zero modulo the old grid. At small external momenta a nonprincipal leg cannot then pair with a principal leg. The opposite nonprincipal legs contribute at most `C |p|³|p′|³` by (7.158), Cauchy–Schwarz in the alias index and the path moment norm. If a test convention holds the coarse sample constant across a cell, its nonprincipal test alias vector has ℓ² norm O(|k|), by the same demodulation/Parseval argument. A term with exactly one nonprincipal field leg then has degree at least five; the exact sample convention must be kept. A single unpaired old root does not obey this alias identity.

For a cubic principal form, three principal curvatures already give total degree three. Therefore only its zero-momentum cubic tensor contributes at this order. Once a nonprincipal curvature occurs, its ℓ² valuation is at least three; full alias pairing with the other factors cannot lower that degree. At fixed finite cutoff this also follows by taking the finite Bloch sum first and inspecting its Taylor orders. The moment removal in Theorem 7.91 concerns the sum with the area term; a separate vanishing cubic projection is not inferred. Finally, the Wick contraction of the quadratic part gives only a B-independent scalar, whereas an invariant cubic contraction to a color vector vanishes as after (7.156). ∎

For finite tori the continuously continued symbol used for a local moment is the Bloch symbol of the lifted homogeneous rule, not an arbitrary interpolation of discrete samples. Periodized summable kernels agree on the actual lattice momenta; paths winding around the chosen cut carry the explicit winding remainder of Theorem 7.88. Equation (7.158) controls the entire normalized squared cell sum and does not require an absolute sum of the fine alias amplitudes.

### 7.54 The actual frustration at birth is a finite curvature kernel plus a quartic tail

**Proposition 7.95 (the bare H insertion on its clean physical chart).** Use the complete oriented staples at bond b in T3 §4.60. For one difference of two matchings write c_α=(+1,+1,−1,−1), take the four corresponding parallel staples w_α with the endpoints of u=U_b, and put `X_α=log(w_α u⁻¹)` on the small plaquette chart. Then the actual local source has the physical decomposition
`h_b=(τβ/3)Σ_{i<j} ‖Σ_{α∈ij} c_α X_α‖² + R_{b,≥4},   |R_{b,≥4}|≤C_N β(max_α‖X_α‖)^4.`   (7.159)
The squared norm uses its trace-bilinear holomorphic continuation. R is a genuinely analytic fixed-stencil tail with zero curvature jets through order three. The first term is an explicit covariant quadratic kernel on paths of uniformly bounded length. Its leading dimension-six derivative-curvature family must be retained before using the stable estimate.

*Proof.* On the real group multiply the tangent force by u⁻¹ to put it in the common Lie space at the initial bond endpoint. Projection of `exp X−I` onto the traceless anti-Hermitian subspace gives `Π_{traceless}[(exp X−exp(−X))/2]=X+O_N(‖X‖³)`. The contraction of the differences of the two matching forces then gives the first term in (7.159); the cross term with the cubic correction and all higher terms begin at degree four. The local bounds follow from the matrix power series on a fixed branch neighborhood. Equivalently T3's exact compact split gives a finite signed combination of loops of length at most six minus a globally nonnegative normal projection. For the loop part the potential cubic trace from the product of its linear anti-Hermitian and quadratic Hermitian slots cancels by cyclicity. The normal projection starts quartically by the determinant and unitarity identities of T3. The holomorphic continuation uses inverses and the traceless trace contraction. All equality statements extend from the real near-identity chart by analyticity. T3, §4.60.

For a given transverse plane, the logarithms of its two oppositely based plaquettes are the oriented old curvature at x and the negative of that at the neighbor transported by the one old edge back to x. Their sum is a covariant single-step difference (with the sign fixed by the orientation of b). Thus for two matching planes the inner vector in (7.159) is a difference of two such directional curvature differences. Its squared sum has no constant or first total derivative moment in the two curvature legs; each leg carries one difference. Its second moment gives the directional derivative-curvature tensor, including the cross-plane piece. This is an all-component assertion; it does not replace the directional current tensor by the full Wilson equation of motion. The output from this finite family admits the explicit moment filing of Theorem 7.91, keeping its nonzero local center.

The tail R_{b,≥4} is gauge invariant and depends only on the finite incident plaquettes. It verifies the old physical analytic ball of Theorems 7.68 and 7.84 with grade d=2 and fixed α; a fixed factor α² can be included in its declared A_b to match the MT41 notation. At an old scale j its β_j prefactor is C g_j⁻². Hence its canonical quartic complex attachment on the homogeneous chart has size `C t^{s′} g_k³ (g_k/g_j)²` before fixed radius constants, from (7.148): one fresh g_k, four current canonical field factors, and the original g_j⁻². The stable part of the explicit quadratic kernel applies to (7.147) after its dimension-six projection and all pointed descendants have been filed. This verifies the actual bare-field kernel and tail data for this insertion; the local center itself is not assigned the stable age contraction. ∎

On arbitrary compact real fields the unexpanded normal term in T3's split has the stronger literal bound `0≤N_b≤C_N β Σ_{p∋b}s_p²`. When its complete stencil lies on a charged native record with a comparable Wilson energy coefficient, this fits the fixed-moment retained-mark estimate of Proposition 7.40. Transport of the whole finite Wilson-loop difference across a sharp branch boundary still needs the actual common coefficient or its flux partner, as shown by (7.136) and T2's outer-boundary example.

### 7.55 A normalized rare estimate for physical fine-plaquette births

A different-denominator majorant cannot generally be divided by a small history mass. On the positive physical Wilson disintegration one can instead bound the normalized probability of an entire class of original fine-plaquette failures, and then integrate every subsequent conditional mean together with its true mass.

**Proposition 7.96 (P/L on the even Wilson tiling).** Assume the even tiling in T3 §4.22 by closed fine cubes of fixed side ℓ, and the actual partition ratio bound `log[Z(β/2)/Z(β)]≤C V` of T3 §4.11, V the number of fine sites. For a specified set S of physical fine plaquettes let
`E_S={β s_p≥u for every p∈S}`.
There are constants c>0 and C₀ depending only on the fixed tiling, group and ratio bound such that
`P_β(E_S)≤exp[−c |S| (u−C₀)]`   (7.160)
for u≥C₀. This is a bound under the normalized original Wilson law.

*Proof.* Every fine plaquette belongs to at least one closed tiling cube, and there are at most D_ℓ fine plaquettes assigned to any one cube. Keep one demanded plaquette from each occupied assigned cube, hence at least |S|/D_ℓ distinct-cube indicators. For one such indicator disseminate its reflected copies into every cube as in the chessboard inequality. If all copies occur, the total physical energy obeys `β S_W≥M u/D′_ℓ`: there are M tiling cubes and no copied plaquette can be shared by more than D′_ℓ cubes. Here S_W denotes the Wilson action, to distinguish it from the set S. Therefore its normalized probability is at most
`exp[−M u/(2D′_ℓ)] Z(β/2)/Z(β)`.
Since V/M=ℓ⁴ is fixed, its M-th root is bounded by `exp(−c₁u+C₁)`. Apply the site-reflection chessboard inequality to the selected distinct-cube indicators and multiply these bounds. This proves (7.160), including arbitrary plaquette orientations after reflection. T3, §§4.11 and 4.22. ∎

**Corollary 7.97 (conditional saved physical mean and innovation).** Let Y be a product of a fixed number of complete original local marks whose L^{2p} norm on this Wilson law is bounded by M_p, p>1. The local ordinary and frustration marks have such finite-order bounds by T3 §4.22. Take any positive physical downstream disintegration and let `ℋ` include the recorded event E_S and any of its retained exterior/history data. Then
`E[1_{E_S} (|E[Y|ℋ]|² + E[|Y−E[Y|ℋ]|²|ℋ])] ≤ M_p² exp[−(1−1/p)c|S|(u−C₀)].`   (7.161)

*Proof.* Conditional orthogonality makes the left side exactly `E[1_{E_S}|Y|²]`, including a mean depending only on the exterior history. Hölder and (7.160) prove the estimate. For products of distinct fixed source marks use the same Hölder estimate on their actual joint law; no independence is assumed. Additional stages of positive conditional expectation satisfy the same bound by the tower identity. There is one normalized event probability, with the indicated reserve fraction, irrespective of the number of subsequent conditionings. ∎

A primitive failure `‖I−U_p‖_{HS}≥c g₀ p₀(g₀)` has u comparable to p₀(g₀)² because `‖I−U_p‖_{HS}²=2s_p` and β=2N/g₀². Thus (7.161) supplies a genuine normalized physical birth bank for any branch known to imply those specified fine failures. The operation is carried out before signed Mayer/R resummation. It does not bound the conditional mean at each fixed pin, or identify failures defined only through a re-averaged coarse constraint with original fine-plaquette events. Such substitutions would require further evidence.

### 7.56 Fixed blocks of clean steps and the physical core radius

Applying (7.143) at every stage on a smaller disc would progressively reduce the old physical core. A fixed block of h original clean integrations permits a different choice. For a birth no later than the entrance to that block, even the most recent old field has scale ratio at most L⁻ʰ relative to the terminal graph. This restores the analytic margin for the *source readout* under explicit fixed choices. The relative baseline, including its gauge, must be common for all h steps.

**Lemma 7.98 (common relative chart on a homogeneous block).** Put N=k+h, t=L^{j−N} for j≤k, and take the original small external terminal field W(q). There is a source-only representation of its actual invariant old readout on the h-step clean physical tower such that the old raw argument in that representation is `v_j(q,Z)`, with Z the h physical independent fluctuations, and
`v_j(q,0)=log[Mʲ U_*(q)],  U_*(q)=U_N^{Landau}(q),`
`‖v_j(q,0)‖_{κ,loc}≤C_κ t‖q‖,   ‖v_j(q,Z)−v_j(q,0)‖_{κ,loc}≤C_{h,κ} max_i ‖Z_i‖.`   (7.162)
The local norm is the weighted current-carrier norm for the vector of bonds in one old cube, using the terminal-block grid and a fixed smaller homogeneous analytic chart. The first constant is independent of h,j,k. The second is finite for fixed h and independent of k. Take all constituent native charts and walks with the spare margins used for the relative homogeneous map in (1.17)–(1.21). This statement concerns gauge-invariant insertions on the physical tower; a gauge-sensitive entry in an independently specified axial frame is different.

*Exact representative at the origin.* Work in terminal units and set `V̄_i=MⁱU_*`, for every scale i in the block and also for the old scale j. By nesting, `U_*` is on the regular minimizing orbit of each homogeneous constraint with target V̄_i. One may replace the top prescribed field by the gauge-equivalent `V̄_N` in a conditional invariant scalar as in Lemma 7.79. Suppose the upper target in an intermediate conditional is `exp(i b)V̄_{i+1}`. Use the relative Landau minimizer about the *known* critical background U_* from CMP102 (172)–(181), denoted U^{rel}_{i+1}(b;U_*). It equals U_* at b=0. For real b its top average is in the same gauge orbit as the prescribed upper target. One can integrate the lower invariant conditional scalar at this representative since the original map, denominator, Haar and selector transform together. Form `V=Mⁱ U^{rel}_{i+1}(b;U_*)`. At this current blocking step let `a_i(b)` be the based site gauge equal to its averaged contour from the block center to each site (inverse under the opposite orientation). Then `V^{a_i(b)}` has G=0 and is the actual soft-gauge saddle at the corresponding upper target. Apply the original selected-corridor map in its canonical B_i coordinates there, obtaining `V′ V^{a_i(b)}` with `V′=exp(i[C Z_i−h_i D(C Z_i)])`; here h_i in the last expression denotes the native selected-bond operator. For the next lower invariant conditional use the gauge-equivalent target
`(V′ V^{a_i(b)})^{a_i(0)^{-1}}`.
Precisely at b=0,Z_i=0 this is V̄_i, not merely an unspecified representative of its orbit. This construction is iterated from top to bottom using normalized conditional kernels. Each use of a gauge-equivalent upper target is pointwise in the already integrated outer coordinates. At the bottom evaluate `Mʲ U^{rel}_{k}(b_k;U_*)`. Its complete invariant scalar equals the original one for real variables. Keeping the same real integration coordinates gives the associated holomorphic continuation. No transformation satisfying an unverified pointwise replacement for the condition (124) is differentiated.

*Connected analytic bounds.* Lemma 7.77 gives the single terminal U_* on fixed patches with norm C_κ‖q‖ in its homogeneous value and first-difference norms. The raw j-fold average on such a patch costs `C_κ t‖q‖`: (7.117) gives the gauged link logarithm of this size and each undoing endpoint frame at level l<j has size at most `C τ_l‖q‖`, with `Σ_{l<j}τ_l≤t/(L−1)`. The combined collar has terminal width O(t), and Banach polarization on the patch gives the same bounds in the weighted source representation. This proves the first bound in (7.162) without composing h terminal minimizing maps.

For the variations keep this same U_* as the external background of every relative map. The weak-map equation (1.17) has zero relative field at zero relative input, even when its propagator walls are weakened. The original extended small (U,J) domain in (1.18)–(1.21) permits this source localization about U_* and its current. For a constituent relative scale, those external variables in its own units have size bounded by a fixed multiple of the terminal native norm: the potential and current rescale by τ_i and τ_i³ respectively. The exponential support bounds after substitution follow by local smooth patch decomposition and Lemma 7.80, as in Lemmas 7.77 and 7.87. The current contour gauges a_i(b),a_i(0) and their inverses use fixed current stencils. Relative differences of these operations vanish at b=0, independently of the weakened-map values. Their holomorphic boundedness and the segment estimate therefore bound each new deviation by a fixed multiple of the previous deviation plus `C‖Z_i‖`. Grouping the h original grids in a common terminal grid costs only a finite factor depending on h,L,M. For clarity a field norm on all slots of one terminal cube may be bounded by summing its native patch norms; there are at most `C L^{4h}` such patches at a constituent scale. This factor belongs to C_{h,κ}, not to the direct all-zero endpoint bound. For finitely many compositions choose the intermediate substitution radii so the per-cube factors in (7.144) consume less than a prescribed total spare decay. Smallness of q and the internal radii can be imposed after h is chosen, within the larger original *unmarked* charts. Induction over these finitely many relative maps gives the deviation estimate, and the same calculation bounds the bottom log v_j. All weak functions here are auxiliary source localizations; only their physical endpoints are used in the orbit identities. ∎

**Corollary 7.99 (resetting the source domain at block boundaries).** Fix an old clean core and a desired new core with the *same* radius α and weight a, and fix the finite interpolation/polarization slack needed for (7.143). Let D be the fixed enlargement of the external radius required for the improved real-to-complex and Cauchy restrictions. Choose the single-map walk parameters, then take h large enough that
`C_κ D L^{-h}<1/(8e)`, and `C_{
m cover}(κ+log B_d)L^{-h}<a/4`.
The covering constant measures an old connected path in terminal localization cubes and is independent of h. At every block from k to k+h and every j≤k, choose the uniform old/new α sufficiently small to fit all the *unmarked* intermediate charts, and a uniform physical internal cutoff ε₁ sufficiently small that `C_{h,κ} ε₁<α/(8e)`. Then the old readout lies inside its original α-core with the spare radius needed for carrier substitution, even while the terminal field ranges over Dα. The sum over old long carriers has the needed fixed spare decay. Both choices are independent of the number of blocks.

*Proof.* Apply (7.162) on that enlarged terminal disc. For the rough old localization a connected old carrier of n cubes is covered by at most `C(1+n L^{j−k−h})` terminal cubes; traverse its connected old cell path as in Theorem 7.84. The displayed inequalities pay the geometric and support costs. The factors involving h in the finite relative deviations multiply ε₁; they do not multiply the direct old endpoint. Choose α and then ε₁ as stated. This gives the same α for the next block, with the Cauchy reductions already included in D. At the finitely many initial or terminal incomplete steps one may use the finite-step smaller chart or end at an integral number of blocks. ∎

The last corollary proves the domain budget for the old physical source graph. The original conditional density on all h fields also contains background-dependent Gaussian determinants and conditional partition functions. They must be included to obtain a uniform block formation estimate; the source budget alone does not estimate them.

### 7.57 Normalized density on a fixed clean block

An h-step Markov product introduces one scalar normalization at every upper conditional field. Keeping these factors makes the block comparison compatible with the actual measure.

**Lemma 7.100 (exact density and localization for the clean block).** Use the representative and physical source/domain margins in §§7.55–7.56, with h fixed. Let C_i(Z_{>i},q) denote the positive-gauge Gaussian covariance of the i-th normalized conditional, in its computational coordinates, and put H_i=C_i⁻¹. Let L_i(Z_{>i},q) be the log of its normalized-Gaussian integral of the original selector times exp V_i. Write the superscript 0 for the value at Z_{>i}=0 at the same q. In the common real B coordinates the product of all h normalized conditionals has, up to a q-dependent scalar, density
`Π_i dμ_{C_i^0}(B_i) χ_i(B_i) · exp[Σ_i (V_i −½⟨B_i,(H_i−H_i^0)B_i⟩ +½Tr log[H_i(H_i^0)⁻¹]−(L_i−L_i^0))].`   (7.163)
In V_i one can further subtract its value at all B=0, changing only that same scalar. The expression is first a real identity; in the smaller common complex chart it defines the holomorphic normalized integral. The signs of the determinant and normalized-log terms are part of (7.163).

*Proof of the identity.* Write out each original `dμ_{C_i} χ_i e^{V_i}/exp L_i` in the coordinates of Lemma 7.98. The centered Gaussian density in those variables is proportional to `det(H_i)^{1/2}exp(−½B_iᵀH_iB_i)`. Dividing by the corresponding reference at Z_{>i}=0 gives the quadratic and positive log-determinant terms in (7.163); multiplying by exp(−L_i) gives the displayed negative scalar difference. All factors independent of B cancel in the normalized output. Changing current representatives inside this calculation uses a real adjoint transformation on the full independent field at that conditional, including its selector. Each conditional is integrated in its original order. Pointwise invariance of the remaining inner scalar justifies the gauge-orbit choice at each step even if the upper target frame varies with the outer fields. Thus this computes the actual tower for invariant scalar tags.

*The common-grid bounds.* We specify the parameter margin for this block. Require the one-species native exponents in their own grids to have enough slack for the fixed polymer counting on the final coarsening, for the fixed enlargements of conditioning domains, and for the substitutions of §7.56. Grouping to a coarser grid costs at most a fixed enlargement per original connected support; on an arbitrarily finer constituent grid the diameter in final units decreases. In an h-block the number V_h of real coordinates of all species in one final localization cube is at most `C h (M L^h)^4 dim G`. Take the positive quadratic comparison slack `α₅ V_h` below the determinant budget of CMP116 (2.38), and its operator-norm counterpart below the uniform spectral margin. These are fixed finite restrictions after h is chosen.

Here is the source-free localization giving those small coefficients. In the relative construction every regular background differs from its own all-zero baseline by analytic carriers of norm O(C_h‖Z‖). The background at the baseline is the single homogeneous graph of U_* with its bounded endpoint rotations. The covariance walks of CMP99 Theorem 3.15, the soft correction (7.141), and smooth-patch substitution as in Lemma 7.87 give an absolute carrier expansion of C_i in these data. Their size differs from C_i^0 by O(C_h‖Z‖), since the difference vanishes at zero internal fields. For the inverse, first use the flat inverse's exponential matrix bound in Theorem 7.74, representing an entry on any fixed connecting path. The corresponding size weight is allowed by choosing the native localization cubes large enough relative to that exponential rate. The analytic covariance differs from the identity-background covariance by O(C_h(‖q‖+‖Z‖)) in this weighted norm; the inverse Neumann series about the flat *matrix* therefore converges on the small chosen chart. It gives the same O(C_h‖Z‖) bound for H_i−H_i^0. The norm here sums the two fluctuation slots and includes their carrier. The determinant term in (7.163) now expands by convergent connected trace cycles in `(H_i−H_i^0)C_i^0`; it is a sum of scalar carriers vanishing at Z=0 and bounded by C_h‖Z‖. This argument only uses an exponential matrix bound at flat background, without a finite-range assumption.

For L_i use the actual unmarked localized scalar of CMP116 (2.41) evaluated on the relative homogeneous graph, on its native field/current chart. Its difference from its own baseline again vanishes at Z_{>i}=0; the smooth patch substitution and (7.144) give localized analytic coefficients with scalar bound C_h‖Z‖. The original V_i split into inherited bounded scalars, finite-measure factors, and fresh phase terms of cubic physical valuation as in Lemma 7.92. The terms multiplying B_i twice in (7.163) now have coefficient norm O(C_h ε₁) after the physical selector, including the native bare third-order term written with its two B_i factors. The remaining normalized scalar changes have size O(C_h ε₁). If a proper difference was first localized as a difference of two expansions, subtract each carrier's common zero-input value, since their total difference at zero vanishes. Choose ε₁ and the small full q chart inside the fixed margins above. This verifies the required smallness simultaneously with (7.162). On the actual selector `Z_i=g_i B_i` every tagged proper scalar term is bounded by its coefficient times `C_h g_{max}(1+max |B_i|)^3`: apply radial Schwarz to its vanishing Z-dependence, including in a quadratic coefficient multiplying B_i twice. For the inherited/fresh V_i use the segment and cubic bounds of Lemma 7.92, with scalar values at the all-zero upper background subtracted. Here `g_{max}=max_{k≤i<N}g_i`.

Finally (7.163) has a direct sum of h native centered references. In CMP116 (2.3)–(2.8) condition each species on its own interior bonds in the common union of blocks, whiten only its exterior, and use the same operator weakening as in the single-species proof. The joint determinant cancellation is a product over h; its per-cube expense is bounded using V_h α₅. Finitely many cross-species analytic interaction terms share the same interior variables and have the small scalar/quadratic estimates just proved. Component factorization uses connected supports of the coarsening; the Mayer and failed-selector resummation then has exactly the positive comparison and cluster bounds used for two species in Theorem 7.37. This establishes the finite-block extension on its stated common margins. ∎

**Theorem 7.101 (complex stable innovation for a block of original clean steps).** Use Lemmas 7.98 and 7.100, take `g=g_N` with g_max≤C_h g, and a whole original old invariant row p=2,3,4. Use the same radius α at both block boundaries as in Corollary 7.99 and all its source/kernel hypotheses. Write T_h R_p(q) for its normalized mean through the h-step block and `D_h R_p(q)=R_p(q,0)` for the exact deterministic tag on the direct graph. Write c_p for the B-independent flat Gaussian contraction of the degree-p joint polynomial if p=2, and set c_p=0 if p=3. Then on a canonical external disc of size c g the physical rooted bounds are
`‖T_h R_p−D_h R_p−c_p‖≤C_h M_p t^{s′}g^{p+1}  (p=2,3)`,
`‖T_h R₄−D_h R₄‖≤C_h M₄ t^{s′} g^4.`   (7.164)
On a fixed physical disc of size d≤α the proper difference has the bounds
`‖T_h R_p−D_h R_p‖≤C_h M_p t^{s′} g(d+g)^{p−1}.`   (7.165)
The complete p=2 vacuum contraction is filed separately. All results concern the homogeneous invariant scalar chart and the actual averaged upper representative. Lower families whose coefficients are filed when constructing this stable row must still be evolved.

*Proof.* On the true graph with internal fields turned on, the lower reconstruction is U_k of the actual perturbed lower constraint, so its regularity in units of the entrance scale follows from the same original homogeneous minimum estimates. Its crude constants may depend on h. Using terminal instead of entrance units changes the old root count, dimension-six factor, path lengths and regularity constants only by fixed powers of L^h. Hence (7.132) and (7.153) give the improved real old-age estimate, taking the terminal smallness and the internal physical radius within the stated native charts. For a true arbitrary partial activation of the cube inputs, use that same actual tower. For the rough estimate use the relative maps of Lemma 7.98. Their deviations are bounded by C_h ε₁ and their single all-zero endpoint is bounded by C_κ t Dα. Corollary 7.99 pays both the old analytic radius and the old support cost. The proofs of (7.143),(7.145),(7.148) therefore give the same rooted valuation-p representation in all h internal and terminal physical inputs on the common block. Input cube variables are grouped in the terminal grid. The enlarged terminal q-disc Dα supplies the interpolation and Cauchy reductions, leaving α at output; the internal cutoff may be chosen with its own strict slack after h.

Apply the polynomial tag estimate of Lemma 7.82 to the joint law (7.163). Interpolating its entire small interaction by a scalar in [0,1] retains the same positive comparison; its marked derivative has the g_max times cubic polynomial bound in Lemma 7.100. Thus replacing the joint interacting reference by its truncated Gaussian costs `C_h M_p t^{s′}g(d+g)^p`. As in (7.155), on the canonical ball replace R_p by its joint homogeneous degree-p polynomial, remove the original h selectors *only for this polynomial* using their failed-selector estimates, then replace all C_i^0(q) by C_i^0(0). The first error is `C_h M_p t^{s′}g^{p+1}`; the others have the same or smaller bound, including `exp(−c min_i (ε₁/g_i)^2)`. The flat reference is a direct sum in the h species, with each canonical physical factor g_i retained. Wick averaging subtracts the deterministic polynomial value, leaves only a scalar trace for p=2, and vanishes for p=3 by the color argument following (7.156). At p=4 its finite remaining polynomial is bounded by `C_h M₄ t^{s′}g^4`, with no false extra g. The deterministic polynomial approximates D_h R_p with the same Taylor error. This proves (7.164). For (7.165), apply the one-tag estimate directly to the internal proper difference; its segment factor g_max and remaining p−1 powers give the bound as in (7.156). The deterministic tag remains the original earlier tag on the next block by nested critical-orbit uniqueness. ∎

For p=4 with old declared degree d=2 or 3, `M₄=A_j α^{d−4}g_j^{-d}`. The coefficient in (7.164) has at least one extra g relative to `A_j(g/g_j)^d`, so it fits the stable innovation budget. The p=2 trace in (7.164) lacks a fresh g; it belongs in the scalar/pointed ledger instead of the stable recurrence.

### 7.58 Summation of histories staying in the homogeneous stable sector

**Theorem 7.102 (homogeneous stable-sector Green bound, P/L on the preceding parameter margins).** Choose the fixed block length h and the homogeneous parameter margins of §§7.56–7.57, and let the declared canonical source grade be d=2 or 3. At every block boundary file the vacuum, lower, local quadratic/cubic and winding terms separately by (7.152)–(7.154). Consider the linear response histories of a completed physical stable birth that use the stable output at every subsequent innovation; its deterministic tag is kept at its original age until the next innovation. On the homogeneous small-field tower, the sum of these histories from an old boundary birth j₀ to N obeys
`A_{N←j₀}^{stable,new}≤C_h g_N (g_N/g_{j₀})^d L^{-s₂(N−j₀)} A_{j₀}  (N>j₀)`   (7.166)
for a fixed s₂>0, uniformly in the number of blocks and cutoff on the stated weak trajectory. This bounds the sector in which those filed families do not re-enter; it is not the full coupled source transfer.

*One-block norm.* Use the intersection grade `A_j` consisting of the fixed physical sup weighted by `(g_j/α)^d`, the two covariant kernel norms weighted by g_j²,g_j³, and the quartic physical tail with its declared fourth-order radius. The quadratic/cubic caps can be taken as `A_j min(g_j^{-p},α^{d−p}g_j^{-d})`. Let `g=g_N`, `t=L^{j−N}`. At the canonical output disc the p=2 innovation in (7.164) has size `C M₂g³t^{s′}`, the p=3 innovation has size `C M₃ g⁴t^{s′}`, and the p=4 row is `C M₄g⁴t^{s′}`. With its known cap this last row supplies g^{4−d}, at least one fresh g for d≤3. The other two rows obey `C_h g(g/g_j)^d A_j t^{s′}`: for d=3 use the canonical p=2 bound and the weak-trajectory comparison of the ratios; for d=2 the physical p=3 cap gives the extra g/α. On the weak decreasing-in-inverse-coupling range the ratio g/g_j≥1. If only a uniform drift estimate is available, a fixed power of the relative ratio or its inverse can instead be paid by reducing the positive age exponent, provided the two-sided relative drift is at most polynomial in N−j. This alternative is not a payment for an absolute inverse power of an old coupling.

On the fixed physical output disc, multiply (7.165) by `(g/α)^d` and use the physical cap `M_p≤A_j α^{d−p}g_j^{-d}`, including p=4. The bound is again `C_{h,α}g(g/g_j)^d A_j t^{s′}`. Subtracting the p=2 vacuum c_p also respects this physical cap, because it is O(M₂g²t^{s′}) and gains g² at fixed α. Its canonical scalar value is filed without a fresh-g assertion. Fixed canonical Cauchy extraction gives the weighted quadratic/cubic kernel cap on the next stable output. The same physical Cauchy estimate gives the additional physical cap in (7.151), and the common-gauge proof of Theorem 7.89 bounds the new quartic remainder at its later readout. The projection (7.154) transfers the area term with its actual grade. Spend fixed margins in the preceding raw carrier weights for the output path surgery and desired path moments, and fixed extra radius in D for the finite derivative Cauchy circles. The requirements in Corollary 7.99 are imposed for these *pre-extraction* margins. Consequently the post-extraction norm is the same a,α at every boundary, not a geometric sequence of smaller norms. Thus one stable innovation at N from a deterministic tag of birth j has output
`A_{N←j}≤C_h g_N (g_N/g_j)^d L^{-s₁(N−j)} A_j`   (7.167)
for some fixed s₁>0. All constants can be chosen for the same h; subsequently require ḡ small enough for the following scalar renewal. Here ḡ denotes the upper bound on the running g_j.

*Exact stable bookkeeping and convolution.* The difference decomposition of a normalized mean into D_h R plus its innovation is linear and exact. At each step retain the deterministic term as the original old tag evaluated on the next minimizing graph; nested critical-orbit uniqueness gives the common direct endpoint. File its full projected partners as prescribed, and iterate the innovations that remain in the stable sector. Each path with a specified last stable innovation at N has a unique preceding birth j; between them its deterministic tag has not been reclassified as a new activity. Consequently (7.167) bounds this part of the exact linear expansion by the ordered convolution over block boundaries. Let s₂<s₁. Multiplying each boundary norm by `L^{s₂(N−j₀)}(g_{j₀}/g_N)^d` makes the coupling ratios telescope. The convolution kernel then has row sum at most
`C_h ḡ L^{−(s₁−s₂)h}/[1−L^{−(s₁−s₂)h}]`.
Take this below 1/2. The nonnegative Neumann series is bounded by two times the initial norm; for N>j₀ the final innovation retains its explicit g_N, giving (7.166). The separately propagated single unbroken deterministic tag is the original readout and is not counted as a new birth. This proves the result. ∎

The proof uses no bound for a lower-dimensional operator re-entering the stable sector through a later step. Those paths, the complete multi-source/contact state, large-field returns and genuine mixed walls need their own estimates. The scalar trace, all local projected coefficients, and the sharp-boundary flux are recorded rather than discarded from the full physical identity.

### 7.59 A lower bound for the bare action source's second derivative

The physical action source and its scalar contact subtraction must also be distinguished. There is a direct full-Wilson lower bound with no small-field approximation.

**Proposition 7.103 (P on the weak even-torus trajectory).** Let n be even, V=n⁴, and assume the full Wilson first-moment bound `E_β s_p≤C/β` used in T3 §4.11. With d_G=dim SU(N),
`liminf_{β→∞} (β²/V) Var_β(S) ≥ d_G/4.`   (7.168)
Consequently the unrenormalized constant-test insertion S/N in (1.1) has variance growing at least as `c n⁴/β²` on the stated weak trajectory. A contact-renormalized second derivative and a zero-free radius are different assertions.

*Proof.* Select all positively oriented direction-one links whose three transverse site coordinates have even sum. There are V/2 of them and no elementary plaquette contains two selected links: the two parallel direction-one links of any plaquette are one transverse lattice step apart. Conditioning on all other links makes the selected variables independent. Their conditional one-link actions are
`φ_b(u)=Σ_{i=1}^6 [N−ReTr(u w_i⁻¹)]`,
where all six staples w_i are fixed exterior SU(N) elements joining the endpoints of b. The action is the sum of these functions plus an exterior constant. Hence total variance gives
`Var(S)≥Σ_{b selected} E Var(φ_b | exterior)`.

The event that all staples lie within a fixed small δ of w₁ is exterior-measurable. It has probability (1−O(1/(βδ²))), since `‖w_i−U_b‖_{HS}²=2s_{p_i}` for the appropriate orientation and the given plaquette first moment applies to each. On that good compact parameter set the one-link phase has a unique minimum with a uniformly positive Hessian. Indeed after multiplication by w₁⁻¹ the phase is a C³-small perturbation of `6(N−ReTr u)` near identity, whose Lie algebra Hessian is positive definite. The latter has a unique global minimum and a fixed positive gap outside a small identity neighborhood by compactness. The implicit function theorem and the gap persist uniformly for small δ.

For completeness, in exponential coordinates about its minimum write `u=u_* exp(X/√β)`. The Haar Jacobian is smooth and positive, and `β(φ_b−min φ_b)=½⟨X,H_bX⟩+O(β^{-1/2}|X|³)` on bounded X, uniformly over the good parameter set and with `cI≤H_b≤CI`. An inner fixed chart has uniform Gaussian domination by its quadratic lower bound; the complement has an exponential tail by the uniform gap. Integration, also with the first two powers of the scaled phase, therefore gives variance tending uniformly to that of `½⟨X,H_bX⟩` for `X∼N(0,H_b^{-1})`, namely d_G/2. On the bad exterior the variance is still nonnegative. Summing V/2 contributions proves (7.168). ∎

For fixed physical volume n⁴ is proportional to a⁻⁴ and β grows logarithmically on the admitted weak scaling. Thus a statement of cutoff-uniform *bare* first and second source coefficients for every constant Tr F² direction requires clarification; its bare second coefficient already fails in (7.168). A quadratic scalar contact can alter this zero-source derivative. In contrast a scalar exponential cannot alter the locations of the physical H zeros in Proposition 7.86.

### 7.60 The constant physical action at any homogeneous clean step

The scalar coupling direction has a special determinant cancellation. It leaves a summable field-dependent error even when the physical coefficient is shifted at every clean scale.

**Theorem 7.104 (summable physical action remainder, P/L on the homogeneous clean chart).** Let S_i(V)=S(U_i(V)) be the bare minimizing Wilson action in its physical normalization, β_i its physical coefficient in the i-th clean kernel, and retain all original gauge, selector and measure factors. For a bounded complex additive Wilson coefficient v on that conditional kernel,
`E_{V|W} exp[−v S_i(V)] = exp[−v S_{i+1}(W)] (1+v/β_i)^{-d_{phys,i}/2} exp D_i(W,v)`,
`‖D_i(·,v)‖_{root}≤C |v| g_i⁴ p_i²,   p_i=D log(1/g_i).`   (7.169)
The functions D_i are gauge invariant and holomorphic on the original homogeneous physical source chart, with native connected localization. The constants and a fixed v-disc are independent of i and the number of sites on the stated weak native parameter range. The physical dimension `d_{phys,i}=3 dim G (n_i−n_{i+1})` uses site counts n_i. This does not vary the physical domain of integration.

*Proof.* At fixed W, the perturbation is exactly `−v[S_i(V)−S_{i+1}(W)]` after extracting its constant. The restricted minimizing action has zero linear fluctuation for every W, by the original constrained stationarity in CMP109 (2.2)–(2.8). In physical variables z the original quadratic Hessian is the sum of the physical Wilson part and the actual exponential gauge part. Vary the former by the relative factor `1+b=1+v/β_i`. On the homogeneous carrier chart the perturbation is a small quadratic interaction uniformly for b in a fixed small disc. The required locality of its Hessian follows from (7.141)–(7.142) and the local gauge part, or by the inverse localized covariance construction in Lemma 7.100; stationarity is imposed on the physical fiber, not on independently varied current data. The original cubic and higher phase and unscaled scalar terms, including the complete inherited difference, have the fixed physical analytic bounds of Lemma 7.92. The physical minimizing action and its derivatives are themselves localized by (1.17)–(1.21) on the homogeneous graphs, using its plaquette sum and the physical η⁴ bound below. Thus the same normalized source construction as in Theorem 7.32 applies at this step.

In the split (7.141) the Gaussian physical Hessian annihilates the based gauge directions and is positive on the hard slice. Hence this relative perturbation changes its Gaussian integral by precisely `(1+b)^{-d_{phys,i}/2}`, independent of W. The original determinant of the linear coordinate change cancels in the ratio. There are four current bonds per current site, four constraints per coarse site, and one based generator per noncenter current site, giving the displayed rank times dim G. In particular the determinant does not count the extra soft-gauge coordinates as physical.

For the error, freeze W,b, all prior E_j and all original selector choices. On the symmetric inner balls |B|≤p_i introduce the independent ε in the physical fluctuation εB and divide the centered bare Wilson/gauge phase by ε². The singularity is removable by stationarity. The inherited scalar difference is the fixed analytic function on its true extended chart evaluated at this physical readout. Its dependence on old couplings is held fixed. At ε=0 extract the just computed Gaussian determinant; at nonzero ε the centered integral is even under `(ε,B)↦(−ε,−B)`. On the disc |ε|≤c/p_i the native localized interaction and Gaussian reserve bounds hold uniformly, as in §§7.14–7.18. Cauchy and parity therefore give O(g_i² p_i²) per carrier relative to ε=0. Restore the original outer balls and the full ε=0 Gaussian by the same tagged failed-selector bounds; choose D so these costs are smaller. Subtract the value b=0 and apply Cauchy on the spare fixed b-disc. The resulting difference is at most `C |b|g_i²p_i²`, with the exponentially small cutoff terms included. Since β_i is a fixed multiple of g_i⁻², this is (7.169). All contour changes use the same reference fiber at physical g_i. Gauge invariance of these source carriers follows as in Proposition 7.67. ∎

The decreasing weak trajectory x_i=g_i⁻² has increments bounded above and below by fixed positive constants in ultraviolet-to-infrared order for sufficiently small ḡ. In particular
`Σ_{i<K} g_i⁴ p_i² ≤ C Σ_{m≥0} [log(x_K+c m)]²/(x_K+c m)² <∞`   (7.170)
uniformly in K. By contrast the extensive scalar trace in (7.169) is retained as an analytic vacuum term.

**Lemma 7.105 (the constant scalar marginal representative).** In the translation- and hypercubic-invariant homogeneous class, the local quadratic curvature moment of a gauge-invariant scalar is a scalar multiple of the Wilson curvature square. The genuine S_i has this moment with the same normalization at every i, has a uniform analytic rooted norm per current cell, and can be used as its fixed physical representative. Winding contributions are separately retained.

*Proof.* Invariance under sign change of a coordinate eliminates off-diagonal pairings between different unordered plaquette planes. Permuting the four axes makes all diagonal coefficients equal. Constant color conjugation gives the invariant bilinear form on the simple Lie algebra. The orientation-odd topological tensor changes under a coordinate reflection and therefore does not enter this constant scalar sector. The original clean action and full sum of invariant insertions preserve the indicated lattice symmetries by CMP109 (2.16)–(2.18).

For S_i on the near-identity graph, the original fine curvature is O(η²‖q‖) as a plaquette logarithm in current units. Lemma 7.77 and the bounded C¹-to-curvature map used in Corollary 7.78 give the same estimate in the local carrier representation. The analytic plaquette action is quadratic in that logarithm, hence O(η⁴‖q‖²). A current cell includes O(η⁻⁴) fine plaquettes, giving a uniform physical carrier bound. Its quadratic form at identity is the energy of the original linear constrained minimum of Theorem 7.58. At a small terminal momentum p the nonprincipal fine curvatures have ℓ² size O(|p|³ |q|) by (7.158). The area-average cochain identity gives d q as the average of the fine curvature. Its principal alias filter equals I+O(|p|), and its remaining contraction is O(|p|³ |q|). Thus the fine principal curvature agrees with the coarse d q at degree one in p. The quadratic energy agrees with the ordinary Wilson d q energy at degree two in p. This identifies its invariant local marginal coefficient as one in Wilson normalization. As in Theorem 7.94 this is the homogeneous lifted local symbol; separately filed winding paths carry their finite-size tail. ∎

### 7.61 Constant coupling through the homogeneous action and irrelevant rows

For the constant scalar source the marginal just identified has a summable one-step defect. The other scalar rows need only a positive gain after dimension-four normalization. Their dimension-six moments can therefore be left together in the irrelevant remainder in this calculation.

**Lemma 7.106 (age of an unamplified scalar with its marginal removed).** At a homogeneous old scale let a translated gauge-invariant real scalar family have rooted analytic norm A on the common fixed α-disc, with its vacuum and its complete local quadratic curvature moment removed. Assume the invariant tensor vanishes after the full translated source sum. On the h-step joint chart of §7.57 its entire old readout in a smooth terminal unit patch has a connected carrier expansion bounded by `C_h A t^s` on the fixed physical disc, for some s>0 and t=L^{j−N}. Its proper difference from zero internal fields is bounded after one polynomial-tag integration by `C_h A t^s g_N`. No dimension-six factor t⁻² is applied here.

*Proof.* Construct the physical quadratic and cubic kernels and quartic tail as in §§7.49–7.50; here fixed-radius Cauchy costs only fixed constants times A. For the quadratic kernel the constant translation/curvature moment vanishes. Move the two curvature slots to one root. On a short path the C^{α₀} modulus of the actual old curvature from (7.116) gives cost `C ε(t(1+|P|))^{α₀}`; real parallel transport costs additionally O(εt|P|). Translate the smooth test by its recorded offset with the same or stronger gain. The unshifted constant moment cancels. This argument requires no vanishing second moment. The old curvature factors t⁴ have already paid the t⁻⁴ root count. The cubic contributes t² and the quartic contributes t⁴ after that same count. Winding kernels carry `exp(−c n_j)` with `n_j≥1/t`, paying the root count and any fixed positive age. Longer paths are bounded with their exponential path moments. The calculations can be done on each smooth target-scale root patch; using translates of a partition of unity localizes the sum without a sharp test seam.

Use the actual coarse restrictions and rough representation of §§7.44–7.57. The rough exponents are no worse than the previously paid dimension-six ones and the h-step chart restores its α. Interpolate the positive real gain first to the required smaller complex disc, then use (7.143) to get the claimed carrier norm. For the proper difference at fixed terminal q take one radial derivative in the internal Z variables on their spare physical disc. Its pointwise growth is `C_h a_X t^s g_N max_{b∈X}|B_b|`, with summable carrier weights, because h is fixed and g_i≤C_h g_N. The one-tag proof of Lemma 7.82 gives the last assertion. The unsourced or slightly perturbed measure in which the tag is evaluated may include any other uniformly small bounded scalar activities on the same native margins. ∎

**Theorem 7.107 (homogeneous constant-action source disc, P/L under the fixed-block clean margins).** Consider the original all-clean conditional tower on its homogeneous near-identity scalar chart. Allow the complex source `exp[−v₀ S]` with v₀ a constant. On the specified weak trajectory and native margins, there is a cutoff-independent radius v_* > 0, possibly depending on the fixed stopping volume, with the following properties.

At each full block boundary k its normalized source density ratio can be written as
`exp[λ_k(v₀)−v_k(v₀) S_k(W)+Σ_{j≤k} R_j(D_{j,k} W;v₀)]`.   (7.171)
Here D is the actual deterministic old readout on the homogeneous nested graph, each R_j has its scalar and marginal removed, and the physical carrier amplitudes A_j satisfy
`|v_k(v₀)|+Σ_{j≤k}A_j(v₀)+Σ_{b≤k}|v_b(v₀)−v_{b-h}(v₀)|≤C |v₀|`
in the pointwise majorant sense: at each fixed v₀ in the disc the right side is C|v₀|. The functions are holomorphic and λ_k keeps all vacuum terms, including their possible ultraviolet divergence. For the homogeneous stopping integral restricted to a terminal near-identity chart (or its real gauge saturation), the normalized log pressure after vacuum subtraction has a fixed analytic disc. This conclusion does not integrate rough terminal sectors or any history with a large-field transition.

*Block identity.* Suppose (7.171) holds at k. Put v=v_k and denote the source-free normalized conditionals by μ_i. For each constituent introduce the normalized tilted conditional
`μ_i^v = exp[−v S_i(V_i)+v S_{i+1}(W)] (1+v/β_i)^{d_{phys,i}/2} exp[−D_i(W,v)] μ_i`.
It integrates to one by (7.169). Multiplying these h identities telescopes the actions exactly. If `R_{in}=Σ_{j≤k}R_j` is evaluated on the entrance field, the block ratio with the old scalar λ_k extracted becomes
`exp[−v S_N(q)] Π_{i=k}^{N−1}(1+v/β_i)^{-d_{phys,i}/2}`
`× E_{prod μ_i^v} exp[ R_{in}(V_k)+Σ_{i=k}^{N−1}D_i(V_{i+1},v)]`.   (7.172)
The notation for deterministic old readouts inside R_in is as in (7.171). Do not replace the D_i by constants: their upper fields are retained integration variables.

The tilted product has the block measure estimates in Lemma 7.100. In fact its Gaussian multiplies only a physical quadratic part by `1+v/β_i`, with a uniformly small analytic perturbation O(|v|g_i²) in the native weighted precision. Its physical determinant ratio is already extracted in (7.172). The finite remaining centered source corrections are bounded by the same physical scalar/positive quadratic reserves used for (7.169) and (7.163). Equivalently use (7.169) to normalize each constituent and its spatially localized numerator before the direct-sum conditioning. This gives the one-tag complex estimate on the tilted product for |v| in a fixed small disc. It does not require a spectral inequality for a complex probability law.

*Innovations with an ordinary scalar exponential.* In (7.172) split each old term into its deterministic endpoint at all internal Z=0 and its proper difference Δ_j. The endpoints give exactly the old tags in (7.171) at N. By Lemma 7.106 the Δ_j have uniform summed scalar sup norm `C_h Σ_{j≤k} A_j t_j^s` per terminal root, and a distinguished Δ_j gains the factor g_N after integration, where `t_j=L^{j−N}`. The h local rows D_i have total terminal-root norm `C_h |v| Σ_{i=k}^{N−1}u_i` with `u_i=g_i⁴p_i²`. Indeed their original roots lie at most h scales below N, hence their root counts and all finite chart/carrier conversions cost only C_h. For these recent rows use the ordinary native large physical domain and bounded localization of (7.169); no age interpolation or inverse-g_j factor is required. Choose the boundary core α small inside their fixed native radius and the native support slack sufficient for these finitely many conversions. Apply the smooth patch substitutions of §§7.49 and 7.56 on the actual intermediate graph. Vacuum values may be split off at this stage as well.

Let `B_{in}=Σ_j Δ_j+Σ_iD_i` on this block. Under a bootstrap `|v|+Σ A_j` sufficiently small on the common disc, exp(s B_in), 0≤s≤1, is an ordinary bounded scalar polymer perturbation on the fixed selector and its localized support norms fit the strict CMP116 margin. It need not be treated as an exponential of a globally unbounded polynomial in uncut Gaussian variables. The extra connected log equals exactly `∫₀¹ E_{s B_{in}} B_{in} ds` on the normalized tilted product. This follows by differentiation of its nonzero connected log; at s=0 it has the zero value. Designate just one differentiated proper difference at a time. Under the small scalar perturbation the one-tag comparison of Lemma 7.82 retains its g_N factor. A designated D_i uses simply its bounded scalar norm. This proves for the new physical scalar F_N, in a connected carrier norm and its full terminal q-disc,
`‖F_N‖≤C_h [|v| Σ_{i=k}^{N−1}u_i + g_N Σ_{j≤k}t_j^s A_j].`   (7.173)
The scalar norm sums per terminal root. The part proportional to its total number of sites is entered in λ_N. To retain invariant rooted summands when needed, designate the physical old source root in the above derivative, and distribute the resulting old root sum using the smooth translates of a partition of unity at the terminal scale. The entire invariant scalar at a designated root transforms with the whole tilted integral; local carrier summands need not be invariant separately. For D_i use its gauge-invariant native carriers. The complete sum is translation- and hypercubic-invariant for the original constant test. The extended U,J arguments may again be put on the homogeneous physical q graph as in Lemma 7.87. A finite extra native support and external-radius margin is reserved for this extraction at every block, as in Corollary 7.99.

*Scalar projection and summation.* Apply Lemma 7.105 to the full new scalar. Its dimension-four quadratic moment m_N has `|m_N|≤C_α ‖F_N‖` by the rooted Cauchy/path moment bounds. Subtract its constant and m_N S_N as whole physical functions, and set `v_N=v−m_N` with this sign convention. This yields the single new residual R_N with `A_N≤C_α‖F_N‖` and zero marginal tensor on the full translation orbit. Subtracting the genuine S_N, rather than only a quadratic polynomial, is essential for reusing the next identity (7.169). Winding terms are included with their exponentially small old support norm. This establishes the inductive shape in (7.171).

Start with v=v₀ and no residual. Put `X_N=|v₀|+Σ_{b≤N}(|v_b−v_{b-h}|+A_b)`, with b at successive block ends and v at the initial end equal to v₀. Summing (7.173), the second term contributes at most half of ΣA_b if ḡ is sufficiently small depending on h,s and the fixed native constants, by the geometric age sum. Consequently
`X_N≤2|v₀|+C_h Σ_{b≤N} (Σ_{i=b-h}^{b-1}u_i) X_{b-h}`.
The elementary discrete Gronwall product gives `X_N≤2|v₀| exp(C_hΣ_i u_i)`, uniformly by (7.170). Choose v_* so this stays inside the bootstrap scalar and coupling margins. The finitely many initial steps if K is not divisible by h can be treated as one shorter first block: there are no preexisting residuals, and its native action errors have the larger original domain as above. Thus this shortened block entails no iterative radius loss.

Finally take any original positive terminal measure restricted to the indicated homogeneous near-identity domain of nonzero mass. At stopping the number of terminal sites is fixed. The physical minimizing action is bounded there by the per-cell estimate of Lemma 7.105. The residual deterministic readouts have total per-cell bound CΣA_j by Lemma 7.106 on the same graph. Therefore the full field-dependent exponent after λ_K has sup norm ≤C_{T_*}|v₀|. On a sufficiently small disc `E|exp(field-dependent exponent)−1|<1`, so its integral cannot vanish. The analytic vacuum exponential never vanishes. This proves the homogeneous restricted pressure assertion. ∎

Equation (7.168) explains why an unrenormalized bare second derivative is not supplied by this analytic-radius argument. The λ_k terms in (7.171) may have large derivatives. The uniform part is the field-dependent conditional ratio on the displayed homogeneous chart and the vacuum-subtracted restricted integral.

### 7.62 A genuine blocked bare insertion at the true boundary, and the H Hessian test

**Proposition 7.108 (first-birth realization and limits of the branch bound).** Under the true-boundary empty-wall construction in T2 Propositions 4.42 and 4.44, its tangential fourth-difference curvature packet can be made the literal old coefficient of a bounded finite-stencil bare gauge-invariant insertion on the first clean fiber. On the indicated deterministic small-Y half-patch this actual early birth fails any independent positive-age bound. The claim is about a purpose-built bare insertion and the specified raw branch quantity.

*Proof.* On the first coarse lattice let `X_p(W)=Π_{Lie}[(W(∂p)−W(∂p)⁻¹)/2]` for the fixed plane used in T2's mode. Form the old rooted finite packet F₁ by pairing X_p with the tangential operator `(T+T⁻¹−2)²` on that curvature, using its true straight parallel transports. Give it the declared g₁⁻² coefficient and the original old-root/engineering normalization of that packet. Define the corresponding bare term on the fine lattice to be `F₁(MU)` on the regular patch containing all one-level averaging descendants. The required number of fine links is fixed because L is fixed. If a globally defined compact insertion is desired, multiply by a smooth gauge-invariant function of the elementary plaquette defects on that enlarged patch, equal to one on the first clean selector there and vanishing before the local analytic averaging chart ends; extend by zero outside. The regular thresholds may be reduced with the given first-step spare margin. Thus on the actual first clean constraint fiber W=MU the insertion is exactly F₁(W), including its compact orientation and old phase. Its first normalized coarse action derivative is a genuine born coefficient, with no Gaussian approximation. This is a finite local blocked observable; it should not be silently identified with the prescribed unblocked H.

The primary root-incidence calculation in T2 §4.35, Proposition 4.44, uses one *complete* minimal old support per root, including its tangential paths and all determining descendants. On its selected pinned layer each such support lies in the same minimal Y₁=Z. Thus the curvature words in that family see the actual common small-Y record, and their depth-one rows are either present or replayed from their fixed children. The Cartan mode in T2 (4.65)–(4.66) has the old tangential frequency where the fourth-difference symbol is strictly positive. Replacing the physical logarithm by the sine/traceless variable above changes it by O(|X|³) in the small old plaquette defects, hence does not affect the leading lower bound. With its smooth tangential root pairing the specified half-patch sum is bounded below by `c_L g₁⁻² τ²/r−C_L g₁⁻²τ²`, while the stored cutoff data have the stated finite canonical size, as verified in T2 (4.69)–(4.70). Its zeroth and second moments vanish and the straight paths have zero area. This excludes the corresponding independently normed deterministic branch estimate. A connected covariance with a fresh vertex can vanish for a purely pinned tag, and signed branch partners may cancel; those operations are not bounded below by this calculation. T2, Propositions 4.42 and 4.44. ∎

**Corollary 7.109 (the genuine first H birth's quadratic kernel).** Write b=log W for physical first-step upper coordinates about identity, and let E_bond(W)=E_W h_bond on the homogeneous original first clean kernel. With γ=g₀²β and F_bond the unsmeared physical matching function H_bond,
`g₀² D_{b(y)}D_{b(y′)} E_bond(I) = γ D_{b(y)}D_{b(y′)} [F_bond(U₁(exp b))]|_{b=0} + e(y,y′),`
`Σ_{y,y′} e^{c tree(bond,y,y′)}(1+tree)^m |e(y,y′)|≤C_m g₀².`   (7.174)
The leading term is precisely the bare quadratic matching force evaluated on the linear constrained mean.

*Proof.* Equation (7.123) gives the leading βF_bond plus the two Jacobian/Hessian one-loop terms and its rooted error. The latter terms are analytic on a fixed physical external disc with exponentially summable carriers, uniformly as g₀ tends to zero. The external graph substitution on the first step is the one verified in §§7.41–7.45. Cauchy to order two and a fixed carrier-moment payment give (7.174), also after any fixed bounded moment projection such as (7.154). At identity the matching force vanishes; its first potential variation at the physical constrained minimum is the linear minimizing response, so the quadratic Hessian of its square is the asserted free one. The kernel can be tested on infinitesimal complex Bloch modes whose growth exponent lies below its available anchor decay, by absolute summation on the homogeneous lift. The statement alone does not identify a half-space localized R-operation coefficient with that homogeneous lift, and analytic continuation outside the common source decay is not claimed. ∎

### 7.63 Area paid exactly by a complete invariant scalar

For ordinary variance at a fixed cutoff one can allow the transported scalar amplitudes to grow slowly with depth. This avoids requiring analyticity of an exponential source for the frustration and avoids identifying all anisotropic marginal flows. It is important here to keep the *exact* fourth power from the old root whenever the observable may have a marginal quadratic term.

**Lemma 7.110 (one rooted old scalar, with no marginal subtraction).** Use the homogeneous h-step setup and the survey of parameter margins in §§7.56–7.57. Let F_{j,o} be an invariant scalar associated with one old root o, with its vacuum value subtracted. Suppose its q-only connected carrier amplitude on the fixed α-disc is a_{j,o}, as in (7.150), without any further physical moment condition. Then its readout through the h-step block has a joint source-coordinate carrier representation `Σ_X F_{o,X}(q,Z)` rooted at the terminal cube containing o, with
`Σ_X e^{a|X|} sup|F_{o,X}| ≤ C_h a_{j,o} t^4,   ord_{(q,Z)=0}F_{o,X}≥2,  t=L^{j−N}.`   (7.175)
Choose the raw localization and final weights with the same return margin as in Corollary 7.99. No old roots are summed in (7.175).

*Proof.* The constant color action at the identity annihilates the first link-field jet of F_{j,o}. Subtract the individual zeroth and first Taylor coefficients from its old local pieces; their total is zero. The remaining pieces thus have valuation two and the same type of weighted norm. The exact gauge-invariant total is available for each old marked root.

In the rough source calculation use the physical fine minimizing field at the entrance scale k, with units of that scale for local regularity. The relative common-baseline construction in Lemma 7.98 supplies the same uniform analytic native value and first-difference bounds on its weakened fields as on the small physical chart, by (1.18). Repeated original averages in their local gauges as in (7.117) retain these norms. Apply to this weakened old potential the single root affine gauge in Theorem 7.89, with smooth cutoff in entrance units. This is a source-only evaluation. On the actual real graph the *whole* F_{j,o} is invariant, so it has exactly its original value after this change; the equality extends holomorphically. On an auxiliary weakened graph only an analytic extension in its physical old variables is being evaluated.
