Writing `t′=L^{j−k}=L^h t`, the bound on the old link logarithms restricted to a carrier of n old cubes is `C_h(1+n)(t′)^2 R`, with R the fixed radius of the larger input chart. This is the pointwise short/long carrier estimate in Theorem 7.89 applied to the complex analytic small potentials, whose Taylor and Lipschitz estimates are unchanged under bounded complex matrix products. Simultaneously their plain global size stays inside the old α-ball: at zero internal fields the physical potential in entrance units is O(C_κ L^{-h}Dα), by the single terminal endpoint. The additional global derivative of the affine gauge costs a fixed multiple of this quantity in entrance units. Internal deviations cost C_{h,κ}ε₁ as in (7.162). Impose the fixed endpoint radius margin also for these constants. For the other regions of the old carrier the real-space bump equals identity; its derivative across its cutoff is still uniformly bounded. The affine gauge at o needs only the neighboring old patch and the support of this fixed smooth cutoff. Its root patch uses a fixed number of terminal cubes, not one new cube for every fine site.

The radial valuation-two bound now contributes `C_{h,α} (1+n)^2 t^4` times the old carrier norm directly on these weakened analytic fields. The center(s) of the cube-localized extensions and the exterior Cauchy variables can be taken as in (1.9). More explicitly, regard the weak conditionally localized maps as in Lemmas 7.77, 7.80, 7.98 on each old patch; their first-difference norms have the same root-sum bound. Smooth gauge correction uses the same root field value at all old slots. As a map in the local potential Banach norm, its corrected logarithm is bounded by (C(1+n)(t′)^2) times that norm, for all complex potentials in the smaller regular ball. This follows from the same cancellation of the constant old potential and the bounded first differences used in Theorem 7.89, with the uncorrected global norm used when n t′ is large. Cauchy/polarization of this analytic map, or Cauchy in the native weakening parameters on the root base X₀, retains that factor. Joining the old slots/bump and the marked root costs at most the base size `C(1+nt)`; the original exponential old norm absorbs it by Corollary 7.99. If the current gauges used to represent the relative fields are undone at the bottom, use the recursively gauged old field in the invariant scalar; no separate gauge invariance of the pieces is required on the weak graphs. The resulting sum of native connected coefficients has the claimed t⁴ weight. All auxiliary relative maps vanish at their zero relative inputs, so raw zeroth/first jets of those old pieces remain zero. This proves (7.175). In contrast to (7.143), the full t⁴ here is obtained inside the weakened estimate itself; interpolating a t⁴ bound with a crude t⁰ bound would lose a power at the marginal root count. ∎

**Lemma 7.111 (outer physical field moments on the homogeneous block tower).** Suppose the top retained measure is supported on the fixed small terminal chart, with the original invariant positive conditional kernels below it, and the stopped coupling x_K=g_K⁻² bounded above by a fixed constant. At every block boundary k the computational representative of its physical current link `W_k=exp b_k` can be chosen so that, for each fixed p needed below,
`sup_{D} ‖ max_{e∈D}|b_k(e)| ‖_{L^p} ≤ C_{h,p} g_k.`   (7.176)
Here D runs over individual native cubes at scale k. The constants are uniform in cutoff and the terminal measure on this chart.

*Proof.* Starting from its top representative, generate the actual positive conditional tower in the order of Lemma 7.98. At the bottom of each block choose the raw old field of the relative minimizing graph as the representative passed to the next block. It lies in the same gauge orbit as the physical lower target, so the law of all invariant scalar observations and their normalized conditional means is unchanged. On the independent real block variables one has `E[exp(s|B_i(y)|²)|q]≤C_h` for small fixed s>0 uniformly in q on its chart, by the single-site quadratic probe in the joint expansion (7.163). Taking its positive real expectation requires no comparison to a different denominator.

Let P_k denote the left side of (7.176). At j=k the all-zero endpoint in (7.162) has analytic carrier norm bounded by C_κ L⁻ʰ‖q‖ and vanishes at q=0. In each endpoint carrier the local radial bound therefore costs C L⁻ʰ times the maximum of q on that carrier. At fixed p its L^p norm is at most a fixed polynomial in the number of cubes times P_N, paid by the spare exponential. For this endpoint estimate the constant remains independent of h: one patch of old size L⁻ʰ is inside one fixed terminal neighborhood, and the single H_N(q) and the repeated endpoint frames have the uniform bound from (7.162). The same holds for the maximum in one old native cube by taking the local Banach sup norm on its patch. Internal deviations vanish at all Z=0 and obey the sum of localized upper bounds C_h times their local maxima. The one-site moment probe, fixed h, and spare carrier decay give an L^p bound C_h g_N for them. Thus
`P_k≤C_* L^{-h} P_N + C_h g_N.`
Choose h with the endpoint constant small enough that λ=C_*L⁻ʰ<1/2; this is the same kind of choice as in Corollary 7.99. The relative flow gives (g_b/g_k≤C(1+b−k)^q) for b≥k on the weak trajectory, with a fixed power q. Iterating the recursion sums this polynomial against λ per block. The top remainder λ^{(K−k)/h} P_K is at most C g_k because P_K is bounded, x_K is bounded and x_k≤x_K+C(K−k). This proves (7.176). A terminal law with its own (P_K≤C g_K) can be used instead. ∎

### 7.64 Susceptibility on the restricted homogeneous tower

**Theorem 7.112 (P/L on the fixed-block homogeneous chart).** Normalize the actual all-clean tower with its stopping field restricted to the common near-identity domain or its real gauge saturation of positive mass. Use the weak parameters and fixed original selector/block margins of §§7.56–7.57, with x_K bounded above as in Lemma 7.111 (or its stated terminal moment replacement). For any finite local gauge-invariant original bond family Y_b whose vacuum-subtracted fixed-chart carrier amplitude is at most Cg₀⁻², with uniformly bounded stencil, and all spatial marks f_b,
`Var_{hom}(Σ_b f_b Y_b)≤C Σ_b |f_b|².`   (7.177)
In particular this holds for the unamplified local frustration and ordinary r_b on that restricted law. There is no smoothness assumption on f and no fixed analytic exponential-source hypothesis in this result.

*Rooted first derivative and birth sizes.* Use the exact Markov tower of real homogeneous conditionals and its conditional mean process. Subtract constants whenever estimating a variance. Denote the old scalar at birth j and designated native-cell root o by F_{j,o}, with fixed physical amplitude a_{j,o}; collect finitely many fine bond slots of one initial cube at their common root. Initially `‖a₀‖_{ℓ²}≤C g₀⁻² ‖f‖_{ℓ²}`. The direct initial family has this bound because it has fixed local support and the real group expressions are analytic on its fixed small physical chart. Gauge invariance eliminates its linear link-field coefficient at identity. The ordinary r_b includes a local Laplacian/vacuum contribution; subtracting its constant leaves the same local quadratic-valuation bound. The estimate for the frustration also follows from (7.159).

At a block from k to N retain the deterministic tag of every old F_{j,o} and regard
`E[F_{j,o}(q,Z)|q]−F_{j,o}(q,0)`
as its new scalar innovation. The equality is exact; any constant of that innovation is filed before the next variance calculation. The endpoint tag still evaluates the same original old function at the next common minimum. By (7.175) its joint carrier sup is `C_h t_j⁴ a_{j,o}`, where `t_j=L^{j−N}`. Its proper difference gains one `g_N max|B|` by the spare internal disc. A single polynomial-tag integration on the original normalized block therefore bounds the new physical carrier norm, uniformly on the *same boundary α-disc*, by `C_h g_N t_j⁴ a_{j,o}`. Each complete marked-root scalar mean and deterministic term is gauge invariant. After pulling the localized physical output onto q by Lemma 7.87, its zeroth/first raw Taylor pieces may again be removed carrierwise (their total after the vacuum subtraction is zero). This ensures the next application of (7.175). No curvature moment or anisotropic marginal is discarded. The fixed pre-extraction margins for this procedure are among those of Corollary 7.99.

Assign each new invariant innovation to the terminal native cube x containing its original old root. Let π(o)=x be this assignment and use the nested half-open grid convention. Then
`a_N(x)≤C_h g_N Σ_{j≤k} t_j⁴ Σ_{π(o)=x} a_j(o).`   (7.178)
The supports of these coefficients may extend beyond x with the available exponential weight; the distinguished root in their carrier is x. There are at most C t_j⁻⁴ old roots per terminal cube, disjoint under this assignment. Hence
`‖t_j⁴ Σ_{π(o)=x}a_j(o)‖_{ℓ²(x)}≤C t_j² ‖a_j‖_{ℓ²}`.
Set `b_j=L^{2j}‖a_j‖_{ℓ²}`, `B_k=Σ_{j≤k}b_j` over boundary birth indices including zero. It follows that `b_N≤C_h g_N B_k` and
`B_k≤C g₀⁻² ‖f‖_{ℓ²}(1+C_h ḡ)^{k/h+1}.`   (7.179)
The additional factor allows the single initial short block if needed. These are finite linear insertions; no smallness of the original amplitudes a₀ or their signed f is required.

*Variance of one exact block.* For a carrier F_{o,X} in (7.175), the zero internal value is deterministic in the conditional law. Since the joint valuation is at least two, Taylor's integral and separate internal Cauchy on the spare disc give the pointwise bound
`|F_{o,X}(q,Z)−F_{o,X}(q,0)| ≤ C_h a_{o,X} g_N (1+max_X |B|)^2 [q_X+g_N]`,
where `q_X=max_{y∈X}|q_y|` and the a_{o,X} have rooted sum ≤C_h t_j⁴ a_{j,o}. To verify the q_X factor, differentiate once along the internal direction Z: its derivative vanishes at (q,Z)=0, so the larger-disc radial bound for the remaining derivative is linear in `max(q_X,‖Z‖_X)`. The other factor is `‖Z‖_X≤C_h g_N max_X|B|`. These estimates need only one quadratic moment of q after pairing. At fixed real q apply the two polynomial-tag conditioning estimate to two such carriers. Their connected term costs the product of the displayed coefficients with the remaining support-distance exponential. Now average q in the actual outer law. Lemma 7.111 bounds `‖q_X+g_N‖_{L²}≤C_h g_N(1+|X|)^{1/2}`; pay the two support polynomials with the unused carrier weight. Summing the connected carriers retains exponential decay between their terminal designated roots. The original `Var(·|q)` is unchanged by dropping each deterministic value individually.

Put `A(x)=Σ_{j≤k}t_j⁴Σ_{π(o)=x}a_j(o)`. Exponential convolution on the terminal grid thus gives
`E Var(Σ_{j,o}F_{j,o}(q,Z) | q) ≤ C_h g_N^4 Σ_{x,y}A(x)e^{−c dist(x,y)}A(y) ≤ C_h g_N^4 L^{-4N} B_k².`   (7.180)
This includes the actual dependence of the conditional measure on the outer field through both its precision and its scalar normalization. It estimates the variance of the *sum* in that one measure.

*Summing the tower.* Conditional orthogonality gives the sum of (7.180) over block boundaries plus the variance of the last retained mean in its actual terminal law. That terminal field is on the fixed physical chart. The deterministic bound from (7.175) and the new K-birth amplitudes give sup norm of the nonconstant last mean ≤`C n_K² L^{-2K} B_K` by Cauchy–Schwarz in the fixed terminal root count; n_K denotes linear site count here. This accounts for the between-field mean, rather than trying to bound it by an internal Poincaré inequality.

On the fixed stopped trajectory `(g_N/g₀)^4≤C(1+N)^2` by the relative flow, and `g₀^{-4}=x₀²≤C(1+K)^2`. Insert (7.179) in (7.180). The normalized sum is bounded by a fixed multiple of
`Σ_{N≥1}(1+N)^2 [L^{-4}(1+C_h ḡ)^{2/h}]^N`,
including the finite terminal term with its fixed n_K. Choose the admissible weak ḡ so the ratio is less than one; it can be chosen after h. This proves (7.177), with constants independent of lattice spacing. ∎

The result applies within one homogeneous regular sector, including the replicated short-period comb and ordinary fine marks. It gives its *own-law* conditional variance: the sector is normalized with its own stopping mass. None of the estimates has replaced the other history masses in the complete Wilson law by that mass. Completing the susceptibility requires the rough-sector innovations and the variance between their conditional means, or another genuine full-law argument.

### 7.65 Real regular stopping fields and flat holonomies

At a fixed stopping volume the near-identity requirement can be achieved before the last finitely many globally regular transitions. The argument concerns the real terminal fields; no chart around a nontrivial toron is used in the preceding complex source proof.

**Lemma 7.113 (small-curvature global link gauge on a periodic grid).** On a periodic n⁴ lattice with SU(N) links assume `max_p ‖W(∂p)−I‖≤b/n²`. There exist b₀>0, n₀, C depending only on d=4,N such that if b≤b₀ and n≥n₀, the configuration has a periodic site gauge in which `max_e ‖W_e−I‖≤C/n`. The constants are uniform in all flat holonomies.

*Proof.* Work on a coordinate fundamental box and use the rooted, nonwrapping coordinate-order tree of §7.9. Gauging its links to identity makes every nonseam link at most C n times the plaquette bound away from I: commute its extra coordinate step to the canonical position in its tree loop, using at most (d−1)n plaquettes. All conjugating matrices are real unitary. Denote the seam in direction μ at transverse coordinate z by S_μ(z) and its base value by H_μ=S_μ(0). For neighboring transverse coordinates not crossing a seam, the elementary seam plaquette shows their seam values differ by at most C b/n, because its two transverse nonseam links have that bound. Hence `‖S_μ(z)−H_μ‖≤C b` throughout the fundamental transverse box. The constants H_μ are the straight base cycle holonomies. Their pairwise commutator loops bound the area-n² coordinate sheet of plaquettes, so `‖H_μH_ν−H_νH_μ‖≤C b`, again by product cancellation and unitarity.

There are commuting H_μ⁰ with `max ‖H_μ−H_μ⁰‖≤ω_N(Cb)`, where ω_N(s)→0. Otherwise a sequence of almost commuting tuples in the compact product SU(N)^4 would have a convergent subsequence with a commuting limit at a fixed positive distance from all commuting tuples. Simultaneous diagonalization supplies commuting traceless anti-Hermitian logs X_μ, `exp X_μ=H_μ⁰`, `‖X_μ‖≤C_N`: choose eigenangles and adjust their sums by multiples of 2π to give trace zero. Use the site gauge `u(x)=Π_μ exp(−x_μ X_μ/n)` on the fundamental vertices, extended periodically as values on the discrete torus. Interior link sizes are now O((C_N+b)/n). Every seam link is within `δ_s=C_N/n+Cb+ω_N(Cb)` of identity, since the identical calculation with a constant commuting seam H_μ⁰ gives a link exp(X_μ/n), up to a fixed conjugation.

It remains to replace δ_s by C/n on the seams. Repair the directions in order. At the μ-th repair let S(z) be its current seam link and use `v(x)=exp[−(x_μ/n) log S(z)]`. Its value is I at x_μ=0. The transformed seam is exp[(1/n)log S(z)] and hence O(1/n) from I. All nonseam links in direction μ stay O(1/n). For a transverse bond already known small, both copies of that bond at x_μ=0 and x_μ=n−1 are O(1/n); this holds also for a previously repaired transverse seam. Their common seam plaquette implies `‖S(z+e_ν)−S(z)‖≤C/n+b/n²`. On the chosen small log ball, log and exp are Lipschitz. The variation of v along that bond is therefore O(1/n), so every previously good bond remains good. Unrepaired seams change by at most a fixed multiple of their previous small size, because `‖v−I‖≤C max‖S−I‖`. There are only d repairs. Choose b₀ small and n₀ large enough that these finitely many logs remain on their common branch. After the last repair all bonds satisfy the stated bound. ∎

**Corollary 7.114 (emerging inside the homogeneous chart).** Fix the terminal linear site count n_K on T*. Consider an original purely clean final segment whose terminal background has the real CMP102 regular minimizing chart with sufficiently small fixed regularity ε (depending on n_K), including the actual local collars of (9). Use periodic lifts for a cube crossing a period when the original homogeneous critical orbit lifts, as in §7.28. For a sufficiently long but fixed number m of last steps, its field at K−m has a gauge representative in the fixed α-disc of Theorems 7.107 and 7.112, provided the original physical internal cutoff ε₁ is sufficiently small after m is chosen. The assertion includes flat terminal torons. A second sufficient condition, independent of any upper history geometry, is simply that the real retained field at K−m has plaquette deviation ≤b₀/(n_K L^m)^2.

*Proof.* Start with the genuine fine regular minimum U_K(W) at the terminal W; its local CMP102 gauge (9) gives uniform C¹ control in terminal units on the required regular cubes. Apply Lemma 7.54 locally in these cubes to its original (K−m)-fold mean V̄_{K−m}. Its coarse plaquette deviations are at most `C ε L^{-2m}` by the four-link expansion, independently of winding of distant paths. The stencils have adequate collar on a periodic lift; gauge-invariant plaquette values descend. With `n=n_K L^m` this is the hypothesis of Lemma 7.113 when `C n_K²ε≤b₀`. Choose m so n≥n₀ and `C/n` is below a fixed small fraction of α. Thus the actual direct mean is globally near identity in some real site gauge.

For the finitely many upper clean fluctuations compare the final field at K−m to that same direct mean before applying its new gauge. The finite relative construction in Lemma 7.98 applies on the real regular terminal orbit using U_K(W) as baseline. The local relative minimum has value O(‖b‖) in current-unit regular norms by CMP102 (172),(190) and the original hard chart, uniformly over this regular family. On each fixed native patch put the baseline in its local real gauge (9), apply (7.117) to the baseline and its relative potential and undo the bounded endpoint frames. This bounds the difference of their raw current means by C‖b‖ in the same frame, hence in any real endpoint frame by unitarity. The last based averaged-contour gauges and their inverses are local uniformly Lipschitz on these regular contour charts. Iterating this finite real estimate for m steps bounds the uniform difference by `C_m ε₁`, up to the gauge-equivalent representatives used in the exact tower. Its constant is independent of K: the number of constituent steps is m and (190) and the repeated-average bounds are independent of the fine-to-current depth. This argument uses local real charts on the true terminal minimum, not an analytic toron parameterization. Reduce the physical selector to `C_m ε₁< cα`. Applying the same real gauge as for the direct mean shows the fluctuating field lies in its α-disc saturation. The separate sufficient condition follows immediately from Lemma 7.113 with no comparison of upper fields. ∎

For all-clean histories satisfying this terminal regularity, one can therefore stop the previous arguments at K−m instead of K and integrate their conclusions against the *actual* induced positive distribution of that retained field. It is a fixed lattice, its site count enlarged by only the fixed factor L^{4m}. The action pressure disc may be reduced by this fixed size. For the variance use bounded x_{K−m} (which follows from bounded x_K and fixed m), and the terminal retained-mean estimate in (7.180). More generally the same reasoning applies to a positive later-history law independent of fine variables given W_{K−m}, whenever this field has the separate near-flat support condition just stated and the lower conditional law is the original homogeneous clean tower. This does not include histories with rough components in the earlier K−m scales.

### 7.66 A polynomial replica route for the surviving T5/T6 interface

**Proposition 7.115 (conditional finite-jet chessboard transfer).** Assume the source-free S94 comparison on the actual admissible tori, the original even cell/slab and margin hypotheses of T6 §4.5, and strictly local coefficient maps splitting across those margins. For k test insertions in a cell let P_c be their finite renormalized coefficient, including its nonlinear Ψ/contact terms, as an actual bounded cell function at each fixed cutoff. Reflections act by conjugation on the cell images. Let M be the fixed number of cells on T*. Suppose on that reference torus
`⟨𝒟 P_c⟩_{T*}^{1/M} ≤ C_D^k (k!)^{p_D} Π_i ‖f_i‖_{
m test}`   (7.181)
uniformly in the cutoff, with the required separated-distance powers if applicable. Here 𝒟 is the fully disseminated product with alternating reflected conjugates. Then the corresponding product of cell coefficients on T=qT* obeys the same type of m-th moment bound, uniformly in q, with a fixed factor per occupied cell from S94. This statement does not assume an analytic source exponential for P_c.

*Proof.* Apply the original chessboard inequality to the actual finite functions P_c, one per occupied cell. A replica of a single P_c across an even torus gives the slab operator alternately A and A*, since the slices are related by reflection/conjugation and the Wilson boundary plaquettes are split equally. At a fixed cutoff the bounded cell functions give a Hilbert–Schmidt slab operator. Hence the period pair is AA*≥0 trace class, and the elementary trace submultiplicativity under repeating a period applies just as in T6 §4.5(ii). It uses the multiplicative replicated cell weights, with no logarithm of P_c. Repeating the bound in each coordinate gives `Z_{qT*}[𝒟 P_c]≤Z_{T*}[𝒟 P_c]^{q⁴}`, with the same replicated pattern and compatible even periods. The same proof works when the fixed reference period contains several slab pairs, since their repeated pattern is used, and it is required that the paired slab operator has the stated positive transfer representation in each direction. Zero disseminated integrals pose no logarithmic difficulty. Normalizing by the respective source-free partition functions and applying S94 gives
`⟨𝒟 P_c⟩_{qT*}^{1/(Mq⁴)}≤exp(C₀ Vol(T*)/M) ⟨𝒟 P_c⟩_{T*}^{1/M}`.
Multiplying the resulting bounds over occupied cells and using `Π_c (k_c!)^{p_D}≤(m!)^{p_D}` proves the claim. Additivity/locality is needed to identify the product of P_c with the actual global renormalized coefficient; otherwise cross-cell contact operators would remain.

A sufficient new input for (7.181) is a fixed-reference bound for the corresponding **kM-th joint coefficient**, including strict locality of its prescribed replica product. Indeed `((kM)!)^{1/M}≤M^k k!` by the multinomial inequality. Thus finite order k on the large torus needs more than order k on the reference torus; all orders with controlled constants suffice. This does not follow by taking the raw unreduced absolute moment of a contact-renormalized distribution unless the cell polynomial representation and the equality of its replicas to those coefficients are verified. T5 source, T6, §4.5. ∎

### 7.67 A signed healing operation with the returning boundary retained

We now take a concrete mixed transition. An old large-field component returns to the small-field class at the R-operation. Fix the external record in (1.72) and take the case with no component of its second (still-live) class. Earlier histories inside the returning component can be genuinely large. In particular this is not a homogeneous clean fluctuation integration. At this transition the correct denominator for the signed return is its entire curly bracket in (1.72).

Use the printed formulas of Balaban, LFR II, pp. 378–390, (1.71)–(1.75), (1.89)–(1.100). The reversed Faddeev–Popov removal on p.378 gives an equivalence **after integration of the gauge variables**; the unintegrated densities are not equated. A complete old plaquette made from its V_h or explicitly stored endpoint rows defines a bounded function of these integration variables and fixed exterior data. At a true returning edge it may have a different value on another determining record.

Write `B=1+Σ_{compatible nonempty families} Π_P w_P` for (1.90), with P=X′ and w_P=F(X′) exactly as in (1.91). Compatibility is the original polymer-family compatibility. `sup_x Σ_{P∋x} a_P exp[κ₁ |P|] ≤ C exp[−p₀(g_k)]`
at a reduced rate κ₁ on the fixed localization cubes, with the connected root sum/entropy paid out of the native `exp[−(1+β)κ d_k(P)]` factor. Equivalently work in that native length norm. Here the temporary symbol β in this last exponent is the geometric constant of LFR II. To see why the rare factor is retained, q≥1 in (1.95) in this case: take one `exp[−p₀(g_k)]` before performing (1.96). No absolute value is taken after cancellations in w_P in lieu of its actual record majorant.

**Theorem 7.116 (same signed denominator and one rare return).** In this actual return bracket designate one native returning component X_* containing a fixed old charged site. In (1.91), mark the histories forming this component by one or two complete compact readouts M_i on their *actual* integrated/pinned records. For a labelled linear source in this sector, the derivatives of w_P are the same sum/integral with M_i, respectively M_iM_j, inserted. If their absolute bounds there are K_i,K_j, the exact normalized logarithm contributions at this fixed external state obey

`|D_iD_j log B|≤C K_iK_j (exp[−p₀(g_k)]+exp[−2p₀(g_k)])`.   (7.182)
The same-component joint product is paid once. The inequalities include all other compatible returns and their signs, even though the designated tag is confined to X_*. *Proof of the exact denominator.* Let B_{\bar P} be the same polymer sum with P and every polymer incompatible with P excluded. Connected-log expansion (1.98) gives

This is a ratio of two *actual signed polymer sums*, not of two independently estimated field masses. The exclusion shell has at most a fixed multiple of |P| cubes. More explicitly the proof bounds that root sum by a constant times the small anchored activity norm above; a polymer reaching P through distance is joined by the same connecting path, whose spare exponential pays the endpoint count. At zero tags differentiation of the compatible sum gives
`D_i log B=Σ_P w_{P,i} B_{\bar P}/B`.
Every w_{P,i} for this labelled part contains the genuine selected component X_* and hence P contains its home. For the two labels on X_* the middle sum is zero because both required polymers contain its home. Apply (7.183) and the anchored bank. This proves (7.182). It also shows precisely where an unnormalized rare majorant divided by a different Z would give a wrong result. ∎

**Concrete returning-boundary readout.** Use the genuine first clean birth `M_1(V_1)=s_p(V_1)/N` for a single complete depth-one plaquette formed by a bare one-level blocked plaquette (s_p(MU)/N), with the same local smooth extension and first-fiber equality as Proposition 7.108. If a link is held outside the returning region, retain its actual exterior value in M_1. A stencil meeting the edge requires its full collar in the tagged carrier; adding its fixed number of cells costs only the fixed support slack. This applies to a literal old row in (1.71) or a complete pinned/replayed determining row at the selected component. It does not replace an already integrated arbitrary fine mark by a new coarse loop.

For comparison with the actual true-edge mode from T2, retain both original determinations whenever present. On the small-Y empty-wall in T2 (4.66) the recorded old logarithm is `r² c′_L τ sin(2πm₂/L+θ_L)T`, whereas the larger Y⁺ reads a flat plaquette on that patch. Consequently
`M_-−M_+ = [−Tr(T²)/(2N)] (c′_L τ r²)^2 sin²(2πm₂/L+θ_L)+O_N(τ⁴r⁸).`   (7.184)
This is a *nonzero* returning-boundary discrepancy on a positive fraction of the native layer. It is of order τ²r⁴ per pinned root, and order τ²r on the entire O(r⁻³)-root face patch for this unamplified observable. The two Y's are distinct weak determining domains, not automatically a returned/no-return pair. To compare two *actual weights* w^- and w^+ with different pins, use the identity `w^-M_-+w^+M_+=(w^-+w^+)M_+ + w^-(M_-−M_+)` with their original signs; if the second record is absent, do not invent it. On other records use the actual compact bound. Thus this transition treats a genuine edge and signed normalization without imposing false pointwise equality on its two sides.

For the designated blocked plaquette this proves a restricted physical source contribution to the healed R′ class at fixed outer record. On the normalized real V_h integration it is also valid for a literal original fine plaquette if its complete fine stencil is still actually in that integration/pin. The real compact pointwise bound by itself does not establish these hypotheses for the interacting integrated H birth, nor does it supply the between-record response of the exterior T″ factor or a visit to an unresolved live neighbor. Those are the missing parts of the amended I-1M.

### 7.68 The physical first H birth on the true pinned returning edge

The exterior partner of a returning source is specified by the actual addition and subtraction preceding (1.70), LFR II printed p.377. There the missing terms meeting Z are added to the new action A′_k and subtracted in V(Y). Its value on the new *extended* outer field need not equal its value on the flat physical critical orbit, even when the prescribed new coarse target is identity.

**Proposition 7.117 (exact cancellation of one physical returning-boundary row).** Use the no-still-live healing bracket of Theorem 7.116 and the actual empty-wall single-component record in T2 §§4.29–4.35. Take an old depth-one determining support with depth-zero fine bonds in its inner boundary strip, and choose a root whose complete incident fine plaquettes and one stencil collar lie strictly in that strip. Consider the actual first clean H source birth from (7.123) before any omission of its completed lower partner. Its classical local part is `β₀ H_b(U)`, evaluated on the fine U argument of that old activity. On the pinned strip the old *minus added* classical source term in V(X⁻) is identically zero, including before the signed normalization. Its exterior A′_k term is still present.

*Proof of the physical readout and partner.* In (7.102a) the first-step source is the actual physical β₀H_b of the fine constrained readout. At zero fluctuation the readout is U on the external old graph, so its extracted linear critical-value coefficient is precisely β₀H_b(U). This is a finite analytic function of the complete original fine plaquettes in that star, not of a newly postulated current-scale loop. CMP119 (2.13) leaves a depth-zero pinned strip between the first Ω₁ and the boundary of the one-step determining region, of width M₁Lη in the example. Choose the fine root away from the ends of this strip. The empty-wall localization of (1.61) fixes the entire fine star to the outer fine values U for every integration variable in this returned component. The old determining map q_old here actually keeps the depth-zero links, and P_old preserves them. This is the fine-pin assertion supplied in T2 in addition to the weaker equality of first coarse plaquettes.

For the *same local term*, the extended new action uses the identical function β₀H_b(U) of those outer U links. Thus LFR II's add/subtract operation supplies `β₀H_b(U)−β₀H_b(U)=0` in V on this pinned record. The added A′_k term is β₀H_b(U), exactly once. This also holds for a compact marginal/contact representative whose entire actual readout uses these very same fixed links. It does not apply to a coefficient with additional hidden fields or currents outside the star. In particular in this example the new homogeneous *physical* minimum at its identity target is flat, while its extended E(X,(U,J)) on the pinned outer data can be nonzero. Replacing the exterior partner by the flat value or by the distinct Y⁺ wall in (7.184) would create a spurious signed return contribution.

On the Cartan wave in T2 (4.65), inside its flat tangential cutoff patch, the direction-three fine link has angle θ_n=O_L(τr²) in the fixed Lie direction. The two transverse matching force differences have linear parts `[2(cosh λ−1)]θ_n T` and `[2(cos(2π/L²)−1)]θ_n T`, which are opposite, and the remaining one vanishes. The sine/projection errors start cubically in θ_n. Thus β₀H_b(U) is of order β₀τ²r⁴ at roots of nonvanishing phase. Its disappearance from the proper V term is an exact subtraction of the same value; it is not smallness of two unrelated determining fields. LFR II, printed pp. 376–379, T2, §§4.30, 4.33–4.35. ∎

**Proposition 7.118 (first two H source jets in this signed component, P/L on its actual admitted readouts).** Continue with this fixed complete fine pin and fixed source root. The remaining one-loop/Jacobian part of the genuine first H birth and its higher-order error have first-source norm O(1) on the original spare old field/current chart, with their native exponential carriers. Their old-minus-completed proper return contribution to the *signed* first logarithmic row is bounded by `C e^{-p₀(g_k)}`. For the inherited second-source row at the same fixed root, the bound is
`C e^{-p₀(g_k)} [1+β₀ u_b²] + C e^{-2p₀(g_k)}`,   (7.185)
where u_b bounds the matching forces on the common fine star in its actual pins and its added extension. In T2's wave `u_b≤C_Lτ r²`. Use I-2 only for its stated spare-domain admission of the nonlocal old readouts. For an unverified wall/readout the corresponding assertion is conditional on that admission.

*Proof.* Before any later subset re-filing, the original first-clean source localization has its finite classical term and connected coefficients on native X from CMP116 (2.14),(2.41). From (7.122)–(7.124), after removing β₀H_b(U), their first-source norms are bounded by a rooted exponentially summable constant on the smaller native old chart: log j and the centered Hessian variation have that property by the walk and source estimates in §§7.25,7.32. A fixed compact moment extraction preserves this old-coordinate bound.

For the second-source jet the displaced critical term in (7.124) is

At fixed one old birth and root their additional localizations are estimated by the original supported Cauchy operations of LFR II (1.65)–(1.69), retaining the native connecting factors for activated wall cubes. Equivalently for a specific record use its actual absolute majorant in (1.91) with those bounded functions inserted. The assertion for this sector is for source pieces in the returned component and its attached carriers, not a change to the unmarked weight outside them.

Insert these proper first/second coefficients into (1.91). The zero term of Proposition 7.117 is absent. The first derivative costs a bounded recordwise quantum proper difference. For the second derivative there is its inherited second row plus the product of the two proper first rows, once on a common returned component. Formula (7.183) divides by the full signed bracket and gives (7.185); the product-of-means subtraction has two rare factors at this fixed home. No lower bound on an individual signed activity or conditional mass is used. The local outer action term cancels nowhere else by this argument.

For a deterministic pin tag of value m in one disjoint returning subrecord class, a useful check is exact. If B_tag is that class's *undivided signed weight* before inserting m, its tagged ratio is `1+(e^{sm}−1)B_tag/B`. The corresponding rows are `mπ` and `m²π(1−π)`, π=B_tag/B. This isolates an actual physical H contribution passing through a return boundary, rather than only a blocked test example. The nonlocal covariance/old-current terms on different recorded supports, summation over all old roots, cases with live neighbors, and the complete outer normalized mean are still required for the amended interface.

### 7.69 A rare marked return with other components still live

The optional second integration in LFR II, printed pp.391–392, is needed when the returning component coexists with large components that survive this transition. Even at fixed exterior data, the live variables can change the proper conditional mean. Exponentiating only the curly bracket of (1.72) would miss that change.

**Theorem 7.119 (one prescribed healed body in the two original expansions).** In the actual R-operation (1.72), fix the new exterior determining record, a family of still-live components Y_i, and a particular admissible returning body X_* with its fixed native position and shape outside their union. Apply all the T′(Y_i) operations as in (1.103), holding constant the exterior factors in (1.72) preceding these operations. Write D for this whole integrated factor at zero source on the original unmarked admissible domain. The following marked readouts are allowed. When X_* occurs, M is a bounded function of its original (1.71) integration record and its outer field on that support, with |M|≤K in the real comparison of (1.73) and on the native analytic extension needed for (1.99). Its insertion must preserve the localization of this body as used in (1.91). It may also select a subclass of the interior histories of that same body by an indicator on their discrete labels. The localization condition excludes insertions whose evaluation would require a further unrecorded region. Denote the undivided contribution with this indicated insertion by D[M;X_*]. Then, uniformly in the fixed admissible live family,
`|D[M;X_*]/D| ≤ C K exp[−p₀(g_k)]`.   (7.186)
The claim uses the native weak interval and decay slack of both constructions culminating in (1.98) and (1.104). It does not require an absolute lower bound on any T′(Y_i)1.

*Proof.* Put a factor 1+sM in T′(X_*) precisely if this prescribed returning body occurs. Use no factor in any T′(Y_i). Before Mayer expansion the family of disjoint returning components contains X_* at most once, so the exact combined expression is affine:
`D(s)=D+sD[M;X_*]`.
We will prove that D(s) has no zero for |s|≤c exp[p₀(g_k)]/K, with c fixed. The case K=0 is immediate.

In the first expansion leave the domain supports, the D-family of Mayer edges in (1.91), and all other field factors exactly in place. The absolute record majorant (1.92) for a term containing X_* picks up at most 1+|s|K from (1.73). It is essential here that we multiply the *body measure*, before it acts on the full integrand. No division by a Mayer factor is involved. In (1.95), with p=p₀(g_k), retain the full exp[−3p/2] at that distinguished body. It has no placement sum: for a fixed polymer X′, remove precisely X_* from the unordered q-tuple in that subseries. The q−1 remaining bodies have the very same upper placement sum (1.96), with their unrestricted estimate exp[−p(q−1)/2]. Its exponential in |X′ outside ∪Y_i| is absorbed as in the printed proof. The distinguished factor costs at most (1+c exp p)exp[−3p/2]≤C exp[−p/2]. All tree/outer-volume factors of (1.95), and the factor c₀ there, are kept. For the unmarked part use (1.97) itself. Thus the same (1.97) estimates hold with small uniform prefactor bounded by
`C max{α^{1/3}, exp(−p/2)}`
and the same native tree rate. When X′ meets the fixed live family the case q=0 still has its original α^{1/3}; it did not acquire a marked factor. When X′ is disjoint the weakened exp(−p/2) is sufficient. Absolute uniform convergence of the original connected series gives (1.98) and (1.99) with these new small prefactors. Localization on X and the field domain persist term by term: fixing the position of X_* breaks translation covariance of a coefficient but neither changes its bound nor its dependency set. Each boundary coefficient continues to contain its original complete incident live domains.

Split these coefficients exactly as at (1.100)–(1.103). Those disjoint from the live region factor out as an exponential. The remaining operations are the normalized T′(Y_i)/(T′(Y_i)1) acting on exp of the boundary coefficients. In the second primary Mayer proof on printed p.391 the absolute price for each such normalized operation is at most e³, from (1.75). Its input smallness is a constant times the first expansion's boundary prefactor, with the geometric decay rate reduced by the specified β/4 slack. We have changed only that small prefactor and left every geometry, including the fixed Y_i, unchanged. Taking the original weak interval small enough supplies this same second expansion. In particular there is no new sum over Y_i in this second exponentiation. Its connected logarithm converges absolutely throughout the s-disc. The combined result is a product of the nonzero original T′(Y_i)1 and the two exponentials, the same expression as (1.104) before its exterior prefactors. It cannot vanish on this disc. This argument does not use a pointwise small-phase bound on the sum of boundary coefficients over a large live region. The second exponentiation is what allows such a large region.

If D[M;X_*]≠0, the affine polynomial has its unique zero at s=−D/D[M;X_*]. The zero exclusion just proved implies (7.186). This divides by the actual full signed sum after the live integrations, including all compatible returns. Balaban, LFR II, printed pp. 378–380, 388–392, (1.71)–(1.75), (1.90)–(1.104). ∎

**Corollary 7.120 (same-body second logarithmic row including the live-variable covariance).** Give this one body its literal conditional source exp[tM+uN+tuH] when present. Write π(F)=D[F;X_*]/D. Its first derivative is π(M), and its mixed second logarithmic derivative is
`π(MN+H)−π(M)π(N)`.   (7.187)
Consequently its magnitude is at most C exp(−p)[K_M K_N+K_H]+C² exp(−2p) K_M K_N, under the support hypotheses of Theorem 7.119 for the indicated products. Differentiating the unexpanded (1.72) proves the identity; Theorem 7.119 bounds each full ratio separately. In particular M and N sharing one returning body spend the main return factor once. For real records this includes the covariance of the conditional means over the live variables, because the combined operator in π has already performed their integration. For complex analytic records the same formula is a signed identity.

The blocked plaquette of §7.67 on a wholly retained X_* stencil fits this theorem directly, even with other live components. The fine-pin cancellation of Proposition 7.117 also remains exact on any such admitted local record where the pinned star and its identical added outer completion are maintained when the live fields vary. A proper old coefficient actually contained in the body exponent V(X_*⁻) can be applied as M after taking its first source derivative there. A proper term in a crossing wall V(Y), however, generally enters a Mayer vertex, and its derivative cannot be placed inside T′(X_*) as a bounded multiplicative factor by this theorem. Those nonlocal crossing kernels, the outer T″/new-action factors, the sum over possible distinguished bodies and their roots, and the comparison across different exterior records are still part of I-1M. In particular (7.186) supplies no uniform distant-tail susceptibility estimate for the complete original measure.

### 7.70 A marked crossing interaction at the same return

The preceding argument can keep an actual crossing wall rather than assign its derivative to an interior body measure. The relevant bound is a norm on the same connecting support that enters printed (1.68). It is not the absolute size of a completed scalar on a different determining record.

on all the native configurations used for this edge. One may sum over an admissible family of such Y of the original class, using a common K and one labelled copy per original Y. Denote this sum on the record by M_tot. Then

Neither the fixed X_* placement nor the requirement that it occurs is discarded before its exp[−3p/2] is extracted from (1.95). Thus throughout |s|≤c α_* exp(p)/K the marked subseries again has the prefactor C exp(−p/2) in the intermediate bound, with the usual native decay. The unmarked T′(Y_i) operations and the second expansion (1.103) are handled exactly as in Theorem 7.119. The affine zero exclusion gives (7.188). For the joint product use 1+s M_tot N_tot and two typed mandatory edges in the active summand, both incident on X_*. The charge |s|K_1K_2/α_*² is made once; both edge decays are left in the native graph estimate. Coincident supports are permitted as two typed edges. This proves the product bound. ∎

For an actual first derivative M(Y)=∂_t V_t(Y)|₀ on the chosen returning records, the pre-Mayer derivative of exp[Σ_Y V_t(Y)] is its insertion in the *undivided* weight. No quotient by exp V(Y)−1 is used; that factor can vanish at the reference field. The second derivative has an inherited ∂²V on one wall and a product of two first derivatives. Equations (7.187)–(7.188) give the same single bank for the signed, fully integrated same-body response when these marks have the required norms. In particular, for the adjacent actual wall Y⁺ in the true-edge experiment of T2, adjoining its fixed layer of one current M-cube has bounded d_{k,Z'} on the records where X_* is its protected component and the original incidence holds. Its proper old term must still be paired with the actual completed exterior A′_k value. For admitted readouts, a first-H quantum term with the original bounded proper sup norm at this fixed birth gives O(exp(−p)) at this adjacent wall. A classical proper difference bounded by Cβ₀ times the sum of the squared old forces on its two records costs that very bound times exp(−p); the larger-wall force cannot be assumed to equal the small-wall one. Proposition 7.117 supplies the separate exact zero only on the identical fine-pin/outer pair. Neither (7.185) nor (7.188) proves that all such old walls enjoy the required joint norm after all earlier mixed steps. These estimates leave separate the unrare, added exterior source and the sum over the new external determining records.

### 7.71 Summing the shapes through a prescribed home

**Theorem 7.122 (all returning shapes at a home and the two-home decomposition).** In the situation of Theorem 7.119, fix one current localization cube x outside the still-live union. On each native returning body X containing x take a possibly different readout M_X of the same allowed type, bounded by K. Write M_x for its value if that body occurs and zero otherwise. There is at most one such body per configuration. For the whole integrated factor at fixed exterior record,
`|D[M_x]/D|≤C K exp(−p).`   (7.189)
The same estimate holds for the **sum of absolute values** of the signed normalized contributions of all the individual shapes at this home. Factors of modulus at most one can distinguish interior record subclasses with the same body, provided they depend only on its recorded variables. A connecting proper insertion of the type of Proposition 7.121 can replace the interior readout, with the additional fixed smallness-ceiling cost there and the same uniform native connecting norm. The constants refer to the current home, not to a sum over all fine roots in that cube.

*Proof.* Mark all bodies containing x, with the factor 1+sM_X. Affineness before Mayer still holds, since two disjoint simultaneous bodies cannot contain x. In the marked part of (1.95), q≥1 and the family identifies at most one distinguished body, without choosing its shape in advance. For |s|K≤c exp p the marked part is bounded using
`c exp(p) exp(−3pq/2) ≤ c exp(−pq/2),  q≥1.`
Now perform **all** placements by (1.96); its exponential cardinality is paid by the last volume term in (1.95) exactly as before. The prefactor c, chosen sufficiently small independently of p, supplies the small input formerly furnished by exp(−p/2) in the fixed-shape argument. The unmarked part keeps the primary bounds. The same second exponentiation and affine-root argument give (7.189). For each fixed exterior evaluation, choose an independent unit scalar per shape to align all its signed normalized contributions. The resulting marks still obey the same K and support conditions; these selected scalars are constants in the native analytic-domain proof. Taking the bound on that marked sum proves the absolute-shape statement. The same argument works on disjoint discrete classes of the recorded body. For the crossing insertion retain the extra supported edge and its α_* cost in this placement calculation, as in Proposition 7.121. ∎

For x,y outside the still-live union let M_x,N_y be two such body readouts with bounds K_x,K_y. Define their full connected response as the mixed derivative for exp[s M_x+t N_y] on the underlying records, with zero outside the indicated occurrences. It satisfies the exact decomposition
`∂_s∂_t log D(s,t)|₀ = C_dist(x,y) + D[M_x N_y ; same body]/D,`
`|C_dist(x,y)|≤C K_x K_y exp(−2p),   |D[M_x N_y ; same body]/D|≤C K_x K_y exp(−p).`   (7.190)
An already formed second coefficient on that same body is added in the last term. The first quantity includes subtraction of the complete two first means, as appropriate to the normalized signed sum.

*Proof.* Instead of exponentiating inside a body, put `1+s M_X 1_{x∈X}+t N_X 1_{y∈X}` on every returning X, taking value 1 if neither home belongs. This drops just the same-body mixed coefficient of the original exponential. The undivided integrated polynomial is separately affine in s,t and has the normalized form P=1+A s+B t+C st. The coefficient C uses two distinct bodies. In the absolute majorant for its nonconstant part there are at most two marked insertions on distinct bodies, costing at most c exp p per active body at radii R_x=c exp(p)/K_x and R_y=c exp(p)/K_y. If both homes lie on one body it has only the sum of the two single marks. There are at most three possible nonconstant choices per whole disjoint family (x only, y only, or both on different bodies). In (1.95) each term with v active bodies, 1≤v≤q, satisfies c^v exp(pv)exp(−3pq/2)≤c^v exp(−pq/2). Thus (1.96) again performs all placements, leaving the small factor O(c), and both original exponentiations converge. P has no zero on the bidisc.

In particular |A|≤1/R_x and |B|≤1/R_y by restriction to a coordinate axis. For each |t|<R_y the affine polynomial in s gives |A+Ct|≤|1+Bt|/R_x≤2/R_x. The one-variable coefficient bound then gives |C|≤2/(R_xR_y). Hence |C_dist|=|C−AB|≤3/(R_x R_y). For the missing common-body term, at home x require y∈X and insert the single product M_X N_X, bounded by K_xK_y. Theorem 7.122 gives its stated estimate. These arguments apply also to coincident homes; in that case C=0. The same proof with one labelled connecting edge per marked readout uses Proposition 7.121 on each active body only when the incidence/majorants are certified on these actual records. ∎

The two-body gain is uniform over the fixed live neighbors but has no stated summable separation factor in y. It therefore cannot be summed over arbitrary lattice momenta as a susceptibility proof. For example, in the second primary CE (1.103), two marks at different locations can be connected through one fixed live Y_i; that step only gives decay outside Y_i. To recover a physical-distance kernel one must keep and estimate the actual distribution of live Y_i and the outer mean after (1.104). The result above removes the *placement sum of a single marked return through its home* from that residual. It does not sum opportunities at different scales or the later live records.

### 7.72 An extensive signed bound for a source summed over all current returns

**Theorem 7.123 (polynomial zero count at a mixed transition).** Keep the fixed external determining record and arbitrary fixed live family of Theorem 7.119. Every possible healed body X may now carry its actual record observable A_X, including the chosen source weights and summed roots assigned to that body. Assume its native (1.71), (1.73), (1.99) analytic/real-comparison sup bound is U, uniformly among those possible bodies, and that it is localized on their records as in Theorem 7.119. Let m be an upper bound on the number of nonzero A_X in any one compatible returning family. It is enough to take m equal to the number of current localization cubes; if every marked body must contain a cube of a prescribed set E one may instead take |E|. Include exp[s A_X] on every occurrence and write D_s for the entire resulting factor after all fixed live integrations. Then
`|log(D_s/D_0)| ≤ C m exp(−p)       (|s|≤c₀/U),`
`|∂_s^j log D_s|₀ ≤ C m exp(−p) j! (C U)^j,   j≥1.`   (7.191)
The logarithm is continued from s=0. If each recorded root has bound K, each healed body has at most b eligible roots (counting its actual old multiplicities), and |f_x|≤1, use U=bK. For Fourier modes or their real or imaginary parts, (7.191) bounds the second response of their **whole sum over the healed bodies at this transition**, including all between-body terms and live-variable means. Its spatial normalization is the number of current cubes, with the explicit factor exp(−p)b²K². It makes no estimate for sources on the exterior or the still-live bodies themselves.

*Proof.* Temporarily insert on every possible returning body the factor 1+u(exp[s A_X]−1), irrespective of its location. At u=1 this is exactly the required simultaneous source, and at u=0 all of it is absent. Choose c₀ so that |exp[s A_X]−1|≤1 for |s|≤c₀/U. On a term of (1.91) with q integrated bodies, the extra absolute price is at most (1+|u|)^q. In (1.95) for |u|≤c exp p this is bounded with the body bank by
`(1+|u|)^q exp(−3pq/2) ≤ (c+exp(−p))^q exp(−pq/2).`
If q=0 no source was inserted and its original c₀ of (1.95) (here an edge-count prefactor distinct from our radius c₀) is untouched. For q≥1 choose c small and the weak interval so c+exp(−p) is less than the fixed allowed smallness ceiling. Perform (1.96) on all q placements as printed; the final volume damping pays its exponential. The connected log and boundary terms of (1.98)–(1.99) therefore have the needed native rates and small prefactors. The second expansion (1.103)–(1.104) again proves nonvanishing of the whole integrated expression for this u-disc without dividing by separate large-field masses.

At fixed s the original expression, *before* Mayer differentiation, is a polynomial P_s(u)=D(u,s)/D_0 of degree at most m, with P_s(0)=1. All allowed configurations obey the same degree bound, regardless of how many histories each body can contain. Accordingly P_s(u)=Π_{l=1}^{m'}(1−u/z_l) with m'≤m and every |z_l|≥c exp p (the constant case has no factors). For c exp p≥2 the logarithm continued from u=0 satisfies
`|log P_s(1)|≤Σ_l 2/|z_l|≤(2/c)m exp(−p).`
This branch is holomorphic in s on the stated disc: it is equally the integral over real u∈[0,1] of (∂_u P_s)/P_s, where the denominator is nonzero. At s=0 it vanishes. Cauchy now proves all inequalities (7.191). No rooted cluster counting inside a live region or assumed decay across it is used. The polynomial degree, not a termwise estimate of the unmarked extensive pressure, gives the volume factor. ∎

The same proof admits a source already depending analytically on s inside each healed body: replace exp[s A_X]−1 by its actual source multiplier minus 1, bounded by one on a disc r, vanishing at zero, and preserving that body's native support. The conclusion is (7.191) with C U replaced by 1/r. This includes a bounded inherited second row on that domain when it is genuinely internal to the body measure. If one only knows derivatives, one can interpolate its first two jets by a quadratic polynomial multiplier on a smaller explicitly bounded disc when just those two derivatives are required. Crossing derivatives estimated in §7.70 need a joint bound on their *sum per connected body* before using this all-location pressure conclusion. Nothing here gives such a bound or cancels the variation of the entire conditional mean over new exterior histories. The result does give a signed extensive estimate without requiring the open all-history source pressure or the impossible physical H disc.

### 7.73 Physical compact readouts in a fixed early window

**Corollary 7.124 (summed, completely stored microscopic H returns at bounded depth).** Fix k₀. In (1.72) at k≤k₀ assign to a healed body of diameter at most 100 MR_k the fine H roots b whose *entire original* matching stencil is integrated, stored, or explicitly pinned within that body's record. Include only the literal physical readouts of §7.22; an already integrated nonlinear old H coefficient cannot be replaced by a new loop under this rule. Take |f_b|≤1 and set A_X=Σ_b f_b h_b on those records. This is a proper sector of the original source by its indicated record incidence. On the common real compact or admitted complex chart for these complete stencils, the signed conditional variance of this entire sector after integrating all the fixed live neighbors satisfies
`|∂_s² log D_s|₀ ≤ C n_k⁴ exp(−p₀(g_k)) β₀² (100 M R_k L^k)^8.`   (7.192)
In particular it is O_{k₀}(n₀⁴) on the stated weak trajectory, uniformly in the specified exterior record. The same bound applies to the separate real and imaginary parts of a plane wave. The assertion includes all simultaneous healed shapes in this size range and all compatible unmarked returns.

*Proof.* Each original finite staple/trace expression on a real compact record is bounded by Cβ₀; its holomorphic continuation on the admitted fixed compact tube has the same size with a different C. For a retained original stencil this is the actual H_b, including the source normalization in (7.102a); it counts no derivative of an earlier conditional law. The number of fine roots in a cube of edge 100MR_k current units with its fixed collar is at most C(100 M R_k L^k)^4. Thus A_X in its original (1.71) integral has absolute bound U=Cβ₀(100 M R_k L^k)^4. Set A_X=0 for the other shapes or absent stencils. There are at most C n_k⁴ disjoint marked bodies in any compatible family. Equation (7.191) gives (7.192). For bounded k the ordinary inverse-coupling step bound of I-0 gives g₀⁻²≤g_k⁻²+C k₀. The native R_k is polylogarithmic in g_k⁻², and p₀(g_k) grows faster than log g_k⁻² on this weak trajectory. Consequently exp(−p₀(g_k))β₀² R_k^8 is bounded uniformly, and n_k⁴≤n₀⁴. The scale index k₀ is fixed before the cutoff is removed. ∎

For k unbounded the same literal count divided by n₀⁴ has the extra factor L^{4k} from the squared per-body root bound. The elementary size estimate alone therefore cannot be used at all ages. One needs the actual saved source norms of the integrated old packets, or a second-moment estimate inside the long-lived stored record that improves its squared root count. Furthermore a bound on ∂_s² log D_s for each fixed exterior record does not bound the covariance over different exterior records of ∂_s log D_s. These are two distinct steps in comparing (7.192) to the ordinary full-torus susceptibility.

### 7.74 Which homogeneous selector the clean estimates use

The CMP109 pure conditional calculations fix the cutoff of that construction (e.g. P_out=ε₁/g in (7.64)). The complete CMP119 branching construction uses a smaller selector even when Ω₁=Λ₁=T. Its first step has an exact coordinate dictionary. CMP119 printed p.249, immediately after (1.14), says the linearization changes only the determined bonds b₀(c). Removing the delta functions gives A′=CA; A denotes the **independent** bonds Ω₁*=Ω₁ minus these pivots. Printed p.250 (1.18) restricts the supremum of *these A variables* to P₀=δ₀/g₀, of order p₀(g₀). On the globally clean branch the second factor of (1.19) equals one on this domain and the changes (1.22) near the large-field boundary are absent. Thus the retained cutoff is a product of fixed independent-coordinate balls in this case. It does not move under a change of the external coarse background. Balaban, CMP119, printed pp. 247–252, (1.14)–(1.24).

**Proposition 7.125 (finite source jets at the genuine clean first cutoff).** On the homogeneous first-step physical-background chart with the spare margins of §7.13, take an external q for which the original clean constrained fluctuation action has the native unmarked CMP116 localized comparison there, including its indicated holomorphic extension in q. Let F_{P₀} and F_out be the two conditional logarithms with the smaller and larger independent-coordinate selectors, separated from the common exterior characteristic function. For the actual local first H source and |η_b|≤c g₀² the nonzero conditional logs have a difference bounded in the native connected activity norm by C exp(−c′P₀²). Consequently, for each fixed source order m, the difference of their rooted m-th coefficients costs at most C_m g₀^{-2m}exp(−c′P₀²) with the usual spare support weights. Fixed-order external q derivatives obey the corresponding Cauchy estimate on a strictly smaller admitted q-chart. In particular a g₀²-normalized one-source, two-q Hessian differs by O(exp(−c′P₀²)) at fixed physical q-radius. This is a finite-jet assertion, not a fixed nonflat H disc on every shrinking CMP119 record.

*Proof.* On the larger native first-step analytic tube the original finite plaquette words for H_b have uniformly bounded dimensionless size. For |η_b|≤c g₀² their scalar perturbation η_b β₀ H_b has uniformly small absolute norm on a fixed supported stencil, including on a spare complex physical-background chart. Keep the actual hard selectors on the independent starred coordinates. In the difference of the two localized logs apply the failed-selector comparison of Lemma 7.25 with inner radius P₀: an extra local defect occurs only where some independent coordinate exceeds P₀. The unchanged conditioned native Gaussian reserve there pays exp(−c′P₀²), using the joint-tail comparison before resumming the connected coefficients. All source, measure and field-comparison constants are bounded on this source disc; there is no source-induced translation and no derivative of a selector. Cauchy gives the m source factors g₀^{-2m} and the inverse spare q-distances for exterior variations. The first physical H expectation is the derivative with the true field held fixed during insertion; it retains its complete vacuum/action/contact terms. Since P₀ grows as a fixed power of log g₀⁻² greater than one, this tail beats every fixed inverse power of g₀. The physical q chart is an extension of the conditional activity; a discontinuous outer χ factor is not analytically differentiated. ∎

There is a separate units issue at subsequent scales. CMP119 printed p.265 after (3.4) defines δ_k=g_k(A₁/A₀)p₀(g_k). Printed p.267 before (3.15) explicitly rescales A′_k=g_k A_k and displays the canonical quadratic form in A_k. In that notation the displayed (3.16) on printed p.268 nevertheless reads `|A_k(b)|<δ_k`, without the inverse g_k that occurs in (1.18). LFR II printed p.380 evaluates the corresponding R_j-failure by exp[−γ₀δ_j²g_j^{-2}(LM₂R_j)^{-d}|R_j|]. A canonical Gaussian cut at δ_j alone would give a δ_j² cost instead. The mutually consistent interpretation, used when importing that native rare factor here, is the physical criterion `|g_k A_k|<δ_k`, equivalently a canonical cutoff P_k=δ_k/g_k. This is an explicitly identified correction of units, not a literal transcription of (3.16). Both alternatives partition unity, but the much smaller literal canonical cutoff would not have the quoted rare-bank proof. CMP119, printed pp. 265, 267–269, (3.4), (3.15)–(3.20), LFR II, printed p. 380.

Theorems 7.102, 7.107 and 7.112 give homogeneous results on their stated fixed analytic and cutoff margins. Under the consistent repeated selector, the cutoff tails at unshifted finite-order insertions are again smaller than any coupling power; this follows from P_k of polylogarithmic size and the same native joint Gaussian comparison *if its full inherited interaction hypotheses hold on the required common chart*. Identifying the whole repeated fixed-margin proof with the specific CMP119 empty-wall sector also requires that common unmarked extended-domain induction, the carried field-dependent scalar, and the outer χ multipliers on their real supports. Proposition 7.125 supplies the first-step comparison. For a translated source saddle additionally require its displacement to fit the actual g_kP_k margin. The mixed results in §§7.67–7.73 take the actual printed LFR II operations (1.71), (1.90), (1.103) and their stated unmarked majorants as input and use no comparison to the CMP109 fixed-selector law.

### 7.75 The promoted effective source on the next exterior record

**Theorem 7.126 (carrierwise signed promotion from all healed bodies).** Under Theorem 7.123 write the actual final expression of (1.104), before the exterior action and its unchanged factors, as
`D(u,s)=[Π_i T′(Y_i)1] exp[Σ_X R_X(u,s)+Σ_X B_X(u,s)]`.
Here R_X are the first expansion's terms disjoint from the remaining large region, and B_X the resulting boundary terms including the normalized second expansion. `|R_X(1,s)−R_X(0,0)| ≤ C exp(−p) a_X,`

*Proof.* Keep the native coefficient filing: in the first expansion each term is the connected log (7.13) of the primary article cited in the proof of (1.99), with its localization; in the second use exactly the new connected coefficients distinguished after (1.103). These expansions, established in the proof of Theorem 7.123, converge absolutely under the same geometric majorants throughout |u|≤R=c exp p and |s|≤c₀/U. The existing proofs of (1.99) and of the final boundary expansion are termwise bounds by these majorants, not a bound only on their sum over X. The all-body multiplier preserves each connected support because it acts only on the T′ measure of that same body. At u=0 the coefficient is exactly its original zero-source value for every s; at s=0 it is independent of u. The explicit series fixes the logarithm normalization and its individual carriers across this comparison.

For either coefficient F_X, Cauchy in u bounds its m-th Taylor coefficient at zero by a_X R^{-m}. Therefore
`|F_X(1,s)−F_X(0,0)|≤a_X/(R−1)≤C exp(−p)a_X.`
Cauchy on a slightly smaller s-disc and on the actual external directions gives the stated derivatives. The operation T′(Y_i)1 preceding the exponent is unchanged by these source pieces; its possible smallness was handled by (1.75) in the second expansion. For disjoint R_X a fixed number of freely summed slots inside X can be counted by |X|^l and absorbed in a spare ordinary carrier rate. In contrast d_{k,∪Y_i} gives no equivalent price for slots anywhere deep inside a large live Y_i. Such sums cannot be inferred from (7.193). Balaban, LFR II, printed pp. 390–392, (1.98)–(1.104). ∎

For the complete compact marks at bounded old depth in (7.192), the output from their healed interiors is thus a small analytic **exterior** coefficient as well as a small integrated pressure. A finite factor δ^{-l} with δ^{-1} at most polynomial in g_k⁻¹ and powers of log g_k⁻² is absorbed by a fraction of exp(−p); this follows by taking logarithms and using p/(log g_k⁻²)→∞. This is a concrete R-5 promotion for this marked sector. It does not identify the saved engineering grade of nonlocal inherited H packets. ### 7.76 The next clean integration after an earlier return

The resulting localized logarithm, including the separately carried analytic background and identity scalars, is holomorphic in u on |u|≤c′ exp(p/2), |s|≤c₀/U. In particular if L'_k(V),L''_k(V) denote the two previously promoted log rows as functions of the intermediate field V, direct differentiation of the physical next integral gives
`∂_s² log Z_{k+1}(s)|₀ = ⟨L''_k(V)⟩_{next} + ⟨L'_k(V)^2⟩_{next} − ⟨L'_k(V)⟩_{next}².`

This is a return followed by a small conditional transformation, with the actual fresh R coefficient passed between them. The source-free selector, readout-domain and unmarked conditioning hypotheses in the proposition are substantive. If one keeps a neighboring old B carrier, the shrinking mixed domains (3.43) and its original nonlocal pinned data must be checked on the next transformation. Even in a sequence of regular steps the loss of a factor two in the exponent at every use of (7.194) would eventually exhaust the initial bank. A depth-uniform continuation needs a single analytic budget propagated with summable losses, together with the exterior action and all marginal partners.

### 7.77 Internal sites of one still-live component

Fix an actual previous R transition at which the external T″ rough region is empty and one component Y survives in the second class of (1.72); the first class, summed over in that formula, contains the earlier healed sources. Take an eligible Y inside a cube of side 100 MR_k. This is the size condition (i) for the regions subjected to the preparatory operation; the size assumption suffices even if the remaining external record has further restrictions. The number v(Y) of current M-cubes in Y is at most C(100R_k)^4. The next determining record has this genuine rough component, possibly with other new failures. A new fluctuation variable at the T step is integrated only in the small part Λ_{k+1}. It does not independently vary every fine link in the whole retained Y.

**Lemma 7.128 (recovering an ordinary carrier for this live body).** Suppose the prior conditional source is a complete, gauge-invariant marked H readout of §§7.69–7.73 through a fixed current home x outside Y. Preserve that home in the record before the (1.103) integration. In (7.193) retain the individual source-dependent terms on their original connected supports. At each fixed birth k, and on the same old admissible chart, their source difference has ordinary weighted carrier norm bounded by
`C exp[−p+C₁ v(Y)]`   (7.195)
on its declared source disc; j-th source derivatives acquire j!(CU)^j. This estimate takes the sup over a prescribed current home and permits an absolute sum over all its carriers, with a spare ordinary exp(ηd_k(X)) weight. The native carrier rate is chosen with the normal lattice-animal counting slack. A completely stored, bounded-depth physical H first birth on the earlier returned side of an actual surviving component is one example. A crossing proper source requires the previous true-domain estimate of §7.70. A sum of older fine roots per current home still carries its U price. The cost in (7.195) comes from the actual size of Y, not from pretending that a prior decay path ran through its interior.

*Proof.* In the connected first and second expansions an activity depending on the source at x contains the designated body and its home. Its cluster support still contains x after integrating Y in (1.103). A contributing boundary cluster meets Y and has connected union X in the ordinary current cube incidence, as in the second Mayer construction. The prior carrier bounds have spare decay in the length outside Y; see LFR II (1.67), (1.93), (1.99), and the modification after (1.103). For clarity approximate this length conservatively by the sum of the tree lengths of the connected components of X outside Y, in M-cube units. If a component has n cubes, a tree intersecting all of them has length at least c n−C, since each segment of length M meets only a bounded number of lattice cubes. The number of exterior components is at most C v(Y) if Y is incident: each component touches a cube face or a fixed-width incidence collar of Y, and there are only C v(Y) such cells. Thus, with D_out any of the preceding native lengths controlling these connected pieces,
`|X|_M ≤ C[1+D_out+v(Y)],    d_k(X)≤C|X|_M.`
If Y is absent the usual connected estimate applies. This argument allows a singleton exterior component to have zero individual length. The number of connected n-cube animals containing x is at most c_d^n, by encoding the forward and backward steps of a spanning tree. Hence, with a smaller η>0 than the spare native rate, summing the bound in (7.193) yields (7.195). The same estimate with a fixed polynomial in |X| follows by another fixed reduction of rate. One may equivalently choose the unmarked κ large before fixing these rates, as allowed in CMP119 (2.31)–(2.42). This proof never sums over a location for the fixed Y. A formula with several fixed live components includes the size of **all the incident ones** in the cost; dropping those sizes does not follow.

The previous weak choice 2κ(100R_k)^4 ≤ c p is part of the budget used in LFR II (1.95). To use (7.195) uniformly with strong remaining smallness, specify C₁ C(100R_k)^4≤θp with θ<1 on the weak interval; it is sufficient that the chosen polylogarithmic exponents have R_k^4=o(p₀(g_k)). This extra numerical margin refers to the actual constants in our animal conversion. With it the initial small amplitude is exp[−p+C₁v(Y)] and no further fraction of p has been spent. Without this numerical margin (7.195) remains the displayed estimate with its actual size price. ∎

**Lemma 7.129 (sum of slots on the true fluctuation polydisc).** On each localized output Y₀ in CMP119 (3.43) the independent canonical A variables have support in Y₀∩Λ_{k+1}^{(k)*} and sup norm less than C₁p₁(g_k). At a point with uniform slack d_A in this norm, any holomorphic bounded coefficient G on the simultaneous source/field chart satisfies
`Σ_y |∂_{A_y}G|≤C ||G||/d_A,   sup_z Σ_y |∂_{A_z}∂_{A_y}G|≤C ||G||/d_A².`   (7.196)
Here each matrix component can be measured in a fixed finite-dimensional basis. The estimates have no number-of-sites factor. They also hold with z one fixed source coordinate of radius r, replacing the first d_A in the second estimate by r. Conversely, if all source coordinates have a simultaneous sup-polydisc of radius r, the same sign argument sums the source-home index with a fixed field slot. This does not give the unrestricted double absolute sum of a Hessian.

*Proof.* For scalar complex derivatives choose phases v_y of modulus one so that every term ∂_{A_y}G v_y is nonnegative real. The direction v belongs to the closed unit sup-ball, up to a fixed color-basis norm constant. Evaluate G(A+tv) and apply the one-variable Cauchy inequality. In the second claim use two variables, one in direction v and one along the fixed coordinate z, on discs of radii d_A/3 in the independent chart. The mixed derivative is exactly the indicated signed row. Repeated or identical coordinates give the same estimate with the harmless combinatorial constant. The product domain in (3.43) is explicit on printed p.276. This proof applies to its independent A slots. For external constrained U,J variations it only applies to a separately verified simultaneous chart of the proposed directions, including all gauge, layer and raw-target conditions. It cannot assign independent phases to redundant or fixed fine links. CMP119, printed pp. 262, 276, (2.42), (3.43). ∎

### 7.78 The promoted boundary source through the next mixed T

**Theorem 7.130 (one old live component, next genuine mixed integration).** Use the single old live Y of Lemma 7.128 and a previously completed physical source whose boundary coefficients satisfy (7.193) on the original old boundary analytic domain. In particular take the simultaneous compact H sources of Corollary 7.124, selecting their literal stored stencils on the earlier healed bodies, with total absolute source readout per body bounded by U. Introduce independent coefficients η_x for their indicated homes, normalizing them so the simultaneous sup-disc is |η_x|≤r=c/U. The estimates (7.123),(7.193) are uniform on that polydisc: their proofs use the sum of the absolute readout bounds in each body and permit independent complex signs. Keep just the resulting promoted **boundary family** F(η)=Σ_X F_X(η) from (1.104), F_X(0)=0. Its old norm from (7.195) is ε=C exp(−p+C₁v(Y)), with the stated spare ordinary carrier rate. Every source label in a coefficient is still in its support. Include the other source-free returned terms and the positive factors T′_k(Y)1 in their original positions.

Fix an admissible *mixed* determining record at k+1, with the old rough component retained in its covered exterior and Λ_{k+1} nonempty. At its next T take the original kernel (3.15),(3.26)–(3.27), including its true gauge, field normalization, old large-region operations and native selectors. Use its admitted boundary domains (2.34)–(2.42),(3.43) and the original unmarked conditioning bounds. The following bounds concern this boundary-source contribution at a fixed new outer record. With r as above they give the two distinct terms in its second connected source response:
`sup_x Σ_y |⟨F''_{xy}(V)⟩_{next}| ≤ C_step ε r⁻²,`
`sup_x Σ_y |Cov_{next}(F'_x(V),F'_y(V))| ≤ C_step ε² r⁻².`   (7.197)
Here primes mean derivatives of the previous promoted log, V is its actual old readout through the next transformation, and the averages are under the same unmarked new normalized law. Source coordinates with no contributing old home have zero derivative. A fixed source root with β or normalization costs is included through r; for the bounded-depth compact H choice r⁻¹ can be taken to be Cβ₀(100MR_k L^k)^4. The result is conditional on the displayed *native* input, not on a factorization of the marked response, an independent estimate of a small denominator, or a root-decay assumption inside Y.

*The true readout.* In (3.15) the boundary contribution is B_k(U_k(exp i[g_k C A_k−hD(g_k C A_k)] V^(k)),...)−B_k(U_{k+1},...), with the background B_k(U_{k+1},...) filed in the outside action. The original fixed old fluctuation labels are retained where applicable. Denote the full old readout by V(A), its background readout by V_*, and the normalized unmarked conditional expectation by ⟨·⟩. For this promoted source the exact next log is
`F(η;V_*) + log ⟨exp[F(η;V(A))−F(η;V_*)]⟩ = log ⟨exp F(η;V(A))⟩.`   (7.198)
At the physical point the measure (3.27) is positive. For complex external variables the same identity uses the connected normalized analytic continuation on its admitted domain. The old multiplicative T′(Y)1 has no η dependence from these markers. Differentiation of (7.198) gives ⟨F''_{xy}⟩ plus the displayed covariance. In particular a new variable that is pinned in both readouts can contribute to the exterior first or second row even when it gives no fresh fluctuation derivative.

*Transfer of the bounded carrier.* After (7.195), the perturbation has the very type of B-terms in (2.40)–(2.42). This includes ordinary carrier decay, covariance under gauge transformations, and the actual old dependencies. The boundary convention resummed over fixed large components is explicitly allowed on printed p.262; the ordinary bound here restores the version used in (2.42) before taking the next step. On printed pp.275–277 the old B difference in (3.15) is expanded by (3.6),(3.7) of CMP109, then weakened and localized with the mixed cover. The substitution is evaluated on the original old boundary space; the reserved dyadic differences in (2.36)–(2.39) pay the minimizing-field displacement H_k, and the localized output has domain (3.43). Applying those linear operations to the additional small B carrier uses the same original sup estimate. The proper difference has an O(ε_k) fluctuation factor in the printed argument; it suffices here to bound that factor by a constant. No formal independent variation of fine U,J at pinned sites enters this substitution. It is important that the earlier mark is a bona fide promoted coefficient from (1.104); substituting an arbitrary old nonlinear saved kernel on an unverified chart would not meet the hypotheses. In particular we use no T2 deep-core estimate on a larger record than its verified readout.
