For a bounded inserted scalar carrier G_X of this class, integrating it against the (possibly tilted) normalized mixed law has the primary marked numerator (3.44). Its root polymer Z₀ includes the inserted carrier in the localized expansion. The unmarked polymers have the restrictions giving exactly the exclusion exponential (3.45)–(3.46). In the absolute estimate for the root, keep the old marked carrier and its old source home before summing; a weakening connector or covariance path is attached to its actual support in the mixed cover. The root may be enlarged by the old X and the supports of these connectors. The original exponential rates with a spare margin pay this union exactly as in the marked numerator/denominator construction; the fixed factor L in changing the current grid costs only fixed constants. Equivalently sum first over the inserted current support X containing x, with the input carrier slack for its finite slot count, and then sum normalized clusters touching that support using (3.45). The additional exclusion shell has O(|X|) current cells; its exp(c|X|) majorant is covered by the old ordinary carrier slack. This yields |⟨G_x⟩|≤C_step b for a family rooted at fixed x of old norm b. The same argument works under a sufficiently small complex bounded scalar perturbation in the (2.42) norm: multiply the connected Mayer edge bound by its sup perturbation, leaving the unmarked Gaussian comparison and cutoff fixed. The auxiliary s,t in (3.26) already implement this scalar boundary perturbation. At the tilted value the exclusion in (3.45) is formed with the same tilted denominator, never by a lower estimate on a different integral. For a single current-scale B birth there is no sum over prior birth scales in this bound. The constants can depend on native rates/parameters; if a particular implementation pays extra finite inverse-coupling chart factors include them in C_step. CMP119, printed pp. 260–262, 268, 271, 275–279, (2.40)–(2.42), (3.15), (3.26)–(3.27), (3.43)–(3.47).

*Both anchored rows.* For |v_y|≤1 define G_v=Σ_y v_y F'_y and H_{x,v}=Σ_y v_y F''_{xy}. Cauchy in one direction v of the simultaneous η-disc gives G_v an unpointed old (2.42) norm at most C ε/r. Cauchy in the fixed x direction gives F'_x a pointed norm C ε/r; H_{x,v} has pointed norm C ε/r² by the two-direction calculation of (7.196). The previous home survives in its carrier. Apply the preceding normalized marked estimate to H_{x,v}. For the other term tilt the actual unmarked law by exp(t G_v). The convergent normalized marked estimate gives |⟨F'_x⟩_t|≤C_step ε/r throughout |t|≤c r/ε; choosing c within the native small scalar budget keeps the perturbed B family admissible. Cauchy in t gives |Cov(F'_x,G_v)|≤C_step ε²/r². Take v_y to align the complex coefficients, separately for the two rows, at the chosen external evaluation. This proves (7.197). The same argument with a fixed finite number of independent A-slot directions on a strictly smaller (3.43) domain uses (7.196); it is not a license to select arbitrary external fine-link directions.

There is also a new *carrier filing*: using the actual connected coefficients in (3.47) before summing their last supports gives a boundary family in the next ordinary native norm with size C_step ε (on a fixed smaller η-disc). One formal way to keep this small factor intact is to multiply the whole old promoted perturbation by an interpolation w; the preceding scalar construction is uniform on |w|≤c/ε, so its u=1 physical contribution, with w restored to one, costs O(ε) by Cauchy. Here u denotes the earlier return fugacity and is already set to one. This is a numerical multiplication by C_step on the restored small norm, not a replacement of p by p/2 at each propagation. The separate background value in (7.198) must be filed as well. This proof concerns the next *T* at a mixed record. A further R operation at that scale may again collapse newly live bodies and would require its actual boundary norm. ∎

### 7.79 Keeping a returned home through arbitrary positive outer integrations

**Proposition 7.131 (the real conditional bank is paid once).** On a physical real record let x be a fixed current home with a bounded literal tag M_x when its returning body is present, zero otherwise. Let E denote that the indicated return occurs at this transition. The pre-Mayer representation (1.71)–(1.72), including the actual real integrations and any fixed still-live integrations, gives a positive conditional measure. The estimates of Theorem 7.122 for the indicator and for the bounded readouts imply, uniformly on the exterior states on which they are defined,
`0≤Pr(E|exterior)≤C e^{-p},   |m_x|=|E(M_x|exterior)|≤C K_x e^{-p},   E(|M_x|²|exterior)≤C K_x² e^{-p}.`
Here and below the indicator restricts to the represented physical return class; it is not a product of signed Mayer probabilities. Whenever the tag is defined only on a verified subset of exterior records, use the estimate there and set this selected observable to zero on its complement. Real gauge-invariant source factors permit the FP equivalence preceding (1.72) after the required group integration. On any further physical positive integration of these states, including a mixture of subsequent real determining records, the same three uniform bounds hold for its integrated first/second raw moments. The already formed mean m_x itself satisfies
`Var_{outer}(m_x)≤ C² K_x² e^{-2p}`   (7.199)
independently of the number of intervening steps. The formula is for this released home contribution, not for an exterior action term that was never part of that tag.

*Proof.* All three positive moments are integrals with a single indicated insertion inside the same marked component; for the second use |M_x|² in the real estimate, or its real polynomial continuation for a physical compact H and fixed complex source weights. Equivalently bound the positive conditional second moment by K_x² times the indicator probability. Average these pointwise inequalities with any outer positive probability kernel. This operation has sup norm one, and iteration has the same norm. At real source zero one has |m_x|²≤C²K_x²e^{-2p}; centering can only decrease its real Hilbert-space variance, proving (7.199). Conditional martingale increments of that exterior mean over nested retained records are orthogonal: their squared norms telescope to at most this same bound instead of being charged again at each scale. A compact support-dependent inactive tag can be set to zero only when its actual selected sector is specified, not as a way to erase a missing operator in the full Wilson insertion. ∎

For two different homes the same tower bounds the absolute outer covariance of their released means by C²K_xK_y exp(−2p). Summing that estimate over all y without connection information would cost the torus volume. For the boundary coefficient itself (7.195)–(7.198) are stronger at the next mixed T: they give an absolute summable second row, not just this pointwise consequence of positivity. Subsequent real averaging of an already bounded *row of conditional second moments* preserves its row bound; what must be added at every conditional-log step is the covariance of the new means at the new outer state. Formula (7.199) by itself cannot sum those covariances over all homes.

### 7.80 Physically separated still-live components at the original R

There is a different way to retain ordinary position information in the live integration of (1.103). It uses real exterior data, and can handle arbitrarily many separated live components without exp of their total volume. Here distance is in current M-cube units. Require the actual fixed components Y_i to have diameter at most C₀R, volume at most C₀R⁴ and mutual distance at least aR, where R=R_k and a>0 is fixed. This is a sufficient subclass of genuine records, including separated eligible rectangles; no separation assumption for every mixed post-R family is made.

**Theorem 7.132 (many separated live neighbors; uncollapsed physical source row).** In this real subclass take the allowable compact healed-body source family and simultaneous independent home disc of §§7.72, 7.78. For x,y outside the fixed live components, let J_{xy} be the mixed second derivative after the T′(Y_i) integrations in (1.103), with their fixed old/exterior factors retained. On the native weak interval, for sufficiently large R or equivalently the small-cross-influence condition in the proof, there is h>0 such that
`sup_x Σ_y e^{h dist(x,y)/R}|J_{xy}| ≤ C r⁻² [exp(−p)+R⁴ exp(−2p)].`   (7.200)
This bound is uniform in the number of fixed live components. It includes the covariance of their conditional means. No weight is assigned to a physical path inside one Y_i without first bounding its actual diameter. The represented source acts only on the earlier returning bodies. The exterior new action and other tagged terms have their own responses.

*First-stage geometry.* Before the live integrations, (1.98),(1.99) give the log as W=Σ_P W_P over connected P. Write S(P) for its outside M-cubes and I(P) for the incident complete Y_i. The actual first-stage metric (1.67) counts a single tree contained in P intersecting **all** outside M-cubes, including when S(P) is disconnected. Its dimensionless length is D(P). A tree of length M D is covered by a connected animal of ≤C(1+D) M-cubes, by following a doubled spanning traversal and marking successive intervals of length M. Every outside cube touching the tree is in a fixed collar of this animal. At fixed outside root x there are at most exp[C(1+D)] possibilities for S(P) at length ≤D. All incident Y_i must touch S(P), since they are disjoint separated components and P is connected. Once S(P) is fixed there are at most 2^{C|S(P)|} choices of the incident components, which are already fixed in location and shape. Excluding purely internal terms, these counts give a uniform rooted sum with the spare native e^{-κD(P)}, independent of the volumes of the Y_i or the torus. A term with S(P) empty meets at most one Y_i and only changes its own single-site measure. A source root outside has no such term.

For the unmarked W_P use its native first-stage bound; write a_P=C e^{-κD(P)} with the indicated prefactor/slack. For the change when a source η is turned on, apply the u-Cauchy proof of (7.193) *before* (1.103). Uniformly in the still-live variables,
`|W_P(η)−W_P(0)|≤C exp(−p)a_P` on the simultaneous source disc. Derivatives labeled x vanish unless x belongs to the outside S(P); at order two the two labels belong to that same S(P). Weighted sums over y within a fixed P use directional Cauchy on the simultaneous disc and the fact dist(x,y)≤C(1+D(P)). This proves
`sup_x Σ_y e^{h dist(x,y)/R} ||W''_{xy}||∞ ≤ C r⁻² exp(−p).`
For the unmarked interaction involving both i and j, the tree must reach outside cubes touching both of them. Consequently D(P)≥dist(Y_i,Y_j)−C. Choose a center c_i∈Y_i. For each i one can root such a P at an outside cube touching Y_i, with at most C v(Y_i) choices. The number of j it can meet is ≤C|S(P)|. The preceding counting then gives
`sup_i Σ_{j≠i} e^{h dist(c_i,c_j)/R} b_{ij} ≤ C R⁴ exp(−c aR),    b_{ij}=Σ_{P:i,j∈I(P)} ||W_P(0)||∞.`   (7.201)
Indeed dist(c_i,c_j)≤C R+D(P)+C and a fixed fraction of the spare e^{-κD} pays the aR gap. This is the point at which the explicit intercomponent separation matters. LFR II, printed p.376, (1.67), pp.390–392, (1.98)–(1.104).

*The actual live law.* On the real record each T′(Y_i) has its positive reference (1.71). Split off the terms with I(P) empty as scalars. Absorb all W_P(0) with I(P)={i} into the real positive measure for that individual live variable ξ_i and normalize it. The remainder is precisely the Gibbs weight exp[Σ_{|I(P)|≥2} W_P(0)] against the resulting product. This is an equality for the original (1.103); a sum of one-site potentials may be large but it cancels from every change of another site's conditional law. Holding all other sites fixed and changing site j alters the i conditional log density by an oscillation at most 4 b_{ij} before normalization. The total variation influence is thus ≤exp(4 b_{ij})−1=:C_{ij} for i≠j. Set C_{ii}=0. By (7.201) its weighted row sum is at most 1/2 when R is large enough on the weak interval (or impose this displayed condition directly). The inverse D=(I−C)⁻¹ then has weighted row sum at most two, by nonnegative matrix convolution and the triangle inequality for center distance.

For bounded real F,G, let osc_i F be its maximum change under alteration of ξ_i alone. The conditional comparison estimate gives
`|Cov(F,G)|≤C Σ_{i,j} osc_i F D_{ij} osc_j G.`
Here is a direct argument. Tilt the same positive law by exp(tG) for t real. Its one-site kernels at unchanged neighbors differ from the old kernels by total variation at most C|t| osc_i G when t→0. Couple the two stationary laws by repeated random single-site heat-bath updates, selecting the same site and maximally coupling its two conditionals. The disagreement vector after an update at i is bounded by the tilt discrepancy plus Σ_j C_{ij} times the prior disagreement probabilities; telescope changes of differing neighbors one at a time. Averaging updates and iterating this substochastic contraction gives in the limit an upper disagreement bound D times the tilt discrepancies. This uses only the marginals' stationarity and finite site count; the arbitrary initial disagreement decays under random updates. The change of the expectation of F is at most the scalar product with osc_i F by telescoping sites. Divide by |t| and take t→0. Fixed complex F,G follow by splitting real and imaginary parts. This comparison uses no positivity of the individual Mayer terms.

*Pointed source sums.* At zero source put H_x=∂_{η_x}W and A_{xi}=osc_i H_x. From the first-stage rooted count and the single-body bank,
`sup_x Σ_i e^{h dist(x,c_i)/R} A_{xi} ≤ C r⁻¹ exp(−p),`
`sup_i Σ_y e^{h dist(y,c_i)/R} A_{yi} ≤ C v(Y_i) r⁻¹ exp(−p).`
For the first row root at x and count incident sites by C|S(P)|. For the second root at an outside cube touching Y_i, and sum the source labels using the same polydisc; all their centers have distance ≤CR+C D(P) from c_i. The absolute row of the covariance of H_x,H_y is bounded by multiplying these inequalities with the weighted row bound for D. Direct differentiation of the full conditional law gives exactly J_{xy}=⟨W''_{xy}⟩+Cov(H_x,H_y). The earlier bound for W'' proves (7.200). This proof identifies the real interaction paths that connect different live bodies while allowing arbitrary dependence within one finite live body. ∎

This additional physical-position estimate at scale k is compatible with the next genuinely mixed T estimate (7.197) in its common one-live subclass. It does not by itself continue the tilted single-site decomposition to all complex (3.43) readouts with arbitrarily many old live components. In particular a joined record with touching or nonseparated live bodies may not satisfy (7.201); shrinking its number of sites does not establish that inequality.

### 7.81 A first-birth estimate on the independent old fine slots

**Lemma 7.133 (old U,J Hessian at the actual first selector).** Use the genuine CMP119 clean first selector of §7.74 and the first-step extended unmarked (U,J) domain with fixed spare physical radius in the directions under consideration. For the original analytic conditional coefficient, subtract its literal classical term β₀ H_b(U) at a fixed fine root. The remaining first-source family has rooted supremum O(g₀⁻¹), and on a smaller fixed old fine-slot chart its two external derivatives have rooted supremum O(g₀⁻¹)=o(g₀⁻²). These derivatives differentiate the stored native fine-coordinate extension, not the coarse-target graph. Free summation of finitely many supported physical slots is allowed with a spare original carrier rate; unrestricted absolute sums on an unavailable mixed graph are not asserted. On an external radius δ instead, the elementary two-derivative price is O(g₀⁻¹δ⁻²).

*Proof.* At the genuine first constrained coordinate transformation the physical readout on each of the finitely many fine plaquettes of H_b is the product with exp i Ψ(g₀A), where Ψ includes the original corridor injection, nonlinear pivot and external configuration dependence. At A=0 its readout is the old U itself. The independent current J occurs in the already defined extended unmarked kernel; this statement concerns its specified analytic extension, not a newly defined nonstationary physical fiber at arbitrary J. The exact ray identity on the fixed original physical tube is
`β₀ [H_b(U^{g₀A})−H_b(U)] = (γ/g₀) Σ_l A_l c_{b,l}(g₀A;U,J).`
Here c is the integral of the physical readout derivative along the ray, including the derivative of its true local transformation. It has uniformly bounded magnitude, finite original first-step stencil and the native holomorphic continuation in the external old slots. Thus for |η_b|≤c g₀, each added term is a small linear-growth perturbation, bounded by Cc(1+Σ_l |A_l|²); the aggregate over b has bounded overlap. The analytic coefficients have the same localization as the original transformation, and the same positive Gaussian reserve proves its normalized connected expansions as in §7.12. One may split the small-|A| part from |A|≥1 in that comparison to pay the linear term with bounded scalar and quadratic majorants. No translated saddle is needed and the canonical cutoff of (1.18) is unchanged. Alternatively the native (3.43)-type polylogarithmic ceiling Q≥P₀ gives the more conservative O(Q/g₀) from a source radius c g₀/Q if the comparison is formed just on that analytic fluctuation tube. Taking one source derivative by Cauchy on the radius c g₀ costs C/g₀. Two external derivatives on a strictly smaller fixed tube cost only its fixed inverse radius squared. The classical term is a single finite supported carrier; splitting it off commutes with the normalized integral. These bounds do not improve a shrinking old-domain derivative unless g₀/δ² tends to zero, or a different old-domain proof controls that derivative. ∎

### 7.82 An explicit nonempty second mixed geometry and its exterior completion

Another case of (7.197) needs no post-R still-live χ_k^c example. In LFR II (1.99)–(1.100) the new boundary carriers include those meeting the **separate unprocessed rough exterior** Z_k (with its indicated collar), not only those meeting a still-live Y_i. If the live family is empty, the decay in (1.99) is ordinary d_k for these carriers too. The old T″ factors are held in their actual place.

**Proposition 7.134 (two distant physical seeds, successive eligibility).** Use a weak trajectory interval with R₁=R₂ and the ordinary rounded widths constant until one step after the first qualification, on a torus large enough in the corresponding current units. In the verified geometries of T2 §§4.16,4.19, install the b=1 seed A and, sufficiently far away, a b=2 pure Q₂ seed B. At k=1+R₁ in their stated waiting convention A qualifies and can heal. B is still in the separate noneligible rough exterior, one wait short. The next T at k+1 is genuinely mixed, with B in its old large-field region. At k+1 the B component first qualifies. This supplies an actual geometry for the B_X of (1.99) meeting the separate exterior, with (7.197) and with no volume charge from an old still-live domain. It proves existence of the determining/source family on that sector, not nonvanishing of any individually assigned connected coefficient.

*Proof.* At A use the finite fine plaquette seed inside its pinned interior, with level-one mean equal to the identity in the prescribed endpoint frame. Take the B seed to be a block-constant fine lift of a level-one compact nodal gauge spike at a nonpivot interior bond, identity outside its fixed blocks and at the level-two nodes. Its original coarse average is identity. The spike can be chosen strictly above the Q₂ threshold and below the allowed axial-path ceiling as in T2 §4.19. Here the small additional plaquette angle used for the stronger lower bound (4.44) is unnecessary: the pure gauge gives the same strict Q₂ test. The two lifted gauges are disjoint. On the first mixed constrained readout all changed fine plaquettes at A are pinned. The other plaquettes have zero Wilson action on the flat/pure-gauge field, so this combined field realizes the constrained minimum on the free part. Thus local (1.18) and (3.2)–(3.4) tests near B and at A give the same strictly separated outcomes as in the two original constructions; no inferred independence of a general nonlinear minimizer is needed. For m≥2 take the higher targets to be identity and the allowed small outside fluctuations zero. On each newly inspected exterior cube the regional P,Q comparisons are flat; for the (3.16) test use the original local comparison and the exponentially small correction of (3.17)–(3.19), as in T2 §4.19. The small regions are covered and padded by S at each ordinary step. Choose the initial positions so that the padded rectangles and the finite test collars stay disjoint through k+1. Both remain smaller than 100MR in their current units. At k the waiting count of A reaches N=R₁; the flat extension in (1.75) and zero returned fluctuation in (1.82) allow its small choice. At B the waiting count is still short at k and met at k+1. All statements about the representatives are understood on the physical compact fibers. Strict test margins allow the associated neighborhoods of these determining choices. T2, §§4.16,4.19.

At k the mark is an actual stored fine H on the admissible part of the healed A record. The signed (1.98) logarithm splits between (i) terms disjoint from the unprocessed B exterior and (ii) terms hitting it. Keep the latter as the physical B_X boundary family of (1.99), even though its returning home lies at A. With no Y_i the shortest tree sees the distance from A to the old B region; every such contributing source X includes its old home and intersects that region. Thus ordinary rooted summation with a spare rate gives another exp[−c dist(x,Z_k^-)] if this distance is large. This is a bound on the actual signed subfamily and need not be strictly positive on the flat target. At the next mixed T its readout is the original (3.15) old field and original V_* exterior term. Equations (7.197)–(7.198) apply in the genuine mixed kernel (3.27), with ε=C exp(−p_k), and with the extra old distance weight available on this subfamily. The same positivity calculation covers its inherited second row and the covariance of its preceding conditional mean. In this example the old B denominator coincides neither with an unmarked T′ inside A nor with the value of a different Y⁺ determination. ∎

**Second R, a useful precise bound and its input.** On the same schedule B can now be tested for healing. Consider the *proper* part contributed by a preceding boundary source when B occurs. If its old/current readout is admitted on the actual new (1.61) walls, with first and second proper norms K₁,K₂ in its internal T′(B) measure and crossing (1.68) vertices, §§7.69–7.70 give the actual next signed bounds
`|D'_{proper}|≤C e^{-p_{k+1}}K₁,`
`|D''_{proper}|≤C[e^{-p_{k+1}}(K₂+K₁²)+e^{-2p_{k+1}}K₁²].`   (7.201a)
These are derivatives of the normalized log for that designated insertion, with the full compatible background summed. An older rare factor in K_i multiplies the fresh bank here only because A and B are two distinct realized bodies at different releases. The original completion is copied into A′_{k+1} and carried separately; it is not multiplied by a B occurrence. In particular an identical pinned term has zero proper row as in §7.68, while its completed exterior can vary. The fact that a specific reference configuration is real and pure gauge in B does not prove simultaneous complex admission for every wall in that second R. For an older nonlocal H packet (7.201a) is conditional on its actual proper norm there; no such norm is deduced from the seed alone.

### 7.83 A persistent budget during ordinary mixed waits

**Proposition 7.135 (ordinary waiting segment, fixed original home).** Start with a boundary birth of norm ε from (7.195), or with ε=C exp(−p_k) from the noneligible-exterior example in §7.82. Keep its microscopic source labels on a common sup-disc of radius r as before. Consider m successive native **ordinary T steps** on admitted mixed determining records during which this packet is carried as boundary data. The original compact kernels on the unprocessed rough record are held in their original order and not normalized away. No intervening R operation at which this packet acquires a new changed large-field readout is included in this statement. In each step use the ordinary (2.42) input and output rates and original (3.43) domains. Let C_i≥1 bound the rooted scalar transfer of both the fixed-background part and the innovation at that step, including any actually needed field-radius, blocking and old-home filing costs. Then the packet's effective amplitude and the row of already formed connected second responses through this segment are bounded at its end by
`A_m ≤ ε Π_{i=1}^m C_i,`
`sup_x Σ_y |∂_x∂_y log D_m| ≤ C r⁻² A_m`   (7.202)
for the selected conditional packet response while the small scalar margins hold. This estimate uses a single original budget
`-log A_m ≥ p_k−C₁v(Y)−Σ_i log C_i−C.`
It does not repeatedly halve p_k.

*Proof.* Propagate the full analytic family vanishing at zero source, not just its differentiated mean. At one step put an independent complex scalar t in front of this entire input family. For |t|≤c/A_i, the old B perturbation fits the original scalar estimates, and the (3.26)–(3.47) procedure of Theorem 7.130 gives its bounded localized output log on the same η-polydisc. The fixed background is added before the next step. Cauchy in t gives A_{i+1}≤C_i A_i at t=1. The proof uses a new auxiliary t for a norm estimate at that step; it does not shrink the physical η-disc. Prior old B^{(j)} that occur unchanged are kept with their earlier labels. A newly created boundary part has the improved original rates after T described on CMP119 printed p.262, before any subsequent R; the input may be measured at the stated fixed ordinary (2.42) rate if these original margins are available. Any expense to pass between actual old domains or source homes is included in C_i, not hidden by assigning a new fine birth. The rooted scalar comparison follows from (3.44)–(3.47) as in §7.78. Taking one fixed anchor x and a signed direction in the remaining source coordinates gives the last inequality by two-variable Cauchy. Equivalently the second response is the conditional variational identity (7.198) at each step; the transported previous second row and the fresh covariance are both present. For real fixed outside variables, any further averaging of this *conditional* kernel preserves its sup row bound. It does not include the next exterior covariance unless that next operation is also taken. ∎

For example, on a checked ordinary waiting interval of length m≤C R_k, if throughout it one has C_i≤C (1+g_i⁻²)^d (1+R_i)^d at fixed d, the extra logarithmic budget is at most C'R_k log(g_k⁻²) on a weak plateau with comparable couplings. If the chosen native exponents have R_k log(g_k⁻²)=o(p_k) and C₁v(Y)≤θp_k for θ<1, then (7.202) retains exp[−p_k+C₁v(Y)+o(p_k)] uniformly in that waiting length. The condition on the actual C_i matters: an old slot requiring a loss exponential in its unverified pre-entry depth need not satisfy it. T2's continuously retained-core and sharp-wall results preclude assuming this condition for arbitrary saved packets. Bounds just for real conditional probabilities such as (7.199) require no such product for one home, but do not give an absolute spatial row.

The separated-body result (7.200) controls a full real released row without the total-size cost. It has not transported selected B_X analytically through **all** subsequent changes of the live family. In particular corner-touching/post-R families have no verified small cross-influence bound here, and different determining records can have different exterior-completion means. The explicit unequal small-Y and Y⁺ sharp first-H rows in T2, Proposition 4.58 illustrate this last issue: for its specified coarse lower representatives the signed adjacent proper row includes the large negative exterior partner. One may not discard that partner from a branch before (7.198) or (7.201a).

### 7.84 A general transferable part and a forced-exterior test

**Corollary 7.136 (restriction by incident live volume).** The next mixed T of Theorem 7.130 applies with an arbitrarily large fixed previous live family to the subfamily of actual (1.104) source carriers for which the **total** number of current M-cubes in their incident old live components is ≤V. Replace v(Y) in ε by V, uniformly in other fixed components. In particular one may take V≤θp/C₁ for fixed θ<1; the same single old bank then pays the ordinary slot and source-home sums for this part. This is a filing of the actual connected coefficients according to their supports, not a modification of any old field or a claim that the omitted carriers vanish.

*Proof.* In the proof of Lemma 7.128, for each surviving X use the sum of its incident v(Y_i). Components of X outside the live union are adjacent to at least one of these same incident bodies unless X is completely disjoint. Ordinary animal counting from x does not require specifying nonincident bodies; the fixed live set determines its intersecting components once X is specified. Hence that proof gives C exp(−p+C₁V) on this selected family. The rest of §7.78 uses just this ordinary norm and the admitted old (2.42) domain. ∎

For the real first-R estimate of §7.80 the analogous geometric relaxation groups all components within distance aR into a common cluster. If these clusters have diameter ≤C R' and volume ≤V', with R'≥R, use each entire cluster as a supersite and absorb all within-cluster factors into its one real measure. Distinct clusters have gap ≥aR. The proof of (7.201) gives weighted cross row C V' exp(−c aR) with metric dist/R'. Provided this is sufficiently small, (7.200) follows with R' in the distance scale and V' instead of R⁴ in the last coefficient. This covers close pairs and bounded chains of old live bodies; no assertion of such a cluster bound for every history is required.

**A limitation at fixed exterior data.** A rare occurrence bound for *every* live region conditional on its external field cannot replace the preceding size and spacing estimates. Already at the first coarse transformation choose a real coarse field on a contractible patch in the local averaging chart with a fixed small but nonzero coarse plaquette holonomy there. Take g₀ so small that its deviation is larger than C_L ε₀, where ε₀ is the earliest small-plaquette threshold and C_L is the fixed one-step averaging constant. An all-small lift on the complete averaging patch would contradict this choice: in a finite axial tree gauge bounded fine plaquette deviations force all local fine links within C_L ε₀ of identity, hence the analytic coarse averaging/plaquette word within C_L' ε₀. Enlarge the fixed patch by its full contour dependencies and use C_L' in choosing the cutoff. The displayed retained value is attainable. For example use the face-constant fine lift on the neighboring L-blocks, with the selected nonidentity coarse link across their common face and all other directions identity; internal tree links are identity, so the original crossing means equal that coarse link. More generally the finite small-chart constraint submersion gives a positive neighborhood of such coarse data from a positive Haar/Wilson cylinder. Conditional on this coarse neighborhood, some fine small-field test in the full dependency patch must fail with probability one. Its *unconditional* rarity does not yield a small conditional probability uniformly over such external fields.

This example forces rough coverage, not a particular Y_i class or a lower bound on a physical H source derivative. Source addition/subtraction can cancel a proper local term against its matched exterior as in §7.68; it cannot make the excluded small lifts possible or change this conditional support statement. When a flagged carrier in Corollary 7.136 has incident live volume much greater than p, the missing ingredient is consequently a joint estimate in the actual outer measure, or a direct connected spatial estimate such as (7.200) in an applicable geometry. Charging each forced live body as though its conditional probability were exp(−p) is not such an estimate.

### 7.85 The joint Wilson normalization and the component genealogy

Write the original real joint measure using its positive disintegration before applying either Mayer expansion. At the kth return, let ξ comprise V_k, the exterior determining records, the fixed still-live Y_i, the old exterior variables and the real characteristic/gauge weights preceding the curly bracket of (1.72). Let dM_k(ξ) include the remaining T″ actions as positive integrals on their original variables, with the external action. Write D_ξ for the whole integrated return bracket including the still-live integrations as in (1.103), and D_ξ[M] for insertion before those integrations. For gauge-invariant physical marks the FP equivalence is taken after its specified group integration. The exact normalized assigned contribution is
` [∫ dM_k(ξ) D_ξ[M]] / [∫ dM_k(ξ) D_ξ] = ∫ dP_out(ξ) [D_ξ[M]/D_ξ],     dP_out=dM_k D_ξ/∫ dM_k D_ξ.`   (7.203)
Common Wilson vacuum constants cancel in this expression. Keeping the original fine fields and the selected positive labels gives its joint form on (U,history). Each indicator decomposition partitions unity; the real R resampling integrates its reference inside the selected component to one on its actual exterior, as in LFR I (0.3),(0.4). Thus a probability bound for a **bare gauge-invariant fine event** may be used under this joint law. A bound for a signed cluster coefficient is applied at fixed ξ, and only then averaged under the outer law in (7.203). A signed connected cluster is not itself a random physical history.

**Lemma 7.137 (no splitting of an ordinary ancestry).** At one fixed stage, every actually retained old connected component has at most one ordinary successor before a fresh failure is counted. Distinct current components have disjoint continuing component lineages. Every merger consumes its previous components once. Eligibility followed by complete healing ends that line. A later new body can be formed in its former area only through a new actual failure or growth from a different still-live component. The statement concerns the pre-Mayer indicators, not the overlapping virtual clusters in (1.98).

*Proof.* The construction of Λ_{j+1}^c covers a previous component by current aligned cubes and adds native layers; its resulting S-image is connected. A union of such images and newly failed regions is then decomposed into connected components. The optional small rectangular completion enlarges a component; it cannot make two pieces of its old connected image. The graph used in LFR II (1.84)–(1.86) has one vertex per contributing old/new component; connected images that intersect or touch are combined. Thus the forward component relation is functional until healing. In LFR I printed pp.177,182,193 and 200–201, the eligible set starts as a union of whole components of Λ_k^c. The successive exclusions are of whole components. The later division into X and Y in LFR II p.378 is again by whole component. Removing or keeping that component therefore does not turn one previous connected component into two different live ones at the same scale. Inside a current body many old components can have merged; they cannot all be counted again in a different current body.

In (1.79) the factors from different components are multiplied on this actual history. The continued component carries κ_j(Z) and its distinguished earliest p₀(g_{j(Z)}). In (1.85) the child κ terms and child first-failure terms enter as a sum, the one new distinguished first-failure term is subtracted, and the size/placement cost is subtracted. The graph induction (1.86)–(1.88) spends the redundant child's bank at merger to pay the growth budget. It does not grant a fresh p₀ at every intermediate time of one waiting component. At K=0 the resulting (1.89) and (1.95) give actual **undivided** component estimates. In particular the product of the real T′(Y_i)1 for distinct fixed eligible components has all of their native banks. These factors also occur in dP_out's denominator. Dropping them from that denominator, or asserting an equal probability bound conditional on the given retained fields, is invalid; the forced-coverage test in §7.84 applies. LFR I, pp.177,182,193,200–201, LFR II, pp.378,383–390. ∎

### 7.86 A normalized arbitrary-volume tail with bare physical ancestors

This subsection treats a definite positive class in (7.203). All contributing ancestors of the specified live bodies arise from initial bare P₀ plaquette failures. In their continuing genealogies permit ordinary waiting and arbitrary mergers, but no new P,Q,R or failed preparatory selector before the final observed test at k. Their χ_k^c at the final return need not be small; for an upper bound we only require the components to reach the test. Other histories elsewhere are arbitrary until they merge, in which case their leaves become part of the specified ancestry. Work on a weak plateau R_i=R through these steps, with the native ordinary wait N=R in LFR II (1.80). The length k and number of components are not fixed. Comparable long plateaus on a weak trajectory are discussed in T2 §4.45, Proposition 4.57; the statement below is uniform over volumes on any such plateau.

A one-ancestor estimate with a placement at every possible fine site would cost C L^{4k}R⁴ per terminal body. This estimate loses the history restriction for long waiting times. The following construction recovers it.

**Lemma 7.138 (binary backward witnesses on the physical-birth class).** Measure distances in M-cube units at the indicated scale. There are fixed constants b,D and H=ceil[C(R+log(2+R))] such that the following holds. A cell occupied by such a continuing genealogy at time t≥1+H has, at time s=t−H, two occupied cells among its *actual component ancestors*, within distance b L^H R from its scaled-back location and separated from one another by more than D R in s-units. Constants may be chosen with D>8b; increase the fixed C after choosing b,D. Iterating yields at least 2^{floor((k−1)/H)} spatially distinct leaf requirements per reached body. For different current bodies use their own disjoint ancestry sets.

*Proof.* An ordinary forward step coarsens the aligned cover and adds ten layers. It moves any occupied cube by at most cR in its new units from a previous occupied cube. A small rectangular completion also has that property, since it is performed only inside a cube of width 100R. With no new failure this gives, after any number of steps, a backward reach ≤b₀ L^{t−s}R in s-units by summing the geometric series. The same bound applies to any point at an intermediate merger and to both its contributing sets. Choose b a fixed sufficiently large multiple of b₀ and D>8b. All reasoning can be confined to this actual ancestor union: an outside component that merges into it is then already an ancestor, by Lemma 7.137.

If the asserted pair did not exist, all time-s occupied ancestors in the displayed outer cone would lie in a single box of width C D R. At least one of them is in the smaller b₀ cone, by the reach bound. No remote ancestor from beyond the b cone can join the descendants of this small set by time t: before the first such join these descendants lie in the enlargement by b₀ L^H R of their initial box in s-units. The incoming part at that join also has an occupied s ancestor within b₀ L^H R of its point of contact. If its ancestral connected component already stretches from this neighborhood outside the b cone, it has occupied s-cells in the intervening annulus, giving the required separated pair. Otherwise this is an incoming occupied s-cell inside the b cone, hence already in the small set. The constant C D R in its initial width is smaller than the cone margin b L^H R by increasing H. This argument can also be applied to the outermost rectangular completion at a first join, whose extra displacement is included in b₀. Thus the entire continuing part that can rescue the chosen home is the ordinary growth of components initially in this bounded box.

Before erasures, a single bounding box for these descendants has width w_{r+1}≤w_r/L+22R in the new units: cover rounding adds at most two cells of the MR partition and the two added sides contribute twenty. Small rectangular completions inside the bounding box cannot increase its bounding width. After a fixed number d₀=O(1+log_L D) of steps this is less than 64R, and stays there. Every subsequent predecessor component in this part satisfies the native size condition (i). After another R+O(1) steps condition (ii) holds, since there are no new failures on its lineage. It then qualifies; with no failed preparatory or second-class test before t it heals. Take H>d₀+R+3. This contradicts its presence at time t even if the test at t itself is allowed to fail. The same death criterion is the one preceding LFR II (1.80)–(1.81).

Descendant leaf cones of the two selected time-s cells are disjoint: their radius measured back in s-units over further macrosteps is at most bR(1+L^{-H}+⋯)<2bR (enlarge b for the final incomplete interval). The D separation therefore suffices. Across distinct terminal components the actual occupied ancestor components cannot coincide. At the initial inspection a single bare plaquette can occur in at most C_ov of the finite-overlap P₀ test cubes; retain only distinct plaquettes and allow this fixed multiplicity. If the periodic side in terminal units exceeds a sufficiently large fixed multiple of MR, the cones and annuli used above have ordinary local lifts. Otherwise the whole terminal torus contains only C R⁴ current M-cubes; an incident-volume tail above θp_k is empty there when R⁴=o(p_k). No infinite-volume limit is used. ∎

**Theorem 7.139 (the annealed incident tail on this class).** Let D₁,…,D_m be specified distinct possible current eligible components in the geometry of Lemma 7.138; each is contained in a 100MR_k cube. For the real original normalized Wilson/history law, uniformly over torus sizes and all admissible k on the plateau,
`Pr(all D_i occur on the stated physical-birth class) ≤ exp[−c p₀(g₀)^2 m 2^{floor((k−1)/H)}].`   (7.204)
The constants hold on the sufficiently weak interval with the normalized physical chessboard assumptions of (7.160), in particular the fixed reference ratio bound used in that theorem. The estimate is for actual pre-Mayer bodies in the joint law, not for independent signed activities or probabilities at a prescribed exterior field.

*Proof.* Choose one home in each specified shape. At each branch of Lemma 7.138 there are at most [C L^{4H}R⁴]^2 spatial choices for the pair of time-s cells. At the last interval shorter than H, each chosen occupied cell has a bare P₀ failed plaquette within C M R L^H fine sites, by the same backward reach and the initial native padding. Thus the total number of labeled witness placements is at most exp[C(H+log(2+MR)) m 2^l], l=floor((k−1)/H). One counts just the locations of witness cells, not all possible histories realizing them. Continuing components from different roots have disjoint actual lineages and within a root the separated cones are disjoint. After deleting any duplicate inspection witnesses there are at least m 2^l/C_ov distinct original fine plaquettes. Each has β₀ s_p≥c p₀(g₀)^2 by the defining bare P₀ threshold. Apply (7.160) once to that set, with its true normalized Wilson probability, and sum over placements. Since H+log(2+MR)=o(p₀(g₀)^2), the entropy is absorbed. The other history variables have conditional mass at most one, because we are bounding an implication by an event on the original physical field under (7.203). This proves (7.204). ∎

For the marked home x, let V(X) denote the sum of current M-cube volumes of live bodies incident to a support X of its promoted boundary coefficient. Resolve the expectation under (7.203) by the actual positive ancestral labels, *after* forming that coefficient at the original external state. On the subfamily where all its incident live bodies have the physical-birth ancestry above, (7.204) pays the omitted-volume part of Corollary 7.136:
`E_out Σ_{X∋x: V(X)>V₀} e^{ηd_k(X)} |F_X(source)−F_X(0)| 1_{physical-birth class of incident bodies}`
`≤ C exp(−p_k) exp[−(c p₀(g₀)^2 2^l/(100R)^4−C') V₀].`   (7.205)
Use a smaller positive η and the same simultaneous source disc as (7.193). For a fixed source derivative use its Cauchy price. The expectation notation includes the auxiliary positive resolution of the ancestor indicator. It does not assert that a post-Mayer coefficient is the coefficient of an independently re-normalized conditional history law.

Indeed, for a fixed connected n-cell support and its actual incident set I, the outside tree bound gives exp(−c κ n+C κ V(X)), by the component count of §7.77. The number of rooted n-cell supports and possible incident-body assignments within them is at most C^n: choose the full subset of cells in the live components, then take its actual components (or encode the component boundaries on its cube faces with another fixed C^n bound). The native κ slack pays this counting. Now V(X)≤C(100R)^4 |I|, and each assignment with its incident shapes required has actual probability (7.204); no fixed-exterior lower bound on T′ is used. Absorb CκV(X) and take an additional part of the rare exponent for the V₀ tail. This proves (7.205). Equal-class events outside the incident bodies are unnecessary. The result applies at arbitrary incident volume and arbitrary connected source-support size, including long waiting times on the plateau.

### 7.87 Normalized axial witnesses and the first physical selectors

**Lemma 7.140 (an actual normalized gauge-coordinate atom).** In the soft axial fixing (1.5),(1.7) of CMP119, and its iteration preceding (3.3), use only sites where this operation is performed. With the based nodes y fixed, the variables H_{j,t}=V_j^u(y,t) at its nonroot sites can be sampled conditionally on the prior physical fields as independent group variables with law
`z_j^{-1} 1_{||H−I||<ε_j} exp[−g_j^{-2}(1−Re tr H)] dH.`
In particular for fixed c₀>0 their actual event ||H_{j,t}−I||≥c₀δ_j has conditional probability at most C exp[−c p₀(g_j)^2] on the weak interval. For any prescribed collection at different sites and times the product upper bound holds simultaneously with (7.160) for prescribed original bare plaquettes.

*Proof.* The based transformation sends the path variable V_j(y,t) to V_j(y,t)u(t)⁻¹ (or to its left fixed nodal rotation). Left/right Haar invariance in the independent endpoint u(t) makes each H exactly a group variable with the printed normalized factor. The selection of blocks for this operation precedes these endpoint draws; variables for unused sites may be sampled independently and ignored. A ball ||H−I||≤c g_j has Haar volume ≥c' g_j^{dim G}, lies inside the cutoff and has exponent bounded below by a constant. On the indicated failure set 1−Re tr H≥c δ_j², with δ_j/g_j a fixed multiple of p₀(g_j). The resulting inverse-volume polynomial is absorbed into its exponential tail. Use the tower in the generation order of the normalized gauge identities and R resamplings to attach each event; equivalently pre-sample the independent endpoints conditional on the original Wilson field. This proof is specific to the product identity (1.5). It does not make the graph-section variables of LFR I (1.100) independent bonds. CMP119, printed pp.247,265, (1.5)–(1.7) and the paragraph before (3.3). ∎

**Lemma 7.141 (first transformation births).** Work with the source's first bare threshold convention ε₀=g₀p₀(g₀) and a weak plateau R₀=R₁=R. In a fixed enlarged inspection patch of the first transformation, an actual bare P₀, regional P₁, approximate Q₁ or independent R₁ failure implies at least one of the following:
(i) an original fine plaquette defect at least m₀=c δ₀/(1+R)^3 in the enlarged patch, or
(ii) a sampled soft axial path variable with defect at least c δ₀ in the actually gauged small blocks of its original test.
Constants may depend on L,M₂,M,N and the finite patch enlargements. Test boxes have side C R in fine units with these parameters fixed. P₀ uses just (i). The assertion for the independent R₁ concerns its native interior test of (1.18), where the local/global comparison after (1.19) is valid. Use ordinary local lifts or a patch not wrapping its required collar.

*Proof.* If every fine plaquette in a contractible box of this fixed enlarged size has defect ≤m₀, its coordinate-order tree gauge puts all nonwrapping fine links there within C R m₀ of I. In the tree loop for any extra bond commute that single step across the subsequent coordinate segments, using ≤C R plaquettes and unitarity. In this same nodal gauge the true one-level averages V have ||V−I||≤C_L R m₀ on the regional data in (1.2): the averaging uses fixed finite paths, is equivariant at the nodes, equals I at I and is Lipschitz there. The resulting estimate on V does not require small soft gauge coordinates.

Use the face-constant one-level lift Q^{s*}V as a competitor in the regional constrained problem (1.2),(1.3). It is identity inside each L-block and has the prescribed V on its crossing bonds; its true means are precisely V. It agrees with the prescribed exterior simple-lift data. Its axial path cost is zero within the free blocks. The localized Wilson action on all plaquettes that can change in this regional problem is at most C R⁴(R m₀)^2; there are only C R⁴ such plaquettes and the enlarged collar bounds their links. Terms outside the collar are identical and cancel in comparing actions. By minimization this bounds the action on those plaquettes of U_{1,□}(V). Equivalently minimize first on the compact fiber: the competitor gives this bound, hence all varied plaquettes of the absolute minimum have defect ≤C R³m₀, inside the regional regular chart at this choice of c. Its based axial representative with the prescribed small coarse targets is on the regular orbit, so the uniqueness in the first regional variational problem identifies the regular minimum used in (1.2). This comparison also follows by minimizing within the original regular domain since the competitor is in it. Every original fine plaquette of the interior minimizing field has defect ≤C R³m₀. Choosing c small makes it strictly less than ε₁ L⁻². This precludes the regional P₁ failure.

For the Q₁ comparison extend the nodal gauge from the fine tree gauge block constantly in the fine variables. For the actual fine U, its difference from the full fine tree gauge within each L-block is controlled by the true based path H(y,t) and the path in the tree-gauged U, the latter being O_L(Rm₀). This is the identity H^u(y,t)=u(y)H(y,t)u(t)⁻¹. Thus, if all the indicated H are within cδ₀, every actual fine link in this block-constant gauge is O(Rm₀+cδ₀) on the tested stencil. The regional minimum in its prescribed based axial representative has link deviation O_L(sup||V−I||+sup||∂U_{1,□}−I||). To see this on one fixed L-block, choose fixed internal tree paths. All alternative paths with the same endpoints differ by O_L of the plaquette ceiling. The axial path condition fixes their common value to I up to that same error; a crossing path's common value is its prescribed coarse average up to that error. Triangle inequalities give the asserted link bound. This argument uses only the finite-block mixed axial/gauge conventions of the actual first minimum. Hence the actual and regional links on (1.8) differ by less than 2δ₀. Only tested blocks were gauge-fixed in (1.5); the Q₁ test and its finite block collar are inside that gauged region. A tested P₁ box itself needed no axial witness.

Finally on the original interior of (1.18), the global U₁ and its local regional comparison in (1.19) have link difference O(exp[−c L M₂R] ε₁) on the tested independent bonds. With the preceding constants tightened, the true centered link there has distance <δ₀/2 from I, and its principal logarithm has norm <δ₀. On starred independent bonds that logarithm is g₀ A; the transformation changes only excluded pivots. Thus the R₁ test cannot fail there. These implications concern actual first selectors only and do not assume a uniform conditional probability for an already rough retained exterior. CMP119, printed pp.245–252, (1.1)–(1.9), (1.12), (1.18)–(1.19). ∎

For specified initial failures choose a fine witness in the enlarged regional patch of each, and choose only distinct witnesses. The finite-overlap partitions of the comparable initial test widths have bounded multiplicity, independent of R. There are at most C(1+R)^4 choices per patch. By (7.160) and Lemma 7.140 the true joint cost per distinct first-stage witness is at least exp[−c p₀(g₀)^2/(1+R)^6]. This is a conservative cost of the proof using a regional action competitor. The explicit exponent margin p₀(g₀)^2/(1+R)^6≫R⁴ (e.g. the log-power of p₀ exceeds 5r for R≍(log g⁻²)^r) will be used when the target needs to repay exp(CV).

### 7.88 The fresh graph-section sample at an eligible R

**Lemma 7.142 (a paid reset witness on the admitted real reference section).** In an actually eligible component with the admitted real exterior and extension of LFR I (1.75), use the **new** graph-section variable V′ in (1.100),(1.101), on its original Λ and graph G. Write V′=exp(i g_j B_new) there. At fixed complete exterior, determining and graph choices in that formula, for a prescribed set S of its free bonds,
`Pr( |B_new(e)|≥a p₀(g_j) for all e∈S | exterior,section ) ≤ C^{|S|} exp[−c_M a² p₀(g_j)^2 |S|]`   (7.206)
for fixed a>0, sufficiently weak g_j, with a possible change of the fixed constants. Such bounds multiply across the distinct reference sections in the actual product (1.100). There is no assertion that bonds in a section are independent, or that this bound holds after conditioning on χ_j^c. The probability on the left precedes that final split.

*Proof.* In (1.100) the new reference ratios are a product over components, with precisely the same fixed exterior and graph in the numerator and its denominator. The old integrated B′ and its preparatory χ′ are in a different old integral. On a real admitted section the analysis in LFR II (1.2)–(1.11) removes the common critical scalar and g_j-dimensional factor. The remaining B_new variables are real with graph bonds zero and |B_new|≤M₀ ε_j/g_j. Their dimension is bounded independently of the ultraviolet depth: printed pp.357–358 use Λ inside a cube of side 100M in current units. The linear residual in (1.6) is bounded on this domain, the nonlinear remainder in (1.2) is O(g_j^{1−β_geom})|Λ|, and the small-chart Haar factors have uniformly bounded upper/lower ratios there. The quadratic form satisfies the fixed positive lower bound (1.9) on the graph section, depending on M. Its upper bound on the fixed-dimension unit ball follows either from the local bounded Hessian in (1.7) or the same regular-background comparison. Integrating on that ball lower-bounds the reduced normalization by a positive M-dependent constant. On the indicated tail, half the lower quadratic bound pays c_M a² p₀(g_j)^2|S|; integrate the other half. The fixed-dimensional constants can be placed once per affected section, hence at most once per demanded bond. The estimate survives averaging the graphs with the actual weights. For several stages of the original normalized sequence, use this conditional upper bound at each draw before imposing any future selector. LFR I, printed pp.193,200–201, (1.75),(1.100)–(1.102), LFR II, pp.356–359, (1.2),(1.6)–(1.11). ∎

The still-live example in T2 Proposition 4.59 chooses a flat admissible exterior with V_Λ=I and two such new free bonds of angle ±2ε_j. Its strict test neighborhood has a new large-B_new witness; (7.206) is therefore a genuine upper probability bound for that selected reset before conditioning, even though the reset is possible. T2 (4.94) further says that, at the fixed complete old exterior in its physical factorization, the new section is independent of the old integrated interior. This does not make χ_j^c conditionally rare on an exterior which already violates its coarse small-field test. The simple diagnostic A=event "χ_j^c and at least one actual new section coordinate exceeds a p₀(g_j)" is always valid on the admitted real sections. For a larger class one must prove the implication from its χ test to such a coordinate; we do not postulate it.

### 7.89 An annealed incident-volume bound with later witnessed births and resets

Call a real ancestry **witnessed** for the purposes of this theorem if every new failure or failed eligibility/reset which continues a component in the ancestry, except the possible final split at the observed stage, has a normalized witness at the corresponding creation step. Allow the actual first selectors of §7.87. At later stages allow the large soft axial coordinates of Lemma 7.140 or the large new admissible graph-section coordinates of Lemma 7.142 within a fixed multiple of the contemporaneous MR-cell range of the failed test. Count each actual space-time coordinate only once. A birth need not have both kinds of witness. An ordinary no-change S step needs none; a merger requires witnesses only for its genuinely new failures, not for connecting already existing ancestors. These are measurable restrictions on original positive records, not a proposed equivalence with all failures. They include the genuine early Q₂ gauge spike, the delayed gauge strings in T2 §4.45 and the new-section reset subcase of T2 §4.47. Other events outside the specified lineages remain unrestricted.

**Theorem 7.143 (all-size witnessed tail at arbitrary weak times).** Set x_t=g_t⁻², and write p for the log-power exponent in p₀(g_t), reserving p_t=p₀(g_t) for the bank itself. On the weak trajectory with bounded increment of x and the usual weak monotone running, choose parameters with p>5r, where R_t is the rounded power of (log x_t)^r; more generally require the smooth budget
`b_t=(1+log x_t)^{2p−6r}`
to dominate R_t⁴ and R_t uniformly, with a sufficiently large weak cutoff. On a constant plateau the argument only needs local comparability and these inequalities. For m specified contemporaneous eligible components, uniform in all volumes and admissible cutoff depths,
`Pr(all occur on their witnessed class)≤exp(−c b_k m).`   (7.207)
Consequently the right side of (7.205) is replaced on this larger class by
`C exp(−p_k) exp[−(c b_k/(100R_k)^4−C') V₀].`   (7.208)
These estimates allow arbitrary incident volume even when a new witnessed reset prevents healing for many successive eligible intervals.

*Proof of the local alternative.* At time t use H_t=ceil[B(R_t+log(2+R_t))], with B sufficiently large and fixed. Over H_t steps of the weak trajectory, x_s=x_t+O(H_t), hence x_s/x_t=1+o(1) and b_s/b_t=1+o(1) uniformly there. The unrounded widths vary by a 1+o(1) factor. On the usual monotone trajectory the rounded widths therefore stay on at most two adjacent plateaus differing by L; at most one drop occurs in this window. In particular earlier R_s≤L R_t. On the initial interval t−1<H_t, go directly to the initial source events or to an intervening witnessed birth. For a trajectory without this local scale comparison the following argument applies with it explicitly imposed.

The backward reach bound of Lemma 7.138 holds in the window with a larger fixed b. Ordinary rectangular completion adds at most C R_current current units even when the component is subsequently filled. Now either there is a recent new failure/reset in the actual ancestry inside the enlarged reach cone, or there are two separated old occupied cells at s=t−H_t. In the first case choose one of its actual witnessed coordinates. In the second case the proof by isolation is the preceding lemma: near-home ancestors in a box D R_s cannot be rescued by an incoming body from beyond the larger cone without an ancestor or new failure inside it. For changing widths the normalized bounding width satisfies
`w_{i+1}/R_{i+1}≤ [R_i/(L R_{i+1})](w_i/R_i)+22.`
Apart from the at-most-one drop the first factor is 1/L. At the drop it is one. Thus after a fixed burn-in depending on D the normalized width is strictly below 64 when there is no drop, and below 100 even if the drop occurs afterwards. If the drop falls in that burn-in, add a fixed number of further steps. These bounds use the original sufficiently large L. There is still room for the required previous ordinary age N≤L R_t in H_t. Without a new failure or an earlier nonhealing choice the resulting compact component qualifies and disappears before t, giving the asserted alternative. If a rescue uses a newly born region far away, the cover/dilation reach argument at its first contact with the small group still forces a contemporaneous failing cell or old occupied cell in the enlarged cone. Only the initial inspected cubes, fixed-width enlargements and the S operations before their joins are used; global component history does not permit propagation without one of these contacts.

Across successive unequal macrosteps the total backward radius of descendants in their parent's current units stays ≤C b R_t. Indeed the preceding rounded R grows by at most L at each macrostep backwards, while the spatial rescaling is ≥L^{H_min} with H_min>2; sum the resulting geometric series. Choose the separation D at the old time to exceed twice the full radius there. The two child subtrees then cannot choose the same space-time witness. Across distinct present components Lemma 7.137 gives disjoint actual continuing ancestries. A given axial endpoint or refreshed bond can witness at most a fixed number of separate flagged input boxes at its own time: the required location lies in a C MR_t neighborhood, the original MR_t partition is aligned, and each such distinct newly affected component occupies an MR_t cell there. Enlarging by the fixed number of inspection layers only changes this bounded overlap. If the same physical atom is cited more than once, delete duplicate citations. This costs only a fixed factor in the sum of the leaf budgets; no atom is paid twice. A failure lacking such a same-step verified coordinate is outside the class. The final observed χ^c itself is not used as a free extra charge.

*Probability and entropy.* For any placement of the resulting forest the distinct bare plaquette witnesses have the joint bound (7.160). The other distinct atoms have their product conditional bound by (1.5) or by (1.100) on the checked real sections. The two types for a stage are drawn at their actual different operations; iterating their conditional estimates is legitimate, without conditioning on their future successes. If a fixed graph-section coordinate is unavailable at the chosen position its stipulated event is empty. A first physical witness pays at least c b₀ and a later witnessed soft or section coordinate pays at least c p_s²≥c b_s; local comparability of the smooth budgets allows each stopping leaf at its parent t to be charged c' b_t after the bounded duplication loss.

There are exp(C H_t+C log(2+MR_t)) possibilities per branch pair, or for the location, time and kind of a stopping witness, in the indicated cone. Do not replace this by an entropy exponential in the whole fine volume traced by the home. Summing the alternatives recursively, a bound e^{-c' b_t} for a root is preserved: the terminal alternatives cost exp[C H_t−c''b_t], and the two-child alternatives cost exp[C H_t−2c' b_s] with b_s/b_t≥1−o(1). Choose c' below c''/2 and a sufficiently weak interval to absorb the two sums. Equivalently sum binary-tree shapes, which have at most an exponential multiplicity in their number of leaves. For distinct roots use only witness forests obeying the verified disjointness/overlap rule before enlarging their placement sum. The probability bound after deleting duplicates factorizes in the leaf budgets, so the remaining forest count is at most the product of the root counts; no independence of the survivor events was assumed. This proves (7.207). For periodic grids one uses lifted cones when the spatial side in current M-units is sufficiently larger than R_t. If it is smaller, the omitted-volume part is empty when the target is V₀≥θp_t and R_t⁴=o(p_t); for (7.207) itself in that small-torus case require that the indicated ancestral cones have the local lifts used above. Thus (7.208) for the omitted volume is uniform over both size regimes. The last ordinary-animal/incident assignment sum is exactly the proof of (7.205), with b_k in place of its restricted initial-ancestry exponent.

For the actual released old source m_x, (7.208) bounds the expectation of the flagged outer carrier norm including its signed completion, since (7.193) used the genuine combined denominator. A fixed second source derivative or a sum over its second home can be bounded using the simultaneous source-direction Cauchy estimate before taking the annealed average. The proof gives no volume-independent Schur bound for the covariance of two *different outer-state means* on the whole unrestricted law merely from their separate annealed absolute sizes. Nor may the discarded complementary ancestries be identified with an impossible or unphysical event. ∎

### 7.90 All selectors in a slowly growing initial interval

The preceding restriction to a directly marked gauge coordinate can be removed for an initial interval whose number of transformations tends to infinity with the ultraviolet cutoff. This is an extension of the conservative regional-competitor argument; its loss is explicit.

**Proposition 7.144 (a physical witness for the pre-reset interval).** Up to a level j with no prior nontrivial R resampling in the complete fine dependency patch, take an original P_j, Q_j or R_j inspected box, with the enlarged regional and block-average collars of (3.2)–(3.4),(3.16). In particular this holds in the initial interval shorter than the first possible ordinary qualification under the wait convention used above. There is a constant C_*>1, independent of j and volume, such that a failure implies either a sampled (1.5) axial endpoint of size ≥cδ_{j−1} in its actually inspected blocks, or a bare fine plaquette with
`||U(∂p)−I|| ≥ m_j = c δ_{j−1}/[C_*^j(1+R_{patch})^3]`   (7.209)
in its full lifted input patch. Here R_patch is the largest of the comparable current widths of the regional construction. The regional selector uses the original fine-area threshold ε_j L^{-2j}, not ε_j alone. For the R_j test use the physically consistent canonical cutoff δ_{j−1}/g_{j−1} discussed in §7.74. This statement makes no claim for a patch whose input V has already been replaced by a new R reference sample.

*Proof.* The fine dependency enlargement has side ≤C L^j R_patch in fine units. Suppose all its elementary plaquettes have defect below m_j. The coordinate-order tree gauge then has fine link deviations ≤C L^j R_patch m_j on the required inward patch. On this patch the target V_j is gauge equivalent to the literal nested original averages: before a local R replacement, each T delta enforces its prescribed one-step average, and the intervening gauge changes transform endpoints covariantly. The near-identity means are Lipschitz on their finite one-step charts with constant C_L, independent of j. Shrink the patch by all finite contour dependencies at each average, already included in its enlargement. It follows that `||V_j−I||≤C_L^j C L^j R_patch m_j` in that nodal gauge, and similarly for the preceding top target. All these means are within their native small physical charts for (7.209).

In the regional minimal hierarchy use the complete iterated fine face lift of V_j. Its internal links equal I and any crossing fine face link receives the corresponding target link. At each scale the true mean reduces to the same lower face lift; relative contour words inside a block are identity. This is exactly the prescribed simple-lift generating field for the regional data in the analogue of (1.2) and (3.4), so it meets *all* retained regional rows, including any prescribed fine exterior. Outside the free part and its nearest-plaquette collar its action cancels identically in comparison. At most C L^{4j}R_patch^4 fine plaquettes can change. The resulting action comparison bounds each tested fine plaquette of the regional minimum by
`C L^{2j}R_patch² [C_L^j L^j R_patch m_j].`
As in Lemma 7.141 the compact minimum with this upper action bound is in the regular branch for sufficiently small c, hence gives the regular minimizing orbit specified by the regional problem. Taking C_* sufficiently large pays all displayed powers of L,C_L, including the additional L^{2j} required by the P_j threshold. All its regional P_j tests pass. This argument does not use a false scale-independent bound on the physical action of a rough fine configuration; it uses a competitor on a specified finite constrained patch.

For Q_j the reference of (3.4) is M^{j−1} of this minimum. A complete plaquette of its preceding-scale target has holonomy within C_L^j L^j times the fine minimizing plaquette ceiling: use the local fine tree gauge on the complete O(L^j) dependency patch of this one coarse plaquette, then the j−1 finite Lipschitz mean bounds. This is gauge invariant. In the last based axial representative, blockwise paths for the previous-scale field are I (within its plaquette ceiling for alternate paths), and its true current mean is V_j. The fixed L-block estimate of Lemma 7.141 therefore makes its links within C_L of the sum of its preceding-scale plaquette ceiling and ||V_j−I||. This remains <c'δ_{j−1} on choosing C_* with the spare exponential-in-j constant. For the actual V_{j−1}, first use the gauge in which its nested average of the bare fine field is within C_L^j L^j R_patch m_j of I. If the current sampled axial endpoints are <cδ_{j−1}, replacing that gauge by its block-constant extension changes this bound by at most C_L times that endpoint ceiling, exactly by the endpoint identity in §7.87. The same block-constant change applies to the regional minimum. Thus (3.3) does not fail. On the interior independent (3.16) tests use (3.17)–(3.19): the global/regional difference has size O(exp(−R_{j−1})ε_{j−1}) there on its native regular determining record. Tighten c to put the physical logarithm within δ_{j−1}. This excludes R_j failure as well. Overlapping regional witnesses have the fixed same-scale multiplicity of their original outer patches. CMP119, printed pp.265–269, (3.2)–(3.4), (3.10),(3.16)–(3.19).

Fix ν>0 with 2p>10r+ν, and let J=floor[a log(1+log x₀)] for sufficiently small a>0. Then J≪R₀, and x_j/x₀=1+o(1) up to J. When the native initial waiting convention excludes a prior eligible R there, (7.209) applies to every such inspected physical selector. Otherwise retain the explicit no-prior-local-R qualification of the proposition. Its weakest bare normalized fine cost is c(1+log x₀)^{2p−6r} C_*^{-2J}, since β₀δ_{j−1}² is comparable to p₀(g₀)^2 on this short interval. A given fine plaquette can be cited by a bounded number of boxes per scale and by O(J) scales; discard duplicate citations, spending this factor only once per fine witness. The number of fine-site placements per such early leaf grows by at most exp(CJ) times a polynomial in R₀. Therefore for a chosen a small enough the budget `b_t=(1+log x_t)^{2p−6r−ν}` in (7.207)–(7.208) still suffices, and it dominates R_t⁴. One may now allow *all* these early P,Q,R births, not only the first-step or soft-gauge certified ones; all later witnessed births and new section resets from §7.89 remain allowed. At ages comparable to x₀ the C_*^j loss in (7.209) destroys this particular bare fine localization. It is a failure of this bound, not a counterexample to physical susceptibility. ∎

### 7.91 Moving an exterior mark to its first later healing

There is another way to normalize the event of old live components. It uses the actual time at which a marked region stops being exterior, rather than assigning it a false conditional probability while it is still forced. This argument does not require the birth to be one of the gauge-coordinate witnesses of §7.89.

**Lemma 7.145 (a one-time reward inside an unbroken native large history).** Fix S, a list of m prescribed distinct eligible still-live shapes/positions at a single scale k. At a later scale ℓ let X be a native unbroken component, and n_X the number of those specified k-bodies in the continuing lineage of X. Ignore completely healed older components when computing n_X. In the absolute *undivided* estimates of the original T′_ℓ(X), the positive factor exp[a p_k² n_X] can be inserted while retaining (1.89) and the ensuing (1.92)–(1.97), for a fixed small a>0 on the stated native weak margins. The same marked majorization applies to the earlier retained part of the estimate (1.79) for an unprocessed large component. This is not yet a bound for the ratio of that component to its own small mass.

*Proof.* Work with the original unintegrated live-operator form (1.102), so that the histories of continuing components are still inside their operators. An earlier fully healed component has ceased to be a predecessor and is never reopened. Choose one earliest ordinary birth component Z_j^{(i)} for each of the indicated k-bodies. It must exist by (1.76): the initial large region is formed by the true original large-field tests, ordinary continuation and merging do not create a new disconnected component without such a birth, and the preparatory selections act only on existing components. Distinct k-bodies have disjoint predecessors. A given connected ordinary birth is consequently chosen at most once. If working directly with overlapping elementary cube tests, use their fixed overlap factor, or use the connected birth factor in the printed (1.79). No extra choice has to be summed: choose the first spatially ordered earliest birth in each actual genealogy to justify a pointwise inequality before taking the original supremum.

The main product in printed (1.79), p.383, retains the factor
`exp[−(γ₀A₁²/2) p₀(g_j)^2(d'_j(Z_j^{(i)})+1)−2p₀(g_j)]`
per ordinary new birth. In particular it is p₀ squared in the first term. The index j≤k and the weak trajectory give p₀(g_j)≥c p_k (or use the corresponding infimum on the indicated prefix). Spend a small fixed part of the squared coefficient at each of the chosen births. This pays exp[a p_k² n_X] while retaining the full distinguished 2p₀(g_j), the preparatory factors, and a fixed positive squared coefficient. The proof of (1.81)–(1.88) goes through with this smaller squared coefficient: the initial geometry expense is O(M⁴R_j^5(d'_j+1)) and the choice of weak interval makes it smaller than the remaining squared term; the merger inequality (1.86) uses the two distinguished *linear* p₀ terms, which have not been reduced. Keep the original waiting terms and charge (1.95) only from the resulting current return estimate. This use of (1.79) is inside its actual positive reference majorant before summing the history. Any (1.73) small complex phase and the actual localized V factors are estimated as in (1.92), with no enlargement of their support by the historical selector. The indicator is a discrete component label within the true T′ support. This proof does not assert a local lower bound on its mass. LFR II, printed pp.380–390, especially (1.76),(1.79),(1.80),(1.85)–(1.89),(1.95). ∎

**Theorem 7.146 (all ancestor types that later heal).** In the real normalized joint Wilson/history law let N_heal be the number of the specified k-bodies in S which actually occur and whose continuing descendant heals by the final R at K. Count a body exactly once at that first healing, even if several specified bodies have by then merged. On the native margins above,
`E exp[a p_k² N_heal] ≤ exp[C m Σ_{ℓ=k+1}^K exp(−p_ℓ)].`   (7.210)
Consequently the probability that at least h of those m specified components occur and subsequently heal is at most
`exp[−a p_k² h + C m Σ_{ℓ>k} exp(−p_ℓ)].`
The running sum is bounded on the usual weak trajectory with lower positive inverse-coupling step drift. This result is uniform over physical torus volume; it treats arbitrary history pedigrees and does not assume that a nonhealing reset had a particular normalized microscopic witness.

*Proof.* At a particular ℓ>k use the real pre-Mayer (1.72). Hold fixed its entire exterior, including V_ℓ, the separate T″ data and *the integration variables of every still-live Y_i*, with their retained histories. Do not yet perform the optional second exponentiation. The remaining conditional normalized law of the hidden, currently healing bodies is the positive curly bracket divided by its own full sum D. Within one such returned X put
`1+u(exp[a p_k² n_X]−1).`
At u=1 the product over all healing X is exp[a p_k² n_ℓ], where n_ℓ counts only the indicated k-bodies whose first subsequent healing is ℓ. At u=0 it is the native law. A component selected in S which has already healed never reappears in n_X, even if a later fresh component occupies its former sites. Existence of the marked k-shape and its unbroken path is a property of the stored determining data inside X, since an old connected component has a unique successor until it disappears.

In the first Mayer majorant (1.91) with q returning bodies the extra absolute price is ≤(1+|u|)^q exp[a p_k² Σ_X n_X]. Lemma 7.145 pays the latter factor in the full unmarked-reference majorant. For |u|≤c exp(p_ℓ), the remaining (1.95) factor is at most (c+exp(−p_ℓ))^q exp(−p_ℓ q/2). Perform all placements with (1.96) and choose c below its fixed smallness ceiling. The q=0 case is exactly unchanged. The first connected expansion (1.98), with the *live variables held fixed*, proves nonvanishing throughout this disc. No altered live mass needs to be divided out. The exact normalized bracket P(u)=D(u)/D(0) is a polynomial whose degree is at most m: any nonconstant factor must contain at least one specified past k-body and distinct simultaneous healing bodies cannot use the same one. Its constant term is one. Factoring the polynomial as in (7.191) gives, pointwise in the fixed data, `E(exp[a p_k² n_ℓ]|fixed data)≤exp[C m exp(−p_ℓ)]`. This uses real positivity just for interpreting the endpoint u=1; the root bound came from the genuine signed expansion.

It is necessary to justify multiplying these conditional inequalities over ℓ. In the real positive joint construction, the degrees of freedom and determining data internal to a body which heals at ℓ are summed in the T′_ℓ(X) and the curly bracket. The factors on the other side of that bracket in (1.72) are independent of its family of healing bodies. All later transitions may be drawn by using the surviving exterior state, including its retained old operators and coordinates. Equivalently first perform (1.98),(1.102) at that state and sample the hidden positive return record conditionally afterwards. The previous `V(Y)` dependence on old records *inside* X remains in the curly bracket, as specified directly after (1.72); it is not an omitted dependence of A′_ℓ.
