Gauge equivalence is used only after the indicated gauge integrations; the label on the old component geometry is unchanged by their simultaneous transformations. For t>ℓ, n_t uses only k-bodies that are still present inside the surviving unprocessed/live components after ℓ, plus subsequent transition data. Their histories are among the variables held fixed in this conditional bound. A completely eliminated X cannot participate in any n_t with t>ℓ. Adding future random choices to the conditioning therefore leaves the same hidden-body kernel, whereas conditioning on the fixed healing X itself would have invalidated the estimate. Apply the inequality first at k+1, leaving Σ_{t>k+1} n_t in the outer expectation, and repeat to K. There is no sum over partitions of the m labels among release times. This proves (7.210). ∎

In particular the earlier annealed ordinary-volume compensation (7.205) applies with rate a p_k² per required live body if all its incident ancestors subsequently heal before stopping, irrespective of their birth types. It also applies when any fixed positive fraction of them subsequently heal, with that fraction multiplying the rate. The remaining marked ones are not conditionally declared rare. This is a bound on real completed exterior-law weights in (7.203); the signed source term has already been assigned to its native carrier before the outer estimate.

### 7.92 The terminal factor and the volume qualification

Let N_∞ count the members of S still in an unbroken large component at the final scale, including components that are not eligible there. This is measurable from the terminal *unprocessed* operations, not a fresh rare event at each late time. Keep N_∞ in the outer expectation at every use of (7.210). With the same S and the same single payment at its old ordinary ancestors,
`E exp[a p_k² (N_heal+N_∞)] ≤ exp[C m Σ_{ℓ>k}e^{-p_ℓ}] E exp[a p_k² N_∞].`   (7.211)
In particular no normalization has been gained for N_∞ merely by reaching the stop.

**Proposition 7.147 (terminal-stability comparison).** Use the native ultraviolet stability normalization at the last scale, i.e. the common vacuum subtractions in CMP119 (2.49)–(2.50) for the same torus and the same cutoff. Write V_stop for the terminal-volume factor in that estimate in its current units, Z_stop=∫ρ_K(V)dV for its unmodified normalized integral. Then the terminal factor satisfies
`E exp[a p_k² N_∞] ≤ exp(C_+ V_stop)/Z_stop.`   (7.212)
The constant is a stability constant at the stopped coupling, not a constant per old marked body. Whenever the native integrated lower at the stopped scale is `Z_stop≥exp(−C_- V_stop)`, one obtains for m specified shapes, **with no restriction on their births or terminal fates**,
`Pr(all m occur at k) ≤ exp[(C_++C_-)V_stop + C m Σ_{ℓ>k}e^{-p_ℓ} −a p_k² m].`   (7.213)
At fixed stopped reference torus the terminal-volume factor is a fixed prefactor under that input. For an arbitrary larger physical torus this proof gives exactly the displayed volume expense, even when the marked cluster occupies a small part of that torus.

*Proof.* Take the actual unmarked terminal inductive representation before the optional final integration of a surviving T′(Y_i)1. Insert the terminal factor only inside the operations of the terminal large components, on their continuing ancestry. Lemma 7.145 retains the full original large-field estimate and its geometric damping on each such operation after multiplication. For other large components the estimates are unchanged. The argument of CMP119 (2.45)–(2.50) and LFR II p.387 bounds the terminal absolute integral: all E,R,B, Wilson/gauge normalizers and field-independent vacuum terms outside those altered record indicators are the original ones; this is an insertion at the terminal integrand, not a change to every earlier vacuum counterterm. The earlier use of (7.211) has already dealt with all previously eliminated components. The geometric sums in (2.49) and the combinatorics following it require the same fixed-parameter weak slack as before; the squared birth coefficient can be kept above its required lower margin as in Lemma 7.145. Thus the bound is exp(C_+ V_stop) for the marked undivided numerator, just as for the unmarked terminal upper bound with possibly a different constant. Divide by the original Z_stop to get (7.212). Equation (7.211) and Markov's inequality now give (7.213). CMP119, printed pp.262–264, (2.42)–(2.50), LFR II, pp.383–390, (1.79)–(1.104).

For clarity, a sufficient form of the lower input in (7.213) is a terminal all-small Haar cylinder of measure ≥exp(−C V_stop) on which the global regular action is ≤C V_stop and the original terminal χ_K is one. This is the lower side of (2.50) integrated over that *same* cylinder. At a fixed terminal coupling in a compact weak interval one tests a small fixed physical link neighborhood of I: the global target and its regional simple lifts have their completed plaquette rows (CMP102 (7)) uniformly small. The native regularity (8) bounds the fine minimum's plaquettes by C ε η² in the top region, with ε the input ceiling. Take ε sufficiently below ε_K for the terminal regional tests on their top interiors. Summing their squared fine-area factors over the whole torus gives C ε² V_stop for the global action; the product Haar mass of the terminal link ball costs exp(−C V_stop). This application requires the original admissible terminal partitions/regular hierarchy (or the corresponding verified periodic lift), and the terminal coarsely measured volume convention. If one has only the pointwise printed (2.50) without those identifications, retain (7.212) with the actual Z_stop. One cannot substitute a lower bound on a different bare or differently vacuum-normalized partition function.

The annealed carrier argument following (7.205) now applies to every incident set with the additional common factor exp[(C_++C_-)V_stop], on the terminal normalization just specified. This pays exp(C V(X)) for arbitrarily large incident support on a fixed reference torus. It is volume-uniform without that terminal factor on the eventually-healed sector of (7.210), on the witnessed class of (7.208), and for sets so large relative to V_stop that a fixed part of a p_k² m absorbs the terminal factor. It does **not** give an arbitrary-physical-volume local probability for terminal survivors from a comparison of global positive partitions. The outstanding comparison would bound the terminal expectation in (7.212) by exp(Cm), or bound its local connected response directly, while preserving the same surrounding exterior. Even a marked pointwise pressure bound for all clusters does not alone control covariance of exterior means at distant homes.

### 7.93 A connected two-home row with continuous live age

Consider two actual marks at homes x,y of the k-lattice which are still carried in the recorded compact data. When their marked components heal at a later R at ℓ, define the new source there by their literal stored values (including an inherited second jet if present). A component absent at the indicated home has zero tag. This is the part with a **continuous** occupied path from k to ℓ; it does not reopen a tag which previously healed. An older physical H/quantum boundary packet fits this statement only when its actual readout is admitted throughout that interval and remains within the indicated old component or its certified crossing edge. Earlier clean age and the completed exterior mean must be kept separately.

**Theorem 7.148 (summability of the simultaneous-release conditional covariance).** At ℓ retain the full signed R bracket and all its still-live integrations but fix the separate outer record. Mark the specified k-homes only when their continuing component releases at this ℓ. Let C_{xy,ℓ} be the mixed derivative of the log of that normalized conditional weight; it contains the inherited second row plus the covariance of the two first rows over both the returning and the integrated live variables. Assume pointwise record bounds K_x,K_y for the two stored first rows and C K_xK_y for the indicated same-body second coefficient (or use its actual separate bound). A fixed entry-grade factor belongs in these K's. Choose any fixed s>4. With `B_stop=exp(C_+V_stop)/Z_stop` from (7.212), the annealed estimate is
`E_out |C_{xy,ℓ}| ≤ C B_stop K_x K_y exp(−a p_k²) L^{-s(ℓ−k)} exp[−c d_k(x,y)/L^{ℓ−k}].`   (7.214)
Here d_k(x,y) is the ordinary distance in k M-cube units and constants include fixed rooting/collar factors. If the source starts at the native fine subcell within its M-home the usual bounded offset is immaterial. Consequently
`Σ_{ℓ>k} E_out |C_{xy,ℓ}| ≤ C_s B_stop K_xK_y exp(−a p_k²)(1+d_k(x,y))^{-s}.`   (7.215)
In particular this contribution has an absolute summable row in the second home with bounded K_y. On the subsequently-healed incident class of (7.210) or the side-certified class of (7.208) one omits the terminal factor, using their respective annealed rates. Without a verified stopped scalar convention keep B_stop literal.

*Proof.* Use finite two-source interpolation before (1.91). On a component with indicated payloads put 1+zM_x+wM_y+zw(M_xM_y+H_xy), where a missing indicated home contributes zero; for two different components keep the product of the two single tags. This has exactly the physical mixed Taylor coefficient, including the inherited second derivative H_xy. In the positive reference majorant first reserve a small part of the squared earliest-birth factor of (1.79), as in Lemma 7.145. When both homes have the same k-body split its one squared bank between the two finite markers. Also pay L^{s(ℓ−k)} for each continuously recorded marked interval by the occupied-volume estimate of Theorem 7.47. More explicitly `exp[s log L · (# tagged occupied steps)]` is bounded by exp[C_s Σ_{j=k}^ℓ |Z_j|_j]; the component contains at least one occupied site at every counted stage. The native positive geometric cost in (1.79) allows this fixed additional coefficient, and the retained original squared birth and linear merger reserves still dominate it on the stated weak range. This argument is for two fixed marks, not all old roots assigned an independent geometric bank. Take the actual source-free (1.98) and (1.103) expansions uniformly with independent radii R_i=c exp(a' p_k²)L^{s(ℓ−k)}/K_i for these *finite* tags, using a' small enough for a shared body. The tag is a polynomial, not a physically large exponential inside a compact integral.

At these radii every active tag's large modulus and time cost has been paid on its true occupied history. The only other price is a fixed scalar multiplicity per marked body; by weakening the constants in (1.95) this leaves its q placement estimate and its small prefactor. At q=0 no such source appears. The second CE still has the same supports and normalized T′(Y_i) factors. On their connected log carriers Cauchy therefore gives a bound C K_xK_y exp(−a p_k²)L^{-s(ℓ−k)} times the original connected carrier majorant, with spare decay. The second-log derivative is calculated on the **same** unmarked bracket; it is not the product of two rewarded rare masses. In the formal expansion both old homes, mapped to the ℓ-grid, are in the connected support P of any such mixed coefficient. They may be connected through large incident Y_i, in which case the original bound need not decay through its full interior.

Convert the outside metric of P as in §7.77. If n is its ordinary number of M-cubes and V(P) the total incident live volume, its reduced majorant is bounded by C exp[−cκ n+Cκ V(P)]. One may reserve a separate positive fraction of κ for the distance between the projected homes, at least `d_k(x,y)/L^{ℓ−k}−C`. Sum first on real coarse exterior records and their actual incident shapes. To restore the size loss, (7.211)–(7.212) give `Pr(all incident shapes occur)≤B_stop exp[C m Σ_{t>ℓ}e^{-p_t}−a p_ℓ² m]` for m shapes. The fixed weak choice makes a p_ℓ² dominate Cκ(100R_ℓ)^4, so this pays the exp(CκV(P)) and the finite incidence-assignment count. The remaining ordinary connected animals rooted at the projected x have their counting slack. All of these are absolute estimates *after* taking the mixed logarithm and its actual normalization. Thus the inherited conditional second row and the fresh live/return covariance have not been omitted. This proves (7.214). To sum the scales split at L^{ℓ−k} comparable with 1+d_k(x,y): on the later side use the geometric time factor, and on the earlier side the remaining exp(−c d_k/L^{ℓ−k}) dominates any polynomial in that ratio. This gives (7.215). ∎

This is an actual connected **outer** contribution to total covariance: at that release its conditional expectation integrates the older physical marks and includes the dependence between their earlier histories. If a tagged field is born at j<k and its admitted entry bound is additionally L^{-s'(k−j)}, it multiplies (7.214); the proof supplies no such factor for an unverified sharper pre-entry projection. If the marks release at different times, the earlier conditional mean becomes an ordinary exterior coefficient; its later covariance is not one of the simultaneous-release derivatives above. Likewise the covariance of the two already formed means over terminal records is still present. Therefore (7.215) cannot be substituted for the complete two-point function or the limiting SUS row.

### 7.94 A joint elapsed-age estimate under the outer law

Let h_i be an elapsed time at a prescribed k-body for which the actual history records a continuous predecessor chain for h_i steps before k. Fix a deterministic rule when there is more than one possible chain, for example one earliest contributing ancestor. A nonzero h_i cannot be assigned to an interval after a complete healing merely because the same spatial point later becomes rough again.

**Corollary 7.149 (one residence budget per actual occupied part).** In (7.210) one may replace a p_k² N_heal by the sum of a p_k²+λ h_i log L over the subsequently healed specified bodies, for any fixed λ on the corresponding weak margin. The same replacement in (7.211)–(7.213) for the terminal bodies keeps B_stop=exp(C_+V_stop)/Z_stop. In particular the joint cost for m specified occurring bodies with elapsed ages at least H_i contains the additional factor L^{-λ Σ_i H_i}.

*Proof.* At a fixed earlier time the continuously occupied chains of **different** k-bodies use different components. There is no forward splitting between that time and k. Thus the number of active chains at each time is bounded by its actual occupied-volume count, even for unbounded m. Multiply the positive history weight by L^{λ Σ_i h_i}. This adds at most C_λ Σ_j |Z_j|_j to the log of the native geometry majorant. As in §7.27 this is paid by enlarging the fixed coefficient in the cost of (1.79), with the original nonempty-component size and the strengthened weak margin. It is not m copies of the cost for one common ancestor. At a later merger retain the distinct k-labels, but their **past** charged chains only run up to k, before that merger. The extra first squared-bank fraction in Lemma 7.145 is kept as well. The polynomial-in-u argument and eventual/terminal decomposition do not depend on the numerical value of the positive reward inside a returned component after it has been paid. This proves the assertions. ∎

For example T2 (4.102) bounds the actual complete projected first-H readout on its specified real chart by a fixed grade times r^{s₁} L^{Bn_o}, where n_o is the oldest local retained-layer age near that test. On the **same** verified physical readouts, Corollary 7.149 pays a fixed first or second power of this L^{Bn_o} when the maximizing local body is in the marked class; one can sum its shape with the rooted counts above. This preserves the positive pre-entry power r^{s₁} without reusing the live-time bank or assuming a new independent failure at each age. It neither proves T2's underlying chart off the checked field nor controls all other source coefficients emitted before that readout. T2, Propositions 4.56, 4.63–4.64.

### 7.95 A two-home covariance over the actual stopped exterior

Write B_stop literally as in (7.212) and B̄_stop=max(1,B_stop). All covariance here is under the actual normalized joint stopped Wilson/history law (including the remaining real compact variables). This provides a result for the constituent source families of the terminal action, with their stated birth norms; it does not supply those norms for missing earlier source generations.

**Lemma 7.150 (terminal layer cost).** On a terminal determining record, a home in Ω_n outside Ω_{n+1}, n<K, belongs to Z_t=Λ_t^c for every t=n+1,…,K. For a fixed home in that layer and fixed A>0,
`Pr(home in this layer) ≤ C B̄_stop L^{-A(K−n−1)}.`   (7.216)
The same conclusion holds for occurrence of a specified j-carrier touching Z_j of the final record, with K−j occupied steps. If its support contains a whole set of indicated j-live components surviving in this terminal record, one can also include their joint squared first-birth factor from (7.212).

*Proof.* The exact terminal nesting is Ω₁⊃Λ₁⊃Ω₂⊃Λ₂⊃⋯⊃Ω_K⊃Λ_K, CMP119 (2.1). If the indicated physical location is out of Ω_{n+1}, it is in a terminal large component at each of the stated earlier scales. The component containing a persisting point has an unbroken chain. For a carrier meeting Z_j choose one such contained point by any deterministic order. Insert L^{A(K−n−1)} or L^{A(K−j)} only on this event in the actual terminal unprocessed operators. This costs a fixed multiple of Σ_t |Z_t|_t along the chain, as in (7.105), without opening any past healed variables. The original (1.79) positive majorant still applies with its geometric coefficient increased by this fixed amount, and the terminal upper comparison followed by division by the same Z_stop gives (7.216). For multiple incident components at j use the disjoint first squared births of Lemma 7.145; one can pay the time cost for one or two selected chains at the same time. This is an annealed assertion, not a bound at a fixed exterior that forces a layer. CMP119, pp.254–255, (2.1)–(2.3), pp.257–258, (2.18)–(2.21). ∎

**Theorem 7.151 (retained ordinary marginal and rough boundary rows).** Fix a source home x at birth scale j. Consider a genuine promoted scalar family R_{x,j}(X) of ordinary R-type as in (2.30)–(2.32), with its original gauge-invariant old physical readout and an ordinary anchored bound b_j exp(−κd_j(X)) on its admitted old chart. Keep its source home in X and the possible missing identity/vacuum terms. In particular b_j can be the first-derivative size from (7.193) for an ordinary returned interior. On the stated real mixed physical graphs the terminal contribution G^R_x from this old family admits a deterministic identity scalar c_x such that
`||G^R_x−c_x||_{L²(P_stop)} ≤ C B̄_stop^{1/2} b_j P_j (1+K−j)^q L^{-4(K−j)}.`   (7.217)
Here P_j is the finite old-chart Cauchy/slot cost, at most a fixed polynomial in g_j⁻¹ and its logarithms on the native (2.28) margins; q is fixed. A fixed finite number of old external slots is allowed with its explicit P_j. For a retained B^{(j)} boundary family with the same finite-home source norm b_j (including the collapsed convention of (7.193)), the right side can instead use L^{-D(K−j)} for any fixed D, with corresponding native constants and B̄_stop. It refers to the terms actually filed in the terminal boundary sum (2.40),(2.41), not to all earlier field-dependent scalar emissions under a new name.

*Ordinary field-dependent difference.* At a source home in layer Ω_n outside Ω_{n+1}, use the primary estimate for the individual R-term in the proof of CMP119 Theorem 2. Printed p.282 states, before summing X to obtain (2.44), its O((L^{j−n})^4 g_j^{κ₀} exp[−κd_j(X)]) bound after the identity (3.49). This is a vacuum-subtracted old R on the physical mixed graph. For small X use the stated regular chart at its actual native scale n: in the alternate gauge proof (3.68) the common old potential near the home is O((1+n−j) ε_n (L^{j−n})²). The constant color rotation kills its linear jet; two old-slot factors give the displayed fourth power. The corresponding native current extension is the one in (3.49), not an arbitrary off-shell gradient at independent fine sites. For X missing the local collar (3.48) spends half its old rate and pays any fixed power of L^{j−n}. The operation is linear in each old R scalar, and stops before extracting an isotropic coupling; no extra Euclidean invariance of the source label x is needed for this size bound. Scaling the old norm to b_j, paying the finitely many retained slot radii and polynomial support moments on the spare κ, gives
`|Σ_{X∋x, admitted} [R_{x,j}(X,U_K)−R_{x,j}(X,I)]| ≤ C b_j P_j (1+n−j)^q L^{-4(n−j)}.`
This uses exactly the old R readout type and real regular graph of that primary estimate. It is not a statement about an arbitrary unadmitted old H kernel on a joined wall. CMP119, pp.263,279–284, (2.44),(3.48),(3.49),(3.68).

Square and average. The n=K term has its deterministic age. For j≤n<K apply (7.216) at the fixed x with A>8. Thus the sum over n is bounded by C B̄_stop b_j² P_j² (1+K−j)^{2q} L^{-8(K−j)}, since L^{-8(n−j)} L^{-A(K−n−1)} is geometrically summable relative to L^{-8(K−j)}. Supports excluded because the home itself is below layer j need no old R readout; their missing vacuum case is handled next.

*The vacuum membership and B terms.* For a fixed old R carrier the identity value on its wholly regular domain is the same local coefficient whenever that carrier is present, by the local support clause of (2.30)–(2.32). Separate the full deterministic sum of its identity values at x. A missing summand due to the restriction X⊂Λ_j (or its indicated fixed-width collar) is supported on a terminally retained old rough component meeting this support or its fixed collar. Keep its original scalar with that boundary indicator; it is not a common vacuum constant to discard before centering. If the convention has already vacuum-subtracted all these terms, track only the history-dependent missing part of the actual scalar normalization. Each missing term costs its own b_j exp(−κd_j(X)). For its square sum apply the terminal layer proof to one of the incident persisting components in the two supports. Counting rooted ordinary supports on a spare rate gives C B̄_stop b_j² L^{-A(K−j)}. Take A>8 to get (7.217).

For a genuine old B-term in the final (2.41), X meets Z_j of the **final** stored record; its data do not depend on a disconnected part of a different eliminated history. At least one such rough component persists from j to K, even if several of its branches subsequently merge. For the product of two B coefficients, take the union of their incident eligible Y sets in the final recording and pay each first birth only once. The terminal weighted (1.79) comparison gives B̄_stop L^{-A(K−j)} exp(−a p_j² m) for the relevant assignments of m incident prescribed Y's; the other noneligible rough region, if any, only needs its one continuous age charge. This pays exp(C total incident Y-volume) when converting the reduced supports to ordinary rooted animals, as in §7.77. If m=0 the support bound is already ordinary; its incidence with the retained noneligible Z_j supplies the age. Sum both rooted support lists and their local incidence assignments. This proves the B assertion for any fixed A, after taking its square root. It also addresses the scalar completion when its identity value depends on the retained B history. If a component has previously healed, its new coefficients at that healing must be treated at **their** birth scale; the old component cannot be assigned a terminal age after it has disappeared.

*Connected outer covariance.* Cauchy–Schwarz with the two deterministic subtractions in (7.217) gives for these actual terminal first rows, at two birth homes i,j,
`|Cov_stop(G^R_x,G^R_y)| ≤ C B̄_stop b_i b_j P_iP_j (1+K−i)^q(1+K−j)^q L^{-4(K−i)-4(K−j)}.`   (7.218)
The same calculation covers B,R cross terms and B,B terms with their stronger age. These are genuine covariances of exterior means, not conditional variances of a single fresh component. In particular on the fixed torus there are C n_K⁴ L^{4(K−j)} homes at scale j. The four age powers pay that spatial multiplicity, with only the stated polynomial and terminal factors. One can use an exponent arbitrarily close to four to absorb a polynomial when only a smaller saved-age target is requested; at the exact marginal an unwarranted summability in j or uniform all-orders estimate is not implied by (7.218). This proof leaves open the accumulated b_j of all lower/contact/innovation births outside the stated classes, the matching of their source-dependent scalar conventions, and the unresolved common terminal normalization in B̄_stop. ∎

### 7.96 The same-torus terminal scalar at a fixed stopped coupling

**Proposition 7.152 (terminal Haar cylinder for (2.50)).** Fix the stopping convention L^K a=ℓ₀, work in units ℓ₀=1, and let g_K=g_* be fixed in the admitted weak interval (a compact subinterval bounded away from zero works too). Use an admissible periodic torus and the complete regional determining sets of CMP119. At this stop both sides of the *same* primary density inequality (2.50) give
`exp[−C(g_*) n_K⁴] ≤ Z_stop ≤ exp[C(g_*) n_K⁴],    B_stop≤exp[C'(g_*) n_K⁴].`   (7.219)
Here n_K is the number of sites on one side at terminal spacing, so n_K⁴ is the number of terminal sites. This is a bound on the Balaban-normalized integral used for numerator and denominator of the single-torus history ratio; it does not compare the vacuum subtractions on two different tori.

*Volume and scalar convention.* CMP109 printed pp.251–252 (0.1) defines T_ε and its T_ε^{(k)} by the same continuous torus partitioned into cubes at the indicated spacing. CMP119 printed pp.243–244 starts from exp[−A/g₀²−E] and stops when the current lattice is the unit lattice. Printed p.263 specifies counts in the respective scales for the action estimates preceding (2.50). The notation in LFR II (0.1) is explicitly the same type of stability estimate as in [16]. Its referenced primary predecessor spells out the volume convention: in three dimensions (3) on printed p.256 identifies |T_ε| with the sum of ε³ over its lattice points and the text after (5) identifies the count of current unit-lattice sites with the sum of η³ over the fine lattice at η=L⁻ᵏ. In the d-dimensional cubical geometry (0.1) the same cell-volume count is Σ_{x∈T_η}η^d; directly each current unit cell contains L^{dk} such fine cells. In four dimensions at the prescribed stop this is L^{-4K} n₀⁴=n_K⁴. This argument transfers the geometric measure convention only, not a three-dimensional stability theorem. CMP119 p.264 (2.49),(2.50) uses the one inductively normalized density ρ_K in both its bounds. The scalar E introduced in ρ₀ is already present in the numerator of (7.212), since the terminal reward is an insertion in its terminal history integrals, and in its denominator ∫ρ_K. Thus no bare partition function with a different E is being bounded below. Bałaban, three-dimensional stability, printed p.256, (3)–(5), [original Michigan archival PDF](https://backend.production.deepblue-documents.lib.umich.edu/server/api/core/bitstreams/c7173c4d-aedd-46fb-9680-37834ace6a15/content), [CMP109, (0.1)](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01215223), CMP119, (2.50).

*The regional input really satisfies (7).* Restrict each terminal link to a fixed real ball ||V_e−I||<r_*; the size r_*>0 will depend on g_* and the original constants only. For the global homogeneous determining set the prescribed plaquette products then lie within 4r_* of I. For each regional U_{K,□′}(V), use the same prescription as (1.2),(1.3),(3.2),(3.6): take B_K(□′^{~4}) with the mixed targets from the complete simple lift Q^{s*}V. In the original K-level simple lift, links inside each terminal block are I and those crossing one terminal face equal its V on that bond. One original averaging step gives exactly the same face lift on the next lattice: each relevant coordinate path stays in its two blocks, all internal factors are I, and all crossings between them give the same terminal face link. Induction proves this simultaneously at every intermediate level. There is no iterated Lipschitz cost C^K. It follows that at each determining interface in CMP102 (7), any missing bond completed by the mean of the finer prescribed rows is the same link of this coarser face lift. The four completed plaquette factors are each I or a terminal link (or its inverse), so their product deviation is at most 4r_* uniformly in K. This is why merely counting the fine plaquettes of a nonsmooth face lift as an action competitor would not suffice for the terminal lower bound. CMP119, printed pp.246,256–257,265–266, CMP102, printed pp.278–279, (2),(3),(7),(8).

Choose r_* below the Theorem 1 threshold in CMP102. Its assertion (8) places each regular minimal orbit in the space (2) with ceiling B₃·4r_*. On the top layer of a regional determining set this gives ||∂U_{K,□′}−I||≤4B₃r_* L^{-2K} on the required fine plaquettes. The tested □′^{~} in (3.2) is inside the support □′^{~4} with its native test layers; CMP119 p.256 explicitly places the support with two top M₁ layers removed inside Ω_K of the minimal determining set. The three spare inspection layers give at least this clearance under the original M₂,R_K choices. The same check uses periodic lifts when the original admissible partitions cross a chosen fundamental domain. Take 4B₃r_*<ε_K with strict margin. Every factor of the *original* χ_K(T_η) on this cylinder then equals one. For the global minimal orbit all fine plaquettes are top-layer plaquettes. Since the Wilson defect is bounded by a fixed constant times ||∂U−I||² on the real compact group,
`A(U_K(V))≤C n₀⁴ r_*² L^{-4K}=C r_*² n_K⁴.`
The candidate Haar cylinder for the terminal integration has measure at least [c_G r_*^{dim G}]^{4 n_K⁴}, by the regular exponential-coordinate Haar density. Integrate the lower side of the actual (2.50) on this cylinder; g_*⁻² and r_* are fixed. The upper side integrates over normalized product Haar. This proves (7.219) with its same-torus constants; a varying g_K tending to zero would not have the same conclusion. No global gauge fixing, toron restriction on the rest of the integral, or comparison between distinct scalar normalizations was used. ∎

Under these explicit stopping and domain conventions one may bound B̄_stop in (7.213)–(7.218) by exp(C(g_*) n_K⁴) on the fixed reference torus. The volume cost remains present for a small cluster in a growing physical volume. Where the stopping convention or the stated native χ cylinder differs, the unshortened ratio exp(C_+V_stop)/Z_stop is the appropriate statement. The S94 cross-torus vacuum matching and T5/T6 source coefficient hypotheses remain separate.

### 7.97 The layer and age estimate before the stop

**Lemma 7.153 (intermediate layers under the full physical law).** Replace the terminal scale K in the *layer* event of (7.216) by any intermediate stage t≤K, and evaluate its probability in the same normalized original joint law up to the true stop K. The bound holds with `C B̄_stop L^{-A(t−n−1)}`, with no extensive factor exp(C n_t⁴). It applies also to a specified old carrier meeting the active Z_j of the t-record. In the latter case it can be combined with the squared-bank estimate for any specified incident eligible shapes.

*Proof.* At the intermediate record, (2.1) gives an occupied chain up to t. There is at most one current rough component containing the indicated home; do not sum unrestricted placements on its t-grid. If it heals at its next or any later R at ℓ, its complete continuing history is an internal T′_ℓ insertion. Give just the indicated chain the factor L^{A(t−n−1)}: by the occupied-volume estimate in (7.105) the original majorant still applies, at sufficiently weak native parameters. The affine u insertion and the normalized curly bracket argument of Theorem 7.146 give probability ≤C exp(−p_ℓ)L^{-A(t−n−1)} after summing all possibilities for its shape through the home. For a pre-R t record include ℓ=t itself. The sum over ℓ up to K is uniformly bounded by the running sum already displayed in (7.210). An uninterrupted terminal descendant is estimated by (7.212) with the same age insertion. This also works when the component was unprocessed rather than eligible at t; only the *later* healing needs a bona fide T′ interior. When several incident shapes are marked, each squared earliest-birth reward is charged once. An additional future elapsed time need be paid here for only one or two selected continuous paths, not once for every ancestor after they have merged. ∎

For an actual old scalar of the R or B type in §7.95 evaluated on its admitted unmarked *intermediate* physical readout, the same proof of (7.217) gives
`||G^R_{j,x}(U_t)−c_x||₂ ≤ C B̄_stop^{1/2} b_j P_j (1+t−j)^q L^{-4(t−j)}.`   (7.220)
Indeed on each layer use the original pointwise bound from (3.48),(3.49), then average with Lemma 7.153 instead of (7.216). A retained boundary carrier touching the current t-record's Z_j has the stronger arbitrary fixed age as there. The identity scalar and any missing-carrier term are treated by the same subtraction, including its rough-membership indicator. This assertion uses only the actual t-marginal physical data; it is not an inference from the unmodified Gaussian law. It concerns the direct retained term, not the full accumulated source mean unless every emitted family of that mean has been identified and summed.

**Proposition 7.154 (a two-age comparison for a normalized fresh T row).** Let two admitted *direct retained* scalar inputs be born at i,j≤t, with true source homes x,y. Let K_{xy,t} denote their covariance when the next original small-field variables of (3.27) are integrated at a fixed mixed record. Suppose they obey (7.220) on the physical t-marginal (or its stronger B version). Assume also the following rough spatial bound for this same normalized fresh calculation, keeping all geometry prices visible:
`E_out |K_{xy,t}|≤ C_* b_i b_j P_i P_j L^{D[(t−i)+(t−j)]} exp[−c dist_t(x,y)]`   (7.221)
for fixed D,c>0. On native kernels with fixed old/current age this is the ordinary marked-numerator/exclusion bound (3.44)–(3.47) on an admitted (3.43) readout; Theorem 7.130 proves the relevant one-step boundary transfer with its explicit incidence price. For arbitrary old age (7.221) requires its actual source-home localized old substitution and compatible ordinary/annealed support norm. In particular (7.220) alone is not a proof of (7.221).

Then for 0<θ<1, writing m=t−i, n=t−j, the same two-home connected row obeys
`E_out |K_{xy,t}| ≤ C' b_i b_j P_i P_j (1+m)^q(1+n)^q L^{-[4(1−θ)−Dθ](m+n)} exp[−cθ dist_t(x,y)],`   (7.222)
with C' containing the stated terminal and spatial constants. Thus at equal birth scales the row summed over y has a positive summable elapsed power whenever 8(1−θ)−2Dθ>4. This comparison keeps the two physical means and their normalization; it does not replace a mixed kernel by a clean one.

*Proof.* Conditional Cauchy–Schwarz and then unconditional Cauchy–Schwarz bound E_out |K_{xy,t}| by the product of the two rooted L² norms in (7.220). The deterministic identity constants disappear from conditional covariance; membership holes have already been included in (7.220). Take the weighted geometric mean of this bound and (7.221) to obtain (7.222). The sum over old y of the exponential costs C_{θ,c} L^{4(t−j)} by current-cell counting. At equal ages any sufficiently small positive θ leaves a strictly decaying geometric series in t−j. This is an explicit reduction of the different-release-time problem to the *localized normalized fresh covariance* on each still-missing mixed readout; a mere scalar sup pressure cannot replace (7.221). ∎

### 7.98 An absolute late-scale row without a spatial assumption

**Corollary 7.155 (the last part of the mixed tower for direct retained rows).** Use the actual mixed law and the two specified old families of (7.220), including their original membership indicators. Let m=t−i, n=t−j and d=K−t. For the true fresh covariance, without (7.221),
`sup_x Σ_{y at scale j} E_out |K_{xy,t}| ≤ C B̄_stop n_K⁴ b_i b_j P_i P_j (1+m)^q(1+n)^q L^{-4(m−d)}.`   (7.223)
This holds for the real normalized conditional integral at any mixed stage to which (7.220) applies, irrespective of the number and arrangement of its active rough regions. The transposed column has exponent −4(n−d). At equal births i=j and fixed reference volume, fix 0<δ<1/2. The entire part `t≥i+(1/2+δ)(K−i)` is absolutely summable in t and y, with extra bound `C_δ B̄_stop n_K⁴ b_i² P_i² (1+K−i)^{2q} L^{-8δ(K−i)}`. One can instead require `m≥(1+δ)d` to obtain a positive power of the elapsed age. For a genuine retained B input at x its exponent 4m in this calculation can be replaced by any fixed A m at the corresponding weak margin. Arbitrarily large fixed multiples of the late range can thus be covered when that home is a surviving B. 

*Proof.* The individual conditional covariance satisfies `E_out |K_{xy,t}|≤||G_{x,i}−c_x||₂ ||G_{y,j}−c_y||₂` even if the positive conditional means vary across all the outer records. Apply (7.220) twice. The number of j-homes is at most `C n_K⁴ L^{4(K−j)}`; multiplication cancels the second factor `L^{-4n}` and leaves (7.223). At equal births m−d=2t−K−i increases by two at each step, so the stated time sum follows by a geometric series. If x has a surviving B, replace L^{-4m} in the same product by L^{-Am}, retaining the factor L^{4d} after summing y. This method uses only the true full-law second moments and the fixed reference size, hence does not require any off-shell derivative of a gauge frame. The factors b_j and P_j in the conclusion are the actual given birth and chart costs. The assertion pays the fresh covariance of these direct rows, not every conditional mean newly emitted from their previous integrations. ∎

### 7.99 A localized earlier row on the mixed small-field integral

Here is one class at arbitrary old age where (7.221) can be replaced by a stronger estimate. Specify the term *before* any R operation at the new stage. Take an old ordinary scalar of the original (2.30)–(2.32) type, with source home x in its old carrier X at scale i and physical norm `b_i exp(−κ d_i(X))`. Use the small-X cover terms of CMP109 (3.4),(3.5),(3.33),(3.34), for which X is inside the specified local regular chart and its carrier/old root lies in the indicated initial cover cube and its fixed collar. Keep the actual Taylor remainder after degree four in (3.34). Denote the resulting part of the integrated insertion by F⁵_{x,i}. Sum allowed old X through the *particular* x, without summing x over its old grid. Take a fixed top-layer cover assignment at x, or more generally the assignment of a scale-n cover with x in its physical layer n≥i. If needed, choose each contribution separately with its original bounded partition functions. Consider the original (3.27) mixed conditioned law on records having the ordinary unmarked support estimates, with a spare native decay and small-activity reserve, on its (3.43) domains. No free passage across a resummed live body is included in those estimates. This includes original T waits with the regular region nonempty and an unprocessed rough exterior before the first eligible R, on the native unmarked domains. Arbitrarily long such waits exist on trajectories with increasing first qualification scale as in §7.82, by using the single seed there before its first qualification. The kernel and the integration are the original mixed ones. No alteration of the real selector is made.

**Proposition 7.156 (two rooted fifth remainders in a mixed ordinary T).** For two such selected assignments at physical layers n_x,n_y and old scales i,j, the actual conditional covariance obeys
`|Cov_T(F⁵_{x,i},F⁵_{y,j})| ≤ C b_i b_j P_i P_j L^{-5(n_x−i)-5(n_y−j)} exp[−c dist_t(x,y)].`   (7.224)
Here t is the incoming scale of (3.27), the layer indices are those in its mixed cover, and shifting a top index by one changes the fixed constant only. P_i includes the old-chart Cauchy factors through order five and fixed original test radii. This is a bound on the Taylor remainder of the actual admitted ordinary term. It does not assert a fifth-order zero of its complete physical insertion.

*The localized remainder.* On a chart of side 2M at its native n scale, CMP109 (3.32)–(3.36) and the domain verification through (3.54) control the fifth Taylor remainder by the fifth power of the small old physical potential scale `L^{i−n}`. The argument is Cauchy's estimate for the old scalar on its extended (U,J) domain and Taylor's integral along its actual localized field; its factor scales linearly with the old sup norm. CMP116 (1.9),(1.10),(1.23),(1.24) make this estimate *with the weakening variables switched on*. The starting domain contains the cover cube and its four-collar. If this domain is disconnected from any other component of the switched-on variables, the equations (1.3),(1.4) separate and a derivative in that component vanishes. Thus the localized term has a connected support through the starting domain. Cauchy in the weakening parameters gives its exponential support rate as in (1.24),(1.25). The factor `(L^iη)^5` is explicit in the proof prior to (1.27), where the unrestricted sum over old cubes would spend four of its powers. At a fixed x that volume sum is absent. The old support sum through x uses (1.26) on a spare old rate. With x in the selected starting collar, the localized kernel therefore has a current-rooted ordinary norm at most `C b_i P_i L^{-5(n−i)}`. Moving a root within that initial collar has bounded cost in current units. The localization is for a bounded scalar potential on the native fluctuation contour, and the same bounds on its weakening contours are what is needed for its insertion in the next cluster expansion.

CMP119 printed pp.275–277 gives the extension of precisely these operations to (3.27): use its layer cover, replace η by L^{-n} for terms assigned at that layer, take the mixed walk expansions and the spaces (3.43) for output touching the boundary. It explicitly treats old R in the same way as old E at this stage, with the coupling subtraction omitted for R. No unique scalar marginal projection is used for (7.224). The metric of the ordinary mixed walks bounds a fixed multiple of the projected t-distance, up to bounded starting collars: each unit of path at the finer native scale advances at most one unit at scale t. In the version of (2.42) with resummed free interiors this inference would fail. [CMP109, §3](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01215223), [CMP116, (1.6)–(1.29), (2.38)–(2.41)](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01239022), CMP119, pp.275–279.

*The normalized connected bound.* Write a_x for the preceding rooted norm including its constant. Insert `z F⁵_{x,i}+w F⁵_{y,j}` in the actual exponent (3.27). On `|z|≤ε/a_x`, `|w|≤ε/a_y`, the two supplemental localized vertices have combined norm ≤2ε, including their weakened extensions. Choose ε inside the original strict reserve in (2.38); equivalently use the first and second polarized coefficients of the exponential, whose norms have the same estimate. Terms independent of the integration field may be carried as exterior scalars and drop out of the mixed derivative. In the unnormalized partition the source-independent polymers are exactly those of its original denominator. Normalizing or taking the logarithm cancels the disconnected ones, as is also seen from the fixed-source exclusion sum (3.44)–(3.46). A nonzero zw coefficient of the connected log has support reaching both initial collars: its two tagged vertices and the intervening overlapping cluster have connected union. Pool a fixed spare part of the ordinary length for the distance between the projected x and y. The remaining rooted sums converge by (2.38)–(2.41), as for the unmarked norm; a cluster coefficient of product type is included only if the two labels lie in its same connected union. Cauchy at the two radii gives `C a_x a_y exp(−c dist_t)`. The mixed derivative is exactly `⟨F⁵_x F⁵_y⟩_T−⟨F⁵_x⟩_T⟨F⁵_y⟩_T`, on the one actual normalized measure. This proves (7.224). ∎

At fixed x,y the allowed pair of native layers n_x,n_y can be annealed under the full outer law while retaining the indicated subfamily of mixed records. For x a home in layer n_x, Lemma 7.153 bounds the probability of that layer by `C B̄_stop L^{-A(t−n_x−1)}`; use one for the top layer. Apply Cauchy–Schwarz to the two layer indicators, including the case of one common occupied component. Taking A>10, the two geometric sums over n_x,n_y converge with their full fifth powers. With bounded overlap of the initial assignments at each home and layer, this gives
`E_out [1_{ordinary mixed records}|Cov_T(F⁵_{x,i},F⁵_{y,j})|] ≤ C B̄_stop b_i b_j P_i P_j L^{-5(t−i)-5(t−j)} exp[−c dist_t(x,y)].`   (7.225)
Here the sum over assignments means the selected initial covers with the homes in their own physical layers; no assertion is made for differently anchored or very long old carriers. For a second-home sum the ordinary exponential costs `C L^{4(t−j)}`, including on a periodic torus. In particular the true covariance of these stable remainder rows is absolutely summable at equal birth scales, even in the earlier half of the tower where (7.223) gives no such conclusion. Degree ≤4, general extended mixed B, sharp-wall completions, and re-emission from conditional means have their own rows. A second jet originally present in either action contributes its conditional expectation separately. The estimate is for the covariance of the identified first rows only.

### 7.100 Several inspection times on the same genealogy

The incident supports of more than one transfer need not be at the same scale. An earlier and a later recorded body may have only one ordinary failure between them. The volume moment has a version which does not count these as two independent birth events.

**Theorem 7.157 (normalized multiscale occupied-volume moment).** Prescribe a finite list S of m distinct pairs (j,Y) of scales and candidate connected live components, at a fixed convention for the pre- or post-R record at each j. At a given scale a realized Y has to be the actual component of that record, not an arbitrary subregion counted many times. Write v_j(Y) for its native M-cube count and `V(S)=Σ_{(j,Y) realized} v_j(Y)`. A chain in a component which completely heals is ended there; a later birth at the same place belongs to its own history. Among the realized labels, match any number of them to **distinct** ordinary birth components in their continuing past, allowing at most one match per label and per birth. Let W(S) be the largest sum of `p_j²` over the matched labels, taking zero for the empty match. For every fixed s>0 on the corresponding weak native margins,
`E exp[s V(S)+a W(S)] ≤ B̄_stop exp[C m Σ_{ℓ=1}^K e^{-p_ℓ}].`   (7.226)
The terminal ratio has the form (7.212) with the allowed stability constant at the chosen s. For labels whose entire realized ancestry heals before the stop, the analogous moment restricted to their contributions omits B̄_stop. The estimates do not require a count of distinct failures from the length of the wait. Time-local indices in the sum over ℓ may be restricted to possible releases. In particular, for a family of prescribed full shapes whose simultaneous occurrence is required,
`Pr(all occur) ≤ B̄_stop exp[C m Σ_ℓ e^{-p_ℓ} − s Σ_{(j,Y)∈S} v_j(Y)]`   (7.227)
with the further matching exponent when there is a guaranteed matching.

*Proof.* In the full positive unintegrated representation, partition earlier labels according to the first healing of each continuing component, or its unprocessed/remaining terminal component. At each scale a contributing native M-cube lies in at most one distinct actual Y. Thus inside any unbroken history the total charged native volume is bounded by its actual `Σ_j |Z_j|_j` up to fixed unit factors. It adds a fixed coefficient s to the occupied-volume expense of (1.79); the size inequalities used in (1.80)–(1.89) pay this on the corresponding weak margin as in (7.105). Preparatory reinstatement preserves the lineage up to an actual healing and gives no duplicate volume at a given inspection. For W, distinct matches use distinct terms in the squared first-birth product of (1.79). The birth time h precedes or equals its matched time j, so `p_h²≥c p_j²` on the running margin. Keep the linear merger reserve and use only a fixed part of the squared one. A maximizing matching can be found inside the actual history; there is no summation over matchings in the bound. The past of one fully released component is disjoint from the unbroken past of the other releases and the terminally unprocessed components. Hence the optimization splits over them. If a still-occupied history has several earlier labels but a single birth, at most one of those labels uses its squared bank. The volume addition still charges each *actual scale-volume* once.

At any release ℓ give each healing X the affine factor `1+u(exp[s V_X+a W_X]−1)` for the labels in its unbroken lineage. These quantities are internal old history variables as in (1.102); later prescribed labels, including a new label at a previously healed position, use the surviving outer record and later randomizations. The same estimates (1.89),(1.95) give the normalized pre-Mayer polynomial a zero-free disc `|u|≤c exp(p_ℓ)` after the occupied-volume and birth expenses just paid. Its degree is ≤m since each nonconstant factor needs a distinct realized label. At u=1 its absolute ratio to the value at zero is at most `exp[C m exp(−p_ℓ)]`, pointwise at the fixed unintegrated surviving data. Multiply these conditional inequalities in increasing order of release as in (7.210), leaving later and terminal labels in that data. The unprocessed terminal weight is bounded by (7.212) with the same occupied-volume addition instead of m copies of the same ancestry; its original upper stability constant can be chosen on the remaining margins. This proves (7.226) and Markov's inequality gives (7.227). For S at one time there is a matching of every realized body by Lemma 7.145. For a single body surviving through many inspection times there need be only one match. ∎

**Corollary 7.158 (annealed sum for a connected history support).** Form the space-time lattice of native M-cube homes: join neighboring cubes at one scale, and each to its parent at the next scale. Finite torus identifications can lower its degree. Consider an actual family of connected terms whose absolute bound, *after forming its own correctly normalized signed kernel*, is a sum over such connected supports rooted at x. In a term let V be the native space-time volume of the union of its completely incident specified live bodies, using any site only once at a given stage, and N the number of remaining sites of its connected support. Suppose its coefficient outside the history indicators is bounded by `D exp(C₀V−κN)` and that its extra filings at a fixed colored support have multiplicity at most `exp(C₁(V+N))`. Then on the above weak/decay margins the total annealed absolute connected sum through x and y is bounded by `C D B̄_stop exp[−h dist_hier(x,y)]`, for h below the residual ordinary and occupied-volume rates. Here `dist_hier` is graph distance on the indicated space-time lattice. The result holds regardless of the number of times or the number of incident components. It applies also to the joint sums of this type arising from products of already bounded kernels; it does not manufacture a bound for a previously uncontrolled conditional mean.

*Proof.* For each deterministic assignment use (7.227). The term `C m Σe^{-p_ℓ}` is at most a constant times V, since m≤V and the running sum is bounded on the stated trajectory. No separate price per ancestor common to many labels is used. The graph has degree at most `2d+1+L^d` up to the fixed enlargement of the chosen home stencils. Connected animals of size v rooted at a specified vertex number at most `Δ^{2v}` by a depth-first traversal. Choices of occupied sites and of intralayer component edges cost at most `2^{(1+Δ)v}`; further allowed filings satisfy the assumed multiplicity bound. Sum with v=V+N, choosing s in (7.227) and the outside reserve κ larger than these fixed costs plus h. Each contributing support then has v≥dist_hier(x,y) (up to the additive root convention), giving the stated bound by a geometric series. At equal birth i the physical distance d_i satisfies `d_i(x,y)≤C v L^v` for a connected support of v vertices: each spatial edge advances at most L^v old units and parent/child offsets obey the same bound. Consequently an arbitrarily prescribed fixed spatial power s₀>4 is available if h is chosen sufficiently larger than s₀ log L, yielding a uniformly summable old-home row. This final reduction needs the stated native absolute support estimate for the signed contributions being summed. Unrestricted generated R/B and marginal rows have not all been placed in that representation. ∎

### 7.101 The complete direct ordinary scalar in one unshifted mixed T

For a complete direct ordinary R, a rough spatial estimate before angular or coupling projections is enough, by Proposition 7.154. Fix an unshifted mixed record (`S_{t+1}=∅` in the source-dependent readout of (3.21)–(3.25)) with the ordinary unmarked one-step support estimates, native (2.28) old R domains and the cover/weakening margins of CMP119 pp.275–277, as in §7.99. Keep the actual fixed exterior and use (3.27) with its unmarked interpolation parameters at the physical endpoint. Denote this class of exterior determinations by D. In particular it permits unprocessed rough exterior during an ordinary wait. No plus-part rescue of a signed denominator is used. An A or J slot of an external B record is not an ordinary R of the prescribed type merely because it agrees on some real physical configurations.

**Proposition 7.159 (two direct ordinary first rows before a new R).** On D take two complete direct old scalar rows R_{x,i},R_{y,j} satisfying (7.220), with the original gauge-invariant holomorphic birth functions and specified homes through every old X in the respective sum. Retain their original restrictions to Λ_i,Λ_j. Their fresh covariance on D satisfies (7.221) with some finite D₀ in the exponent, where the letter D₀ here denotes a numerical exponent only. More precisely it has the pointwise bound `C b_i b_j P_i P_j L^{D₀[(t−i)+(t−j)]} exp[−c dist_t(x,y)]`.
