This gives a summable old-home row at equal births at *every* scale of this class, including the part before (7.223) applies. The result only uses given direct old source families with these hypotheses.

*Proof.* Subtract the actual background value from each insertion inside its normalized conditional covariance. The subtraction is constant at fixed outer state. On this unshifted record the difference is exactly the physical substitution (3.3),(3.4) with each actual old X, not a new lower representative at the current mesh. The old restrictions in (2.30),(2.31) are fixed for this conditional integral. For a fixed x, keep X∋x everywhere. Here is the localization estimate for the *whole* difference with an intentionally rough age cost.

For the cover cube □ in (3.4) use both cases of (3.5). If X is not contained in its two-collar, use the unaltered analytic extension (3.6)–(3.17). These are the native derivative and physical-current formulas, including the covariant-Laplacian condition on the original H, rather than a derivative bound in an independently chosen axial frame. For the far case, (3.9),(3.17) pay the separation of X and □. For a large X the old support exponential also pays its diameter. CMP116 (1.30)–(1.32) defines X₀ to be the smallest current localization domain **containing X**, and switches on the walk variables outside X₀. Thus each localized term contains the old home. The two rates in (1.32) pay a current output tree and the sum over old X∋x respectively. The sum over the cube where (3.4) was differentiated is exactly the cube sum subsequent to (1.32); fixing x is a restriction of the unmarked absolute sum. Its cost at any fixed output support can alternatively be bounded by its cube volume in the finest permitted native cover. If n≥i, the number of such n-cubes per current t-cube is ≤C L^{4(t−i)}, allowing the crude cost in the statement. An extensive sum over all current output carriers is not taken.

If X is contained in the two-collar, its projection and x lie in the fixed starting collar of (1.10). For the rough estimate one can retain the complete old function on this chart without extracting any marginal coefficient. More explicitly, in (3.33),(3.34), the local function of the old physical field and current on the shortened patch has its analytic extension on the actual weakened fields by (3.31)–(3.54), (1.17)–(1.22). Its norm is bounded by the old sup bound times the fixed shortened-chart factor P_i. For the Taylor polynomial through degree four the same statement follows by Cauchy on a smaller ray disc in the extended argument of (3.36); for the fifth remainder use (1.24). Equivalently retain the entire evaluation at the physical ray endpoint instead of its Taylor decomposition. The proof of (1.23) differentiates the cover parameter by a Cauchy circle as well, (1.22), so this evaluation estimates the localized response in (3.4), not just an unvaried scalar on an arbitrary external field. The local-to-regional difference in (3.21) is localized by the same procedure, as specified immediately before CMP116 Lemma 1 (1.33). No Euclidean-invariance cancellation or identification of individual low coefficients is used in this bound. The original old chart estimate carries `exp(−κd_i(X))`. The Cauchy estimates for switched-on cubes generate the current tree factor (1.24),(1.25) even when the extra fifth Taylor power is dropped. For definiteness take each localized term on a strictly smaller fixed contour and use a spare old support rate; the finitely many Taylor/physical derivatives used here are among P_i. Sum over X through x with (1.26). The sum over possible □ per current cube and over n≥i costs at most `C(1+t−i)L^{4(t−i)}`. Initial collars remain uniformly bounded in current units. On mixed D these constructions use the native layer domains of CMP119 p.276 and its actual weakened walk kernels, including output touching a boundary on (3.43). These are the places the original unmarked analyticity/ordinary decay margins and the old readout type are used.

In both cases the resulting extra bounded scalar vertex family has an *ordinary* localized norm through the projection of x, at most `a_x=C b_i P_i L^{D₀(t−i)}`, e.g. enlarging D₀ to pay polynomial cover factors. The corresponding statement holds for y. This rough norm does not assert any age gain on nonphysical weakened fields. The factor `exp(i[g_tCA−hD(g_tCA)])` and its original cutoff are kept; no fine variable in a pinned core is freely varied. Apply the two finite-source argument of Proposition 7.156 on radii ε/a_x,ε/a_y. A connected logarithmic derivative contains both projected homes, because its input carriers contain their initial roots also in the remote case (1.30). The ordinary unmarked support slack supplies the distance factor. The derivative is exactly the covariance of the two complete marked differences. This proves the asserted pointwise estimate. For the other bound in the interpolation, conditional Cauchy–Schwarz at the physical endpoint and then the unconditional (7.220) apply with `1_D≤1`. Root identity constants disappear. The geometric mean argument (7.222) now proves the claimed summable row on D. [CMP109, (3.3)–(3.17),(3.21),(3.34)–(3.54)](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01215223), [CMP116, (1.10),(1.22)–(1.36)](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01239022), CMP119, (3.21)–(3.27), pp.275–279. ∎

The same proof applies when one marked proper difference is zero because all its data are pinned; its fresh covariance is then zero exactly, while its outer mean remains. Formula (7.226) addresses the incidence-volume expense of many stages once their *normalized* support bounds exist. It does not turn Proposition 7.159 into an estimate for a new carried boundary frame, for a shifted selector, or for a source resummation whose unmarked polymers already pass freely through large interiors. The outgoing low/contact families generated by the preceding integrations still have to be followed separately.

### 7.102 The exterior selector change in a normalized fresh integral

**Proposition 7.160 (the real conditional covariance under the actual selector shift).** On a real mixed T determination fix the outer target, the original geometry and all independent exterior coordinates. Let I denote the independent A-coordinates integrated in Λ_{t+1} and E the remaining coordinates of this conditional operation. The shifts (1.22),(3.22) act only on independent bonds in E. Write e′ for the coordinates after this change and e=φ(e′) for their actual values before it, with the retained upper fields included as parameters of φ. If F,G are any bounded physical insertions carried through the same coordinate substitution, then almost everywhere on the admitted real exterior,
`Cov_{T,shift}(F∘φ,G∘φ | e′)=Cov_{T,original}(F,G | e=φ(e′)).`   (7.228)
The two conditional first moments and the conditional expectation of an inherited second jet obey the same identity. Consequently Proposition 7.159 applies at shifted records whose back-transformed *real* exterior is in its original ordinary T chart (without the requirement S=∅ on that back-transformed parametrization). Use (7.228) at fixed retained data before averaging over e′ with its actual marginal. The result is for the physical fresh covariance; differentiating a new exterior source represented on an independently complexified e′ would be a different operation.

*Proof.* In (1.20) and in its general version (3.20), Λ lies inside Ω with two layers removed, excludes the enlargement of the failed set R and can only shrink when small complementary components are replaced by their bounding parallelepipeds. The set `S=(Ω\Ω^{~−1})∪R` is therefore outside Λ, with the stated native buffer. In (3.22) the function H^{(t)}(b) depends on the *upper background* restricted to `Λ_{t+1}^c∩Λ_t`. It is fixed in this conditional integral over the independent bonds of Λ_{t+1}. The smooth scalar cutoff g(A′(b)) in (1.22) is evaluated only on an exterior starred coordinate. On the other S bonds this scalar is identically one. Thus the actual transformation is `(I,e′)↦(I,φ(e′))`. The physical reconstructed dependent pivot bonds need not be fixed; their change is determined by these same independent coordinates. No change of phase or arbitrary extension of an edge gauge is implicated. CMP119, pp.251–252 and 269–270, (1.20)–(1.23),(3.20)–(3.25).

If the old joint density at fixed geometry is w(I,e), the transformed density with respect to dI de′ is `w(I,φ(e′)) |det Dφ(e′)|` with the original transformed selectors and Haar factors kept in w. The Jacobian cancels when dividing by its integral over I, at every e′ with positive conditional mass. The selected determinant, background terms and prior geometry indicators have not been dropped from the outer marginal. Applying this equality to 1,F,G,FG proves (7.228), including a source-free shift with an inherited jet. Equivalently, the full S-dependent terms V^{(t)} generated by changing variables are recombined into the original conditional numerator before applying the identity. Dropping V^{(t)} at fixed e′ would not give (7.228).

On S the primary bound is `||H^{(t)}||≤C ε_t exp(−R_t)`. The original exterior displacement in physical link arguments is O(`ε_t exp(−R_t)`), since the group product in (1.22) differs by a factor of this magnitude, uniformly for 0≤g(A′)≤1. On a fixed logarithm chart the corresponding canonical coordinate displacement is at most `C ε_t exp(−R_t)/g_t`. In particular a strict original tube in the independent physical arguments survives this shift if its available margin exceeds this bound in matching units and its required downstream readout already satisfies the original (2.28),(3.43) estimates. This observation does not certify a zero-width old selector boundary, or every nonlocal joined frame, by continuity. The map and its inverse used in changing variables are precisely those of the native real construction. The argument makes no holomorphic extension of the C∞ function g. ∎

### 7.103 The first and second source jets when a marginal coefficient is born again

Use the unamplified physical fine source `Σ_x z_x h_x`, with the designated comb restriction if present. The initial first jet is h_x, the initial connected second jet is zero. No factor a^{-2} is inserted. In the regular field chart (7.159), a single h_x has zero constant-curvature quadratic jet, because each incident opposite-plaquette pair is a covariant first difference. This statement is about its classical physical field dependence; the conditional scalar and marginal jets of its integrated fluctuation action can already be nonzero at its first quantum integration.

Choose the following filing convention at each stage. On a regular localized carrier take its constant value, then its *entire* constant-curvature quadratic tensor in the local rooted field expansion, and retain the exact difference. The scalar action projection is the hypercubic scalar trace of this tensor, with the compact plaquette representative normalized to have that same Hessian on an Abelian constant curvature. The other quadratic components, including electric versus magnetic anisotropy, are carried too. The extraction is linear; projecting a tensor and multiplying its exact chosen representative is the identity on this finite space. Use local moment kernels with the old home and its positions retained, as in §§7.48–7.51; in a periodic winding term use its actual winding remainder. The point at which an arbitrary joined boundary chart has no verified projection is filed wholly in the boundary remainder. A geometry-dependent scalar is part of the fluctuating state until that geometry is fixed. These conventions affect the individual coefficients, but the reconstructed jets are equal on their original domain.

**Proposition 7.161 (the mixed two-jet recurrence with both homes).** At a given physical state write the first log jet as `A_x=d_x+M_x+U_x` and the second as `B_xy=d_xy+N_xy+V_xy`, where M,N are the filed marginal operator rows and U,V are the stable and mixed boundary remainder rows, with all earlier source homes retained. Constants here can be removed before covariance only if they are independent of the variables of this integration. Use the projection vector `P=(P₀,P₄,1−P₀−P₄)` on the justified outgoing carriers, as just specified, and the boundary convention elsewhere. For one physical T, followed by one physical R, the recurrence is exactly
`P A_x^T = P T(A_x),     P B_xy^T=P [T(B_xy)+κ_T(A_x,A_y)].`   (7.229)
In (7.229), κ_T is the connected covariance with the same normalized (3.27) denominator. In particular it contains `κ_T(M_x,M_y)+κ_T(M_x,U_y)+κ_T(U_x,M_y)+κ_T(U_x,U_y)` when d_x,d_y are independent of that kernel. Boundaries, history-dependent constants, and different-age terms are all retained in this bilinear expansion.

For the ensuing R, let C_x,C_xy be the sourced exterior completions from A′ and other fixed log factors. In the *literal* curly bracket of (1.72), let D_x,D_xy denote its proper first and second log jets before the remaining history and live integrations, including the prescribed old-minus-added terms on their true determinations and any earlier T jets. Then
`P A_x^+=P[C_x+⟨D_x⟩_R],   P B_xy^+=P[C_xy+⟨D_xy⟩_R+κ_R(D_x,D_y)].`   (7.230)
An exterior C may fluctuate at the *next* scale. A pinned minus-added term which is identically zero has zero proper contribution, while its C is still carried. The scalar contact is P₀ of these second expressions, the new operator-valued marginal contact is P₄, and the rest is their exact mixed remainder. In particular κ_R is a covariance of the conditional T means as well as of any further proper first jets. The two partial derivatives are taken in distinct formal variables even when their numerical homes coincide. LFR II, (1.61)–(1.75),(1.90)–(1.104), CMP119, (3.25)–(3.29).

*Proof.* Work in the finite algebra `z²=w²=0`. The unnormalized joint numerator at one history has relative density `1+zA_x+wA_y+zw(B_xy+A_x A_y)`. Sum with the original common weights, divide by the same unmarked denominator and take its logarithm. Its zw coefficient is (7.229). Apply the identical calculation to the true bracket while retaining C outside that calculation. In its Mayer representation the mixed derivative consists of the double-tag activity times its exclusion ratio, the two compatible single-tag activities times their joint exclusion ratio, and minus the product of the two normalized derivatives. These are precisely the three terms of (7.183) and remain valid with other live integrations by (1.102),(1.103). The resulting formula is (7.230). Applying the fixed linear filing P last proves all three simultaneous recurrences. At regular bulk carriers lying wholly in the new small domain, the unmarked construction agrees termwise with the homogeneous kernel (CMP119 p.278 following (3.47)); the marked assertion follows on the same verified carriers since the connected rooted construction retains both source labels. Carriers meeting an unverified domain are not projected via this observation. ∎

The actual field derivatives in the marginal row have additional terms. For two chart directions u,v in an admitted fixed real fiber, let `s_u=∂_u log w`, `s_uv=∂_v∂_u log w` for the complete unnormalized density w including Jacobian and gauge factors. At a native physical cutoff, use a fixed-coordinate representation or include its surface responses as in §7.16; do not differentiate a discarded selector. For example the bilinear derivative of the fresh covariance is the exact sum
`κ(F_uv,G)+κ(F_u,G_v)+κ(F_v,G_u)+κ(F,G_uv)`
`+ κ(F_u,G,s_v)+κ(F_v,G,s_u)+κ(F,G_u,s_v)+κ(F,G_v,s_u)`
`+ κ(F,G,s_uv)+κ(F,G,s_u,s_v).`   (7.231)
All cumulants are under that same physical zero-source normalization. Similarly `∂_v∂_u⟨B⟩=⟨B_uv⟩+κ(B_u,s_v)+κ(B_v,s_u)+κ(B,s_uv)+κ(B,s_u,s_v)`. These formulas follow by differentiating the normalized joint log-generating polynomial. Retaining only the Hessian of the directly inserted observable in a second-jet feedback would omit terms even on a finite lattice. Surface and completion terms cannot be omitted by setting the external field to its physical value only after differentiating.

### 7.104 A potentially nonsummable marginal contact in the quadratic mixed kernel

**Lemma 7.162 (the signed dipole term and the complete action).** At a constrained quadratic physical Wilson step, keep *all* fixed pins and native linear average constraints, and let m be the minimizing fine field at those data. Write a fine field as `m+β^{-1/2}ξ`, with ξ in the free tangent space. First use the exact positive centered Gaussian on that space (or its centered inversion-symmetric fixed cutoff in a physical axial slice). Let C=⟨ξξᵀ⟩ be its actual covariance. For a local tensor profile f let `M_f=d* f d` on the physical tangent data, writing S_f(A)=AᵀM_fA/2 and viewing free scores as restrictions. Then the exact conditional covariance is
`κ(S_f,S_g)= β⁻¹ (M_f m)ᵀ C (M_g m) + β⁻² κ(S_f(ξ),S_g(ξ)).`   (7.232)
Here C is extended by zero on directions orthogonal to the free integration coordinates, or the free inclusion is inserted on both sides. In a normalized untruncated Gaussian the last coefficient is `(1/2)Tr(C M_f C M_g)`. On the indicated cut it is the *actual cut covariance* and need not be this trace. For the complete uniform physical action, stationarity gives `(M_1 m)|free=0` for all pinned data. Thus its β⁻¹ mixed contact vanishes for **any** other profile. Anisotropic first rows have to be checked separately. The effect of a nonlinear background and of the changing weights in the R bracket is outside this quadratic identity.

*Proof.* Expand both actions at m. Their linear/constant contributions to the connected covariance reduce to the product of the two linear terms shown. Their odd cross moments with the quadratic terms vanish by inversion symmetry. For an isotropic complete action the derivative of the constrained action at its stationary point annihilates every free variation, irrespective of the number of fixed bonds. ∎

On the homogeneous regular linearized chart take the analytic constant-curvature jet `d m=F`, with any fixed Lie-algebra direction. This is the local affine-field coefficient of a complete bulk carrier, or its infinite-volume Bloch moment with winding terms kept separately; it does not presume a continuous nonquantized periodic flux on a finite torus. For any constant tensor f, `d* f F=0` on the full lattice. In particular a single local plaquette coefficient at home x has dipole score `v_x=d*(1_x f F)`, and the coefficient of the two-home marginal contact at order β⁻¹ is the Gram kernel `v_xᵀ C v_y`. It can have a strictly positive diagonal whenever the dipole is nonzero in the free tangent space. Its row and column sums over a full constant profile vanish *before taking absolute values*, since `Σ_y v_y=0`. Omitting the compensating distinct-home terms can therefore produce an apparent `Σ_t β_t⁻¹` divergence. If the sum is restricted to one side of a mixed boundary, the exact leftover is the covariant flux `d*(1_inside f F)` on its boundary. The complementary side has the opposite flux on the same complete affine evaluation. If the two sides use different pinned readouts, their fluxes cannot be canceled by identifying W⁻ with W⁺. They enter (7.230) with the actual old-minus-added determination and its separate exterior completion.

The bare h_x itself has a stronger property here. Its first quadratic symbol is a sum of products of **differences** of the individual directional plaquette curls, as in (7.159). Thus `K_{h,x} m=0` for a constant affine F, one home at a time. A compatible affine field is the unique physical quadratic minimum with its own constraint and pin data: it satisfies those data, and its first variation against all free directions vanishes by `d*F=0`. Transport on this common affine variation gives neither a linear marginal h row nor the β⁻¹ operator-valued affine contact from a pair of bare h insertions in the quadratic calculation, even with a set of literally fixed bonds whose values are varied on that same common affine field. Its scalar covariance trace remains. This observation only concerns the quadratic kernel on that compatible variation. Nonlinear fluctuation integration, or varying coarse data at *fixed incompatible* rough pins, changes the assertion. The true first clean H quantum row and its roots are instead (7.123)–(7.124).

### 7.105 Summation of a marginal response with zero constant-profile row

The β⁻¹ term in (7.232) must be summed over both home locations before deciding that it accumulates with scale. The following estimate permits arbitrary bounded or square-integrable lattice marks. Work first on the complete periodic grids. Write P_{jt} for averaging a j-grid profile over the L^{4(t−j)} sites of each t-cell. Use the normalized square norm `||f||_t²=n_t^{-4}Σ|f|²`. A profile on the coarser grid is embedded as a constant on its cells.

**Lemma 7.163 (differences of nested cell averages).** For a j-grid profile f and any fixed integer displacement z in t-grid units,
`Σ_{t=j}^K ||τ_z P_{jt}f−P_{jt}f||_t² ≤ C_L(1+|z|) ||f||_j².`   (7.233)
The same conclusion holds with a finite-dimensional vector or tensor at each cell. A local matrix map D_t from the t grid to the t+1 grid with exponential kernel bound `|D_t(B,x)|≤C exp[−c|x−LB|]` and vanishing row sum consequently satisfies `Σ_{t=j}^{K−1}||D_t P_{jt}f||_{t+1}²≤C' ||f||_j²`.

*Proof.* Decompose f orthogonally into `P_{js}f−P_{j,s+1}f` on levels s=j,…,K−1 and the final P_{jK}f. A function h constant on s-cells changes under a t-grid shift z only across boundary strips occupying at most `C min(1,|z| L^{t−s})` of each such s-cell. The same estimate applies to both endpoints of the shift in the square difference, giving `||τ_z h−h||≤C min(1,√|z| L^{−(s−t)/2})||h||` for s≥t. P_{jt}f contains just the orthogonal terms of levels s≥t. Convolution with this summable geometric sequence in s−t, then the square identity for orthogonal differences, prove (7.233). For the last assertion subtract the value of the profile at LB in each row, sum displacements by Minkowski, and use the square bound. Sampling at LB for one fixed offset costs at most L² in norm under the two normalized grid measures. The exponential displacement sum with its square-root moment converges. ∎

**Proposition 7.164 (uniform feedback in this channel).** Consider a marginal component satisfying the actual recurring coefficient equation, whenever it has the form
`m_{t+1}=P_{t,t+1}m_t+α_t D_t m_t+E_t m_t+u_t`, 
where D_t has the bounds in Lemma 7.163, `Σ||E_t||≤ε`, and `||α||_{ℓ²}≤ε`. For sufficiently small ε (depending on the fixed row constants) one has, uniformly in K,
`sup_t||m_t||_t + Σ_t ||m_{t+1}−P_{t,t+1}m_t||_{t+1} ≤ C (||m_j||_j+Σ_t||u_t||_{t+1}).`   (7.234)
No independent identically distributed approximation or sign assumption on the D_t is required.

*Proof.* Let e_t denote the total increment after P. Iterate the identity to get `m_t=P_{jt}m_j+Σ_{r<t}P_{r+1,t} e_r`. For each of these initial profiles, Cauchy–Schwarz in t and (7.233) give `Σ_{t≥s}|α_t| ||D_t P_{st} f||≤C ε||f||`. The operator E_t contributes ≤ε||f|| by contraction of cell averaging. Sum first for the initial profile and then for each earlier increment. This bounds `Σ||e_t||` by `Σ||u_t||+(C+1)ε(||m_j||+Σ||e_t||)`; absorb the last term and use the iterated identity. ∎

For the classical constant-curvature part of a homogeneous marginal, P is the actual principal scaling: a fine field curvature is L⁻² times the coarse curvature, so its squared sum weighted by f gives exactly the cell average multiplying coarse F², with the usual fixed within-cell placement convention. For the pair term in (7.232) on this principal profile, bounded row and column norms of C in native units and the divergence form give the scale-normalized bound `C β_t⁻¹ ||∇ P_{jt}f||_t ||∇ P_{jt}g||_t |F|²`. Summing over t by (7.233) bounds the two-home pairing uniformly even with β_t⁻¹ replaced by a bounded number. The unamplified comb ground profile is allowed, and an individual f need not be smooth. This bound keeps the full signed Gram operator. It is not an absolute row estimate with each home assigned an independent sign separately at every scale. For the nonlinear recurrence, a leading β_t⁻¹ operator correction with zero constant-profile row fits (7.234), since the admitted running law gives `Σ_t β_t⁻²≤C/β_*`. A remaining O(β_t^{-1−b}) or O(`β_t^{-1−b}polylog β_t`) operator is absolutely summable for b>0. These statements specify what is sufficient for the actual recurrent kernels. A nonzero constant-profile correction cannot be called a difference operator by subtracting its row sum without tracking that sum.

With all H-source orientations retained, a homogeneous hypercubic-covariant linear step sends the constant traceless tensor into the traceless sector: the projection onto the invariant scalar is zero by averaging its input over the symmetry group. The same symmetry does not kill the scalar projection of *two* anisotropic inputs. On a mixed record multiplication by a small-domain indicator does not commute with the profile differences of (7.233). The commutator is a boundary forcing with the actual nearby determination and (7.230) completion. None of those terms has been set to zero in (7.234).

### 7.106 An exact Ward defect for the true physical action at a mixed step

**Proposition 7.165 (radial Ward identity with the selector and denominator).** Use an admissible real conditional (3.27) chart of independent integrated coordinates a, at a fixed exterior e. Include all Jacobians, gauge fixing and old interactions in its source-free density `w(a)=exp[−β S(a)−V(a)]` on its actual integration domain D. Here S is the *particular complete physical action representative* whose two jets are being tested, and β is its physical inverse coefficient. Defining V by this identity is valid even if the original local coefficients at rough pins differ from β. Then for the true normalized conditional,

A smooth interior selector can instead be retained with its exact logarithmic radial derivative in RV, or by integration of its differentiated density wherever its logarithm is singular. For a uniform isotropic re-entry m S write its compact plaquette representative as the full conditional classical action S_cl plus its *actual difference*. `−(2β_t)⁻¹ P₄ [ B_t(1)+T_t J_t ]`   (7.236)
*plus* the action-representative difference, any spatially varying profile and the R geometry terms of (7.230). Project only on the domains on which P₄ is defined. The second exact row contains `−(2β_t)⁻¹ P₄[B_t(F)−B_t(1)T_tF+κ_T(J_t,F)−T_t RF]`; in the R step it also contains (7.230)'s covariance of first means. At the genuine first unshifted homogeneous step, the two proportional physical-action estimates (7.90)–(7.94) show explicitly how this term is paid. The Gaussian normalization then contributes only `d_phys/(2β)` to the mean and `d_phys/(2β²)` to its scalar contact. A finite O(1) estimate of their sum would still leave a harmonic cost `Σ_t β_t⁻¹`; the needed conclusion is a constant-profile cancellation, a difference operator controlled by (7.234), or an extra O(β_t^{-b}) in the displayed numerator. For the signed completion the precision/current extensions and the reserve for each incident family must be certified before using the geometric estimate (7.226).

Differentiate (7.237) at θ=0 for mean and covariance. The full current volume is retained in d_phys,t; for the residual use its localized norm. Taking the indicated fixed F² jet costs its established shortened physical derivatives and old support moments. On the weak trajectory `Σ (1+log β_t)^q β_t^{-3/2}<∞` uniformly at fixed β_* and the tail is smaller. ∎

**Corollary 7.167 (the missing homogeneous carriers at an actual mixed boundary).** On the actual mixed records of CMP119 p.278 for which the ordinary one-step expansion agrees termwise on carriers completely inside Λ, consider only this homogeneous part of the uniform-action marginal at an outgoing home c. Relative to the full regular calculation, the omitted Gaussian operator contribution has size at most `C β_t⁻¹ exp[−c₁ dist_t(c,Λ^c)]`, with its corresponding second-source estimate `C β_t⁻² exp[−c₁ dist_t(c,Λ^c)]` for the fully assembled uniform action coefficient. If `Λ^c` is made of the actual old/fresh rough components and their fixed native collars, the annealed first bound is summable on the full fixed reference torus, under the matching and occupied-volume margins of (7.226). Fixed geometry collar enlargements of order R_t are allowed as well.

*Proof.* For the regular deformation before summing its Gaussian carriers, the extra θ kernel belongs to the same localized quadratic source class used in the proof of (7.237), without an additional g_t factor. Thus one θ derivative divided by β_t gives a rooted `C/β_t` support norm on the shortened field chart, and two give C/β_t². Their complete field dependence cancels in the physical uniform Gaussian sum, but a mixed restriction may omit carriers intersecting Λ^c. Each omitted support contributing to a projection rooted at c reaches that complement; its spare ordinary exponential gives the asserted deficit by rooted summation. For the probabilistic bound use the actual real history law. A rough component Y touching a specified t-home gives one possible matching to an ordinary birth. The number of connected shapes through that home of native volume v is ≤exp(Cv). For a collar of radius CR_t enlarge the home sum by O((1+R_t)^4), or use the number of homes times the original exponential distance kernel. Combining with the root bound, or summing the enlarged home count first, gives a summable `C B̄_stop β_t⁻¹ poly(R_t)e^{−a' p_t²}`. Native admissible periodic lifts are used at wraparound. This argument uses (7.226) only for an explicitly identified missing-carrier family with the ordinary bound proven above. It does not transfer this budget to an unestimated signed boundary replacement. ∎

### 7.108 The action-source recurrence on a verified genuine return

**Proposition 7.168 (proper marginal and contact promotion, including the completion).** Put a compact coarse Wilson plaquette representative of a filed marginal, with coefficient m_x, in a real (1.72) returning body or in its admitted complete crossing Mayer edge, as in §§7.67–7.70.
