For any nonzero charged plaquette phase B=h²q_R times its root, the magnetic ghost gap is ≥c|B|: for a unit vector with small covariant differences, `|(T_νT_μ v,v)|≥1−||D_μ v||−||D_ν v||`, while the commutator of D_μ,D_ν bounds `|e^{iB}−1| |(T_νT_μ v,v)|≤2||D_μ v|| ||D_ν v||`. Otherwise the same gap is immediate. These estimates control the full gauge Gaussian including its charged low modes. Stabilizers at flux zero and flux q_R need not have the same dimension; no σ derivative of their ranks is taken.

### 7.122 The periodic proper-time comparison at the quantized flux

**Lemma 7.189 (finite flux and metric derivative in the heat window).** For the charged fine Wilson Feynman/ghost combination at the periodic field of Lemma 7.187, the σ derivative of its flux difference on the proper-time interval `1≤s≤h⁻²`, divided by `R⁴ q_R²` and with the orientation normalization in (7.248), equals `−b k+O_R(1)`, with b>0 independent of k. Here the integrated quantity is the positive effective log determinant, with the minus sign of its heat representation.

*Proof.* We give the finite-flux and periodic estimates needed beyond (7.244)–(7.245), since q_R is fixed on this torus. At a real infinite-lattice magnetic phase B, for small complex metrics |σ|≤σ₀ the magnetic scalar and vector kernels have for `1≤s`, `|B|s≤C`, the bounds
`|K(s;x,y)|≤C s⁻² exp[−c min(r²/s,r)]`,
`|D_i K(s;x,y)|≤C s^{-5/2} exp[−c min(r²/s,r)]`, `r=|x−y|`.   (7.249)
A fixed finite short displacement and replacing s by 1+s also covers s≤1 in the estimates for the following convolutions. To verify these bounds, conjugate the operator by `exp(v·x)`, |v|≤c, first on finite-range hopping matrices or their infinite-lattice path series. Its real part dominates `c Σ D_i*D_i−C(|B|+|v|²)`. This follows by absorbing the first-order exponential weight errors against the magnetic difference form; all bounded spin and extra Wilson finite hops cost C|B|. Its numerical imaginary part has the same sectorial form bound after that scalar shift. Magnetic translations preserve the norms of these kernels per site. The trace per site of `exp(−sH)* exp(−sH)` is bounded by the trace per site of `exp(−2s Re H)` by Lie products and Schatten Hölder, as in Lemma 7.179. The latter is ≤`C s⁻² exp[C(|B|+|v|²)s]`, using the spectral form comparison and the real magnetic walk diagonal bound. In particular each column/row has ℓ² norm ≤`C s⁻¹ exp[C(|B|+|v|²)s]`. These trace statements can first be obtained for rational flux on larger magnetic periods with vanishing relative boundary, and then for every real flux by the fixed-time convergent local hopping series. The conjugated operators are themselves magnetic-translation covariant finite-hop operators on that larger period; no unbounded exponential weight on a closed torus is required for the limit.

For a difference use the sectorial semigroup estimate `|| (H+z)e^{-s(H+z)}||≤C/s` for `z=C(|B|+|v|²)`. This follows by the resolvent contour on a larger sector, with `||(w−H−z)⁻¹||≤C/|w|` there from the numerical range. The real form bound gives `||D_i e^{-sH}||≤C(s^{-1/2}+√z)e^{Czs}` in operator norm for the conjugated matrix. Multiply with another half-time heat kernel and apply the per-site Hilbert–Schmidt bounds (including cyclicity for an adjoint row). Splitting into two kernels at the diagonal then gives the pointwise bounds with their v weight; conjugating D_i itself adds O(|v|). Optimizing v, and absorbing its polynomial factor in a slightly smaller tail, proves (7.249). This argument also controls adjoint or backward differences. 

In a Landau gauge centered at the diagonal root, differentiating one scalar magnetic hop with respect to B introduces the perpendicular displacement from that root. The first derivative of the paired opposite hops has one covariant difference, the second has two displacement factors, and the third has three displacements and a difference. Derivatives of the bounded B-times-Wilson spin/hop remainder of order l have at most `C[(1+r)^{l−1}+|B|(1+r)^l]`, besides bounded local coefficients, with r the vertex distance to the chosen origin. In a Duhamel derivative of order three, use (7.249) on the successive heat segments. Summing spatial displacements of total order m costs at most `C(1+√s)^m` against these Gaussian/exponential convolution bounds; the largest segment supplies the final `C(1+s)⁻²`. Three first scalar insertions give three factors of √s and three integrable inverse square roots of their following segment times. Their time simplex contributes O(s^{3−3/2}), leaving O(s³) times the final heat diagonal scale. A first and second insertion give `O(s^{3/2})` in displacement and one inverse square root in the two-time simplex, again O(s³). A third single insertion costs no more. The spin/hop derivative bounds just stated fit the same count (use |B|≤C/s); for very short segments all differences cost at most a constant. These bounds justify the B differentiations by finite-volume approximation on the universal cover; absolute displaced-path moments are finite. Therefore the infinite heat-diagonal Taylor remainder after order two is `C s⁻² (|B|s)³` uniformly on a small complex σ-disc, so the same bound holds for its metric derivative at zero by Cauchy. The sum over conjugate roots or charge-reversal symmetry removes any linear term. This avoids turning a real probability into an absolute complex-rate path measure. Equations (7.244),(7.245) supply the quadratic coefficient and its `O(s⁻¹/²)` error.

At the actual quantized flux the periodic kernel is the periodization of the magnetic kernel on its true bundle: a path to a translated copy has only a unitary endpoint phase. Formula (7.249) bounds its winding diagonal by `C s⁻² Σ_{w≠0}exp[−c min(m²|w|²/s,m|w|)]`, m=R/h, uniformly on that σ-disc. This bound is also valid at zero flux. Multiplying by `m⁴/(R⁴q_R²)` and integrating ds/s from 1 to h⁻² costs O_R(1) (set u=h²s in the Gaussian part). The cubic finite-flux remainder likewise costs O_R(1), since `B=h² q_R` times the fixed root charge and `∫₁^{h⁻²} (|B|s) ds/s≤C_R`. The quadratic error integrates against `ds/s` with the extra s⁻¹/². What remains is exactly the negative coefficient in (7.245) after the d-metric and d-curvature extraction, times `log(h⁻²)=2k log L`. It is strictly negative because there are noncommuting charged roots in su(N); the commuting colors cannot offset it. This proves the assertion. ∎

**Proposition 7.190 (periodic induced window, and the sign for the completed compact insertion).** In the homogeneous native physical Gaussian family with the regular tangent, chart and cutoff conventions of §§7.103–7.121, there is a constant b>0 and a cutoff-independent constant C_R such that
`|Σ_{t=0}^{k−1} λ_t^J+b k|≤C_R`   (7.250)
for every k. Consequently for every j<k the actual compact input at j, followed with all its classical representative partners through the one-loop window, obeys
`Σ_{t=j}^{k−1} β_t⁻¹ λ^{comp}_{j,t} ≤ −b Σ_{t=j}^{k−1} β_t⁻¹ + C_R/β_{k−1}`,   (7.251)
when the inverse coupling sequence β_t⁻¹ is increasing on the weak trajectory. The same assertion holds with the explicit total variation of the inverse couplings in place of the last constant if monotonicity is not available. Here λ^{comp}_{j,t} is the trace of the *propagated compact input* in (7.247), not the raw standalone compact diagonal at t. Winding terms on the original admissible fixed-volume tori have the summable bound in Lemma 7.180. This is a one-loop coefficient bound, not an all-orders claim about the mixed Wilson law.

*Proof.* It remains to check the proper-time endpoints for the stabilized unconditioned physical determinant from Lemma 7.188. At s≤1 the real infinite heat flux-minus-zero diagonal is O(B²s) including its metric derivative, by the finite-hop series, its charge-paired evenness, and bounded fixed-time derivatives as in the preceding proof. Short periodic winding costs at most `C s e^{-cm}` (a winding path needs at least m bounded single-hop distances, up to fixed stencil factors). Thus this portion is O_R(1) after the normalization in (7.248). At s≥h⁻² the stabilized vector and nonzero ghost spectra have gaps c_R h² and their heat trace at s=h⁻² is O_R(1) by form comparison. This remains a bound `C_R exp(−c_R h²s)` on a smaller complex metric disc for the stabilized vector and the ghost with its true kernel removed, by the numerical real-part comparison and Trotter bound. Metric derivatives of the long-tail integrals are O_R(1). Removing zero ghost modes does not introduce a metric derivative of their dimension, and the lower ghost-gap argument after Lemma 7.188 applies on both fields.

On the finite middle and short intervals the physical stabilizing term and its canonical transformed version have rank O_R(1), norm O_R(h²), uniformly on that metric disc. By Duhamel its heat-trace effect is at most `C_R s h² exp(C_R h²s)` for `0≤s≤h⁻²`: bound one trace factor by its finite-rank trace norm and both semigroups by their numerical-range bounds. Cauchy gives the same estimate for the metric derivative. Its integral against ds/s is O_R(1). The remaining per-site fine determinant is therefore exactly the proper-time comparison of Lemma 7.189 to bounded error for the derivative. Lemma 7.188 transfers this conclusion to the actual hard quotient at both fixed compatible fluxes. The factors R⁻⁴q_R⁻² are fixed independently of k. Finally Lemma 7.187 identifies the result with the induced prefix, proving (7.250). This computation uses no Dirichlet edge in place of the original periodic fiber.

Subtract the two prefix estimates formed on their own fixed-R tori: the local lifted coefficient sequence is common by Lemma 7.180, so every window sum of `λ_t^J+b` is uniformly bounded in absolute value. For increasing weights `w_t=β_t⁻¹`, use `Σ_{j≤t<k} w_t e_t=w_j Σ_{j≤t<k}e_t + Σ_{r=j+1}^{k−1}(w_r−w_{r−1})Σ_{r≤t<k}e_t`. The bounded suffix sums cost at most `C_R w_{k−1}`. By (7.247) and Proposition 7.184 the difference for a compact input at the entrance costs at most `C Σ_{t=j}^{k−1} w_t L^{-s(t−j)}≤C w_{k−1}`. This gives (7.251). Within a fixed sufficiently long block, the negative linear term dominates these bounded comparison costs (on the appropriate sufficiently weak range with bounded ratios of the finitely many weights). The actual second contact of the interacting step, possible repeated perturbative insertions and every nonlinear or large-field boundary replacement still use (7.229),(7.230); they have not been absorbed into b. ∎

The raw scalar sequence in (7.239),(7.242), if interpreted as independently restoring the compact representative and throwing away b_t at *every* step, is a different sequence. Its absolute comparison with (7.250) fails by (7.246). For that raw diagonal alone the charged part of its local scheme difference has not been signed, and (7.251) is not proof of its separate Abel inequality. For the actual compact two-jet recurrence the identity (7.247) is forced: its b_t is present in precisely the stable/boundary channel of (7.229). Equations (7.250),(7.251) give the K-uniform Gaussian upper bound with that partner retained, and identify why the isolated diagonal criterion cannot simply be called equivalent to the physical one.

### 7.123 Compact filing in the recurrent one-loop subsystem

**Corollary 7.191 (uniform recursion with the compact representative retained).** Keep the actual constant homogeneous Gaussian marginal response and the deterministic transports of all its compact representative differences. For this subsystem allow other first source births with a specified absolutely summable norm; their induced marginal forcing is denoted f_t. The resulting marginal amplitude m_t remains bounded uniformly in K on the weak trajectory. This result includes the repeated compact-to-induced feedback, not the unknown input f_t from unrestricted mixed or higher-loop source families.

*Proof.* Write the current row as `m_t C_t+Z_t=m_t J_t+Z̃_t` with `Z̃_t=Z_t+m_t(C_t−J_t)`. By the actual deterministic identity (7.247), the changed residual after a new marginal increment `e_t=m_{t+1}−m_t` is its transported former value plus `e_t(C_{t+1}−J_{t+1})` and any separately given new birth. By (7.184) a single increment's mismatch has ordinary one-loop low response K_{s,t} bounded by `C L^{-a(t−s)}` at t≥s+1, for fixed a>0 (a shift of a single exponent is absorbed in C). This rewriting does not change the prescribed compact operator in the physical source. Absorb its initial mismatch and other specified incoming responses into the forcing with their actual norms. With `w_t=β_t⁻¹` the resulting linear marginal equation therefore has the form
`e_t=w_t λ_t^J m_t + f_t + w_t Σ_{s<t} K_{s,t} e_s.`   (7.252)
This is the Gaussian one-loop transfer together with its recurrent deterministic source remainders. A genuinely different nonlinear/contact return is not represented by K without its own proof.

By (7.250) and the suffix Abel identity the products of `1+w_t λ_t^J` over all intervals are bounded by a constant B independent of K; the λ_t^J are bounded by the rooted one-step trace and the weak stop makes the factors positive. The logarithm of a factor differs from `w_t λ_t^J` by O(w_t²). Let `A=max_t |m_t|`, `E=Σ_t w_t |e_t|` and `F=Σ_t |f_t|`. The admitted running bounds give `w_t≤C(1+t−s)w_s` for t≥s, `Σw_t²≤C/β_*` and `max w_t≤C/β_*`. Thus `Σ_{t>s} w_t|K_{s,t}|≤Cw_s`, and the total absolute size of the last forcing in (7.252) is at most CE. Variation of constants yields `A≤B(|m_0|+F+CE)`. Multiplying (7.252) by w_t and summing yields `E≤C AΣw_t² + (max w_t)(F+CE)`. On a sufficiently weak fixed stop the two small factors absorb the terms in A,E and give `A≤C(|m_0|+F)`. This uses the weighted signed induced drift in its correct order, and controls the effect of reinserting the prescribed compact tensor at every stage through its exact partner. In particular no independent sign assumption on the single-step scheme difference in charged colors was needed. ∎

For an originally present second marginal source the same *linear* propagation applies to it. At compatible uniform tensor data the classical β⁻¹ Gram forcing from two constant marginals vanishes, and the direct Gaussian pair trace costs O(β_t⁻²) with the two home variables kept until summing the profile, as in (7.229),(7.232). Thus this specified constant Gaussian contact forcing is absolutely summable once the first amplitudes are bounded. Additional nonlinear operator-valued contacts, mixed boundary replacements and arbitrary source phases still require their actual two-home estimates. Nothing in this window comparison establishes a fixed bare exponential disc for the physically amplified H.

For clarity the outstanding *isolated* compact diagonal, if separately requested, now has just one unsolved Gaussian scheme term on the periodic homogeneous graph. Using the original local normalizations of (7.239), it is
`χ_t^{chg}= (1/2) P_d Tr_chg { C_t(U) [D² S^compact_{d,t}(U)−E_t(U)* D² S_{d,0}(U) E_t(U)] }.`   (7.253)
Here the evaluation is the same compatible constant-curvature jet, including the dependence of C_t and E_t on the physical background. In neutral colors (7.246) and the suppressed fine-cosine induced contribution give a strictly negative linear prefix term plus a bounded remainder. In charged colors (7.253) is bounded at each fixed step by the rooted regular norms, but no uniform upper window test for its **raw** sums has been proved. In particular an unqualified upper bound for (7.242) with the reset compact coefficient alone would require controlling its positive drift against the strictly negative induced and neutral terms. The actual signed compact recurrence uses (7.252), for which that separate raw Schur estimate is unnecessary. The unresolved mixed-history conditions include the full nonlinear R replacement rather than an absent periodic normalization.

### 7.124 The second mixed return of an already admitted R-origin scalar

Here we use a narrower input class than the saved physical H jet on an arbitrary wall. Suppose the first marked return has already produced a genuine R-origin scalar on the **whole original** CMP119 (2.30),(2.31) domain, including its analytic extension in U,J and the original support, gauge and exterior data. This includes the ordinary disjoint output of (7.193) for the bounded stored compact H sector identified in §7.72. It does not manufacture such an extension for a mark known only on a smaller physical graph. LFR II p.375 immediately after (1.65) states that its extended joined readout lies in the analyticity domain of the old effective-action term. Thus composition of this particular ordinary scalar uses the original unmarked domain inclusion. One does not need to establish a larger saved-radius statement on every fine link in order to bound its value. The substantially stronger old physical projectors or derivatives in an independently varied old frame are still subject to T2's actual domain restrictions.

For explicit normalization, let a_j and b_j bound the rooted *first* and *inherited second* coefficients of the old family at j, respectively: on each X its bound has the factor `exp(−κ d_j(X))` of (2.31), with spare decay for fixed support moments. One may state the bound on a complete polynomial in source variables whose first and second coefficient norms are a_j,b_j. For several source homes we require these bounds also for the simultaneous sup-disc, or equivalently the corresponding directional tests through order two with their fixed homes. This qualification prevents an implicit sum over `L^{4j}` elementary source labels. A bounded number of supports per finest home costs only its indicated native weight. Write `s_j=a_j/g_j^{κ₀}`, `t_j=b_j/g_j^{κ₀}` using the actual unmarked smallness exponent κ₀ in (2.31). A seed has to provide its actual norms; for example a first bank e^{-p_j} multiplied by a finite polynomial in β_j still makes s_j summable.

**Proposition 7.192 (ordinary bulk output of the second R, P/L on native input).** At an actual later mixed R_e take the old j term on the domain just stated. Keep the original (1.61)–(1.65) substitutions, all source-free kernels, raw exterior Z, unprocessed operations and still-live factors. At a new carrier Y *disjoint* from the post-R large set of (1.99),(1.100), the proper first and second coefficient bounds of the new R_e origin, on its native extended field chart, are
`||b_{e,x}(Y)|| ≤ C e^{-p_e} s_j exp(−κ′d_e(Y)),`
`||b_{e,xy}(Y)|| ≤ C e^{-p_e}(t_j+s_j²) exp(−κ′d_e(Y)).`   (7.254)
For two old sources at j,l the product contribution is `s_j s_l`. The bounds include `⟨D_xy⟩+κ_R(D_x,D_y)`, not merely the expectation of a pre-existing contact. They cover the absolute second-home sum of the finite coefficient when the corresponding simultaneous/directional input norm is supplied. Fixed outgoing physical curvature derivatives on an admitted chart of radius ρ_e include their explicit Cauchy factor `Cρ_e⁻²` for a quadratic projection (and its carrier/old-slot factors if needed). A new regular coefficient obtained from a bounded literal physical H in one off-clean body can therefore enter the marginal channel at a **different** mixed return without losing either actual bank.

*Input into the second original R.* Add one normalized old scalar with an auxiliary coefficient u. Take `|u|≤c/s_j`. With two different first rows use independent u,v of radii `c/s_j,c/s_l`, and vary an inherited second row separately at radius `c/t_j`. The added inputs have just the original (2.31) supremum bound with a small fixed relative coefficient. Source homes are retained in X before any localization. In (1.61)–(1.65) each tagged term is evaluated on precisely the same supplied native domain as an undifferentiated R(X); derivatives in u or v make no changes to the frozen selector. The successive weakening integrations in (1.66) leave the old `exp(−βκ d_j(X))` and the rates for its enlarged domains through X. For ordinary R the summation of these terms before (1.68),(1.69) is the vacuum-subtracted R estimate from CMP119 Theorem 2, (2.44),(3.48),(3.49). It uses the original chart size, constancy under color rotations, the complete added/subtracted identity, and the actual mixed layer size in place of the final mesh. It does not assign a small physical field at top resolution to every old fine point. These estimates are linear absolute majorants term by term. Restricting X to contain a home, changing its coefficient by a bounded test, and stopping before identification of a Euclidean-invariant marginal cannot increase their sums. In particular there is no use here of Euclidean invariance of the pointed source to assert that its tensor is isotropic. The result on the auxiliary contours is an allowed small fixed multiple of the original (1.68) proper interaction for Y outside the core and of the original `Σ_n|Γ_n∩Y|` bound (1.69) for an internal body. This last sum belongs inside its undivided positive majorant, not in a putative uniform sup estimate for a normalized forced live body. LFR II, pp.373–377, (1.61)–(1.70), CMP119, pp.259–263,279–284.

*The new signed coefficient.* Use the form (1.102), holding the nonreturning live variables fixed until the indicated step. The just described contribution inside a healing component changes the occupied-volume coefficient in the proof of (1.79) by a fixed amount. With the same weak and counting margins its undivided estimate still gives (1.89),(1.95). Equivalently at fixed order insert the two marked factors into the majorant before the compatible sum; this never divides by a different small mass. The normalized signed cluster coefficient of a bulk Y is obtained in (1.98) and obeys (1.100) on the auxiliary source contours: a cluster of this kind has a returning component and no fixed live neighbor in its support. This also explains why no new complex zero-free assertion for a *conditioned* T′(Y_i) mass at a forced live neighbor is required in this estimate. Cauchy in u, or in u and v, yields (7.254); the exclusion-ratio calculation (7.183) gives the same result before Cauchy. A source-containing term in the normalized log retains the old home because the starting X and all surviving connected unions contain it. On a common sup-disc use one direction at x and one arbitrary direction in the other homes before selecting their signs. Summing the remaining rooted animals costs the spare rate. Extract a new regular P₄ only on the outgoing chart: Cauchy there specifies the displayed radius cost, and on a compatible curvature projection local affine gauges cost only finite moments of d_e(Y). The statement gives a new bulk scalar *at this one R*, irrespective of other steps where a differently shaped B or a missing domain has yet to be identified. ∎

The protected first-Q₂ / second-Q_{j+1} construction of T2 §§4.75–4.79 gives a physical example with a stronger estimate on the old field itself. At j=2+R₂ the old ordinary R-origin is a previously integrated scalar. At e=j+1+R_{j+1} the actual second component first meets its old bounded-diameter carrier. On its protected old charts the unamplified vacuum-subtracted return value is bounded by `C a_{j,X} (h_{j,e}/μ_j)²`, with h_{j,e},μ_j and actual physical current as in (4.143)–(4.146); there is no physical r⁻² amplification in the present SUS normalization. There h_{j,e} has the factor `r² τ_e` plus the exponentially small true localization error. T2 (4.150) pays the second inclusive real release in the original normalized gas, including the full selector support of its verified subhistory. Formula (7.254) instead concerns the complete plain native scalar on the whole (2.31) chart and its *new bulk* R_e coefficient; it need not grant that sharper power on every complex preparation wall. In particular an arbitrary enhanced old projected H jet should not be substituted for this scalar. T2, Propositions 4.88–4.92.

**Corollary 7.193 (summability for the R-origin to R-origin marginal forcing).** For a collection of such normalized first/second old rows write `S=Σ_j s_j`, `H=Σ_j t_j`. The summed new proper marginal forcing from the allowed ordinary output and all its incoming times is bounded by
`C Σ_e ρ_e^{-2} e^{-p_e}(S+H+S²).`   (7.255)
Here one uses the stated homogeneous outgoing local projection, fixed home counts and support moments; at native ρ_e≥c β_e^{-D} this series is bounded uniformly in K. If an old source is born with a fixed polynomial in β_j times e^{-p_j}, its contribution to S satisfies the required summability. In the closed subfamily of newly renewed ordinary R-origins this same argument can be iterated: converting the renewed coefficient to the next normalized first norm adds `g_e^{-κ₀}`, which is still summable against e^{-p_e}. Taking a sufficiently weak stop makes `Σ C g_e^{-κ₀} e^{-p_e}` small. The resulting first-row discrete Volterra inequality closes by absorption, and the second one has the bounded square of the first norms as additional forcing. The bounds do not include ordinary T innovations and unrestricted B origins unless their own input hypotheses have been verified.

*Proof.* Sum (7.254) over its incoming amplitudes and take the finite derivatives on the declared chart. The weak running increment estimate and p-log exponent greater than one imply `Σ_e e^{-p_e} β_e^D<∞` for every fixed D. For repeated renewals apply this inequality first to finite stages and absorb the coefficient multiplying the sum of previous first rows. With that sum bounded, the same second-row inequality is linear in its inherited second norm and has a bounded quadratic forcing. No rare bank is taken twice at the same return, and no powers e^{-p/2} need be reapplied until exhausted. ∎

### 7.125 Finite source jets in the second live integration

The next estimate deals with the normalized live integration at a real exterior on the original (1.103). It does not presume uniform small probability for a body once that body is in the fixed data. Write the first-stage log (1.98) as `Σ_P W_P(ξ_{I(P)})`, where I(P) consists of the complete fixed live components Y_i incident to the carrier and ξ_i are their actual compact variables, including retained internal histories if the (1.102) representation is used. Terms depending on only one Y_i can be included in its one-site measure. On the physical real field the joint density is positive, and the W_P can be chosen real there (take their real parts after their exact summed equality if needed). Normalize the resulting one-site measures to ν_i and keep their masses in the exterior action. The remaining weight is `exp[Σ_{|I(P)|≥2}W_P]`. This equality uses the source-free physical denominator of the second integration.

**Lemma 7.194 (an L⁴ insertion on arbitrary fixed live components).** Assume the original first-stage (1.67),(1.98),(1.99) and the second-stage cluster margins stated before (1.104). The fixed components are disjoint true components; no separation proportional to R_e is needed. For a nonempty set of them I, the product marginal `⊗_{i∈I}ν_i` and the true conditional law on I with the remaining live variables fixed compare in both directions by a factor
`exp[C Σ_{i∈I} v_i]`, where v_i is the number of native M-cubes of Y_i.   (7.256)
A finite first or mixed second derivative with a tag depending on these internal coordinates can be estimated on the normalized second log using its L² or L⁴ norm in the one-site product, respectively, in place of its sup norm. The connected expansion still contains every tagged home and has its original collapsed metric weight outside the tagged support; the tag's own carrier weight must be supplied. If its readout is bounded only in real moments this assertion concerns the real exterior only.

*Proof.* For a first-stage interbody interaction root its (1.67) exterior tree at a cube touching the specified i. There are ≤C v_i such cubes. A doubled traversal of a tree of length D visits at most C(1+D) outside M-cubes and their fixed collars; the number of possible rooted trees/sets with this length is ≤exp[C(1+D)]. Each fixed incident component attaches to an outside cube, since different true fixed components do not touch; its choice is already determined by position among at most a fixed number adjacent to that cube. Choices of subsets have the same exponential count. The original spare decay therefore gives `Σ_{P:i∈I(P), |I(P)|≥2} ||W_P||≤C v_i`. This is the first tree before the second CE; merely counting a second-stage zero-length interior as a large physical path would be invalid. Oscillation of the log weight involving I is now at most CΣv_i. Dividing by its own positive integral proves (7.256), regardless of the number of other components.

For one-site F use the affine factor `1+zF` inside its genuine integral. At `|z|≤1/(4||F||_{L¹(ν_i)})` the mass relative to its unmodified ν_i lies in a disc about one of radius 1/4. Its normalized total variation norm is bounded by 5/3. For two different coefficients on the same body retain `1+zF+wG+zw(FG+H)`; Hölder, the two L² norms and the inherited H bound control these finite coefficients. Use sufficiently smaller radii to bound the same total variation norm. For two multisite tagged carriers the equivalent expansion is to insert each finite polynomial before its actual integral, leaving all unmarked interaction factors in place. Bound these factors by their original sup majorants and use Hölder on the product one-site measure on the union of the indicated coordinates (L⁴ suffices if the two carriers overlap). Each marker occurs at most once at the required coefficient; there is no exponential moment assumption on F. The normalized connected second CE of (1.103) then cancels all terms disconnected from the marks, as in (7.183). For a prescribed extra marked carrier one can first give it the minor activity bound `c exp(−κ d_out)` on its normalized input disc, by including the inverse of that weight in its Cauchy price. Its attached background clusters/exclusion ratio cost at most `exp[C(|P_out|+Σ_{i∈I(P)}v_i)]`, from rooted summation at the touching exterior cubes. Bound each of finitely many such markers first and sum its original supplied support majorant afterward. Constants per incident site fit the spare native estimates or the displayed volume price. This proves the marked claim including the disconnected product subtraction; two separate conditional means have not been silently multiplied in its place. ∎

**Proposition 7.195 (annealed rough covariance at the second integration).** Use the preceding actual live law. Suppose a tagged live or crossing kernel has its complete original carrier P and the supplied native absolute bound on its readout. In precise real terms allow
`|M_P| ≤ A exp[−κ d_out(P)] exp[C U(P)] (1+β_old)^D`.   (7.257)
Here U(P) is total *actual occupied* native volume in the unbroken past of its indicated incident components (each site counted once per time), or any smaller nonnegative charge bounded by this same quantity. The polynomial of the old coupling is allowed only when there is an identified unbroken ordinary birth at or before that old time in the charged component. Supports and positive old labels must be measurable inside these retained histories. A fixed polynomial in the number of old native determining sites, for instance, is allowed when it is controlled by that same occupied-volume/continuous-age budget. Require `d_out` to be the original marked carrier's outside length; (7.257) is not derived for an arbitrary new source by the probability estimate. For two such tags use the actual same-body second tag or its separate supplied bound. Then their normalized mixed log coefficient whose total connected support meets a current live component has an annealed absolute anchored current-home row bounded by
`C B̄_stop^C (A_x A_y+A_xy) exp(−a p_e²)`.   (7.258)
Here A_y denotes the bound in the indicated second-home norm, and A_xy has the corresponding absolute row (or joint directional-disc norm). The ordinary physical distance between projected current homes can retain an exponential with a spare rate/collar. A fixed coarse collar of polynomial size costs its explicit factor. At least one actual live component is required in this statement. Marks inside its volume are included at that incidence, and the native support/homes may not be erased beforehand.

*Proof.* Condition first on the occurring shapes in the outside record, keeping the product operators of (1.103). By Lemma 7.194 distinguish the tagged carriers in the second connected log; their product moment norms multiply the original collapsed connection majorant. Convert a one-site product moment of a tagged readout back to the same real full conditional moment using (7.256) on its incident set, with its other coordinates fixed. For two possibly overlapping tags take Hölder at order four and then Cauchy–Schwarz in the outer record, reserving enough of the geometric and first-birth margins for these fixed powers. The indicator that all incident shapes occur is included in each such outer expectation. This pays at most a fixed exponent per actual occupied cube, not a new probability law normalized on the prescribed shapes.

In an occurring connected support of n native sites and incident current volume V, restore the ordinary rate from the collapsed one as `exp[−c n+C V]`, as in (7.195). Comparison (7.256) has exactly the same kind of extra cost. Multiply these prices and the finite number of (7.257) source factors. The history proof of (7.226) applies to the e-shapes with their complete marked unbroken past reward: the extra `exp[C U(P)]` is absorbed in the fixed coefficient of `Σ_n |Z_n|_n` in (1.79). One selected earlier ordinary birth pays a fixed polynomial in β_old by a fraction of its square p_h²; for shared births reserve part only once and split it between at most the two marked factors. Keep a further fraction of the distinct first-birth banks for all specified simultaneous e-shapes. At first subsequent release of each still-live lineage the affine reward is internal to its undivided T′, and the polynomial/nonzero-disc argument of (7.210),(7.226) applies; terminal survivors keep the fixed-torus ratio. This works also for U(P) determined by an internal history rather than by a prescribed list, because the native pointwise bound is inside that same undivided integral. Its nonzero tag still needs one of the prescribed components. Counting all incident shapes after this estimate preserves a spare birth factor `exp(−a p_e²)` since at least one shape occurs. The remaining ordinary rooted animal and second-home sums converge on the spare rate. This is the covariance of the actual live means and their inherited second response, not an argument based solely on rarity of two separately estimated marginals. ∎

The bound is usable for the unamplified finite-jet SUS normalization. In particular (1.66)–(1.69) supply the outside weight and geometric internal bound for an actually certified native old R/B vertex on its full input chart; the terms left in the live one-body operator use its genuine occupied history. A new boundary function known only on a smaller physical slice does not meet these hypotheses by having a small scalar value on that slice. Also, (7.258) at a real exterior is a variance bound, not a Cauchy estimate for a source-dependent physical gauge frame.

### 7.126 Boundary origin to ordinary marginal at the next mixed return

A genuine native B input at j is a full function of its original U,J, rough fluctuation slots and defining local geometry, with the support condition `X∩Z_j≠∅` of (2.40),(2.41). Use its ordinary (2.42) norm, or the explicitly permitted resummation over complete incident components on CMP119 p.262 with the corresponding reduced length. It is not an arbitrary conditional mean on an unidentified smaller domain. This distinction lets us treat an actual boundary birth that first occurred outside the common clean window.

**Proposition 7.196 (first B→R replacement).** Let a previous genuine R at j produce a boundary coefficient with its full native B-chart norm b_j, including its actual retained slots and source home. In particular one can take the B_X from (7.193) touching an unprocessed exterior in §7.82; its first source is the compact H already integrated inside a different returning component and has its first rare amplitude. Integrate the still-live factors only for carriers that actually need them, or use (1.102) here. Single and double Cauchy estimates prove the assertion. In the two-stage schedule of §7.82 the first component A has healed and the separate B is still unprocessed when the source-dependent B_X meeting it is born. ### 7.127 The exterior mean and the next covariance

Let I^− and I^+ denote the *original membership indicators* of a carried R or B template on the older and newer determination. For a fixed exterior write `C_x=I⁺F_x(U⁺,J⁺,A⁺)`. Thus the exterior cannot be charged with a fresh rare factor, and it cannot be counted again as a new marginal forcing. In particular, if the old physical term and its copy are literally identical on a pinned star, the proper difference vanishes there, and the once-carried old term remains. If a membership changes, its missing scalar remains in D, including the possibility of a missing vacuum constant.

**Lemma 7.197 (the extra covariance after the replacement).** At the next true conditional operation P, after removing the direct/direct row already carried in the recurrence, the new second response due to a proper scalar b is exactly

Here b_xy is the inherited full second jet of the prior proper logarithm; C has its own inherited second term in the direct/direct row. For a newly ordinary b and an admitted direct old R on a subsequent R these terms satisfy the polarized (7.254) bound, with `s_b s_C` in each cross term. For the corresponding normalized mixed T on the actual ordinary support charts of Proposition 7.159, use its connected two-marker localization with the same inputs. When the marks are full native R's, the summed native interpolation (3.26),(3.27) can also be applied without separating their old amplitudes into spurious independent volumes.

*Proof.* Differentiate the same normalized P law with first jets C+b, take its connected log and subtract the answer for C alone. The bilinear expansion gives (7.259). For the subsequent R, apply two independent normalized source parameters with one inserted in C and the other in b, and subtract the product of the two first means within that very bracket. Its Cauchy price is the product of the old cap ratios in (7.254); there is only one new bank if both tags share the new returning body. For the admitted ordinary T the proof is the same with the anchored marked numerator (3.44)–(3.47) and fixed kernel (3.27). For b still wholly inside a live core the correct operation is instead the second positive integration of (1.103), whose mixed normalized response is estimated by (7.256)–(7.258) when its original carrier satisfies (7.257). At the stopped exterior evaluate the direct old ordinary scalar with its actual indicator. Equations (7.217),(7.218) bound the genuine covariance of any two already identified R/B inputs using both their rooted L² ages. For example for current-cell source amplitudes a_j P_j the norm of the sum of all their centered terminally retained ordinary contributions is at most `C B̄_stop^{1/2} n_K⁴ Σ_j a_j P_j(1+K−j)^q` by Minkowski and `n_j⁴ L^{-4(K−j)}=n_K⁴`; include each test's actual aggregate norm. A surviving terminal B has arbitrary fixed stronger residence power as there. Divide the squared bound by the original fine volume for SUS. ### 7.128 The compact/induced pair on the same mixed slot

**Lemma 7.198 (an allowed auxiliary extension with a literal complement).** On an old regular j-cell use `J^ext_{j,Q}(U)=Σ_{p⊂Q} d_p s_p(U)` on the complete fine stars of that cell in its genuine positive top chart. The mask depends only on the stored geometry. On the homogeneous minimizing field this gives precisely the induced representative used in (7.247). On a changing mixed record it is only a chosen analytic comparison, with a completely specified complementary term. It need not be the stationary derivative of a newly proposed mixed minimum.

*Proof.* CMP119 (2.34) bounds the plaquette of the complex U as well as that of its real compact comparator. In j units a dimensionless fine top plaquette satisfies `||∂U−I||≤C α_{0,j} L⁻²ʲ`. On the principal small chart the symmetrized trace is quadratic by tracelessness. The continuation at a fixed geometry is holomorphic in its old positive variables, respects simultaneous gauge transformations and uses only the complete prescribed stars. The scalar is zero where no such star is selected. In particular this definition does not ask for a complex bound on an untested depth-zero plaquette. If a positive layer of depth n<j is instead included on its verified member chart, the corresponding crude count can cost `L^{4(j−n)}`; use it only with its genuine continuous age witness or a matched estimate such as (4.153). Where the nonlinear compact coarse Wilson representative itself is defined on its declared original star, set `D^ext=C−J^ext` on exactly that argument. For two different determinations W⁻,W⁺ the changes then satisfy `δJ^ext+δD^ext=δC` identically, including both masks; bilinear expansion of their four covariance terms gives the original compact covariance. No physical term is replaced by the auxiliary extension. CMP119, printed p.261, (2.34)–(2.42).

This extension removes the need for a false blanket identity between old and new stationary fields on a mixed wall. On the genuine second example with an *originally mixed* old graph, T2 §§4.81–4.84 give (4.153)–(4.159) conditional on the quantitative axial–Landau comparison (1.83)–(1.87) for a varying exterior. The released minimum in (1.50),(1.61) need not be the representative with its old fluctuation set to zero. The general native inclusion after (1.65), and the separately flat retained exterior with a reinstated internal field, have the narrower unconditional scope described in T2. If the compact readout itself was never certified on a particular old source member, splitting it by the algebraic identity cannot supply that missing original input. T2, §§4.81–4.84.

### 7.129 Finite early history estimates and the genuinely remaining outer row

**Lemma 7.199 (extra square reserve for early occupied volume).** Inspect the actual joint law through an early scale J. For any chosen deterministic set of native space-time homes at times ≤J charge the occupied native volume of their distinct actual live components, counting each selected site only once at a time. `E exp(s V_early) ≤ B̄_stop(s) exp[C M exp(−a p_J²) Σ_{ℓ≤K} e^{-p_ℓ}]`   (7.260)
for fixed s on the weak margin, with the terminal qualification of (7.212). For just the contributions whose actual continuing ancestry later heals, the corresponding moment omits the terminal factor.

Degree of the pre-Mayer polynomial is at most M, since each nonconstant X can be assigned one distinct actual early site; arbitrary overlapping proposed shapes are not counted as independent births or polynomial factors. The printed choice (2.5) gives `R_b≥(log g_b⁻²)^r`. In the native range r≥1 and with the first eligibility wait R_b after a genuine ordinary birth, put `J=⌊c log_L β₀⌋`, for instance c=1/4 or c=1/3. Then throughout this prefix `β_t≈β₀` and `J<R_b` for all b≤J at sufficiently large cutoff and fixed L≥2. With the original empty initial history **no R body can yet qualify** there. Punctures on these scales are unprocessed rough T domains. The following estimate concerns actual T integrals, and does not replace the law in a puncture by an independently normalized clean torus.

**Proposition 7.200 (early support sum for certified ordinary T inputs).** Consider the initial finite H vertex or any subsequent finite-jet source family whose entire old extended readouts are certified on the native E/R/B scalar charts in the ordinary pre-R T expansion. The rough seed geometry, all its original selectors and its true exterior coordinates are held in that expansion. Assume the incoming complete-source analytic cap is at most a fixed polynomial of β₀ initially. `C B̄_stop exp[−a p_J²+C J(log β₀+J+log(2+R₀))]`   (7.261)
using the original fine-carrier convention. If a chosen retiling expends `exp(C R₀⁴)` per step, add `C J R₀⁴` in the exponent and require `2p>4r+1` for the same superpolynomial conclusion. These bounds are for already certified native source evaluations and the physical conditional log. *Proof and precise use of the native charts.* Before any R, the original mixed T retains its ordinary support metric. For a single previously admitted gauge-invariant scalar the rough bound for its *whole* conditional substitution follows by the two cases of CMP109 (3.5) as in Proposition 7.159. A large/remote old X retains X₀ in CMP116 (1.30)–(1.32); a small X retains its initial collar in (1.9)–(1.25). For an old B use its full rough slots and (3.6),(3.7); its field-domain allowance is the actual dyadic difference in (2.36)–(2.39). No isotropic marginal identity is needed if the complete low polynomial is retained in this crude bound. A finite number of ordinary old domain derivatives costs at most fixed powers of `β₀` and `2^{t−i}` on the stated original margins. There are at most `C(1+t)L^{4t}` old labels/covers per current cell even if the old age improvement is discarded. For born regular terms of E-type one may use their actual small-cube domains in (2.27); do not rename them MR_j-supported R terms without paying the enlargement. The source-dependent new coefficients are obtained by the normalized connected expansion (3.44)–(3.47) with the original reserve. The smooth scalar of A is in an exterior argument fixed in this conditional operation. This use requires the actual substituted function on the original domain; it does not follow from a pointwise bound on a previously unverified joined frame.

More explicitly with P_t≤`C β₀^D L^{Dt}(1+t)^D(1+R₀)^D` for these fixed-order costs, normalize the finite input before the unmarked expansion by an auxiliary Cauchy parameter of radius `c/(P_t Σ_{i≤t} A_i)`. For the second response use the separate inherited second insertion linearly and two first insertions bilinearly in the same log. These amounts are only used on already admitted localized substitutions with their original support weights and derivatives; real-only live readouts may not be inserted as analytic old scalars by this calculation. The first bare h is a finite holomorphic Wilson-word combination on its original fine plaquette star (7.159), of size O(β₀) on its compact tube; an unresolved off-shell intermediate source is excluded rather than silently granted a radius. Iterating the displayed fixed-order bounds through t≤J yields first and second polynomial tags of size at most `exp[C J(log β₀+J+log(2+R₀))]`. The second bound has the same exponent order, since it is linear in previous *second* jets and only quadratic in the already bounded first ones. No compound exponential 2^J appears. One bounded sign direction followed by a fixed first label gives the absolute second-home row whenever the input has the declared simultaneous home norm.

On a connected carrier completely inside the new regular region the localized calculation agrees with its homogeneous counterpart evaluated on that same U,J argument, by CMP119 after (3.47). A nonmatching carrier or a discarded homogeneous path reaches a rough site at some indicated stage. In the pre-R prefix that occupied component persists in the actual condensed geometry up to the current step; alternatively sum on its own marked stage. Use a spare original decay to count its ordinary supports and the choices of sites/collars. For each inspected stage β_t≈β₀. The one-site consequence of (7.226), proved by summing actual component shapes with the volume bank, is `Pr(a specified rough site)≤C B̄_stop exp(−a p_J²)`. Polynomial collider/cover factors or the crude old-home counts are already in the exponent above. Summing over the early stages proves (7.261). ### 7.130 Summing later exterior covariances of a boundary scalar already present in the positive history

There is a different way to follow a newly emitted B coefficient through subsequent mixed operations. For the real susceptibility, combine its proper and exterior copies and use the original positive history law after its birth. This method estimates the variance of the physical scalar including its stopped conditional mean. It does not estimate the sup norm of each refiled analytic coefficient.

**Lemma 7.201 (length of the actual continuation of one marked body).** Fix a native home q at j. For a rough component containing q, let E(q,j,t) mean that the component has an unbroken continuing descendant through t≥j, counting reinstatements but ending at actual healing. On the fixed reference torus, for any fixed D on the corresponding weak margins,
`Pr(E(q,j,t)) ≤ C B̄_stop(D) exp[−D(t−j)−a p_j²].`   (7.262)

*Proof.* Locate the first subsequent complete healing of the component containing q, or its terminal record. Its history includes at least one native occupied cube at every time j through t on the event in the lemma. Give this one release the affine marker of the proof of (7.226), with reward equal to D times the occupied length since j on the unbroken history containing q plus a fraction of p_j² from one actual matched ordinary ancestor. Rewards on histories missing the marked event are zero. This is an internal variable of (1.71) before the integration; it is bounded by the actual occupied-volume and distinct-birth reserves of (1.79). At most one simultaneously healed body can contain this continuing q, so the degree of the pre-Mayer polynomial at each release is at most one. No enumeration of possible future locations of the marked cube occurs. The successive conditional estimates are bounded by the same product exp[C Σ e⁻ᵖˡ] as in (7.226), with the terminal ratio for a still-surviving component. Markov's inequality gives (7.262). At a merger only one continuation of q is charged. A later birth after complete healing cannot certify E. This proof also allows a fixed sum over q against a summable deterministic spatial kernel. ∎

Let b_{j,q} be the actual once-counted signed scalar already present on the j-history, rooted at a rough native home q, for a real simultaneous source direction |f|≤1. A typical example is a proper B' from (1.98),(1.99) evaluated on its original variables, assigned to a cube in its incident live body, with its source-home sum already bounded. Include the indicators of its original membership and support. Suppose
`|b_{j,q}| ≤ P_j 1_{q rough},  P_j ≤ C(1+β₀+j)^d`
uniformly for the indicated real filing. The same result holds using unconditional fourth moments ≤P_j⁴ and the stated event support, after reducing the rate a and increasing D. These hypotheses concern the actual sum rooted at q. For a single certified B'(Y) they follow directly from (1.99) with its source derivative as in Proposition 7.196, including when its support contains a fixed live body. For a family sum, restore the ordinary supports with cost exp(CV) as in (7.258) and pay this in the same marked reward if it is the volume of the indicated history. Equivalently one may verify the required fourth moment for the actual rooted sum by (7.256)–(7.258). One must not use a bound for an unrelated restricted bracket to conclude that an unidentified source has these moments.

**Proposition 7.202 (all subsequent releases and the terminal exterior).** Set J=⌈K/2⌉, at the fixed physical stop with n_K bounded. Keep each such b_{j,q} for j≥J. For j<J retain its contribution times the indicator E(q,j,J). Let B be the sum of these scalars, including any bounded test on their original source homes. Then
`sup_K Var(B)/n₀⁴ < ∞.`   (7.263)
All subsequent connected second responses arising from a pair of these first insertions, including the covariance of the terminal conditional means, obey this bound in aggregate. For two directions the corresponding bilinear bound follows by polarization or Cauchy–Schwarz. An independently born inherited second coefficient with an analogous absolute aggregate bound contributes its **expectation** to the pressure and is summed separately.

*Proof.* On the real full history, Cauchy–Schwarz and (7.262) imply
`||b_{j,q} 1_E||₂ ≤ C B̄_stop^{1/4} P_j exp[−D max(J−j,0)−a' p_j²]`
after changing D and the constant. For j≥J use t=j. On the fourth-moment version use Hölder with event exponent 1/4. The number of native roots is at most C n_j⁴. Since n₀=L^K n_K, we have n_j⁴/n₀²=n_K² L^{4(K/2−j)}. For j≤3K/4 the admitted running bounds give β_j≥c(1+K), β₀≤C(1+K) and p_j² grows faster than log K. Choose D>4 log L+1. The normalized L² sum for all j≤3K/4 is bounded uniformly even after its polynomial P_j and the K possible times. Above 3K/4 the volume factor alone gives an exponential bound in K. Minkowski proves (7.263) without a supposition about decorrelation between distant q or between different release times. For the inherited second coefficient divide the sum of its expectations by n₀⁴. The density factor is L⁻⁴ʲ. The same rare bound pays its polynomial at the earlier j's, while the density pays it at later j's. This uses a simultaneous two-home norm of that coefficient, not two independently bounded first jets.

For the covariance assertion one can take a decreasing filtration of the retained history from successive stages through the stopped exterior, retaining all auxiliary data needed for its physical disintegration. Center B and set M_t=E[B|𝓕_t]. The L² orthogonal identity is
`Var(B)=Σ_t ||M_t−M_{t+1}||₂² + Var(M_K)`   (7.264)
when the starting history contains B; otherwise include its initial projection residual. The same identity with the actual covariance of successive differences holds for two sources. Equivalently differentiate the full positive partition after putting a new factor exp(zB) in its numerator. Successive integrations give the inherited second coefficient plus the connected covariance of the two first conditional means, as in (7.229),(7.259). This equality is for their signed recombination, not for the sum of absolute Mayer coefficients. A marker depending on future survival is inserted into the *full* history and may be realized at first healing as in Lemma 7.201. Its complement is kept in the remaining first observable; their cross response is bounded by the geometric mean of their variances when the latter complement is estimated. It would be incorrect to interpret this marker as a native j-measurable projector before its occurrence. This is also why a future covariance translated through several B filings need not be paid repeatedly from one squared birth. ∎

For a concrete use, take the already formed B'_j of the two-component return in §7.82 with its full real marked cap (7.193), assign it to the incident still-live body, and sum its late-birth or long-survival terms as above. Subsequent proper B returns, conditional covariances and the stopped mean of this real scalar are all included in (7.264), even if the number of subsequent mixed steps is unbounded. The same argument works for a sum of such inputs satisfying its indicated true rooted bound. It controls a part of the susceptibility at fine-site density; it does not bound an individual outgoing traceless coefficient of (7.252) at every scale.

The remaining early short-lived insertion has an explicit score. Let e<J be its first healing and R_e the true signed bracket with its neighbors and exterior data retained. In the notation of §7.127 its first scalar after that release is C_x+b_x with b_x=⟨D_x⟩_{R_e} including the incident proper responses. Its two-home term is the inherited contact plus the true connected κ_{R_e}(D_x,D_y), followed by (7.259) on the succeeding exterior. On the native ordinary disjoint outputs (7.254),(7.255) give summable returns. For a generic released early source which is analytically certified only as a real internal observable on that first bracket, the covariance of its surviving **early** exterior means is not estimated by (7.263): the crude sum of roots costs L^{4(K/2−e)}, with no surviving occupied interval from e to J. A normalized conditional internal mass can be small; a phase/volume bound on each true (1.103) at real exterior is not a native analytic cap on the next joined (1.65). In particular separate terms of a Mayer expansion may repeat overlapping bodies and are not all realized simultaneously under the positive history law. They cannot automatically be charged as a single continuing genealogy. This specifies the remaining physical exterior operator and why the occupied-volume estimate alone does not supply its arbitrary early-time spatial covariance. No divergence of susceptibility follows from this failure of a norm estimate.

There is also a small factor for a *proper boundary output* that does not require a small ratio for the complex internally tilted measure of a still-live body. Use the (1.102) filing. In R take the source contours c/A and c/Q for the old actual native B families as in Proposition 7.196. The old/domain sum in (1.66) is precisely the boundary sum just discussed there. The last factor in LFR II (1.104) supplies a useful alternative to a sup norm for the preceding internal score. It matters which multiplier is present. This has an arbitrary-depth physical application for a source that stays in the same original one-body factor until true release. On the real common-sequence factors the proof at arbitrary depth is especially direct. One can verify this by induction on a directed chain of positive kernels: normalize each positive reference kernel on its own fixed parent state, apply |E f|²≤E|f|², restore its mass before applying the parent kernel, and repeat. For complex comparisons the induction requires the positive reference composite on which those same child masses and retained slots actually occur. The first unmatched step has a precise algebraic test. If a normalized old score from determination “−” is to be estimated against the multiplier from determination “+”, the signed difference multiplied by m⁺ reads

### 7.133 A positive connected expansion with both old multipliers present

At a real R operation fix the exterior and all still-live shapes in (1.103). Retain their internal integration variables. After absorbing all one-body terms into their own finite measures ν_i, the probability of these variables is proportional to

Here P ranges over the actual interbody carriers, I(P) are the bodies they meet and ξ is the common fixed exterior. The ordinary relative-distance bound is (1.68) or its already verified post-log boundary counterpart with its original small prefactor.

**Proposition 7.205 (replica exchange for the raw mixed bracket).** Let F_x and F_y be real local first source readouts, including old-minus-added terms if present. Their root carriers S_x,S_y contain every variable on which their two determinations depend. Use the smallest connected hull of these actual localized supports, including any whole incident live body in its entirety; ties can be fixed deterministically on a lift. `|κ_ξ(F_x,F_y)| ≤ (1/2) E_{ξ}^{⊗2}|ΔF_x ΔF_y| · Σ_{γ:x↔y} ∏_{P∈γ} min(1,4a_P).`   (7.268)
An empty path is included when the root supports share a relevant vertex. One can also take the minimum with 1 of the path sum on the right. The sources may be unbounded if the displayed positive moments exist. The exact underlying formula is the replica difference expectation restricted to connection, rather than the upper bound in (7.268).

*Proof.* For each replica independently expand the real interaction as e^{V_P}=e^{-a_P}(1+w_P), w_P=e^{V_P+a_P}−1≥0. Choose its open/closed edge conditionally on the fields, with open probability w_P/(1+w_P). The union of the two replica edges is open with probability at most 1−e^{-4a_P}≤min(1,4a_P), independently over P conditional on the fields. The unnormalized joint measure of fields and edges has the factors dν_i(s_i)dν_i(s'_i) and e^{-2a_P} times the corresponding w_P factors on the open copies. This is where both **original** internal masses remain; their normalizers cancel only as part of the common conditional measure.

Write ΔF=F(s)−F(s′). Add the two root carriers as deterministic hyperedges, so that all variables of the same source root swap together. On the event that these two root edges are disconnected in the union graph, interchange the two replicas on the connected component of x, interchanging the associated open-copy labels there as well. The union graph is unchanged. Each open edge has all its incident variables switched together or none, every closed edge is constant, and the product of the two copies of each ν_i is invariant. The integrand ΔF_x ΔF_y changes sign. The event therefore contributes zero to the normalized replica identity κ_ξ(F_x,F_y)=E_ξ^{⊗2}[ΔF_x ΔF_y]/2. Condition on both sets of fields, use the union bound over simple open connecting paths and the conditional edge probability above. This proves (7.268). Variables on the common exterior agree in the two copies. Any function F_x^0 of that exterior, including a separately chosen rooted subtraction on valid data, cancels in Δ(F_x−F_x^0). An exterior copy that itself depends on internal slots is included at the same root before exchanging. Thus this is a connected expansion before signing or comparing the two different internal masses. ∎

**Summation on a collapsed graph of any size.** Give an open P all ordinary cubes in its support as auxiliary vertices, as well as its incident components. This can add potential connections, hence still gives a majorant. Take a shortest path of these hyperedges from S_x to S_y, with repetitions deleted. A component or ordinary cube lies in at most two consecutive hyperedges of the path; otherwise those edges yield a shortcut. In particular the cost of filling the complete interiors of large bodies is incurred at most twice, regardless of their degrees. Write V for their union volume and N for the ordinary nonoccupied size of the path outside the root carriers. Each connected P has at most C[1+d_{e,Z}(P)] ordinary cubes off those bodies, by (1.67). Conversely its true majorant has spare decay in their count; endpoints have their own original carrier decay. On the native animal margin the product of the edge probabilities is bounded by exp[−κ̃ N] times a small factor per edge, using (1.68). For small carriers the chosen α pays any fixed per-edge counting expense; the actual numerical margin is that of the native rooted animal expansion, not a Dobrushin bound proportional to the diameter of a live component.

For detail on the count, encode each successive P by a rooted traversal of an ordinary connected support after adjoining the incident live interiors. Each embedded lattice traversal with specified start has at most exp(C length) choices. Mark its transition cube for the next P; choosing a location on a support of size s costs at most 2^s. Include a traversal of the shared component if the next starting cube there is different. The shortest-path property limits the total traversed ordinary volume to C(N+V+|S_x∪S_y|); extra flags for ordinary cubes, whole components and transitions use the same bound. One must not sum the entire volume of a single large component independently at every edge in an arbitrary nonminimal walk. The proof also works for labeled endpoint terms with their own fixed finite or summably decaying supports and for periodic identifications. If a proposed source enlargement inserts a new long strip without its own support weight, it has not met this counting condition.

For fixed real shapes the bound in (7.268) may therefore be summed after restoring an outside tree at the cost exp(CV). For the *actual* outer history use (7.226) for the union of these specified shapes to pay exp(CV), choosing the weak margin as in Corollary 7.158. There is at least one matched birth when the path uses a live body. The composite law with two interiors has the actual outer marginal and each single replica has the original conditional law. Hölder thus allows root fourth moments rather than conditional sups, and a shared ancestor needs just one reserved fraction of its bank. This gives an annealed absolute second-home row bounded by C B̄_stop^c times the endpoint moment and support constants and e^{-a p_e²} for the live incident contribution. This normalization is obtained without a lower bound for any tiny body mass and without assuming widely separated bodies. Arbitrary other fixed components cancel on the disconnected event; following enlargement their only effect is through open edges on a connecting path. This verifies the required summability before and after enlargement when the actual changed home supports have the stated size/decay. It gives a direct full-real-law analogue of the finite-order majorant (7.258), including for source insertions still recorded as actual raw numerators.

For example take one early root already carried on the retained slots of an actual still-live old body, and a second such root on the same or another body. Restore the first physical numerator as T'_i F_i at its own raw determination as in (7.266). Conditional on the same new exterior, integrate its raw history as part of s_i. An added copy evaluated at that fixed exterior drops exactly from Δ; if it reads another incident body, include that body in S_x and its actual rooted moment in Δ. For a literal fully stored compact frustration star the raw moment is bounded by Cβ₀ per star before admission of any strengthened joined frame. If instead an input has already been refiled as T⁻F⁻/m⁻ evaluated on a different determining record but the sampled raw law contains only m⁺, replica exchange by itself supplies no fourth moment for that readout. Equality of the global physical partition before and after the R transform does not specify a localized raw enlargement. The same distinction applies to the exterior covariance at another scale. It equals the two-level physical covariance minus the expected within-level covariance. The latter is estimated by (7.268); the former requires the true next exterior kernels, including any dependence on the earlier raw masses, on a connected space-time carrier. ### 7.134 A protected ordinary marginal with its original real selector

The first J<log_L β₀/4 steps from empty history have no healing on the margins of §7.129. A punctured top region can still have unprocessed earlier rough exterior data. A useful one-step comparison in that setting concerns the marginal law of the **independent canonical coordinates**, not a complex exponential of the physical source.

First distinguish two gauges. CMP119 printed p.250 after (1.16) proves that a real gauge v of the *new* target induces u₀(x)=v(y) constant on each preceding block B(y); the free A transforms by Ad(u₀) and the actual selector transforms covariantly. If v depends on previously sampled outer coordinates, these rotations in the lower integral are triangular and have real Jacobian one. The same v works for all insertion homes. Thus on the homogeneous real h-block in Lemma 7.98 the common baseline U_* and fixed based contours permit the new target of each lower integral to be changed simultaneously for invariant observables. One can equivalently use the equality of the entire lower invariant conditional integral at those gauge-equivalent targets, without differentiating the unknown gauge relating the two natural representatives. An arbitrary fine gauge varying *inside its own block* is different: even at the linear level Σ A_e=0 need not imply Σ Ad(v_e)A_e=0 if its v_e differ on a straight averaging row. The starred-coordinate constraint, graph gauge and selector then cannot be replaced simply by independent sitewise rotations.

On a punctured cube a coarse gauge v on the protected subcube can be extended by the identity outside a slightly larger cube (there are no continuity constraints on a site gauge), and the lower change uses its block lift. All fixed pins and (3.22) shell coordinates must either be fixed by this extension or be transformed as explicit external arguments. On the common inner cube the lifted gauge is the same as for any other extension agreeing there. This proves exact covariance of physical observables and the Jacobian for this transformation. It does not identify two inequivalent physical minimizers or establish a bound on derivatives of a mixed exterior representative. The contractions in (7.162) refer to its indicated homogeneous near-identity chart, with weak localizations used for the invariant source. They do not assert C² bounds on a newly proposed raw product chart at arbitrary outside pins.

**Proposition 7.206 (local total variation on one original mixed T).** Consider two real ordinary conditional integrations, one possibly homogeneous, on their original CMP119 (3.15),(3.26)–(3.29),(3.37) domains and unmarked convergence margins. Use the same canonical real coordinate frames there, with their actual independent selectors (3.16),(3.19) and all (3.22) terms retained. Write P for the maximum of the corresponding canonical selector radii. If the localized unmarked kernels, including their background arguments and native constrained propagator walks, agree throughout that collar, then for every bounded Borel test f(A_S),
`|E_mix f−E_ref f| ≤ C ||f||∞ exp[C(1+P²)|S|−c b].`   (7.269)

`C ||f||∞ exp[C(1+P²)|S|] · Δ_b.`
Here Δ_b is a bound on the difference of the actual *coupled* local coefficients on the common collar in their original absolute cluster majorants, with all unmarked vertices, conditional precision and its walks included. In particular if there is a simultaneous physical chart of spare radius ρ for all those local arguments and their distance, in its native weighted units, is at most d≪ρ, one may take Δ_b=C d/ρ times any incurred fixed growth or polynomial count in the collar. Thus Z₀ in (2.4) contains S. In (2.5)–(2.6) only the variables on the complement are whitened; the real variables in S stay in the inner integral. In (2.7)–(2.8) the new weakening walls avoid Z₀. In the exterior Gaussian continuation only the unmarked weights require analyticity in the physical fields. In the normalized expectation all clusters not connected to S cancel with the original denominator, by (2.11)–(2.13) or direct differentiation of the logarithm at u=0. The connected S-cluster sum has the preceding root cost with a spare exponential in its reach beyond S. These statements use the *ordinary* mixed T expansion of (3.43),(3.47), with the same scalar vs boundary distinction as in the primary argument. A passive exterior factor depending only on the frozen background (including its vacuum constant) cancels. Apply the same expansion on the comparison graph. Up to the first visit to the outside of the collar the graph, selector, unmarked formulas and their localized inputs agree under the first hypothesis. For the version with changing arguments, telescope the products in the rooted clusters that stay inside, using the difference majorant once and the unmarked bounds for the other factors. Their number or total length is absorbed with a small part of the spare root decay. The analogous telescoping of the local propagator walks uses the same argument. On a common spare chart Cauchy gives the displayed d/ρ estimate. Every cutoff here is a real cutoff on the original independent canonical coordinates. [CMP116, pp.11–18, (2.1)–(2.38)](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01239022), CMP119, pp.268–279, (3.16),(3.22),(3.43),(3.47). ∎

The genuinely useful form for a fresh *current* test is as follows. Let f_mix(A_S)=Φ(V_t(A;ξ)) on the real retained top bonds of interest. For the same real A_S choose f_ref using the reflected real graph, with its own background. If these physical readouts differ by at most δ_f on the actual coordinate balls (or one has their integrated error on the actual mixed conditional), add that error to (7.269) applied to the one fixed function f_ref. Only a bound and matching of the real physical test are required. No prior off-shell continued B(J,A) is inserted as a new source. A true old A- or current-dependent coefficient that is not a function of these real local coordinates and exterior parameters cannot be evaluated by this shortcut at a different argument.

For a support truncation S in a ball of radius s, the conservative root cost is exp[C(1+P²)(1+s)^4]. In the early prefix P is at most a fixed power of log β. Choose s a sufficiently large fixed power of log β and b a still larger fixed power so that (1+P²)(1+s)^4+J²≪b. A test that admits approximants with a uniform real error exp(CJ²−c s) can be treated by (7.269) plus that error. A sequence of at most J real probability integrations passes any previously estimated uniform error with constant one. These facts remove a multiplicative contraction requirement on *inherited real scalar errors*. They do not give the physical-background comparison Δ_b for free. The reflected classical comparison in T3 §4.130 proves a value bound at zero internal fluctuations on its specified charts. To make the above iteration a physical susceptibility proof one must verify the corresponding localized unmarked argument comparisons and approximant bounds along the whole real sequence, including intermediate current, Jacobian and coarse reconstructed data. A real-minimum bound at one terminal classical configuration is insufficient for this conclusion.

### 7.135 Real fluctuation insertions without a sharp-cutoff loss

The P² in the conservative root cost (7.269) is avoidable when only the real canonical test is forced. *Proof.* Interpolate the exponent of each selected source potential in the first Mayer step (2.1). A protected home has a complete regular cube with all required preceding raw descendants, synthetic reference collars, and real original top variables at every operation used. The same assertion compares two such homogeneous problems with identical interior data but different larger tori and different remote exterior. At a mixed fiber that has not been shown to satisfy the stated true chart assumptions it is not an unconditional extension claim.

The corresponding two actual based backgrounds are aligned by the unitary block lift, the physical readouts at the same real A differ by the estimated regional error, and the fixed-disc derivatives of the truncated π cost at most their rooted coefficient norms. For sums of protected homes, the exterior baseline gauge used in this proof can differ from home to home.
