### 7.140 The support charge for a prescribed real Test and the choice of margins

A small input exponential rate cannot automatically pay a cost called C^{|S|} without tracking C. For the single real ordinary T in (7.269)–(7.270) one can avoid assigning the full native output decay κ to the already prescribed S. Here |S| counts cubes of the fixed aligned final localization grid; fixed stencils or the conversion between the original and final grids introduce only the corresponding fixed L-dependent incidence factors.

In CMP116 (2.23)–(2.26) the Gaussian comparison on Z costs exp[C α₅ |Z|_bonds]. The coefficient is
`α₅=C exp(−δ₀M/3)+C(α₀+α₁+α₄)+γ₂.`
Printed p.20 specifies the resulting dimension factor O((LM)⁴ α₅), with constants independent of M in this estimate. If S is forced into Y₀ there is no need to select or encode an unknown unmarked tree covering S, nor to extract exp(−κ d(S)) from a missing unmarked vertex. Sum the unmarked attachments rooted on S by the remaining small per-site activities, using Σ_{D⊂𝒟}∏_{Y∈D}w_Y≤exp(Σ_{Y∈𝒟}w_Y). Attachments reaching out of S retain the original decay for their outside portion. The complement-cutoff failures of (2.3) start outside S; S itself carries its full original real χ. As in (2.34),(2.37)–(2.38), the excess wall and mask count costs an additional exp[C(e^{-c(κ₁−1)}+small failed-bond sum)|S|]. The unchanged Gaussian law at zero perturbation is normalized; dropping its density and bounding the real S-ball by its Euclidean volume would lose this property.

For simultaneous Borel quadratic-growth insertions there is a direct estimate improving the auxiliary product budget of Lemma 7.207. Use the Mayer factors e^{z Φ_S}−1 instead of differentiating Φ in any field variable. For the real integration fields, any K_S≥1 satisfies
`1+K_S |e^{z Φ_S}−1| ≤ exp[K_S |z| |Φ_S|].`   (7.277)
This follows by the exponential series and (1+x)^{K_S}≥1+K_S x for x≥0. Take K_S=exp(τ |S|), τ fixed in cube units. In a fixed root/union domain the sum of the absolute products over source families is bounded by the product of the left sides. When a union of n new cubes outside the prescribed seed is required from these source factors, their K_S supply at least exp(τ n); the union bound gains exp(−τ n). On the right the sum Σ_{S} e^{τ|S|}|Φ_S| is bounded by ε |Z|+δ Σ_{b∈Z}|A_b|² whenever the rooted τ-weighted sums of a_S,d_S in Lemma 7.207 are sufficiently small. Thus this proof does not assume that taking square roots of an arbitrary summable collection preserves summability. In the grouping by Y₀ from (2.2) one declares the fixed seed cubes occupied initially: the part of the source union lying *inside* the seed is not enumerated as an independent unknown subset. At each fixed outside union one can sum all the source families giving it with (7.277), before taking the remaining Gaussian bound. Empty-source/empty-unmarked components give the usual normalized 1 and the disconnected terms later cancel from the marked log.

To spell out the independent combinatorial choices, attached connected sets of n outside cubes meeting a fixed neighbor can be enumerated by a depth-first lattice walk of length ≤2n, at cost D_d^n with D_d fixed by the dimension. Unmarked attachments have the original (2.38) sparse prefactor and decay. Source-created outside volume carries e^{-τ n}; assignments of an outside cube to more than one of source, unmarked, failed bond or added wall may be summed by the fixed additional finite factor per outside cube (or by the original separate (2.27)–(2.37) sums). Families rooted initially at S therefore cost at most exp[C |S|Σ_{n≥1}(C_d e^{-cτ})^n] for this part, since they are attached at the O(|S|) possible adjacent sites. The same reasoning gives the KP exclusion cost exp[C ε_CE |S|] for the connected log around the prescribed seed. Weights for each individual input S are being summed in their given rooted τ-norm; no unrelated number of microscopic home labels is introduced.

Consequently the effective charge on a prescribed S in this one-step estimate can be made smaller than a chosen positive spatial margin. Choose a small target seed charge η, then τ above the fixed lattice entropy so that the displayed attached-set cost is ≤η/8 (including the fixed L cover factor). Choose a homogeneous carrier target a>2τ plus its polynomial/finite-stencil conversion slack. Choose the native rates κ,κ₁ large enough for producing this fixed a and for the walk entropy (including the restrictions (7.99),(7.143) when using the homogeneous fixed-block construction). Next take M large enough for (LM)⁴ exp(−δ₀M/3) and the ordinary walk restrictions, and take the independent small radii α₀,α₁,α₄,γ₂ and weak coupling so (LM)⁴α₅, the failed-bond sum, C ε_CE and the τ-weighted real perturbation norms fit the chosen η. This is the ordering for the real *single-species* T estimate: c_* is not proportional to the full requested unmarked κ and does not grow as an uncompensated power of M. On a fixed h-block one must in addition satisfy its explicitly stated finite-species determinant and field-coordinate margins; the one-step count does not itself verify every choice of constants in an arbitrarily specified fixed h-block construction. ### 7.141 A real unmatched internal numerator that does not require a mass ratio

There is a further class for which the literal m⁺/m⁻ in (7.267) can be avoided even when the two actual positive kernels have different masses. Let P(dξ) be the true outer zero-source law at this return. For each of two determining arguments assume that the old *real physical conditional* is well defined: M^{±}_ξ(0)>0 and its derivatives are obtained by a real raw insertion F^{±}_x inside that very kernel. Keep all its original region constraints and neighbors. Suppose each conditional kernel depends on current random slots only within its verified root hull S^{±}; a fixed exterior may of course enter as a parameter. Write ν^{±}_ξ for the corresponding normalized conditional kernels, u_x^{±} their means and v^{±}_{xy} their connected second moments. These hypotheses apply to the original stored finite compact star on any real admissible one-body return whose full original operator and variable dependence have been kept. They do not follow merely from a formal analytic B coefficient evaluated outside that real conditional interpretation.

Independently sample the two raw histories from ν⁻_ξ,ν⁺_ξ given ξ, with the outer law P. Then the old-minus-added scalar with log-source log(M⁻(z)/M⁻(0))−log(M⁺(z)/M⁺(0)) has the exact completed second derivative
`E_P(v⁻_{xy}−v⁺_{xy}) + κ_P(u^-_x−u^+_x,u^-_y−u^+_y)
= κ_aug(F^-_x−F^+_x,F^-_y−F^+_y) − 2 E_P v^+_{xy}.`   (7.278)
Any genuinely inherited second source row is added in the same way with its own sign. In particular the second sign cannot be implemented simply by replacing F with −F under the added measure: its conditional variance has the opposite required sign. Equation (7.278) follows exactly by the law of total covariance and conditional independence. The law on the right keeps each original unnormalized T′ in its own numerator and its own conditional denominator; it never compares the sizes of those two denominators. For a bounded raw mark both measured moments have finite absolute bounds even if either mass is arbitrarily small.

For use in (7.268) represent each of the two conditional draws as a measurable function of its actual determining slots and an independent uniform random number. This is possible for the finite standard Borel lattice fibers by the usual inverse distribution construction (encode the finite product of compact group and Euclidean coordinates in a Borel interval and use the generalized inverse). Include these auxiliary draws at the joined old/new root before exchanging the two full replicas. An exterior independent conditional draw integrates to one. The augmented observable consequently has exactly the union of its two established determining supports, with no new interactions outside that support. The initial supports used for this calculation must cover all common old data when the two marks share a conditional operator; two independent samples cannot replace the required joint term. For a pair in one shared internal body v⁺ is an internal connected response of that body. For distinct interacting internal bodies use the original positive cluster (7.268) for that conditional response, or keep the whole joint determining support. Thus (7.268) and its animal sum apply when the distinguishing hulls and their true spatial expenses have been identified. Fine compact stars have per-home sup Cβ₀ at the unamplified normalization. The native occupied-volume estimate pays a completed large interior once; unaffected components are summed independently before and after the joined-support enlargement. Nothing here assigns a fourth moment or a joint positive conditional representation to a signed earlier analytic coefficient which never had one. The arbitrary unresolved off-shell row in (7.267) has narrower scope than an inability to compare two real normalized compact insertions.

### 7.142 Exact full-Wilson flow for the fine-uniform additive source

The source here is the unamplified *additive* one D=Y₀/β=Σ_{b∥0}(D_b−|F_b|²/3) of T3 §4.136, D_b=Σ_{i=1}³|F_{b,i}|², F_b=Σ_i F_{b,i}. It is neither the physically normalized dimension-six insertion nor a source for βD. In the Wilson metric let X=−(1/3)Σ_{b∥0,A}F_b^A X_b^A and let Φ_t denote its flow on the whole product group. The following change is made in the full Wilson partition before introducing any sharp history selectors.

**Proposition 7.211 (all-order Ward transformation with a summable contact norm).** There are constants C_κ,c_N>0 independent of lattice side and β such that for |z|/β<c_N the normalized additive partition exactly equals the normalized Wilson integral with extra exponent
`z Σ_{b∥0}[D_b−ℓ_b/(3β)] + Σ_{m≥2} z^m B_m(U).`   (7.279)
Its new terms are real at real z, gauge-invariant, and are sums of connected finite Wilson-word products on supports of at most C(m+1) elementary bonds and plaquettes. In particular
`|Σ_{m≥2} z^m B_m(U)| ≤ (C |z|²/β)/(1−C |z|/β) · S(U)`   (7.280)
on the actual compact group. There is also a rooted version: after weighting each order-m support by exp(κ times its length), its local sum is bounded by C_κ^m β^{1−m} times the incident plaquette energies, with a polynomial-in-m incidence factor absorbed in C_κ^m. On a bounded complex link tube use the squared plaquette matrix defects in place of the real energies. In this formula ℓ_b=Σ_A(X_b^A)^2 S=C_F Σ_{p∋b}(N−s_p). Thus its constant is an analytic nowhere-zero scalar in the partition and its field part is an explicit additive temporal-plaquette coupling. No contact is discarded.

*Proof.* At real t the flow changes Haar volume by J_t with log J_t=∫₀ᵗ(div X)(Φ_s) ds. Set t=z/β and transform the entire compact integral by U=Φ_t(V). For real small z this is an exact diffeomorphism. The transformed exponent, after restoring −βS(V), is z D(Φ_t)−β[S(Φ_t)−S]+log J_t. Now XS=−Σ_{b∥0}|F_b|²/3 and div X=−Σ_{b∥0}ℓ_b/3. Its linear coefficient is the one in (7.279), and for m≥2 its coefficient is exactly
`B_m = β^{1−m}[(X^{m−1}D)/(m−1)!−(X^m S)/m!] + β^{-m} X^{m−1}(div X)/m!.`   (7.281)
This agrees at second order with the Ward contact of T3 §4.7 after converting the normalization. It also shows where the orientation-specific action shift occurs. For each fixed starting link the vector field has fixed-range analytic coefficients on a uniform product of complex group tubes, with uniformly bounded row derivatives. Picard iteration in the product sup norm gives a complex time disc of fixed radius, independently of volume. One may equivalently use the convergent word series below for the transformed integrated density and analytic continuation from the real z interval.

Use the Wilson-word representation of each first derivative F: it is a sum of a bounded number of traces with one generator on an incident plaquette, with the actual generator metric and orientation. An application of X differentiates one occurrence in the existing trace products and inserts one bounded local force. If the current word length is l there are at most C_N l choices; the length increases by at most a fixed constant. Integral-word coefficients and all generator traces have exponential-in-length bounds on the compact group or a fixed complex tube. Starting with these fixed seeds, iterating m times costs at most C^m m! before the denominators in (7.281). Every new plaquette meets the preceding support, so its union has size at most C(m+1). After the first derivative of S, all terms have two first-plaquette-derivative factors. The same is true of D initially, and of X div X by the displayed Casimir formula. Each further operation can destroy at most one such factor by differentiation and contributes a new one from X. Retain these two factors in the estimates; an incident real plaquette force is bounded by C√s_p by the finite traceless anti-Hermitian projection. On a bounded complex tube the corresponding estimate is C||U_p−I|| with the finite tube factors included. Thus each localized monomial is bounded by a constant times the sum of two incident plaquette defects squared. A fixed plaquette can be met only by roots within C(m+1) steps, of which there are at most C(m+1)^4 even on a periodic torus. This proves the indicated rooted estimate, (7.280), and uniform convergence locally for |z|/β small. It proves the complex identity by analyticity, without transporting a sharp cutoff through Φ_t. ∎

There is an actual obstruction to removing the remaining ΣD_b as a total-force derivative. On an even periodic torus take every spatial link equal to I and each time-independent temporal link equal to diag(e^{iθ},e^{-iθ},1,…). Set the angles on the (x₁ mod 2,x₂ mod 2) cell to 0,π/2,π,−π/2 in cyclic order and extend without dependence on x₃. At each spatial site both neighbors on the first axis have phase increment +π/2 or −π/2 and both on the second axis have the opposite increment. The two directional Cartan temporal forces are equal and opposite, and the third is zero. All non-Cartan derivatives vanish by diagonality. The force at a spatial link from its two successive temporal plaquettes also cancels because the configurations do not depend on time and the transports commute; pure spatial plaquettes are flat. Hence every component of the *full* Wilson gradient vanishes. The fine-uniform D is strictly positive per site, whereas at the identity both the gradient and D vanish. Thus D cannot be a constant plus ⟨∇S,X'⟩ for any everywhere regular Wilson vector field. In particular a β-uniform bounded local divergence divided by β cannot repair this identity at arbitrarily large β. The configuration has positive action density and its Wilson penalty is extensive at order β. It is a test of the proposed Ward cancellation, not a partition zero, phase coexistence assertion or counterexample to the additive disc.

## 8. Current summary

The unrestricted bare-source interface I-1 is false. The constant physically normalized dimension-six frustration source has a Wilson zero within O(a²). Section 6.4 distinguishes the analytic sources from physical finite jets and records the modified T5 and T6 inputs.

On the homogeneous chart the physical action defect is summable. The completed compact Gaussian marginal recurrence has a negative charged determinant slope on the quantized periodic flux. The signed representative difference is needed for its uniform bound.

On a mixed return the proper and exterior copies of a pinned classical frustration term cancel. A boundary coefficient admitted at one return can feed a later ordinary marginal with its actual healed factor and connected second response. Occupied-volume estimates count each distinct birth once and retain the terminal partition ratio on the fixed reference torus. Late boundary births and earlier lineages surviving to half the tower have a whole-future variance bound after signed recombination.

A positive replica expansion now bounds real mixed covariances on joined determining supports. Each real conditional kernel retains its own mass even when old and added determinations differ. The unrestricted analytically continued internal score at a changed early argument still lacks an iterable bound.

Before the first healing, measurable tests of independent fluctuation coordinates admit a protected conditional comparison. The early homogeneous independent-cutoff reference has a fixed physical scalar chart on the stated native margins. The aggregate invariant gradient is bounded by coarse plaquette energy without enlarging the random test support. These estimates compare protected real means throughout the prefix. The repeated selector uses the physically consistent correction to CMP119 (3.16) explained in §7.74.

The full-law complex source condition, full ordinary susceptibility and continuum existence remain open. The cross-torus vacuum matching and polynomial replicas still require their own normalizations. A uniform physical complex-source pressure still requires a separate full-history argument.
